# ROADMAP: externalize verilator (drop the submodule, mirror the QEMU pattern)

Follows the same move already done for QEMU (commits "drop the QEMU submodule,
integrate a prebuilt external QEMU" + "set QEMU_BIN_DIR"). andesim stops nesting
verilator as a submodule; it consumes a prebuilt vsim from an external location
(e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`) via `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, exactly like
`QEMU_BIN_DIR` points at the external qemu.

## Why / end state

```
BEFORE:  andesim/verilator  (submodule, andesim builds + records it)
AFTER:   andesim            (no verilator submodule)
         vsim_andesim/      (external sibling repo = hybrid_vsim; built there)
         config.env: VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build   <- new, mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR
```

## Relationship to the abi-split work (already done)

- KEEP: F1 (andesim_abi repo) + F2 (andesim include/ submodule). qemu_plugin and
  the driver still consume the ABI from include/.
- KEEP in hybrid_vsim: F3 (external/andesim_abi submodule + CMake swap). vsim_andesim
  needs it to build standalone. Must reach hybrid_vsim origin (see EX5).
- REVERT: F4's andesim verilator-pointer bump (commit 815259d). With no submodule,
  andesim records no verilator commit. EX3 removes the gitlink entirely.

## Safety gate (before EX3, the destructive step)

`619db38` (the F3 ABI-split commit) is only in local checkouts (andesim/verilator
branch andesim; vsim_andesim branch abi-split-verify), NOT on origin. Before
deleting andesim/verilator, push the F3 work to hybrid_vsim origin's `andesim`
branch so vsim_andesim (and any clone) is reproducible. After that, deleting the
local andesim/verilator loses nothing.

## env-var design (mirror QEMU exactly)

| External thing | env (config.env) | setup.sh exports | driver reads |
|----------------|------------------|------------------|--------------|
| qemu           | `QEMU_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_QEMU`      | builtin_qemu path |
| vsim (NEW)     | `VSIM_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (+ `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR`) | engine scan dir |

Driver already has `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` (scan any executable). New: an explicit
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` seam that keeps the `sim_` prefix, falling back to the old
`<repo>/verilator/build` when unset (dev back-compat until the submodule is gone).

# ROADMAP: externalize verilator (drop the submodule, mirror the QEMU pattern)

Follows the same move already done for QEMU (commits "drop the QEMU submodule,
integrate a prebuilt external QEMU" + "set QEMU_BIN_DIR"). andesim stops nesting
verilator as a submodule; it consumes a prebuilt vsim from an external location
(e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`) via `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, exactly like
`QEMU_BIN_DIR` points at the external qemu.

## Why / end state

```
BEFORE:  andesim/verilator  (submodule, andesim builds + records it)
AFTER:   andesim            (no verilator submodule)
         vsim_andesim/      (external sibling repo = hybrid_vsim; built there)
         config.env: VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build   <- new, mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR
```

## Relationship to the abi-split work (already done)

- KEEP: F1 (andesim_abi repo) + F2 (andesim include/ submodule). qemu_plugin and
  the driver still consume the ABI from include/.
- KEEP in hybrid_vsim: F3 (external/andesim_abi submodule + CMake swap). vsim_andesim
  needs it to build standalone. Must reach hybrid_vsim origin (see EX5).
- REVERT: F4's andesim verilator-pointer bump (commit 815259d). With no submodule,
  andesim records no verilator commit. EX3 removes the gitlink entirely.

## Safety gate (before EX3, the destructive step)

`619db38` (the F3 ABI-split commit) is only in local checkouts (andesim/verilator
branch andesim; vsim_andesim branch abi-split-verify), NOT on origin. Before
deleting andesim/verilator, push the F3 work to hybrid_vsim origin's `andesim`
branch so vsim_andesim (and any clone) is reproducible. After that, deleting the
local andesim/verilator loses nothing.

## env-var design (mirror QEMU exactly)

| External thing | env (config.env) | setup.sh exports | driver reads |
|----------------|------------------|------------------|--------------|
| qemu           | `QEMU_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_QEMU`      | builtin_qemu path |
| vsim (NEW)     | `VSIM_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (+ `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR`) | engine scan dir |

Driver already has `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` (scan any executable). New: an explicit
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` seam that keeps the `sim_` prefix, falling back to the old
`<repo>/verilator/build` when unset (dev back-compat until the submodule is gone).

## Features (one session each; TDD on the driver C++)

### EX1 -- driver: discover engines from VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: DONE (commit ff89fd0). vsim_scan_dir() seam + discover_engines +
  cmd_doctor wired; andesim-engine-registry-test green; `andesim doctor` +
  discovery follow $VSIM_BIN_DIR (verified against /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build).
- Type: behavioural
- Desc: add a pure `vsim_scan_dir()` seam: `VSIM_BIN_DIR` if set, else
  `repo_root()/verilator/build`. `discover_engines()` and `cmd_doctor` use it.
  Drop cmd_doctor's `verilator/CMakeLists.txt` submodule-presence check.
- Key files: `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `driver/cmd_doctor.cpp`,
  `driver/engine_registry_test.cpp` (new)
- TDD RED: `vsim_scan_dir()` returns `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` when the env is set; today no
  such function exists / discover_engines hardcodes verilator/build.
- Verify: new doctest green; `andesim-plan-itest` still green.
- Non-destructive (fallback preserved).

### EX2 -- setup.sh + config.env.example: external VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: DONE (commit 4961631). setup.sh locates external vsim from $VSIM_BIN_DIR
  (validates sim_*), exports it, no longer builds vsim; `clean vsim` neutered;
  config.env.example documents VSIM_BIN_DIR. Verified via `source ./setup.sh`.
- Desc: config.env.example gains `VSIM_BIN_DIR=` (mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR). setup.sh
  reads it from config.env instead of hardcoding `$ROOT/verilator/build`,
  validates a `sim_*` exists (like the qemu-system check), exports `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  + `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` for the driver and e2e scripts, and drops the vsim
  BUILD steps.
- Key files: `config.env.example`, `setup.sh`
- Verify: `source ./setup.sh` with VSIM_BIN_DIR=vsim_andesim/build, then
  `./andesim list engines` lists the external vsim engines.
- Depends on: EX1

### EX3 -- remove the verilator submodule (DESTRUCTIVE; gated)
- STATE: DONE (commit 19410bc). Safety gate passed (619db38 pushed to hybrid_vsim
  origin/andesim). Submodule removed (gitlink + .gitmodules + .git/modules +
  build_vsim.sh); build_all.sh vsim target dropped; run_e2e.sh + all
  tests/{vplat,andes_sim,hsim,lib} scripts resolve sim_* from $VSIM_BIN_DIR;
  cmd_doctor + hsim.py submodule row -> include/(abi); Dockerfile.runtime no
  longer builds vsim in-container. `git submodule status` shows only include.
- Desc: revert the F4 pointer bump; `git rm verilator`; drop the `.gitmodules`
  entry; `rm -rf .git/modules/verilator`; remove `scripts/build_vsim.sh`; update
  `scripts/build_all.sh` (drop the vsim build leg); resolve `Dockerfile.runtime`
  (it does `cd verilator && ./build.sh` -- repoint at the external vsim image or
  drop that stage); fix `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f8.sh` to use VSIM_BIN_DIR.
- Key files: `.gitmodules`, `verilator` (gitlink), `scripts/build_all.sh`,
  `scripts/build_vsim.sh`, `Dockerfile.runtime`, `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f8.sh`,
  `hsim.py` (retired golden -- decide: update or leave frozen)
- Verify: andesim has no verilator/ submodule; `build_all.sh` + `./andesim run`
  work against the external vsim.
- Depends on: EX2 + the safety gate (F3 pushed to hybrid_vsim origin)

### EX4 -- docs
- STATE: DONE (markdown). CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md,
  docs/engine_interface.md updated: one submodule (abi); QEMU + vsim external via
  QEMU_BIN_DIR/VSIM_BIN_DIR; build/setup/scan-dir reflect the external vsim.
  REMAINING (minor follow-up): the .ipynb tutorials (andes_sim_tutorial,
  andes_sim_limitations) still show in-tree verilator/build + verilator/src paths.
- Desc: USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/engine_interface.md, README reflect the
  external vsim (build at vsim_andesim, set VSIM_BIN_DIR) and the removed submodule.
- Depends on: EX3

### EX5 -- publish
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: push hybrid_vsim `andesim` branch (the F3 ABI-split, =619db38 content) to
  origin; push andesim_abi (already done F1); push andesim externalization commits.
  Verify a fresh `git clone --recursive andesim` + external vsim build works.
- Depends on: EX4

## Notes

- Engine TYPE label "verilator" (driver/engine_descriptor, json, docs) is the
  engine FAMILY name, normalized to "vsim" for users. It is NOT the submodule
  path and stays unchanged.
- The driver's `repo_root()/build/qemu/...` for builtin qemu is separate; this
  task only touches the vsim scan dir.

## 三個 repo 的最終狀態

| Repo | 角色 | 狀態 |
|---|---|---|
| **`andesim_abi`** (新) | 共用 ABI(6 headers) | pushed,`main` d9c5d9b |
| **`hybrid_vsim`** (= vsim) | vsim 源碼,自帶 `external/andesim_abi` submodule | `origin/andesim` 619db38,standalone build 過 |
| **`hybrid_sim`** (= andesim) | 頂層,**無** verilator submodule | `origin/andesim` 6e9028b |

## 兩階段做了什麼

**階段一 — ABI split** (F1-F5):把 `include/hybrid/` 抽成獨立 `andesim_abi` repo,同時當 andesim (`include/`) 和 vsim (`external/andesim_abi`) 的 submodule。一份合約,vsim 能單獨 build。

**階段二 — externalize verilator** (EX1-EX5,照 QEMU 模式):
- `VSIM_BIN_DIR`(config.env)指向外部 vsim build,driver 掃它 discover engine(TDD,新 `andesim-engine-registry-test`)
- `setup.sh` 定位外部 vsim(不再 build)
- **移除 verilator submodule**(gitlink + `.gitmodules` + `build_vsim.sh`),repoint ~20 個 build/test 腳本到 `${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-...}`
- docs(CLAUDE/README/USER_GUIDE/engine_interface)更新

- in-tree build:5 sim binary
- **standalone** build(vsim_andesim,無 parent):sim binary 出
- driver:`doctor`/`list engines` 透過 `VSIM_BIN_DIR` discover 外部 vsim
- fresh `git clone --recursive`:只有 abi submodule、無 verilator、driver build 過

cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim && bash build_vsim.sh
# andesim 透過 config.env 的 VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build 用它

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do

- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
The code cells run real commands against this repo, so the key claims are
shown, not just stated.</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, the writable M-mode CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (since L20, 2026-06-12), `mscratch`
(since L23, 2026-06-15), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip`
(since L24, 2026-06-15), and the Andes machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl`
(0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (since L21, 2026-06-16) - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg` - S-mode CSRs the
M-only default engine does not implement - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is still missing: no `satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg` (S-mode CSRs the
M-only default engine lacks). `mip` is restored but not `--verify`d (its
pending bits are hardware-driven).</cell id="cell-3">

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported since L6 was resolved 2026-06-13; the engine's RTL must
  implement it, or the resume aborts loudly. No privilege CHANGE inside
  the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET, both outside the envelope)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- 2 Andes machine-setup CSRs: `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA), `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0)
  -- the cache / misc enable crt0 writes at boot (added 2026-06-16,
  partially closing L21)
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- `reserved[192]` = room for ~24 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR EXCEPT the cache / misc pair above: `mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ... (`mcache_ctl` /
  `mmisc_ctl` are now carried). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3) and `medeleg, mideleg` (L4) -- S-mode CSRs the M-only
  default engine does not implement. (`mscratch` left this set in L23;
  `mepc / mcause / mtval / mie / mip` left it in L24 -- all writable
  M-mode CSRs that round-trip now.) PMP is restored only for
  S/U-privilege handoffs (L6, 2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI
  cannot fetch on a PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP
  pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mepc, mcause, mtval, mie, mip (L24), mcycle, minstret, fcsr,
mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl (L21)`, plus
`dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified after write) and the PMP block
for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`). The writable M-mode CSRs are
re-read at drain and compared by `--verify`, except `mip` (restored +
re-read but not compared -- its pending bits are hardware-driven and
diverge between the engines' clocks).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[192]` fits about 24 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers and branch prediction -- exactly the CSRs that shape the
   cycle figure, which is why the cache pair is now transported (L21):
   restoring `mcache_ctl` at resume re-enables the L1 caches crt0 turned
   on, and it takes the write fine via the debug module
   (`write_csr_tolerant`). Other vendor CSRs may still be RO / locked and
   await the same recipe.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Binary prerequisites

These are not limitations to be fixed — they are **known conditions** of the
simulator that every user binary must satisfy. The vplat runtime
(`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`) handles both automatically;
they only bite when someone links against the toolchain's default crt0 instead.

### P1. Caches must be enabled before ROI entry (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the Andes core resets with I-cache and D-cache **off**. The
  vplat `crt0.S` enables them (`csrsi mcache_ctl, 1` + `csrw mcache_ctl,
  0x703`) in its first three instructions, before `main()`. The toolchain
  default `crt0.o` never touches `mcache_ctl`.
- **When it bites**: a program linked with the toolchain default crt0 runs
  entirely uncached on vsim. Cycle counts are **5–10× higher** than they
  would be on silicon. The number looks plausible (no crash, no hang) — it
  is silently wrong.
- **Note**: this is also why the hybrid handoff transports `mcache_ctl` (L21):
  `crt0` ran on QEMU (functional, cache-unmodeled), so vsim must resume with
  the same value or it would re-run the ROI uncached.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat crt0
  is the only supported entry point for cycle-accurate measurement.
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### P2. No semihosting ARGV probe before `main()` (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the toolchain default crt0 probes `argc`/`argv` via the
  RISC-V semihosting magic triple (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`)
  before calling `main()`. QEMU intercepts this; vsim has no semihosting
  handler — the `ebreak` traps and the simulation **hangs before reaching the
  ROI**.
- **When it bites**: any program linked with the toolchain default crt0, run
  under `--mode cycle` or `--mode hybrid`. The hang is before `main()`, so
  no output appears.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat crt0
  calls `main(0, 0, 0)` with no semihosting probe. (If your program needs real
  `argc`/`argv`, pass them through a different channel — a fixed memory address
  or a startup function inside the ROI-free preamble.)
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.</cell id="cell-8">
<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### P3. `main()` return must reach `_exit()`, not a spin loop (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the toolchain default crt0 does not call `_exit()` after
  `main()` returns. It executes `jr t1` — an infinite spin. The simulation
  never terminates; you must kill the process manually.
- **When it bites**: any program where `main()` returns normally (the common
  case — `return 0;`), linked with the toolchain default crt0. Under
  `--mode cycle` or `--mode hybrid` this runs vsim forever; under
  `--mode fast` it pegs QEMU at 100% CPU.
- **Note**: this is distinct from L1 (semihosting inside the ROI). The spin
  happens **after** the ROI ends, so `--trigger pc` runs complete and drain
  correctly — but then vsim never exits and the driver times out waiting for
  the process to finish.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat
  crt0 calls `_exit(main_return_value)` which writes `return_value` to
  SimControl (`0xe0080000`) and terminates both QEMU and vsim immediately.
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/archive/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore. The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory
  regions (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries, but an M-mode resume writes none of them back. vsim runs the
  ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1 silently disappears.
- Partial since L6 (2026-06-13): an S/U-privilege resume DOES mirror the
  producer's PMP block (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`;
  tolerant writes, entries beyond what the hart implements no-op),
  because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access
  faults - an S/U ROI could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - the mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode handoffs; locked-entry semantics
  untested).

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, and `mip` now round-trip end-to-end (L24, 2026-06-15) -- they are restored by `ResumeDriver` and re-read at drain by `drain_with_passthrough`. The remaining gap is that the ROI is still assumed trap-free: if a trap fires inside the ROI the wrong architectural state (reset-value handlers, no `stvec`/`medeleg`/`mideleg` transport) means the execution cannot proceed correctly, and the drained trap-cause values reflect a mid-ROI fault rather than the intended program state.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` (restores mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip as of L24); `state_drain.hpp` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads them, lines ~113-117); `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are still not restored (S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine lacks).
- Status: PARTIAL (trap-cause CSRs round-trip since L24; taking a trap inside the ROI is still untested and out of the supported envelope).

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).
  Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX set before
  the enter marker, in-ROI self-check, distinct sentinel captured at the
  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`).</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mscratch` (CSR 0x340)
  across the handoff. `mscratch` is the M-mode software scratch register, a
  side-effect-free read/write CSR; using it needs no trap, no interrupt,
  no paging. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never
  re-read at drain, so:
  1. a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
     inside the ROI (the **resume gap**); and
  2. a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the drained state,
     which silently kept QEMU1's pre-ROI value (the **drain gap**).
  `--verify` could not catch (2): `state_diff` excluded `mscratch` as a
  "passthrough CSR". The repo's own guard (`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone
  dead in the 2-phase redesign (its readback `phase_c` sat after the exit
  marker, on the deleted QEMU2 leg), so nothing flagged the regression.
- Why it mattered: this broke a workload sitting ENTIRELY inside the
  "safe" envelope, so that envelope list was incomplete.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-15). `mscratch` round-trips end to end:
  - vsim resume: restored via the tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`
    (`resume_driver.hpp`); no FP/V gate -- it is plain M-mode state.
  - vsim drain: re-read from the hart in `drain_with_passthrough`, so an
    in-ROI write is captured (`state_drain.hpp`).
  - `--verify`: `state_diff` strictly compares `mscratch` in the hybrid
    policy.
  - guard: `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` revived as a live 2-phase
    self-check; unit cases in `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
    `state_drain.test.cpp`, `state_diff_test.cpp`.
- Scope: only `mscratch`. `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` remain unrestored (S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine does not implement; deferred to the L3/paging envelope work). `mtvec` is restored but still not re-read at drain. `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` left this set in L24 (2026-06-15) -- they round-trip fully now.</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L24. Writable M-mode trap/interrupt CSRs did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mepc`, `mcause`,
  `mtval`, `mie`, or `mip` across the handoff. These are writable M-mode
  CSRs; reading or writing them needs no trap, no interrupt, no paging.
  Like `mscratch` before L23, they were drained by QEMU1 but never
  restored into vsim and never re-read at drain, so a value stashed
  before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value inside it (the
  **resume gap**) and a value written inside the ROI was dropped at
  drain (the **drain gap**). `--verify` was blind to them too.
- The fix (mirrors L23): `ResumeDriver::resume` restores all five via
  tolerant abstract writes; `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough` re-reads
  all five; `state_diff` compares `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` under the
  hybrid policy.
- The `mip` exception: `mip` is restored + re-read but **excluded from
  `--verify`**. Its pending bits (MTIP/MEIP/MSIP) are hardware/platform-
  driven, not a plain register; the timer-pending bit tracks elapsed
  time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's
  cycle-accurate clock, so comparing it would false-positive. On the
  M-only default engine the restore is a no-op (M pending bits are
  read-only via CSR); it does real work on S-capable engines.
- Still deferred: `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are S-mode CSRs the default
  M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`) does not implement, so there is
  nothing to restore there; they go live only on an S/U engine (L3 for
  paging, the S/U-envelope work for delegation).
- Guard: `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` stashes the writable CSRs
  before the ROI and self-checks `mscratch`/`mepc`/`mie` inside it (plain
  e2e); a hybrid `--verify` run additionally compares `mcause`/`mtval`
  against the pure-QEMU oracle (115 fields match on the default engine).
- Empirically (`ax45mpv_premium`): all of `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`
  round-trip cleanly -- in particular `mtval` is a real read/write
  register here, not hardwired to zero.</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bit: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary was silently measured in M-mode (both sides
  hardcoded `priv = 3`; DCSR.prv was never written, so `dret` always
  resumed in M-mode).
- Status: RESOLVED 2026-06-13. The privilege now round-trips:
  - QEMU plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` virtual register
    (`hybrid_handoff.c`).
  - `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` and reads
    it back: an RTL without S/U (the default `ax45mpv_premium` has
    `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) WARL-pins the field and the resume
    aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error instead of measuring
    the wrong privilege. Reserved `priv=2` is rejected up front.
  - For S/U states the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + 8 even
    `pmpcfg`, addr before cfg) is mirrored into the hart first: with PMP
    implemented and no matching entry, every S/U access faults (this is
    the L2 slice S/U execution cannot run without).
  - `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` at the exit halt, so the drained file
    records the privilege the ROI actually ran in, and `--verify`
    compares it against the QEMU oracle.
- Residual envelope: the ROI must stay in ONE privilege (no traps/xRET),
  paging stays off (L3), and S-mode CSRs are still not transported -- an
  S-mode ROI that reads `stvec`/`sscratch`/... sees vsim reset values.
- e2e: `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` (CHECK_PRIV=1/0) on the
  S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`.

The old one-line-per-side hardcode is gone; only the plugin's atexit
count record (no vCPU context, minstret-only consumer) keeps a static 3:</cell id="cell-15">

<cell id="cell-17"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L7. [PARTIAL 2026-06-16: static-image fit check landed (L26/F3); runtime growth still unchecked] No check that the workload fits guest RAM; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.
  `--mem-size` sets the program RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that
  PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory
  backend = vsim RAM window. The old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared
  mmap" was misleading. The real limitation is now the RUNTIME-growth fit
  check plus the 2 GiB ceiling.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is now checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`, L26/F3) rejects an ELF whose PT_LOAD
  segments reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a
  clear "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past
  the ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates
  the access, QEMU may see it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB (the window minus the scratch page)
  -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:414` (128 MB default), `:424` (2 GiB - 4 KiB
  pre-cap), `:440-455` (the L26/F3 static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`
  `elf_load_top`); `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size
  check); `verilator/src/main.cpp` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`).
- Status: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. The static PT_LOAD fit check landed (L26/F3)
  and the V scratch can no longer be clobbered (it moved above program RAM,
  L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the ceiling still corrupts silently.
  Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5);
  > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. Resuming
  hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN.</cell id="cell-17">
<cell id="cell-18"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andesim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andesim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--mode hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:799-810` (marker registration; the
  `slti` HINTs are matched in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h:32-33`);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:800-805`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /
  `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs
  await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only (read-only /
  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `docs/archive/vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16).</cell id="cell-18">
<cell id="cell-19"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check is manual, not CI-wired  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value across the handoff.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc) re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU
  oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field
  (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:521-552`). It is manual, not CI-wired.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:396` (marker/pc gate), `:521-552` (oracle).
- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by `--verify`;
  CI wiring still OPEN.

### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 silently skipped

- The QEMU2 leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when the
  stub did not advertise one. The leg no longer exists.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub timeout + racy port pick

- The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with
  the leg.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no
  byte-swap path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror (golden only) uses
  a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:28-31`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent
  mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:28-31`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

### L27. `--gdb` is not supported with `--mode hybrid`

- **When it bites**: a user who wants to attach a GDB client (or ICEman for cycle) while also running a QEMU1->vsim hybrid handoff.
- **What happens**: `andesim run` immediately rejects the combination with 'andesim run: --gdb is not supported with --mode hybrid' (rc=2). The hybrid pipeline runs QEMU1 then vsim sequentially in a pipeline and cannot pause for a debugger to attach between legs.
- **`--gdb` with `fast` and `cycle` does work**: `--mode fast --gdb` injects QEMU's GDB stub and pauses at startup (default port 1234, override with `--gdb-port`); `--mode cycle --gdb` starts vsim with a JTAG port (default 9104) in the background and execs ICEman in the foreground (requires `$ICEMAN` set).
- **Where**: `driver/cmd_run.cpp` lines 768-771 (explicit rejection block).
- **Status**: by design; the hybrid model has no debugger attach point between the two legs.
</cell id="cell-19">
<cell id="cell-20"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L25. ROI code that reads or writes time-variant CSRs produces engine-dependent results  (new 2026-06-15)

- **The rule**: code inside the ROI must treat `mcycle` (0xB00), `minstret`
  (0xB02), `mip` (0x344), and `time` (0xC01) as opaque.  No branches,
  arithmetic, or writes on these CSRs inside the ROI.
- **Why**: QEMU approximates both cycle and instruction counts with a CPI≈1
  model; vsim counts actual RTL pipeline cycles and retires.  `mip` pending
  bits (MTIP, MEIP, MSIP) reflect live timer/platform state that differs
  between QEMU's functional clock and vsim's cycle clock.  These values
  diverge at every architectural moment inside the ROI -- by construction,
  not by bug.
- **What happens if the rule is broken**:
  - *Branch on `mcycle`/`minstret`*: the `--verify` oracle (pure QEMU)
    takes a different branch than the hybrid run (vsim); the diff reports a
    GPR or PC mismatch.  The plain run passes; only `--verify` exposes it.
  - *Write `mcycle`* (e.g. `csrw mcycle, zero` to reset a performance
    counter): `StateDrain` re-reads the reset value at the exit marker; the
    reported cycle delta is near-zero or underflows -- silently wrong.
- **Where**: any `csrr`/`csrw` on `mcycle`, `minstret`, `mip`, or `time`
  between the entry and exit markers.
- **Demonstrated by**: `tests/fixtures/break_mcycle_write.S` (write corrupts
  delta), `tests/fixtures/break_verify_diverge.S` (branch diverges under
  `--verify`).
- **Status**: by design.  A static linter on the ELF could warn on in-ROI
  reads/writes of these CSRs (not built).</cell id="cell-20">

<cell id="cell-22"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: five areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` adds
> a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor, and L11 is now
> resolved (2026-06-12): the wire format carries VLEN 128..1024 and an
> over-ceiling vlenb aborts loudly instead of truncating (L10 partial); the marker
> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13); and `fcsr`
> now round-trips with an FP-rounding fixture in the e2e suite (L20
> resolved - five CSRs restore into vsim now, and the silent FP-rounding
> gap in blocker 1 below is closed). L6 is resolved (2026-06-13): the privilege
> level round-trips (plugin gdbstub `priv` -> `dcsr.prv` write+verify ->
> exit-drain readback), S/U handoffs mirror the producer's PMP block
> (L2 partial), an M-only engine aborts loudly, and `rt_priv_smode` /
> `rt_priv_umode` run in the e2e suite on the ax66_makatau engine. The
> remaining state coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L5, L21) are
> unchanged, so the overall scores below still stand.
>
> Re-check 2026-06-15: `mscratch` (L23) then the writable M-mode trap/
> interrupt CSRs `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24) now round-trip --
> 11 CSRs restore into vsim now, re-read at drain, and (except `mip`)
> compared by `--verify` (13 once the `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` cache pair
> landed 2026-06-16, L21, restore-only); `rt_csr_survival` guards them and blocker 4 below
> is updated. The trap-CSR *data* round-trips, but taking a trap inside the
> ROI is still untested (L4 partial). Still a narrow envelope (L2-L5, L21
> unchanged).

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 25 documented limitations; 13 CSRs restore into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be single-privilege (M/S/U since L6), trap-free, paging-off (L1-L5). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | ~~No S/U mode~~ (L6 2026-06-13), ~~no fcsr~~ (L20); still no HPM; Andes vendor CSRs: only the cache/misc pair (`mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`) transported (L21 partial), rest open. |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[192]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding (rt_c_fcsr) and S/U-privilege (rt_priv_*) covered now; still no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** ~~`fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip
   (L20)~~ - resolved 2026-06-12; `fcsr` now transports and `--verify`
   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** ~~M-mode only~~ (S/U privilege
   transports since L6, 2026-06-13, on an S/U-capable engine), but "no
   traps, no paging, no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L5) still
   rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any
   driver code, anything with page faults. The vplat runtime covers
   bare-metal I/O only.
3. **Andes vendor CSR coverage incomplete.** The cycle-shaping cache/misc pair (`mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`) now transports (L21 partial, 2026-06-16), closing the worst accuracy hazard. But `mmsc_cfg`, `micm_cfg`, `mdcm_cfg`, `mxstatus`, `mdcause`, `mnvec`, and the remaining Andes-custom CSRs are still absent from the wire format -- prefetcher, branch-prediction, and ECC controls can still silently shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 13 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mscratch, mepc,
   mcause, mtval, mie, mip, mcycle, minstret, fcsr, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl),
   plus `dcsr.prv` and
   - for S/U handoffs - the PMP block (L6, 2026-06-13). `satp` and
   `medeleg/mideleg` (S-mode CSRs the M-only default engine lacks; and
   PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never written back into vsim
   (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format but not in the
   simulator. Any future need for paging or S-mode delegation inside
   the ROI needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (e.g. `fcsr` took 8 bytes; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 25 numbered limitations (L1-L27, minus L14/L22) plus 3 binary
  prerequisites (P1-P3) and the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify` oracle (L15) wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.</cell id="cell-22">

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, the writable M-mode CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (since L20, 2026-06-12), `mscratch`
(since L23, 2026-06-15), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip`
(since L24, 2026-06-15), and the Andes machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl`
(0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (since L21, 2026-06-16) - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg` - S-mode CSRs the
M-only default engine does not implement - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is still missing: no `satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg` (S-mode CSRs the
M-only default engine lacks). `mip` is restored but not `--verify`d (its
pending bits are hardware-driven).
!grep -n "static constexpr uint16_t kCsr" verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported since L6 was resolved 2026-06-13; the engine's RTL must
  implement it, or the resume aborts loudly. No privilege CHANGE inside
  the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET, both outside the envelope)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- 2 Andes machine-setup CSRs: `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA), `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0)
  -- the cache / misc enable crt0 writes at boot (added 2026-06-16,
  partially closing L21)
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- `reserved[192]` = room for ~24 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR EXCEPT the cache / misc pair above: `mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ... (`mcache_ctl` /
  `mmisc_ctl` are now carried). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3) and `medeleg, mideleg` (L4) -- S-mode CSRs the M-only
  default engine does not implement. (`mscratch` left this set in L23;
  `mepc / mcause / mtval / mie / mip` left it in L24 -- all writable
  M-mode CSRs that round-trip now.) PMP is restored only for
  S/U-privilege handoffs (L6, 2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI
  cannot fetch on a PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP
  pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mepc, mcause, mtval, mie, mip (L24), mcycle, minstret, fcsr,
mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl (L21)`, plus
`dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified after write) and the PMP block
for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`). The writable M-mode CSRs are
re-read at drain and compared by `--verify`, except `mip` (restored +
re-read but not compared -- its pending bits are hardware-driven and
diverge between the engines' clocks).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[192]` fits about 24 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers and branch prediction -- exactly the CSRs that shape the
   cycle figure, which is why the cache pair is now transported (L21):
   restoring `mcache_ctl` at resume re-enables the L1 caches crt0 turned
   on, and it takes the write fine via the debug module
   (`write_csr_tolerant`). Other vendor CSRs may still be RO / locked and
   await the same recipe.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

## Binary prerequisites

These are not limitations to be fixed — they are **known conditions** of the
simulator that every user binary must satisfy. The vplat runtime
(`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`) handles both automatically;
they only bite when someone links against the toolchain's default crt0 instead.

### P1. Caches must be enabled before ROI entry (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the Andes core resets with I-cache and D-cache **off**. The
  vplat `crt0.S` enables them (`csrsi mcache_ctl, 1` + `csrw mcache_ctl,
  0x703`) in its first three instructions, before `main()`. The toolchain
  default `crt0.o` never touches `mcache_ctl`.
- **When it bites**: a program linked with the toolchain default crt0 runs
  entirely uncached on vsim. Cycle counts are **5–10× higher** than they
  would be on silicon. The number looks plausible (no crash, no hang) — it
  is silently wrong.
- **Note**: this is also why the hybrid handoff transports `mcache_ctl` (L21):
  `crt0` ran on QEMU (functional, cache-unmodeled), so vsim must resume with
  the same value or it would re-run the ROI uncached.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat crt0
  is the only supported entry point for cycle-accurate measurement.
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.

### P2. No semihosting ARGV probe before `main()` (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the toolchain default crt0 probes `argc`/`argv` via the
  RISC-V semihosting magic triple (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`)
  before calling `main()`. QEMU intercepts this; vsim has no semihosting
  handler — the `ebreak` traps and the simulation **hangs before reaching the
  ROI**.
- **When it bites**: any program linked with the toolchain default crt0, run
  under `--mode cycle` or `--mode hybrid`. The hang is before `main()`, so
  no output appears.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat crt0
  calls `main(0, 0, 0)` with no semihosting probe. (If your program needs real
  `argc`/`argv`, pass them through a different channel — a fixed memory address
  or a startup function inside the ROI-free preamble.)
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.

### P3. `main()` return must reach `_exit()`, not a spin loop (crt0 prerequisite)

- **What it is**: the toolchain default crt0 does not call `_exit()` after
  `main()` returns. It executes `jr t1` — an infinite spin. The simulation
  never terminates; you must kill the process manually.
- **When it bites**: any program where `main()` returns normally (the common
  case — `return 0;`), linked with the toolchain default crt0. Under
  `--mode cycle` or `--mode hybrid` this runs vsim forever; under
  `--mode fast` it pegs QEMU at 100% CPU.
- **Note**: this is distinct from L1 (semihosting inside the ROI). The spin
  happens **after** the ROI ends, so `--trigger pc` runs complete and drain
  correctly — but then vsim never exits and the driver times out waiting for
  the process to finish.
- **Fix**: link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The vplat
  crt0 calls `_exit(main_return_value)` which writes `return_value` to
  SimControl (`0xe0080000`) and terminates both QEMU and vsim immediately.
- **Status**: by design — known prerequisite; vplat handles it.

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/archive/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore. The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run
still produces a clean `window_cycles` figure:
