### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory
  regions (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries, but an M-mode resume writes none of them back. vsim runs the
  ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1 silently disappears.
- Partial since L6 (2026-06-13): an S/U-privilege resume DOES mirror the
  producer's PMP block (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`;
  tolerant writes, entries beyond what the hart implements no-op),
  because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access
  faults - an S/U ROI could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - the mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode handoffs; locked-entry semantics
  untested).

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, and `mip` now round-trip end-to-end (L24, 2026-06-15) -- they are restored by `ResumeDriver` and re-read at drain by `drain_with_passthrough`. The remaining gap is that the ROI is still assumed trap-free: if a trap fires inside the ROI the wrong architectural state (reset-value handlers, no `stvec`/`medeleg`/`mideleg` transport) means the execution cannot proceed correctly, and the drained trap-cause values reflect a mid-ROI fault rather than the intended program state.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` (restores mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip as of L24); `state_drain.hpp` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads them, lines ~113-117); `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are still not restored (S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine lacks).
- Status: PARTIAL (trap-cause CSRs round-trip since L24; taking a trap inside the ROI is still untested and out of the supported envelope).

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).
  Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX set before
  the enter marker, in-ROI self-check, distinct sentinel captured at the
  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`).

### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mscratch` (CSR 0x340)
  across the handoff. `mscratch` is the M-mode software scratch register, a
  side-effect-free read/write CSR; using it needs no trap, no interrupt,
  no paging. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never
  re-read at drain, so:
  1. a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
     inside the ROI (the **resume gap**); and
  2. a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the drained state,
     which silently kept QEMU1's pre-ROI value (the **drain gap**).
  `--verify` could not catch (2): `state_diff` excluded `mscratch` as a
  "passthrough CSR". The repo's own guard (`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone
  dead in the 2-phase redesign (its readback `phase_c` sat after the exit
  marker, on the deleted QEMU2 leg), so nothing flagged the regression.
- Why it mattered: this broke a workload sitting ENTIRELY inside the
  "safe" envelope, so that envelope list was incomplete.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-15). `mscratch` round-trips end to end:
  - vsim resume: restored via the tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`
    (`resume_driver.hpp`); no FP/V gate -- it is plain M-mode state.
  - vsim drain: re-read from the hart in `drain_with_passthrough`, so an
    in-ROI write is captured (`state_drain.hpp`).
  - `--verify`: `state_diff` strictly compares `mscratch` in the hybrid
    policy.
  - guard: `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` revived as a live 2-phase
    self-check; unit cases in `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
    `state_drain.test.cpp`, `state_diff_test.cpp`.
- Scope: only `mscratch`. `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` remain unrestored (S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine does not implement; deferred to the L3/paging envelope work). `mtvec` is restored but still not re-read at drain. `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` left this set in L24 (2026-06-15) -- they round-trip fully now.

### L24. Writable M-mode trap/interrupt CSRs did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mepc`, `mcause`,
  `mtval`, `mie`, or `mip` across the handoff. These are writable M-mode
  CSRs; reading or writing them needs no trap, no interrupt, no paging.
  Like `mscratch` before L23, they were drained by QEMU1 but never
  restored into vsim and never re-read at drain, so a value stashed
  before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value inside it (the
  **resume gap**) and a value written inside the ROI was dropped at
  drain (the **drain gap**). `--verify` was blind to them too.
- The fix (mirrors L23): `ResumeDriver::resume` restores all five via
  tolerant abstract writes; `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough` re-reads
  all five; `state_diff` compares `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` under the
  hybrid policy.
- The `mip` exception: `mip` is restored + re-read but **excluded from
  `--verify`**. Its pending bits (MTIP/MEIP/MSIP) are hardware/platform-
  driven, not a plain register; the timer-pending bit tracks elapsed
  time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's
  cycle-accurate clock, so comparing it would false-positive. On the
  M-only default engine the restore is a no-op (M pending bits are
  read-only via CSR); it does real work on S-capable engines.
- Still deferred: `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are S-mode CSRs the default
  M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`) does not implement, so there is
  nothing to restore there; they go live only on an S/U engine (L3 for
  paging, the S/U-envelope work for delegation).
- Guard: `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` stashes the writable CSRs
  before the ROI and self-checks `mscratch`/`mepc`/`mie` inside it (plain
  e2e); a hybrid `--verify` run additionally compares `mcause`/`mtval`
  against the pure-QEMU oracle (115 fields match on the default engine).
- Empirically (`ax45mpv_premium`): all of `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`
  round-trip cleanly -- in particular `mtval` is a real read/write
  register here, not hardwired to zero.

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bit: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary was silently measured in M-mode (both sides
  hardcoded `priv = 3`; DCSR.prv was never written, so `dret` always
  resumed in M-mode).
- Status: RESOLVED 2026-06-13. The privilege now round-trips:
  - QEMU plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` virtual register
    (`hybrid_handoff.c`).
  - `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` and reads
    it back: an RTL without S/U (the default `ax45mpv_premium` has
    `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) WARL-pins the field and the resume
    aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error instead of measuring
    the wrong privilege. Reserved `priv=2` is rejected up front.
  - For S/U states the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + 8 even
    `pmpcfg`, addr before cfg) is mirrored into the hart first: with PMP
    implemented and no matching entry, every S/U access faults (this is
    the L2 slice S/U execution cannot run without).
  - `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` at the exit halt, so the drained file
    records the privilege the ROI actually ran in, and `--verify`
    compares it against the QEMU oracle.
- Residual envelope: the ROI must stay in ONE privilege (no traps/xRET),
  paging stays off (L3), and S-mode CSRs are still not transported -- an
  S-mode ROI that reads `stvec`/`sscratch`/... sees vsim reset values.
- e2e: `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` (CHECK_PRIV=1/0) on the
  S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`.

The old one-line-per-side hardcode is gone; only the plugin's atexit
count record (no vCPU context, minstret-only consumer) keeps a static 3:
!grep -n "priv" verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c | grep -E "= 3|dcsr|0x3"

### L7. [PARTIAL 2026-06-16: static-image fit check landed (L26/F3); runtime growth still unchecked] No check that the workload fits guest RAM; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.
  `--mem-size` sets the program RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that
  PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory
  backend = vsim RAM window. The old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared
  mmap" was misleading. The real limitation is now the RUNTIME-growth fit
  check plus the 2 GiB ceiling.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is now checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`, L26/F3) rejects an ELF whose PT_LOAD
  segments reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a
  clear "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past
  the ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates
  the access, QEMU may see it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB (the window minus the scratch page)
  -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:414` (128 MB default), `:424` (2 GiB - 4 KiB
  pre-cap), `:440-455` (the L26/F3 static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`
  `elf_load_top`); `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size
  check); `verilator/src/main.cpp` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`).
- Status: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. The static PT_LOAD fit check landed (L26/F3)
  and the V scratch can no longer be clobbered (it moved above program RAM,
  L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the ceiling still corrupts silently.
  Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5);
  > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. Resuming
  hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN.

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andesim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andesim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--mode hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:799-810` (marker registration; the
  `slti` HINTs are matched in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h:32-33`);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:800-805`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /
  `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs
  await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only (read-only /
  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `docs/archive/vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16).

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

### L27. `--gdb` is not supported with `--mode hybrid`

- **When it bites**: a user who wants to attach a GDB client (or ICEman for cycle) while also running a QEMU1->vsim hybrid handoff.
- **What happens**: `andesim run` immediately rejects the combination with 'andesim run: --gdb is not supported with --mode hybrid' (rc=2). The hybrid pipeline runs QEMU1 then vsim sequentially in a pipeline and cannot pause for a debugger to attach between legs.
- **`--gdb` with `fast` and `cycle` does work**: `--mode fast --gdb` injects QEMU's GDB stub and pauses at startup (default port 1234, override with `--gdb-port`); `--mode cycle --gdb` starts vsim with a JTAG port (default 9104) in the background and execs ICEman in the foreground (requires `$ICEMAN` set).
- **Where**: `driver/cmd_run.cpp` lines 768-771 (explicit rejection block).
- **Status**: by design; the hybrid model has no debugger attach point between the two legs.

### L25. ROI code that reads or writes time-variant CSRs produces engine-dependent results  (new 2026-06-15)

- **The rule**: code inside the ROI must treat `mcycle` (0xB00), `minstret`
  (0xB02), `mip` (0x344), and `time` (0xC01) as opaque.  No branches,
  arithmetic, or writes on these CSRs inside the ROI.
- **Why**: QEMU approximates both cycle and instruction counts with a CPI≈1
  model; vsim counts actual RTL pipeline cycles and retires.  `mip` pending
  bits (MTIP, MEIP, MSIP) reflect live timer/platform state that differs
  between QEMU's functional clock and vsim's cycle clock.  These values
  diverge at every architectural moment inside the ROI -- by construction,
  not by bug.
- **What happens if the rule is broken**:
  - *Branch on `mcycle`/`minstret`*: the `--verify` oracle (pure QEMU)
    takes a different branch than the hybrid run (vsim); the diff reports a
    GPR or PC mismatch.  The plain run passes; only `--verify` exposes it.
  - *Write `mcycle`* (e.g. `csrw mcycle, zero` to reset a performance
    counter): `StateDrain` re-reads the reset value at the exit marker; the
    reported cycle delta is near-zero or underflows -- silently wrong.
- **Where**: any `csrr`/`csrw` on `mcycle`, `minstret`, `mip`, or `time`
  between the entry and exit markers.
- **Demonstrated by**: `tests/fixtures/break_mcycle_write.S` (write corrupts
  delta), `tests/fixtures/break_verify_diverge.S` (branch diverges under
  `--verify`).
- **Status**: by design.  A static linter on the ELF could warn on in-ROI
  reads/writes of these CSRs (not built).

But `mmsc_cfg`, `micm_cfg`, `mdcm_cfg`, `mxstatus`, `mdcause`, `mnvec`, and the remaining Andes-custom CSRs are still absent from the wire format -- prefetcher, branch-prediction, and ECC controls can still silently shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 13 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mscratch, mepc,
   mcause, mtval, mie, mip, mcycle, minstret, fcsr, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl),
   plus `dcsr.prv` and
   - for S/U handoffs - the PMP block (L6, 2026-06-13). `satp` and
   `medeleg/mideleg` (S-mode CSRs the M-only default engine lacks; and
   PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never written back into vsim
   (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format but not in the
   simulator. Any future need for paging or S-mode delegation inside
   the ROI needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (e.g. `fcsr` took 8 bytes; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 25 numbered limitations (L1-L27, minus L14/L22) plus 3 binary
  prerequisites (P1-P3) and the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify` oracle (L15) wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64" ]; then
    err "no qemu-system-riscv64 under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64 (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim

  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {

    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"

    return 1

    return 1

    return 1

  esac

  export VSIM_BIN_DIR

docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb:559:   "source": "## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andesim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andesim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--mode hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:799-810` (marker registration; the
  `slti` HINTs are matched in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h:32-33`);
  `src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:800-805`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /
  `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs
  await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only (read-only /
  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `docs/archive/vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."

  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andesim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andesim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--mode hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:799-810` (marker registration; the
  `slti` HINTs are matched in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h:32-33`);
  `src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:800-805`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /
  `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs
  await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only (read-only /
  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `docs/archive/vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."

content.text:
完成,已 push(`f2a66b8`,local==origin)。

## 這段做的兩件相關修正

**1. `list engines` 缺 vsim 的根因(`5cb1584`)**
driver 之前只從**環境變數**讀 `VSIM_BIN_DIR`,沒 source 就 fallback 到已移除的 `verilator/build` → 看不到 vsim。加了共用 `config_env_value(key)` helper(env 優先 → config.env,跟既有 `read_hybrid_toolchain` 同 pattern),vsim 與 qemu 路徑都改用它。**現在 `./andesim list/run/doctor` 免 source 就找得到外部 qemu+vsim**。

**2. rv32 qemu engine `qemu32`(`f2a66b8`)**
- `list engines` 現在出 **qemu (rv64) + qemu32 (rv32)**
- `builtin_qemu()` → `builtin_qemu_arch(xlen)`;`run --mode fast --engine qemu32` 用 `qemu-system-riscv32`
- fast `-cpu`:rv64=`andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`(原本),qemu32=`andes-d23`(你選的,對應 vsim:d23)

## 一個要告訴你的實測修正
你的「fast = qemu default(無 -cpu)」**實測會 hang** —— `andes_ae350` 的 generic default cpu 跑不動 vplat fixture(補 `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` 才印出 hello)。所以我**沒有**拿掉 -cpu,fast 仍 pin andes 核;使用者要的話用 `-- -cpu ...` 覆寫。

## 沒碰的部分
hybrid 完全沒動(rv64 fast-leg 原封不動;qemu32 沒有 fast-leg)。**hybrid rv32 + 「-cpu 對應配對 engine core」是後續工作** —— 那需要先決定 cpu 來源(vsim `--describe` 出 qemu_cpu 欄位 vs driver 從 id 推導),你之前選「先只做 fast」,所以留著。

驗證:unit test 綠、兩個 engine 都列出、rv64 fast 仍印 "hello from vplat"、andes-d23 在 rv32 qemu 有效。

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: `doctor` (read-only env-health).
#
#   1. The four carried-over sections (artifacts / submodules / toolchain /
#      runtime) plus the Summary line match `python3 hsim doctor` byte-for-byte,
#      including the exit code, in the ambient (healthy) env.
#   2. MISSING-ARTIFACT: a bogus VSIM_QEMU makes BOTH drivers FAIL the qemu row
#      and exit 1, with identical carried-over output.
#   3. The C++-only engines section reflects F2 discovery: the built-in qemu and
#      a hermetic fake engine both appear under `engines:`.
#
# The C++ driver appends an `engines:` readout after Summary; parity is scoped to
# the carried-over report by truncating at (and including) the `Summary:` line.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
GOLDEN="$ROOT/hsim.py"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# The carried-over report = every line through the `Summary:` line.
carried() { awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}'; }

# 1. healthy parity (ambient env)
g=$("$GOLDEN" doctor 2>&1);  grc=$?
nf=$("$BIN" doctor 2>&1);    nrc=$?
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$nf" | carried)
[ "$grc" = "$nrc" ] || fail "doctor rc differs: golden=$grc new=$nrc"
[ "$g" = "$n" ] || {
  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$g") <(printf '%s\n' "$n") >&2
  fail "doctor carried-over output differs from golden"
}

# 2. missing-artifact: a bogus qemu path -> both FAIL the qemu row and exit 1
bogus=/nonexistent/qemu-xyz
g=$(VSIM_QEMU="$bogus" "$GOLDEN" doctor 2>&1);  grc=$?
nf=$(VSIM_QEMU="$bogus" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1);    nrc=$?
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$nf" | carried)
[ "$grc" = "1" ] || fail "golden doctor should exit 1 on missing qemu (got $grc)"
[ "$grc" = "$nrc" ] || fail "doctor rc differs (missing-artifact): golden=$grc new=$nrc"
[ "$g" = "$n" ] || {
  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$g") <(printf '%s\n' "$n") >&2
  fail "doctor carried-over output differs (missing-artifact)"
}

# 3. engines section reflects discovery (hermetic fake engine via F2)
ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f3.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:fakeD","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD"

out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "^engines:" \
  || fail "doctor missing engines section:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu" \
  || fail "doctor engines: built-in qemu absent"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeD" \
  || fail "doctor engines: fake engine not reflected (F2):"$'\n'"$out"

# 4. mmap tiers section (C++-only, after Summary like engines): both default
# tiers with free space; HSIM_MMAP_DIR collapses it to the single pinned dir.
out=$("$BIN" doctor 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "^mmap tiers:" \
  || fail "doctor missing mmap tiers section:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "/dev/shm" || fail "mmap tiers: /dev/shm row absent"
echo "$out" | grep -q "andesim.*free:" \
  || fail "mmap tiers: cache tier row with free space absent:"$'\n'"$out"

PIN=$(mktemp -d -t andes-doctor-pin.XXXXXX)
out=$(HSIM_MMAP_DIR="$PIN" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "HSIM_MMAP_DIR" \
  || fail "mmap tiers: pinned dir not reflected:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | sed -n '/^mmap tiers:/,/^[^ ]/p' | grep -q "\.cache/andesim" \
  && fail "mmap tiers: pin should hide the default tier list:"$'\n'"$out"
rm -rf "$PIN"

ok "F3 doctor"

lines: || fail "doctor engines: fake engine not reflected (F2):"$'\n'"$out"

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{trigger}`   | the plugin comma-suffix for the trigger (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu` descriptor is always present (QEMU does not implement
   `--describe`; its binary path honors `$VSIM_QEMU`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |

| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Analysis complete. I traced every call site and the `repo_root()` caching behavior.

## Efficiency review: driver diff `ff20602..HEAD`

Verdict: essentially no real efficiency problem. One genuine redundancy exists but its cost is negligible (one-shot CLI startup, tiny file). Reporting it conservatively, plus the explicit answers to your three questions.

**Finding 1 (minor/borderline) — duplicate `config.env` scan for the same key in one call**
- File/line: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:76` (via `builtin_qemu_arch`), reached twice from `discover_engines()` at lines 189 + 195.
- Summary: `discover_engines()` calls `builtin_qemu_arch(64)` then `builtin_qemu_arch(32)`; when `$VSIM_QEMU`/`$VSIM_QEMU32` are unset, each independently opens and scans `config.env` for the *same* `QEMU_BIN_DIR` key, then `vsim_scan_dir()` opens it a third time for `VSIM_BIN_DIR`.
- Concrete cost: up to 3 `ifstream` open+getline scans per `discover_engines()`, 2 of them identical (`QEMU_BIN_DIR`). `doctor` is the worst case: `doctor_artifacts()` opens it twice more (lines 62 + 69) before `print_engines_section()`'s `discover_engines()`, so `QEMU_BIN_DIR` is scanned 3x and `VSIM_BIN_DIR` 2x in one `andesim doctor`. All are startup, one-shot (grep confirms `discover_engines()` is never called in a loop), and `config.env` is a few lines. The `config_env_value` early-returns on a `getenv` hit, so when the env is set there is zero file I/O. The whole cost is dwarfed by `scan_dir`'s per-engine `--describe` subprocess spawns.
- Cheaper alternative (only if you want it): memoize `config_env_value` per key with a `static` cache, or read `config.env` once into a small `map<string,string>` at startup. Given the proportionality, not worth the added state — this is fine as-is.

**Q: extra `builtin_qemu_arch(32)` descriptor every call — cheap? per-engine repeated work?**
- Cheap. It builds one `EngineDescriptor` (~a dozen small `std::string`/vector allocations) plus the one duplicate `config.env` read noted above. It is needed so `list engines`/`doctor` show `qemu32`. No per-engine loop work — `config_env_value` is not called inside `scan_dir`'s per-entry loop (confirmed: `scan_dir` only calls `is_executable_file`/`describe_one`).

**Q: any object built from a captured closure/environment that outlives its scope?**
- None. The only lambdas in the diff (`fail` in `run_hybrid`, `fast_cpu` in the test) capture nothing (`[]`) and don't escape. `config_env_value`/`vsim_scan_dir` return `std::string`/`fs::path` by value; no dangling refs.

Mitigating fact worth noting: `repo_root()` (called inside every `config_env_value` via the `repo_root() / "config.env"` overload) is `static`-cached (`repo_root.hpp:38`), so the repeated calls do not re-walk the filesystem for the root — only the small `config.env` file open repeats.

Bottom line: no hot-path waste; the single redundant same-key scan is real but negligible and acceptable for one-shot CLI startup.

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
