#=========================================================================
# crt0.S : Entry point for RISC-V user programs
#=========================================================================

#ifndef CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
#define CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS 0
#endif

#define mcache_ctl 0x7ca
#define mmisc_ctl 0x7d0

  .text
  .global _start
  .type   _start, @function
_start:
  # Enable icache
  csrsi   mcache_ctl, 0x1

#ifdef ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE
  # Enable dcache coherence management
  li      a0, 1 << 19
  csrs    mcache_ctl, a0
1:
  csrr    a0, mcache_ctl
#if __nds_v5
  bbc     a0, 20, 1b
#else
  srli    a1, a0, 20
  andi    a1, a1, 1
  beqz    a1, 1b
#endif
#endif

  # Enable d-cache and hardware prefetch
  ori     a0, a0, 0x703
  csrw    mcache_ctl, a0

  .weak   _stack
  # Initialize stack pointer (if defined)
  lla     a0, _stack
  beqz    a0, 1f
  mv      sp, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  slli    a0, a0, 12
  sub     sp, sp, a0
#endif

  # Initialize global pointer
.option push
.option norelax
1:lla gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop

#ifdef __nds_v5
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg
  bbc     a0, 3, 1f
  la      a1, _ITB_BASE_
  csrrw   x0, uitb, a1
1:
#if __riscv_xlen >= 64
  bbc     a0, 52, 1f
#else
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg2
  bbc     a0, 20, 1f
#endif
  csrr    a0, mrvarch_cfg
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  la      a0, __jvt_base$
  csrw    jvt, a0
#endif
1:

  # Set mstatus.fs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 13)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Set mstatus.vs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 10)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Enable unaligned memory access (mmisc_ctl.UNA)
  li      a0, (1 << 6)
  csrs    mmisc_ctl, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss

  li      a1, 0xa55a
.Lother_hart_wait_loop:
  ld      a0, other_hart_boot_flag
  bne     a0, a1, .Lother_hart_wait_loop
  j       .Lmain
#else
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss
  li      a0, 0x01234571
  li      a1, 0xe0080000
  sw      a0, 0(a1)
1:
  j       1b
#endif

  # Clear the bss segment
.Lclear_bss:
  la      a0, _edata
  la      a2, _end
  sub     a2, a2, a0
  li      a1, 0
  call    memset


#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  li      a0, 0xa55a
  lla     a1, other_hart_boot_flag
  sd      a0, 0(a1)
  fence
#endif

  call init_mtvec

.Lmain:
  li      a0, 0
  li      a1, 0
  li      a2, 0
  call    main

  call    _exit

.Lloop:
  j       .Lloop

  .size   _start, .-_start

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  .data
  .p2align 3
  .global other_hart_boot_flag
  .type   other_hart_boot_flag, @object
other_hart_boot_flag:
  .8byte 0
  .size other_hart_boot_flag, . - other_hart_boot_flag
#endif

content.text:
已讀完 spec 的 CSR 章節 (Table 6 Andes M-mode、Table 11 Andes U-mode) + 你專案的 `crt0.S`/`core_v5.h`/plugin drain 機制。下面是大綱。

## 答案:還缺 5 組 Andes 專屬狀態

目前 hybrid 只搬了 2 個 Andes CSR:`mcache_ctl` (0x7CA)、`mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0)。要完整支援 bare-metal Andes Core,還缺下面這些。

## 核心架構:把每個 Andes CSR 分成 4 類

這是你要看懂的「樹根」,細節 CSR 是「葉子」:

| Class | 意思 | 怎麼處理 | 例子 |
|-------|------|----------|------|
| **0 配置唯讀** | 每顆 core 焊死,QEMU `-cpu` 必須等於 vsim RTL | **不搬**,只加一次性一致性檢查 | 所有 `0xFCx/0xFDx` (micm_cfg, mmsc_cfg...), crash-save |
| **1 開機設定** | crt0 在 ROI 前寫一次,ROI 內只讀 | drain + restore (像現在的 mcache_ctl) | PMA, mxstatus, uitb, jvt, ILM/DLM, mpft_ctl |
| **2 ROI 內活狀態** | ROI 內會被改,要完整 round-trip + verify | drain + restore + re-drain + diff (像 vxsat) | ucode (DSP 溢位旗標) |
| **3 trap/中斷狀態** | ROI 假設無 trap/無中斷 | **暫不做**,留給 S/U 信封工作 | mdcause, msave*, CLIC, NMI vector |

## 葉子細節:候選 CSR 清單 (按優先序)

| 優先 | CSR | 位址 | 是什麼 | bare-metal 為何需要 | 影響 |
|------|-----|------|--------|---------------------|------|
| **P1** | `uitb` | 0x800 | CoDense 指令表基址 | crt0 已會寫;ROI 內有 `exec.it` 就會錯 | 正確性 |
| **P1** | `jvt` | 0x017 | Zcmt 跳表基址 | crt0 已會寫;ROI 內有 `cm.jt/cm.jalt` 就會錯 | 正確性 |
| **P1** | `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` | 0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF | 實體記憶體屬性 (可快取/device/NAPOT) | core_v5.h 已定義;沒搬 → device 區被當可快取(錯) 或 DRAM 當不可快取(cycle 暴增) | 正確性 + cycle |
| **P2** | `mxstatus` | 0x7C4 | Andes 版 mstatus (DME/IME 對齊例外、PFT_EN) | BSP 開機設對齊處理模式 | 正確性 |

## 一個架構約束你必須先決定:ABI 預算

`hybrid_state_v1` 現在 `reserved[208]` = 只剩 26 個 u64 欄位。

所以:**做不做 PMA,決定要不要把 ABI 升到 v3。**

2. vsim Debug Module 能寫這個 CSR (能 restore)

# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

## The 3 repos every feature (except F0) touches

| Repo | Path | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `andesim_abi` (submodule) | `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h` | wire struct + layout lock -- **F0 only** |
| `andesim` | `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | drain (gdbstub read) |
| `andesim` | `driver/state_diff.{hpp,cpp}` (+ `state_diff_test.cpp`) | `--verify` compare |
| `andesim` | `tests/fixtures/*` | RED fixtures |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`) | `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | restore (DMI write; extend the `write_csr_tolerant` list / PMP-style loop) |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external) | `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | re-drain (DMI read at exit halt) |

Dedup targets (Coding Principle: don't duplicate): restore reuses
`write_csr_tolerant(addr,val)`; PMA reuses the existing `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg` loop
shape; drain reuses the `find_reg` + `read_reg64` pattern.

---

## F0 - v3 ABI + dedicated Andes block  [BLOCKS ALL OTHERS]

Status: TODO. Deps: none.

Define the whole Andes block ONCE so F1..F8 only populate existing fields (no
later offset reshuffle -> features stay independent). Bump
`HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` 2 -> 3; add `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` to gate the block
live; all three readers reject version<3 by magic+version+size.

Proposed block (LE u64; zero = "producer lacked it"):

```c
struct hybrid_andes_csr {     // v3
  uint64_t mxstatus;          // 0x7C4  Andes mstatus companion (DME/IME/PFT_EN)
  uint64_t mpft_ctl;          // 0x7C5  perf throttling (T_LEVEL)
  uint64_t mclk_ctl;          // 0x7DF  clock control
  uint64_t milmb;             // 0x7C0  ILM base + enable
  uint64_t mdlmb;             // 0x7C1  DLM base + enable
  uint64_t mecc_code;         // 0x7C2  ECC code
  uint64_t mhsp_ctl;          // 0x7C6  HW stack protection control
  uint64_t msp_bound;         // 0x7C7
  uint64_t msp_base;          // 0x7C8
  uint64_t mcountermask_m;    // 0x7D1  counter mask (cycle hygiene)
  uint64_t uitb;              // 0x800  CoDense instruction table base
  uint64_t jvt;               // 0x017  Zcmt jump vector table
  uint64_t ucode;             // 0x801  DSP/P-ext overflow flag (Class 2)
  uint64_t pmacfg[2];         // 0xBC0, 0xBC2 (RV64: 16 entries / 2 regs)
  uint64_t pmaaddr[16];       // 0xBD0..0xBDF
};                            // 31 u64 = 248 bytes; recompute reserved[]
```

Key files: `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`; size/version gate in
`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`, and
`driver/state_diff.cpp`. Coordinated: edit `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule
pointer in BOTH `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts `version==3`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, and
`offsetof`/`sizeof` of the new block + every named field (layout lock). All
fields zero on legacy producers.

---

## F1 - CoDense + Zcmt table bases (`uitb` 0x800, `jvt` 0x017)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. (crt0 already emits both conditionally -- the
smallest real gap; good first feature.)

RED fixture: ROI uses `exec.it` (needs `uitb`) and/or `cm.jt`/`cm.jalt` (needs
`jvt`); without transport it faults or mis-executes in vsim. Plus round-trip:
write sentinel pre-ROI, read back inside ROI, `--verify` drain==restore.

GREEN: drain `uitb`/`jvt`; restore via `write_csr_tolerant`; re-drain; compare.

---

## F2 - `mxstatus` (0x7C4)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Andes companion to `mstatus` (DME/IME misalign
exception enable, PFT_EN). Writable M-mode -> full round-trip + verify (model on
`mscratch`). RED: fixture sets `mxstatus` sentinel pre-ROI, reads inside, verify.

---

## F3 - PMA: `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` (0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Biggest + highest correctness/cycle impact.
Memory attributes (cacheable / device / NAPOT). Reuse the `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg`
loop shape in `resume_driver.hpp`. Gated on `mmsc_cfg.PPMA`.

RED fixture: mark an MMIO region device-type + a RAM region cacheable via PMA
pre-ROI; without transport vsim resumes PMA-reset -> wrong cache/device behavior.
Assert via cycle delta (cacheable RAM) and/or a device-ordering check.

---

## F4 - DSP `ucode` (0x801)  [Class 2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. The P-ext overflow (OV) flag is LIVE state, like `vxsat`:
restore BEFORE the ROI, re-drain AFTER, `state_diff` compares it. Gated on P-ext.
RED: DSP op sets OV; round-trip must preserve the bit.

---

## F5 - Local Memory `milmb` (0x7C0), `mdlmb` (0x7C1) [+ `mecc_code` 0x7C2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Base+enable of ILM/DLM. Only live if the linker
script places sections in LM (check `runtime/andesim.ld`). RED: place a hot array
in DLM; transport keeps vsim accessing fast LM (cycle delta) vs DRAM/fault.

---

## F6 - Throttle / clock `mpft_ctl` (0x7C5), `mclk_ctl` (0x7DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Cycle-only. Pairs with `mxstatus.PFT_EN` (F2):
if throttling is enabled, the resumed leg must throttle identically or the cycle
figure diverges. RED: enable throttle pre-ROI, assert cycle delta matches.

---

## F7 - HW stack protection `mhsp_ctl` (0x7C6), `msp_bound` (0x7C7), `msp_base` (0x7C8)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. If crt0 enables stack overflow/underflow
detection, the bounds must survive or vsim either misses protection or
false-traps. RED: enable + set bounds pre-ROI; ROI stack access stays in-bounds.

---

## F8 - Counter mask `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) [+ `mcountinhibit` 0x320]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Cycle-figure hygiene: controls whether `mcycle`/
`minstret` advance in M-mode. RED: set mask pre-ROI, assert the cycle figure
reflects it.

---

## Out of scope (record, do not implement now)

- Class 0 config/RO: `micm_cfg`/`mdcm_cfg`/`mmsc_cfg*`/`mvec_cfg`/`mrvarch_cfg*`/
  `mhvm*`/`mpl2cm_cfg`/`ml1dbf_cfg`/`mccache_ctl_base`, crash-save. (consistency
  assert only, optional later feature.)
- Class 3 trap/NMI/CLIC: `mdcause`, `mslideleg`, `msavestatus`/`msaveepc{1,2}`/
  `msavecause{1,2}`/`msavedcause{1,2}`, `mnvec`/`mrnxvec`, `mirq_entry`/
  `mintsel_jal`/`pushm*`. Deferred to the trap-bearing / S-U-envelope ROI work.
- `mppib`/`mfiob` (PPI/FIO base): platform-static; consistency check, not transport.

1	// Oracle differential compare (verify_oracle F2): field-wise diff of two
2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).
4	//
5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31],
8	//            mepc/mcause (round-trip), mscratch (L23) + mtval/mie (L24) --
9	//            round-trip M-mode CSRs restored at resume + re-read at drain;
10	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
11	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.
12	//   skipped: mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, mip, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[].
13	//            mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp/PMP are passthrough on the vsim side
14	//            (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read). mip IS
15	//            re-read but excluded here -- its pending bits are hardware-driven
16	//            and diverge between the engines' clocks. mstatus is excluded for
17	//            its dirty/impl-defined bits.
18	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret -- the engines count cycles/insns differently
19	//            by design.
20	#ifndef ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
21	#define ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
22	
23	#include <string>
24	#include <vector>
25	
26	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"

28	namespace andes_sim {
29	
30	// One strictly-compared field that differs: "pc", "x5", "f31", "vl",
31	// "v3[7]" (register + byte offset), "flags", ...
32	struct FieldDiff {
33	  std::string field;
34	  unsigned long long ref = 0;
35	  unsigned long long got = 0;
36	};
37	
38	struct DiffReport {
39	  int compared = 0;  // count of strictly compared fields
40	  std::vector<FieldDiff> diffs;

47	// PASS/FAIL verdict. Shared by the state-diff subcommand and run --verify.

50	}  // namespace andes_sim

# Hybrid simulator (QEMU + Verilator) build integration.

option(VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID "Enable hybrid QEMU+Verilator co-simulation" OFF)

set(VSIM_QEMU_ROOT "/local/nick/qemu_v5"
  CACHE PATH "Path to QEMU source tree used to build the hybrid TCG plugin")

# Register a header-only hybrid doctest: build it (vsim_add_test marks it
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL), expose the shared ABI headers from the andesim_abi
# submodule (external/andesim_abi/hybrid), and wire it into the `check`
# target. The include path is inert for the handful of tests that do not
# pull in state_abi.h.
function(hybrid_add_test name source)
  vsim_add_test(${name} ${source})
  target_include_directories(${name} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  add_dependencies(check ${name})
endfunction()

# non-hybrid builds. It has no SystemC/Verilator dependency.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.
#
# What it does (README Option 3):
#   1. Build the `env` target image (verilator + toolchain) from ./Dockerfile.
#   2. Run ./build.sh inside that container with the repo bind-mounted at /work,
#      so build artifacts land in ./build/ on the host.
#
# Trim config.yaml to the CPU(s) you need first to cut build time.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# build.sh / cmake pull in external/ submodules; bail early if they are empty.
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

## The 3 repos every feature (except F0) touches

| Repo | Path | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `andesim_abi` (submodule) | `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h` | wire struct + layout lock -- **F0 only** |
| `andesim` | `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | drain (gdbstub read) |
| `andesim` | `driver/state_diff.{hpp,cpp}` (+ `state_diff_test.cpp`) | `--verify` compare |
| `andesim` | `tests/fixtures/*` | RED fixtures |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`) | `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | restore (DMI write; extend the `write_csr_tolerant` list / PMP-style loop) |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external) | `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | re-drain (DMI read at exit halt) |

Dedup targets (Coding Principle: don't duplicate): restore reuses
`write_csr_tolerant(addr,val)`; PMA reuses the existing `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg` loop
shape; drain reuses the `find_reg` + `read_reg64` pattern.

---

## F0 - v3 ABI + dedicated Andes block  [BLOCKS ALL OTHERS]

Status: TODO. Deps: none.

Define the whole Andes block ONCE so F1..F8 only populate existing fields (no
later offset reshuffle -> features stay independent). Bump
`HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` 2 -> 3; add `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` to gate the block
live; all three readers reject version<3 by magic+version+size.

Proposed block (LE u64; zero = "producer lacked it"):

```c
struct hybrid_andes_csr {     // v3
  uint64_t mxstatus;          // 0x7C4  Andes mstatus companion (DME/IME/PFT_EN)
  uint64_t mpft_ctl;          // 0x7C5  perf throttling (T_LEVEL)
  uint64_t mclk_ctl;          // 0x7DF  clock control
  uint64_t milmb;             // 0x7C0  ILM base + enable
  uint64_t mdlmb;             // 0x7C1  DLM base + enable
  uint64_t mecc_code;         // 0x7C2  ECC code
  uint64_t mhsp_ctl;          // 0x7C6  HW stack protection control
  uint64_t msp_bound;         // 0x7C7
  uint64_t msp_base;          // 0x7C8
  uint64_t mcountermask_m;    // 0x7D1  counter mask (cycle hygiene)
  uint64_t uitb;              // 0x800  CoDense instruction table base
  uint64_t jvt;               // 0x017  Zcmt jump vector table
  uint64_t ucode;             // 0x801  DSP/P-ext overflow flag (Class 2)
  uint64_t pmacfg[2];         // 0xBC0, 0xBC2 (RV64: 16 entries / 2 regs)
  uint64_t pmaaddr[16];       // 0xBD0..0xBDF
};                            // 31 u64 = 248 bytes; recompute reserved[]
```

Key files: `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`; size/version gate in
`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`, and
`driver/state_diff.cpp`. Coordinated: edit `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule
pointer in BOTH `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts `version==3`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, and
`offsetof`/`sizeof` of the new block + every named field (layout lock). All
fields zero on legacy producers.

---

## F1 - CoDense + Zcmt table bases (`uitb` 0x800, `jvt` 0x017)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. (crt0 already emits both conditionally -- the
smallest real gap; good first feature.)

RED fixture: ROI uses `exec.it` (needs `uitb`) and/or `cm.jt`/`cm.jalt` (needs
`jvt`); without transport it faults or mis-executes in vsim. Plus round-trip:
write sentinel pre-ROI, read back inside ROI, `--verify` drain==restore.

GREEN: drain `uitb`/`jvt`; restore via `write_csr_tolerant`; re-drain; compare.

---

## F2 - `mxstatus` (0x7C4)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Andes companion to `mstatus` (DME/IME misalign
exception enable, PFT_EN). Writable M-mode -> full round-trip + verify (model on
`mscratch`). RED: fixture sets `mxstatus` sentinel pre-ROI, reads inside, verify.

---

## F3 - PMA: `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` (0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Biggest + highest correctness/cycle impact.
Memory attributes (cacheable / device / NAPOT). Reuse the `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg`
loop shape in `resume_driver.hpp`. Gated on `mmsc_cfg.PPMA`.

RED fixture: mark an MMIO region device-type + a RAM region cacheable via PMA
pre-ROI; without transport vsim resumes PMA-reset -> wrong cache/device behavior.
Assert via cycle delta (cacheable RAM) and/or a device-ordering check.

---

## F4 - DSP `ucode` (0x801)  [Class 2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. The P-ext overflow (OV) flag is LIVE state, like `vxsat`:
restore BEFORE the ROI, re-drain AFTER, `state_diff` compares it. Gated on P-ext.
RED: DSP op sets OV; round-trip must preserve the bit.

---

## F5 - Local Memory `milmb` (0x7C0), `mdlmb` (0x7C1) [+ `mecc_code` 0x7C2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Base+enable of ILM/DLM. Only live if the linker
script places sections in LM (check `runtime/andesim.ld`). RED: place a hot array
in DLM; transport keeps vsim accessing fast LM (cycle delta) vs DRAM/fault.

---

## F6 - Throttle / clock `mpft_ctl` (0x7C5), `mclk_ctl` (0x7DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Cycle-only. Pairs with `mxstatus.PFT_EN` (F2):
if throttling is enabled, the resumed leg must throttle identically or the cycle
figure diverges. RED: enable throttle pre-ROI, assert cycle delta matches.

---

## F7 - HW stack protection `mhsp_ctl` (0x7C6), `msp_bound` (0x7C7), `msp_base` (0x7C8)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. If crt0 enables stack overflow/underflow
detection, the bounds must survive or vsim either misses protection or
false-traps. RED: enable + set bounds pre-ROI; ROI stack access stays in-bounds.

---

## F8 - Counter mask `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) [+ `mcountinhibit` 0x320]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Cycle-figure hygiene: controls whether `mcycle`/
`minstret` advance in M-mode. RED: set mask pre-ROI, assert the cycle figure
reflects it.

---

## Out of scope (record, do not implement now)

- Class 0 config/RO: `micm_cfg`/`mdcm_cfg`/`mmsc_cfg*`/`mvec_cfg`/`mrvarch_cfg*`/
  `mhvm*`/`mpl2cm_cfg`/`ml1dbf_cfg`/`mccache_ctl_base`, crash-save. (consistency
  assert only, optional later feature.)
- Class 3 trap/NMI/CLIC: `mdcause`, `mslideleg`, `msavestatus`/`msaveepc{1,2}`/
  `msavecause{1,2}`/`msavedcause{1,2}`, `mnvec`/`mrnxvec`, `mirq_entry`/

content.subject: F0: v3 ABI + Andes block
content.description: Bump HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2->3, add HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES and struct hybrid_andes_csr with all fields named. Update state_abi_check.h static_asserts. Update size/version gates in plugin, vsim state_loader/state_drain, driver state_diff. RED: state_abi.test.cpp asserts version==3 + offsets/sizeof.
content.activeForm: Implementing F0 v3 ABI + Andes block

content.subject: F1: uitb + jvt transport
content.description: CoDense uitb (0x800) + Zcmt jvt (0x017). Drain (plugin find_reg), restore (write_csr_tolerant), re-drain (state_drain), verify (state_diff). RED fixture + unit tests.

content.subject: F2: mxstatus transport
content.description: mxstatus (0x7C4) Andes mstatus companion. Full round-trip + verify (model on mscratch).

content.subject: F3: PMA transport
content.description: pmacfg0/2 (0xBC0/2) + pmaaddr0..15 (0xBD0..DF). Reuse pmpaddr/pmpcfg loop in resume_driver. Drain/restore/redrain/verify.

content.subject: F4: ucode (DSP OV) transport
content.description: ucode (0x801) P-ext overflow flag. Class 2 live state like vxsat: restore before ROI, re-drain after, state_diff compares.

content.subject: F5: ILM/DLM transport

# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

## STATUS (transport implemented + unit-tested)

F0 + the transport for F1-F8 are DONE and unit-tested across the 3 repos. The
key design decision: a single X-macro (`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` in the ABI
header) drives all four consumers (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify), so the 13 scalar CSRs are wired
once, not per-feature; PMA arrays mirror the existing PMP loops. This collapses
F1/F2/F4-F8 into the shared machinery + PMA (F3). Verified:

- ABI layout lock: `state_abi.test.cpp` (v3, 126 assertions).
- restore: `resume_driver.test.cpp` (every Andes CSR + PMA, 392 assertions).
- re-read: `state_drain.test.cpp` (whole block round-trip, 604 assertions).
- verify: `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` (per-feature field probes, all pass).
- plugin drain compiles clean; the real Andes QEMU (`target/riscv/andes_csr.c`)
  exposes every gdb mnemonic used (mxstatus/pmacfg/uitb/ucode/jvt/...), so the
  drain captures real values.

Remaining per feature: the silicon-behavior e2e fixtures, which need the
external vsim rebuilt (its podman container) so the sim binary carries the new
resume/drain code. Tracked under each feature below.

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.

# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

## STATUS — F0 + F1 DONE and e2e-validated (stopped at F1 by request)

The key design decision: a single X-macro (`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` in the ABI
header) drives all four consumers (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify), so a scalar Andes CSR is wired
once, not per-feature; PMA arrays mirror the existing PMP loops. A side effect
of that DRY design: building the machinery for F1 (uitb/jvt) also wired the
other 11 scalars (F2/F4-F8) and PMA (F3) through all four sites in the same
loops -- their transport code + unit tests are in, even though only F1 was
finalized/validated this pass.

Verified:
- ABI layout lock: `state_abi.test.cpp` (v3, 126 assertions).
- restore: `resume_driver.test.cpp` (every Andes CSR + PMA, 392 assertions).
- re-read: `state_drain.test.cpp` (whole block round-trip, 604 assertions).
- verify: `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` (per-feature field probes, all pass).
- plugin drain compiles clean; the real Andes QEMU (`target/riscv/andes_csr.c`)
  exposes every gdb mnemonic used (mxstatus/pmacfg/uitb/ucode/jvt/...).
- **e2e** (real QEMU -> vsim, `ax45mpv_premium` rebuilt with the new code):
  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify rt_csr_survival.elf` -> `state-diff
  PASS: 144 fields match`. The Andes block round-trips on hardware.

e2e finding (folded in): `msp_bound`/`msp_base` are engine-reset-divergent --
QEMU resets them to all-ones, the vsim `ax45mpv_premium` RTL has no HW stack
protection so it drains 0. Transported tolerantly, but **verify-excluded** like
`mip` (state_diff.cpp). Not a transport bug.

Not done (out of this F1 pass): the silicon-behavior fixtures that drive a
*non-zero* uitb (CoDense `exec.it`), real DSP `ucode`, real PMA regions, etc.;
and rebuilding the non-premium vsim configs (mp2/advanced/d23/makatau still
carry v2 -- a handoff on those now version-mismatches until rebuilt).

throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a

97	### Two-Phase Handoff
98	
99	```
100	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
101	```
102	
103	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
104	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
105	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
106	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### Two-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
```

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), and (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets them to all-ones, a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0 -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.

Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).

file.content:
# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

## STATUS — F0 + F1 DONE and e2e-validated (stopped at F1 by request)

The key design decision: a single X-macro (`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` in the ABI
header) drives all four consumers (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify), so a scalar Andes CSR is wired
once, not per-feature; PMA arrays mirror the existing PMP loops. A side effect
of that DRY design: building the machinery for F1 (uitb/jvt) also wired the
other 11 scalars (F2/F4-F8) and PMA (F3) through all four sites in the same
loops -- their transport code + unit tests are in, even though only F1 was
finalized/validated this pass.

Verified:
- ABI layout lock: `state_abi.test.cpp` (v3, 126 assertions).
- restore: `resume_driver.test.cpp` (every Andes CSR + PMA, 392 assertions).
- re-read: `state_drain.test.cpp` (whole block round-trip, 604 assertions).
- verify: `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` (per-feature field probes, all pass).
- plugin drain compiles clean; the real Andes QEMU (`target/riscv/andes_csr.c`)
  exposes every gdb mnemonic used (mxstatus/pmacfg/uitb/ucode/jvt/...).
- **e2e** (real QEMU -> vsim, `ax45mpv_premium` rebuilt with the new code):
  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify rt_csr_survival.elf` -> `state-diff
  PASS: 144 fields match`. The Andes block round-trips on hardware.

e2e finding (folded in): `msp_bound`/`msp_base` are engine-reset-divergent --
QEMU resets them to all-ones, the vsim `ax45mpv_premium` RTL has no HW stack
protection so it drains 0. Transported tolerantly, but **verify-excluded** like
`mip` (state_diff.cpp). Not a transport bug.

Not done (out of this F1 pass): the silicon-behavior fixtures that drive a
*non-zero* uitb (CoDense `exec.it`), real DSP `ucode`, real PMA regions, etc.;
and rebuilding the non-premium vsim configs (mp2/advanced/d23/makatau still
carry v2 -- a handoff on those now version-mismatches until rebuilt).

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

## The 3 repos every feature (except F0) touches

| Repo | Path | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `andesim_abi` (submodule) | `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h` | wire struct + layout lock -- **F0 only** |
| `andesim` | `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | drain (gdbstub read) |
| `andesim` | `driver/state_diff.{hpp,cpp}` (+ `state_diff_test.cpp`) | `--verify` compare |
| `andesim` | `tests/fixtures/*` | RED fixtures |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`) | `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | restore (DMI write; extend the `write_csr_tolerant` list / PMP-style loop) |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external) | `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | re-drain (DMI read at exit halt) |

Dedup targets (Coding Principle: don't duplicate): restore reuses
`write_csr_tolerant(addr,val)`; PMA reuses the existing `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg` loop
shape; drain reuses the `find_reg` + `read_reg64` pattern.

---

## F0 - v3 ABI + dedicated Andes block  [BLOCKS ALL OTHERS]

Status: TODO. Deps: none.

Define the whole Andes block ONCE so F1..F8 only populate existing fields (no
later offset reshuffle -> features stay independent). Bump
`HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` 2 -> 3; add `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` to gate the block
live; all three readers reject version<3 by magic+version+size.

Proposed block (LE u64; zero = "producer lacked it"):

```c
struct hybrid_andes_csr {     // v3
  uint64_t mxstatus;          // 0x7C4  Andes mstatus companion (DME/IME/PFT_EN)
  uint64_t mpft_ctl;          // 0x7C5  perf throttling (T_LEVEL)
  uint64_t mclk_ctl;          // 0x7DF  clock control
  uint64_t milmb;             // 0x7C0  ILM base + enable
  uint64_t mdlmb;             // 0x7C1  DLM base + enable
  uint64_t mecc_code;         // 0x7C2  ECC code
  uint64_t mhsp_ctl;          // 0x7C6  HW stack protection control
  uint64_t msp_bound;         // 0x7C7
  uint64_t msp_base;          // 0x7C8
  uint64_t mcountermask_m;    // 0x7D1  counter mask (cycle hygiene)
  uint64_t uitb;              // 0x800  CoDense instruction table base
  uint64_t jvt;               // 0x017  Zcmt jump vector table
  uint64_t ucode;             // 0x801  DSP/P-ext overflow flag (Class 2)
  uint64_t pmacfg[2];         // 0xBC0, 0xBC2 (RV64: 16 entries / 2 regs)
  uint64_t pmaaddr[16];       // 0xBD0..0xBDF
};                            // 31 u64 = 248 bytes; recompute reserved[]
```

Key files: `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`; size/version gate in
`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`, and
`driver/state_diff.cpp`. Coordinated: edit `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule
pointer in BOTH `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts `version==3`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, and
`offsetof`/`sizeof` of the new block + every named field (layout lock). All
fields zero on legacy producers.

---

## F1 - CoDense + Zcmt table bases (`uitb` 0x800, `jvt` 0x017)  [DONE]

Status: DONE + e2e-validated. Deps: F0. Class 1. uitb/jvt are X-list entries,
wired through plugin drain / resume / re-read / verify; round-trip confirmed by
the rt_csr_survival hybrid+verify run (PASS, 144 fields). A CoDense fixture that
sets a *non-zero* uitb and runs `exec.it` inside the ROI is the remaining
deeper check (proves the value is used, not just transported).

RED fixture: ROI uses `exec.it` (needs `uitb`) and/or `cm.jt`/`cm.jalt` (needs
`jvt`); without transport it faults or mis-executes in vsim. Plus round-trip:
write sentinel pre-ROI, read back inside ROI, `--verify` drain==restore.

GREEN: drain `uitb`/`jvt`; restore via `write_csr_tolerant`; re-drain; compare.

---

## F2 - `mxstatus` (0x7C4)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Andes companion to `mstatus` (DME/IME misalign
exception enable, PFT_EN). Writable M-mode -> full round-trip + verify (model on
`mscratch`). RED: fixture sets `mxstatus` sentinel pre-ROI, reads inside, verify.

---

## F3 - PMA: `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` (0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Biggest + highest correctness/cycle impact.
Memory attributes (cacheable / device / NAPOT). Reuse the `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg`
loop shape in `resume_driver.hpp`. Gated on `mmsc_cfg.PPMA`.

RED fixture: mark an MMIO region device-type + a RAM region cacheable via PMA
pre-ROI; without transport vsim resumes PMA-reset -> wrong cache/device behavior.
Assert via cycle delta (cacheable RAM) and/or a device-ordering check.

---

## F4 - DSP `ucode` (0x801)  [Class 2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. The P-ext overflow (OV) flag is LIVE state, like `vxsat`:
restore BEFORE the ROI, re-drain AFTER, `state_diff` compares it. Gated on P-ext.
RED: DSP op sets OV; round-trip must preserve the bit.

---

## F5 - Local Memory `milmb` (0x7C0), `mdlmb` (0x7C1) [+ `mecc_code` 0x7C2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Base+enable of ILM/DLM. Only live if the linker
script places sections in LM (check `runtime/andesim.ld`). RED: place a hot array
in DLM; transport keeps vsim accessing fast LM (cycle delta) vs DRAM/fault.

---

## F6 - Throttle / clock `mpft_ctl` (0x7C5), `mclk_ctl` (0x7DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Cycle-only. Pairs with `mxstatus.PFT_EN` (F2):
if throttling is enabled, the resumed leg must throttle identically or the cycle
figure diverges. RED: enable throttle pre-ROI, assert cycle delta matches.

---

## F7 - HW stack protection `mhsp_ctl` (0x7C6), `msp_bound` (0x7C7), `msp_base` (0x7C8)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. If crt0 enables stack overflow/underflow
detection, the bounds must survive or vsim either misses protection or
false-traps. RED: enable + set bounds pre-ROI; ROI stack access stays in-bounds.

---

## F8 - Counter mask `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) [+ `mcountinhibit` 0x320]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Cycle-figure hygiene: controls whether `mcycle`/
`minstret` advance in M-mode. RED: set mask pre-ROI, assert the cycle figure
reflects it.

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

diff --git a/hybrid/state_abi.h b/hybrid/state_abi.h
index f7af507..751101b 100644
--- a/hybrid/state_abi.h
+++ b/hybrid/state_abi.h
@@ -21,14 +21,19 @@ extern "C" {
 #endif
 
 #define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
-// Version 2 (L11): vreg[] widened from 64 to 128 bytes per register, which
-// shifts every field after it. Readers reject version-1 files loudly (all
-// three consumers check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
-#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2u
-
-#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 (1u << 0)
-#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP   (1u << 1)
-#define HYBRID_FLAG_V    (1u << 2)
+// Version 3 (Andes F0): append struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl, which
+// grows the struct. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to 128 bytes/register.
+// Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers check magic + version
+// + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
+#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 3u
+
+#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
+#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
+#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
+// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
+// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
+// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
+#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
 
 // VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
 // VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
@@ -50,6 +55,48 @@ extern "C" {
 #define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
 #define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
 
+// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
+// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
+// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
+#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
+#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
+#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
+#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
+
+// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
+// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
+// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
+// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
+// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
+// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
+// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
+#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
+  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
+  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
+  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
+  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
+  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
+  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
+  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
+  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
+  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
+  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
+  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
+  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
+  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
+
+// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
+// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
+// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
+// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
+struct hybrid_andes_csr {
+#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
+  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
+#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
+  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
+  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
+};
+
 // All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
 // unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
 // the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
@@ -107,7 +154,10 @@ struct hybrid_state_v1 {
   uint64_t mcache_ctl;
   uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
 
-  uint8_t  reserved[208];  // zero-initialise on write; 256 - 3*8 (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) - 8 (fcsr) - 2*8 (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)
+  // v3: Andes V5 CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES). 31 * 8 = 248 bytes.
+  struct hybrid_andes_csr andes;
+
+  uint8_t  reserved[64];  // zero-initialise on write; v3-compatible growth room
 };
 
 #ifdef __cplusplus

index c3de7ef..cd071e8 100644
--- a/hybrid/state_abi_check.h
+++ b/hybrid/state_abi_check.h
@@ -65,14 +65,25 @@ static_assert(offsetof(struct hybrid_state_v1, mcache_ctl)

+              "andes block follows mmisc_ctl");
+static_assert(sizeof(struct hybrid_andes_csr) == 31 * 8,
+              "13 scalar Andes CSRs + pmacfg[2] + pmaaddr[16] = 31 * uint64_t");
+static_assert(offsetof(struct hybrid_andes_csr, mxstatus) == 0,
+              "mxstatus heads the Andes block (X-macro order)");
+static_assert(offsetof(struct hybrid_andes_csr, pmacfg) == 13 * 8,
+              "pmacfg follows the 13 scalar Andes CSRs");
+static_assert(offsetof(struct hybrid_andes_csr, pmaaddr) == 15 * 8,
+              "pmaaddr follows pmacfg[2]");
+static_assert(offsetof(struct hybrid_state_v1, reserved)
+                == 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX + 48 + 248,
+              "reserved follows the andes block");
 static_assert(sizeof(struct hybrid_state_v1)
-                == 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX + 256,
-              "hybrid_state_v1 total size unchanged "
-              "(reserved shrinks 256->208 to absorb vxsat/vxrm/vcsr "
-              "+ fcsr + mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)");
+                == 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX + 360,
+              "hybrid_state_v1 v3 total size "
+              "(48 trailer + 248 andes + 64 reserved)");
 
 static_assert(HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX == 128,
               "HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX covers VLEN up to 1024 bits (L11); "

Verdict: clean on the reuse angle. No real duplication of an existing helper. Every new block reuses the right primitive and mirrors the sanctioned patterns. Details per your specific questions:

- `andes_verify_excluded` lambda (driver/state_diff.cpp:92-94) — NOT a duplication; no existing exclusion mechanism to reuse. Omission cannot express "skip 2 of 13" inside an X-macro expansion, so a local predicate is the minimal new construct. Keeping it as a file-local lambda (rather than adding a 4th "verify" column to the shared `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`) is correct: it keeps the verify-only concern out of the macro that the other 3 consumers share. Leave it.

Task already sanctions this mirroring.

- "read all CSRs in a list" helper (state_drain.hpp:115-125) — none exists; reuses `read_register_64` per entry, identical idiom to the existing mscratch/mepc/mcause re-reads above it. PMA loops mirror the same shape. Clean.

- `has_andes` detection (hybrid_handoff.c:315-329) — consistent, not duplicated. It follows the existing `has_fp` (lines 283-288) and `has_v`/`has_other_v` (lines 348-353) idiom exactly: a local int set to 1 on any non-NULL handle, then `|=` the flag. There is no `detect_feature()` helper for `has_fp`/`has_v` to reuse — they are inline too — so `has_andes` matching that inline form is the correct consistent choice, not a missed reuse.

- `find_reg`-by-index loops (hybrid_handoff.c:165-173) — the PMA `g_snprintf("pmacfg%d"/"pmaaddr%d") + find_reg` loops duplicate the shape of the existing PMP loops directly below (lines 174-181), but that is the existing inline convention (there is no indexed-resolve helper for PMP either) and the task explicitly sanctions mirroring PMP. Not worth extracting for 2 vs 4 loops.

Nothing to change.

# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

## STATUS — F0 + F1 DONE and e2e-validated (stopped at F1 by request)

The key design decision: a single X-macro (`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` in the ABI
header) drives all four consumers (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify), so a scalar Andes CSR is wired
once, not per-feature; PMA arrays mirror the existing PMP loops. A side effect
of that DRY design: building the machinery for F1 (uitb/jvt) also wired the
other 11 scalars (F2/F4-F8) and PMA (F3) through all four sites in the same
loops -- their transport code + unit tests are in, even though only F1 was
finalized/validated this pass.

Verified:
- ABI layout lock: `state_abi.test.cpp` (v3, 126 assertions).
- restore: `resume_driver.test.cpp` (every Andes CSR + PMA, 392 assertions).
- re-read: `state_drain.test.cpp` (whole block round-trip, 604 assertions).
- verify: `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` (per-feature field probes, all pass).
- plugin drain compiles clean; the real Andes QEMU (`target/riscv/andes_csr.c`)
  exposes every gdb mnemonic used (mxstatus/pmacfg/uitb/ucode/jvt/...).
- **e2e** (real QEMU -> vsim, `ax45mpv_premium` rebuilt with the new code):
  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify rt_csr_survival.elf` -> `state-diff
  PASS: 144 fields match`. The Andes block round-trips on hardware.

e2e finding (folded in): `msp_bound`/`msp_base` are engine-reset-divergent --
QEMU resets them to all-ones, the vsim `ax45mpv_premium` RTL has no HW stack
protection so it drains 0. Transported tolerantly, but **verify-excluded** like
`mip` (state_diff.cpp). Not a transport bug.

Not done (out of this F1 pass): the silicon-behavior fixtures that drive a
*non-zero* uitb (CoDense `exec.it`), real DSP `ucode`, real PMA regions, etc.;
and rebuilding the non-premium vsim configs (mp2/advanced/d23/makatau still
carry v2 -- a handoff on those now version-mismatches until rebuilt).

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

## The 3 repos every feature (except F0) touches

| Repo | Path | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `andesim_abi` (submodule) | `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h` | wire struct + layout lock -- **F0 only** |
| `andesim` | `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | drain (gdbstub read) |
| `andesim` | `driver/state_diff.{hpp,cpp}` (+ `state_diff_test.cpp`) | `--verify` compare |
| `andesim` | `tests/fixtures/*` | RED fixtures |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`) | `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | restore (DMI write; extend the `write_csr_tolerant` list / PMP-style loop) |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external) | `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | re-drain (DMI read at exit halt) |

Dedup targets (Coding Principle: don't duplicate): restore reuses
`write_csr_tolerant(addr,val)`; PMA reuses the existing `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg` loop
shape; drain reuses the `find_reg` + `read_reg64` pattern.

---

## F0 - v3 ABI + dedicated Andes block  [BLOCKS ALL OTHERS]

Status: TODO. Deps: none.

Define the whole Andes block ONCE so F1..F8 only populate existing fields (no
later offset reshuffle -> features stay independent). Bump
`HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` 2 -> 3; add `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` to gate the block
live; all three readers reject version<3 by magic+version+size.

Proposed block (LE u64; zero = "producer lacked it"):

```c
struct hybrid_andes_csr {     // v3
  uint64_t mxstatus;          // 0x7C4  Andes mstatus companion (DME/IME/PFT_EN)
  uint64_t mpft_ctl;          // 0x7C5  perf throttling (T_LEVEL)
  uint64_t mclk_ctl;          // 0x7DF  clock control
  uint64_t milmb;             // 0x7C0  ILM base + enable
  uint64_t mdlmb;             // 0x7C1  DLM base + enable
  uint64_t mecc_code;         // 0x7C2  ECC code
  uint64_t mhsp_ctl;          // 0x7C6  HW stack protection control
  uint64_t msp_bound;         // 0x7C7
  uint64_t msp_base;          // 0x7C8
  uint64_t mcountermask_m;    // 0x7D1  counter mask (cycle hygiene)
  uint64_t uitb;              // 0x800  CoDense instruction table base
  uint64_t jvt;               // 0x017  Zcmt jump vector table
  uint64_t ucode;             // 0x801  DSP/P-ext overflow flag (Class 2)
  uint64_t pmacfg[2];         // 0xBC0, 0xBC2 (RV64: 16 entries / 2 regs)
  uint64_t pmaaddr[16];       // 0xBD0..0xBDF
};                            // 31 u64 = 248 bytes; recompute reserved[]
```

Key files: `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`; size/version gate in
`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`, and
`driver/state_diff.cpp`. Coordinated: edit `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule
pointer in BOTH `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts `version==3`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, and
`offsetof`/`sizeof` of the new block + every named field (layout lock). All
fields zero on legacy producers.

---

## F1 - CoDense + Zcmt table bases (`uitb` 0x800, `jvt` 0x017)  [DONE]

Status: DONE + e2e-validated. Deps: F0. Class 1. uitb/jvt are X-list entries,
wired through plugin drain / resume / re-read / verify; round-trip confirmed by
the rt_csr_survival hybrid+verify run (PASS, 144 fields). A CoDense fixture that
sets a *non-zero* uitb and runs `exec.it` inside the ROI is the remaining
deeper check (proves the value is used, not just transported).

RED fixture: ROI uses `exec.it` (needs `uitb`) and/or `cm.jt`/`cm.jalt` (needs
`jvt`); without transport it faults or mis-executes in vsim. Plus round-trip:
write sentinel pre-ROI, read back inside ROI, `--verify` drain==restore.

GREEN: drain `uitb`/`jvt`; restore via `write_csr_tolerant`; re-drain; compare.

---

## F2 - `mxstatus` (0x7C4)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Andes companion to `mstatus` (DME/IME misalign
exception enable, PFT_EN). Writable M-mode -> full round-trip + verify (model on
`mscratch`). RED: fixture sets `mxstatus` sentinel pre-ROI, reads inside, verify.

---

## F3 - PMA: `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` (0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Biggest + highest correctness/cycle impact.
Memory attributes (cacheable / device / NAPOT). Reuse the `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg`
loop shape in `resume_driver.hpp`. Gated on `mmsc_cfg.PPMA`.

RED fixture: mark an MMIO region device-type + a RAM region cacheable via PMA
pre-ROI; without transport vsim resumes PMA-reset -> wrong cache/device behavior.
Assert via cycle delta (cacheable RAM) and/or a device-ordering check.

---

## F4 - DSP `ucode` (0x801)  [Class 2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. The P-ext overflow (OV) flag is LIVE state, like `vxsat`:
restore BEFORE the ROI, re-drain AFTER, `state_diff` compares it. Gated on P-ext.
RED: DSP op sets OV; round-trip must preserve the bit.

---

## F5 - Local Memory `milmb` (0x7C0), `mdlmb` (0x7C1) [+ `mecc_code` 0x7C2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Base+enable of ILM/DLM. Only live if the linker
script places sections in LM (check `runtime/andesim.ld`). RED: place a hot array
in DLM; transport keeps vsim accessing fast LM (cycle delta) vs DRAM/fault.

---

## F6 - Throttle / clock `mpft_ctl` (0x7C5), `mclk_ctl` (0x7DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Cycle-only. Pairs with `mxstatus.PFT_EN` (F2):
if throttling is enabled, the resumed leg must throttle identically or the cycle
figure diverges. RED: enable throttle pre-ROI, assert cycle delta matches.

---

## F7 - HW stack protection `mhsp_ctl` (0x7C6), `msp_bound` (0x7C7), `msp_base` (0x7C8)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. If crt0 enables stack overflow/underflow
detection, the bounds must survive or vsim either misses protection or
false-traps. RED: enable + set bounds pre-ROI; ROI stack access stays in-bounds.

---

## F8 - Counter mask `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) [+ `mcountinhibit` 0x320]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Cycle-figure hygiene: controls whether `mcycle`/
`minstret` advance in M-mode. RED: set mask pre-ROI, assert the cycle figure
reflects it.

---

## Out of scope (record, do not implement now)

- Class 0 config/RO: `micm_cfg`/`mdcm_cfg`/`mmsc_cfg*`/`mvec_cfg`/`mrvarch_cfg*`/
  `mhvm*`/`mpl2cm_cfg`/`ml1dbf_cfg`/`mccache_ctl_base`, crash-save. (consistency
  assert only, optional later feature.)
- Class 3 trap/NMI/CLIC: `mdcause`, `mslideleg`, `msavestatus`/`msaveepc{1,2}`/
  `msavecause{1,2}`/`msavedcause{1,2}`, `mnvec`/`mrnxvec`, `mirq_entry`/
  `mintsel_jal`/`pushm*`. Deferred to the trap-bearing / S-U-envelope ROI work.
- `mppib`/`mfiob` (PPI/FIO base): platform-static; consistency check, not transport.

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Now let me compile my comprehensive findings report.

## SUMMARY

I've thoroughly explored the CSR round-trip test pattern in andesim. Here are your findings:

---

## 1. Full Source of `rt_csr_survival.S` Fixture

**File**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` (79 lines)

The fixture demonstrates TWO assertion mechanisms:

**Phase 1 (QEMU1, lines 37-54)**: 
- Writes sentinel values to writable M-mode CSRs BEFORE the ROI entry marker
- `mscratch = 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF` (stored in callee-stable `a1` for in-ROI comparison)
- `mepc = 0x0000000080002340` (WARL, stored in `a4`)
- `mie = 0x0000000000000888` (MSIE|MTIE|MEIE bits, stored in `a5`)
- `mcause = 0x8000000000000007` (interrupt | code 7, for --verify only)
- `mtval = 0x0000000080001234` (for --verify only)
- Entry marker: `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (line 56)

**Phase 2 (vsim ROI, lines 58-69)**:
- **In-ROI self-check** (lines 59-64): Reads CSRs back and compares against saved values using `bne`. On mismatch, the fixture hangs (line 77-78), causing e2e timeout/failure.
- Overwrites `mscratch` with new sentinel `0xBADC0FFEE0DDF00D` (line 67) for StateDrain to capture
- Exit marker: `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (line 69)

**Verification coverage**:
- `mscratch`, `mepc`, `mie`: exact round-trip (in-ROI self-checked)
- `mcause` (WLRL), `mtval` (WARL): --verify only (oracle compares engine-vs-engine, not literal)
- NOT asserted: `mip` (hardware-driven bits) and S-mode CSRs (default engine M-only)

---

## 2. The Makefile Pattern: How Fixtures Are Built

**File**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/fixtures/Makefile` (151 lines)

**Key sections**:

**Fixture families** (lines 28-50):
- `RT_FIXTURES` (asm): 10 fixtures including `rt_csr_survival`
- `RT_C_FIXTURES` (C-level): 5 fixtures linked through the vplat runtime
- `RT_C_V_FIXTURES` (V-extension C): 4 fixtures with `-march=rv64gcv`
- `RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES` (runtime smoke tests): 3 fixtures
- `BREAK_FIXTURES` (intentional bugs): 4 fixtures (not in default `all` target)

**Build pattern** (lines 98-100):
```makefile
$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
```
This is a **pattern rule**: a `.S` file automatically becomes a `.elf` without explicit per-fixture listing. All RT_FIXTURES are in the variables list (line 28-30); adding a new fixture means:
1. Create `new_fixture.S` in the same directory
2. Add it to the `RT_FIXTURES` variable line
3. `make` applies the pattern rule

**Compile flags**:
- `CFLAGS = -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall` (line 24)
- `LDSCRIPT = ../../runtime/andesim.ld` (load at 0x00100000)
- `LDFLAGS = -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static` (line 25)

**C-level fixtures** (lines 110-123):
- Linked with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (user's exact command)
- Link against `libandesim_runtime.a` + `crt0.o` + `andesim.ld`
- Include path: `-I$(HELPERS_DIR)` for `rt_c_helpers.h`
- RVV fixtures use `-march=rv64gcv` separately (line 116)

---

## 3. ROI Marker Mechanics

**Header**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/runtime/ROI.h` (35 lines)

The markers are **RISC-V HINT instructions** (rd=x0 = architectural NOPs):
```c
static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)  // line 24
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)    // line 29
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}
```

**Key contract**:
- `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` = ENTER ROI (QEMU1 drains + exits 200)
- `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` = EXIT ROI (vsim drains + exits 200)
- `"memory"` clobber prevents compiler from hoisting computation across markers
- Architecture-portable: same binary runs on fast, cycle, hybrid, AND silicon

**In assembly** (no macro needed): Direct `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` insns (e.g. rt_csr_survival.S lines 56, 69)

The crux is empirical: which Andes CSRs does `ax45mpv_premium` actually implement? An **empty-ROI probe fixture** that writes distinct sentinels to every candidate CSR and runs `--verify` maps it in one run (empty ROI = all writes side-effect-free). Let me read the exact fixture boilerplate first.

1	// rt_csr_survival.S
2	//
3	// 2-phase guard (L23 + L24): the writable M-mode CSRs round-trip across the
4	// QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. A value stashed before the ROI is readable inside it
5	// (ResumeDriver restores the CSR) and a value written inside the ROI is
6	// captured at drain (StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough re-reads it).
7	//
8	// Covered CSRs:
9	//   L23  mscratch                 -- M-mode software scratch (pure read/write)
10	//   L24  mepc, mcause, mtval, mie -- writable trap/interrupt CSRs
11	//
12	// History: this fixture predates the 2-phase redesign. It used to read the CSRs
13	// back in a `phase_c` AFTER the exit marker and exit with the index of the
14	// first mismatch -- but once the QEMU2 handback leg was removed, vsim drains and
15	// exits AT the exit marker, so phase_c never ran and the guard was silently
16	// dead. The check now lives INSIDE the ROI, where the vsim leg actually runs.
17	//
18	// Two assertion mechanisms:
19	//   1. In-ROI self-check (works in the plain e2e harness, no --verify): read
20	//      the CSR back inside the ROI and `bne` against the stashed sentinel,
21	//      held in a callee-stable GPR which the GPR restore round-trips. On a
22	//      regressed restore the values differ, so the fixture spins -- vsim never
23	//      reaches the exit marker, times out, and the harness reports a failure.
24	//      Used only for mscratch/mepc/mie, whose values round-trip exactly.
25	//   2. --verify (VERIFY=1): the differential oracle compares the drained CSRs
26	//      against a pure-QEMU run. Used for mcause (WLRL) and mtval (WARL), whose
27	//      cross-engine legalisation could differ from a chosen sentinel; the
28	//      oracle path compares engine-against-engine instead of against a literal.
29	//
30	// Not asserted: mip (its pending bits are hardware-driven, not writable via
31	// csrw on an M-only core) and the S-mode CSRs medeleg/mideleg/satp (the default
32	// engine does not implement them). See docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb.
33	
34	.section .text
35	.globl _start
36	_start:
37	    // Stash sentinels into the writable M-mode CSRs BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg).
38	    // a1/a4/a5 are callee-stable GPRs the restore round-trips, so the in-ROI
39	    // reads below can compare against them.
40	    li      a1, 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF
41	    csrw    mscratch, a1            // L23 software scratch CSR
42	
43	    li      a4, 0x0000000080002340  // aligned (bit0=0): mepc is WARL
44	    csrw    mepc, a4                // L24
45	    li      a5, 0x0000000000000888  // MSIE|MTIE|MEIE: standard M-mode mie bits
46	    csrw    mie, a5                 // L24 (mstatus.MIE stays 0: no trap is taken)
47	
48	    // mcause (WLRL, a legal cause) + mtval (WARL): set for --verify coverage,
49	    // not in-ROI self-checked (cross-engine legalisation may differ from the
50	    // literal; the oracle compares engine-vs-engine instead).
51	    li      t1, 0x8000000000000007  // interrupt | code 7 (M timer): legal cause
52	    csrw    mcause, t1
53	    li      t1, 0x0000000080001234
54	    csrw    mtval, t1
55	
56	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim
57	
58	    // Read the round-trip CSRs back INSIDE the ROI: each must be restored.
59	    csrr    a0, mscratch
60	    bne     a0, a1, regress         // restore lost? spin -> timeout -> test FAIL
61	    csrr    a3, mepc
62	    bne     a3, a4, regress
63	    csrr    a6, mie
64	    bne     a6, a5, regress
65	
66	    li      a2, 0xBADC0FFEE0DDF00D
67	    csrw    mscratch, a2            // overwrite; drain must re-read this value
68	
69	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT ROI -> vsim drains the CSRs, exits 200
70	
71	    // Unreached on hybrid (vsim stops at the exit marker). Engine-portable
72	    // SimControl exit so the same ELF still runs to completion standalone.
73	    li      t0, 0xe0080000
74	    sw      x0, 0(t0)
75	1:  j       1b
76	
77	regress:
78	    j       regress                 // a restored CSR is wrong: hang -> harness FAIL
79

1	// Shared exit-via-semihosting macro for hybrid round-trip fixtures.
2	//
3	// SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
4	//   Builds the {reason=ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit, exit_code=<exit_reg>}
5	//   16-byte block at 0x00001000, sets a0=SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED (0x20), a1=block,
6	//   then issues the RISC-V semihosting `slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`
7	//   triple. exit_reg may be any GPR holding the desired host exit code; this
8	//   macro clobbers t0, t1, a0, a1.
9	//
10	// QEMU's host-exit returns the low 8 bits of <exit_reg> as the process status.
11	
12	.macro SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
13	    li      t0, 0x00001000
14	    li      t1, 0x20026                     // ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit
15	    sd      t1, 0(t0)
16	    sd      \exit_reg, 8(t0)
17	    li      a0, 0x20                        // SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED
18	    mv      a1, t0
19	    .option push
20	    .option norvc
21	    slli    x0, x0, 0x1f
22	    ebreak
23	    srai    x0, x0, 0x7
24	    .option pop
25	99: j       99b
26	.endm
