file.content:
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

content.text:
QEMU uses symbolic names (`CSR_MXSTATUS`, `CSR_UCODE`, ...) — my hex grep missed them, but the symbolic grep confirms QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` cpu **implements every candidate CSR** (mxstatus, ucode, uitb, mpft_ctl, mhsp_ctl, mcountermask_m, milmb, mdlmb, msp_bound/base, PMA), each with a `WRITE_MASK_CSR_*` (WARL legalization). So `csrw` won't trap in the QEMU1 leg — a combined empty-ROI probe is safe.

Let me build a throwaway probe that writes a distinct sentinel to every feature's CSR and run `--verify`. The per-field diff maps, in one run, which CSRs the premium **vsim RTL** implements (got=sentinel) vs doesn't (got=0) vs WARL-masks.

// rt_andes_probe.S  (THROWAWAY)
// Empty-ROI transport probe: write a distinct sentinel to every candidate

content.text:
The empty-ROI run **timed out in the vsim leg** (90s). Key insight: vsim is cycle-accurate, so it *honors* control CSRs the moment they're restored — even with an empty ROI, the hart runs between resume and the exit marker. Writing `mclk_ctl` (clock control), `mpft_ctl` (throttle), or `mhsp_ctl` (stack-protection trap) likely stalls or faults the hart. The QEMU1 leg (functional) ignored them, so the writes themselves succeeded.

I need to distinguish a **transport bug** (DMI restore of an unimplemented CSR hangs — would affect everything, must fix in `resume_driver`) from an **expected execution effect** (test wrote a clock-gating value). Bisect: data-only probe (drop the 6 control CSRs).

content.text:
Still hangs with **data-only** CSRs — so it's not a control-CSR execution effect. The hang is triggered by restoring some **non-zero** Andes CSR via DMI into premium. Critical realization: F1's "validation" (rt_csr_survival, 144 fields) round-tripped uitb/jvt at value **0** (the fixture never writes them) — so *no Andes CSR has ever been round-tripped at a non-zero value before this probe*. This is the first, and it hangs.

A correct `write_csr_tolerant` should no-op a write to an absent CSR (clean `got=0` diff, no hang). A hang suggests it polls a DMI abstract-command error forever — a **transport bug** (root cause to fix, not avoid). Let me isolate the culprit CSR with parallel single-CSR probes (independent vsim processes, parallel 90s waits).

I now have a definitive empirical map. Stopping the probe sweep here — I've hit genuine architectural/scope decisions that are yours to make, and grinding further (30+ more 90s runs, or editing the external vsim harness) without alignment would be wasteful.

## What I found

I wrote throwaway empty-ROI probes that write a sentinel to each Andes CSR before the handoff, then ran `--mode hybrid --verify` on `ax45mpv_premium`. Results, cross-referenced with QEMU's `WRITE_MASK_CSR_*`:

| Feature | CSR | Result on premium |
|---------|-----|-------------------|
| **F1** uitb | 0x800 | **PASS, non-zero round-trips** (genuinely validated now - F1 was only ever tested at value 0 before) |
| **F5** milmb/mdlmb | 0x7C0/1 | PASS (high-bit sentinel survived) |
| **F6** mpft_ctl | 0x7C5 | PASS but **vacuous** - my 0x2 was outside QEMU mask 0x1F0, so 0==0 |
| **F2** mxstatus | 0x7C4 | vsim drains **0** (QEMU keeps 0x40; premium RTL lacks that bit) |
| **F6** mclk_ctl | 0x7DF | vsim drains **0** |
| **F7** mhsp_ctl | 0x7C6 | vsim drains **0** |
| **F8** mcountermask_m | 0x7D1 | vsim drains **0** (clean no-op) |
| **F3** pmaaddr/pmacfg | 0xBD0/0xBC0 | implemented, but **QEMU and vsim legalize WARL differently** (0xabcde->0xabc00) |
| **F4** ucode | 0x801 | **HANG** (90s) - premium has no DSP |
| **F5** mecc_code | 0x7C2 | **HANG** (90s) - premium has no ECC |

## Three real findings

1. **Engine gap**: `ax45mpv_premium` only implements a *subset* of the Andes CSRs. DSP (`ucode`), ECC (`mecc_code`), and several control bits (`mxstatus`/`mclk_ctl`/`mhsp_ctl`/`mcountermask`) are not in this RTL. They can only be exercised on `mp2`/`advanced`/`makatau` - but those **still carry the v2 ABI** and must be rebuilt (Docker/podman) before they can even accept a v3 handoff.

2. **Robustness bug (the one real defect)**: restoring an *absent* CSR via the DMI abstract command **hangs** vsim (ucode, mecc_code) instead of cleanly no-op'ing the way `mcountermask` does. The "tolerant write" is not uniformly tolerant. Root cause is in the AHB/DMI handshake layer of the external vsim harness.

3. **Cross-engine WARL divergence** (PMA): even when both implement a CSR, QEMU and vsim legalize the written value differently, so a literal-sentinel `--verify` mismatches. Needs WARL-canonical sentinels or verify-exclusion (like `mip`/`msp_bound`).

This is a much bigger and messier reality than "the transport code is wired, just add fixtures." How deep do you want me to go?

| CSR | addr | QEMU mask | premium RTL | note |
|-----|------|-----------|-------------|------|

| mhsp_ctl | 0x7C6 | - | drains 0 | no HW stack protection (matches msp_bound/base reset divergence) |
| mcountermask_m | 0x7D1 | - | drains 0 (CLEAN no-op) | not implemented; tolerant write behaves |

**Repo state:** only the ROADMAP doc is modified, and it's **uncommitted** - review it, then tell me if you want it committed. The pre-existing untracked files (PDF, hello.dump, interface/, etc.) are not mine.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **"continue all features."** (the sole driving instruction this window, after a `/compact`): continue past the completed F1 into F2-F8 of the Andes V5 CSR transport ROADMAP (`docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md`). The transport CODE for F2-F8 is already wired through the shared X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` and unit-tested; the genuine remaining work is per-feature behavioral/round-trip e2e fixtures proving each value actually survives transport on real hardware (not just at reset value 0, which is all rt_csr_survival ever tested).
   - **Final scope decision (via AskUserQuestion):** When I surfaced that the premium engine only implements a subset of Andes CSRs plus a hang bug plus WARL divergence, the user chose **"Just document, stop"** for scope and **"stop here"** (custom) for the vsim-fix question. Explicit intent: record the empirical findings in the ROADMAP, change NO production code, do NOT touch the external vsim repo, then stop.
   - **Standing CLAUDE.md constraints (still in force):** token-efficient answers (answer line 1, no preamble, ASCII-only — no em-dashes/smart-quotes/ellipsis-char); user is ESL (simple English); TDD (RED→GREEN→REFACTOR), no code duplication (leverage X-macro), proper root-cause fixes no workarounds; commit/push only when explicitly asked; end commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>`; if on default branch, branch first; "I'm ur PM, ask me questions to clarify"; update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something user-facing changed (nothing did this pass); convert relative dates to absolute in ROADMAP.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU (functional) → vsim (cycle-accurate, SystemC+Verilator) handoff via shared `hybrid_state_v1` wire struct + /dev/shm mmap. Cycle figure = vsim mcycle delta; no QEMU2 leg.
   - Three Git repos: `andesim_abi` (ABI submodule, at andesim/include/ AND vsim/external/andesim_abi/), `andesim` (driver+plugin+docs, branch `andesim`), `hybrid_vsim` at `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim` (resume/drain, branch `andesim`).
   - X-macro single-source-of-truth: `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` (field, csr_addr, gdb_name) drives 4 consumers: plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore, StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify.
   - v3 ABI: `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` gates the Andes block; struct hybrid_andes_csr = 13 scalar CSRs + pmacfg[2] + pmaaddr[16].
   - Tier-1 (sentinel round-trip via numeric `csrw`/`csrr`) = toolchain-independent. Tier-2 (value actually USED: exec.it, DSP ops, PMA cacheability cycle delta) = needs Andes toolchain custom-insn support + engine extension support.
   - Engines: vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default, M-only, VLEN 512), ax45mpv_mp2, ax46mpv_advanced, ax66_makatau (S/U-capable, VLEN 128), d23 (RV32). Premium pairs with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`.
   - ROI markers: `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER), `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT) — RISC-V HINT NOPs. Header runtime/ROI.h.
   - `--verify` compares pure-QEMU oracle (ref) vs vsim drain (got) per field.
   - WARL legalization: CSRs mask written values; QEMU and vsim RTL can mask DIFFERENTLY (cross-engine divergence).
   - DMI abstract command path: `write_csr_tolerant` (abstract write + clear_cmderr) vs `write_csr_abstract_or_pb` (abstract then Program Buffer fallback). Poll loops bounded to 1024 iters (throw on timeout). Real DmiBus runs over AHB (ahb::signals) in vsim cpu_wrappers.

   - **`docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md`** (THE ONLY repo file modified this session — 109 insertions, 9 deletions):
     - Added a new `## EMPIRICAL FINDINGS (2026-06-28, ax45mpv_premium probe sweep)` section (inserted before `## Mental model: 4 transport classes`) containing: the method description, a full per-CSR result table, and 3 findings (engine gap / robustness BUG / cross-engine WARL divergence), plus a "Consequence for the DONE bar" paragraph noting F1's value-0 round-trip is weak and probe fixtures were throwaway/not committed.

   - **`driver/state_diff.cpp`** (read only this session, unchanged): contains the Andes block compare via X-macro with `andes_verify_excluded` lambda (std::string_view) excluding msp_bound/msp_base. Does NOT compare mcycle/minstret.

CC=$(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc, CFLAGS=-march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall, LDSCRIPT=../../runtime/andesim.ld.

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text: 這正是關鍵檔案。我先把幾個「功能開關」在所有 core 的 config 之間比對,證明每個 core 真的不一樣 - 這就是為什麼要「逐 core 讀 config」。

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external
for f in */andes_ip/*/top/hdl/config.inc; do
  core=$(echo "$f" | cut -d/ -f1)
  printf '%-20s' "$core"
  for k in NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT NDS_PMA_ENTRIES NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT NDS_RVV_SUPPORT_INT NDS_VLEN; do
    v=$(grep -m1 "define $k " "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}')
    printf ' %s=%s' "${k#NDS_}" "${v:-?}"
  done
  echo
done 2>/dev/null | sort

content.text:
Found it, and it is exactly the missing piece. Answer: yes - `config.inc` is each soft-core's feature manifest, one per core.

## Location (per-core)
```
vsim_andesim/external/<core>/andes_ip/<family>/top/hdl/config.inc
```
e.g. premium: `external/ax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl/config.inc` (440 `define lines). Every core has its own, and the gating knobs genuinely differ per core (proven by the grep above).

## Why this solves the problem
The probe results I documented were me discovering at *runtime* what `config.inc` already states *statically*. Each knob predicts each probe outcome:

| config.inc knob (premium value) | Andes CSR(s) | probe result | feature |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CODENSE_SUPPORT = YES` | uitb 0x800 | round-trips OK | F1 |
| ILM/DLM present (`ILM_SIZE_KB 1024`) | milmb 0x7C0, mdlmb 0x7C1 | round-trips OK | F5 |
| all `*_ECC_TYPE = none` | mecc_code 0x7C2 | **HANG** | F5 |
| `DSP_SUPPORT = NO` | ucode 0x801 | **HANG** | F4 |
| `STACKSAFE_SUPPORT = NO` | mhsp_ctl 0x7C6, msp_bound/base 0x7C7/8 | drains 0 | F7 |
| `POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT = NO` | mpft_ctl 0x7C5 | vacuous 0 | F6 |
| `PMA_ENTRIES = 0` | pmacfg/pmaaddr 0xBC0/0xBD0 | WARL mismatch | F3 |
| `PERFORMANCE_MONITOR = NO` | mcountermask_m 0x7D1 | drains 0 | F8 |

Every hang and every drains-0 lines up with a knob set to `no`/`0`. The hang is not random - it is hybrid trying to restore a CSR the RTL does not build.

## The design this points to
Hybrid should compute the transport set per-engine from `config.inc`, not transport all 13+PMA blindly and hope the no-op is tolerant. Knob `no` -> skip that CSR -> no hang, no false WARL diff.

## Which cores unblock the blocked features
The grep shows the engines that DO implement them (and which are already built):

- **F4 ucode/DSP** -> `d45` (`DSP_SUPPORT=YES`) - external only, not built yet.
- **F3 PMA + F6 powerbrake + F7 stack** -> `ax46mpv_advanced` (`PMA=1, POWERBRAKE=1, STACKSAFE=1`) - **already built** (`Vax46mpv_advanced`).
- **Full PMA(16) + S/U** -> `ax66_makatau` - **already built**.

Two directions from here - want me to (a) wire a `config.inc` parser so hybrid derives the per-engine Andes-CSR set automatically, or (b) first just re-run F3/F6/F7 probes on `ax46mpv_advanced` to confirm the knobs predict correctly before building any parser?

content.content:
===README===
# cpu_config_to_march_converter

Tools and analysis for converting Andes RISC-V softcore `config.inc`
files into a versioned RISC-V `-march` string (`NDS_ISA_STRING`) plus
the CPU ID extracted from `NDS_CPUID` (last two hex digits of the
Verilog literal, with an `x` suffix for 64-bit cores — e.g. `45` vs
`45x`).

The repo contains:

1. The upstream **Andes TCL configurator** for 36 CPU variants
   ([`config_tool/`](config_tool/)).
2. A corpus of 97 sample **`config.inc`** files
   ([`config_inc/`](config_inc/)).
3. **Converters** (Python and bash) that derive a `-march` from any
   `config.inc` ([`scripts/`](scripts/)).
4. A **profile exporter** that emits `march` + platform/SOC settings as
   machine-readable JSON for toolchain/simulator integration
   ([`scripts/config_to_profile.py`](scripts/config_to_profile.py)).
5. Downstream **target-format generators** that take the same `config.inc`
   as authoritative input:
   - **QEMU cfg** ([`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`](scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py))
   - **SID conf** ([`scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py`](scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py))
   - **VEP** template patcher ([`scripts/config_inc_to_vep.py`](scripts/config_inc_to_vep.py))
   - **STL runtime CPU header** ([`scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py`](scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py))
   - **Alioth (`sc_sim`) config YAML** ([`scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py`](scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py)) —
     emits both the external customer cfg and the internal `iss` cfg
     (see [`docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_ALIOTH_PLAN.md`](docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_ALIOTH_PLAN.md))
6. A reference **SID conf corpus** ([`sidconf/`](sidconf/)) — 27 default
   AE250/AE350 board templates from AST542, used as templates and as
   ground truth for the SID compare workflow.
7. **Design / analysis docs** for every conversion ([`docs/`](docs/)).
8. Project guidance for Claude Code ([`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md)).

---

## Quick start

```bash
# Python — single file
python3 scripts/config_to_march.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc

# Python — validate against every embedded NDS_ISA_STRING ground truth
python3 scripts/config_to_march.py --check config_inc/*.inc

# Bash port (same output, no Python required, bash >= 4)
scripts/config_to_march.sh config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc
scripts/config_to_march.sh --check config_inc/*.inc

# Profile export (JSON)
python3 scripts/config_to_profile.py --json config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc

# QEMU cfg export (CPU ISA only)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc
# QEMU cfg export (CPU ISA + basic SOC globals: ILM/DLM/HVM)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc --with-platform
# QEMU v9 strict ISA mode (fail only on unexpected unmapped tokens)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc --qemu-v9-strict

# Batch convert normal Andes 23/25/27/45/46/65/66 config_inc files
python3 scripts/gen_qemu_cfg_batch.py --with-platform

# SID cpu-option only
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py config_inc/n25f_0.config.inc --cpu-option-only
# SID full conf (single-core)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py config_inc/a25.config.inc --full-conf --board ae250 -o out/sid_conf/a25.sid.conf
# SID full conf (auto CPU template under sidconf/, fallback to board default)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py config_inc/n45.config.inc --full-conf --board ae350 --template-auto-cpu -o out/sid_conf/n45_auto.sid.conf
# SID full conf (AMP multicore on AE350)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py config_inc/n25f_0.config.inc --full-conf --board ae350 --topology amp --cores 4 -o out/sid_conf/n25f_amp4.sid.conf
# SID batch generate
python3 scripts/gen_sid_conf_batch.py --template-auto-cpu --out-dir out/sid_conf
# SID compare generated vs reference
python3 scripts/compare_sid_conf.py --reference-dir sidconf --generated-dir out/sid_conf --out-dir out/sid_compare

# VEP patch from a config.inc (CPU-first, keeps platform wiring from template)
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_vep.py config_inc/ax45.config.inc ast530-veps/ADP-AE350-AX45.vep -o out/vep_patched/ax45.vep
# VEP batch (matches every normal Andes config.inc to an ast530-veps template)
python3 scripts/gen_vep_batch.py --out-dir out/vep_patched
# Split a VEP diff report into expected vs unexpected (config.inc-authoritative)
python3 scripts/split_vep_diff_report.py out/vep_compare/non46_vep_diff_detail_authoritative.json

# STL runtime CPU header (nds_stl_rte_cpu.h) from a config.inc
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py config_inc/n25f_0.config.inc -o out/stl_h/n25f/nds_stl_rte_cpu.h
# STL header self-validation across the corpus
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py --check config_inc/*.inc
# STL header batch (per-CPU dir + summary CSV)
python3 scripts/gen_stl_h_batch.py --out-dir out/stl_h

# Alioth (sc_sim) config YAML from a config.inc -- both layers
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py config_inc/ax45mp-1c.config.inc
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py config_inc/ax46mpv-1c_0.config.inc --layer external
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py config_inc/ax45mp-8c.config.inc --out-dir out/alioth_yaml/ax45mp-8c
# Validate emitted keys vs the shipped Alioth schema + iss reference
python3 scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py --check config_inc/ax45mp-1c.config.inc
# Alioth YAML batch over the Alioth-supported IP set
python3 scripts/gen_alioth_yaml_batch.py --out-dir out/alioth_yaml
```

Current accuracy: **31 / 36** files with an embedded `NDS_ISA_STRING`
match the converter byte-for-byte. The 5 mismatches are unversioned
ax66-family strings — see
[`docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md §6`](docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md).

---

## Updating the mapping rules

The mapping between config variables and `-march` tokens is **not**
hard-coded. It lives in a single plain-text DSL file —
[`scripts/march_rules.txt`](scripts/march_rules.txt) — that is the
source of truth for both the Python and the bash converter. To add or
change a rule, edit only that file:

```
# format: <condition> | <token1> [<token2> ...]
NDS_RVA_SUPPORT                                          | _a2p1
NDS_FPU_TYPE == dp                                       | _d2p2
NDS_RVC_SUPPORT && !NDS_ZCE_SUPPORT                      | _c2p0

hard-coded. It lives in a single plain-text DSL file —
[`scripts/march_rules.txt`](scripts/march_rules.txt) — that is the
source of truth for both the Python and the bash converter. To add or
change a rule, edit only that file:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SPA-driven derivation of Andes machine-config CSRs (mmsc_cfg / mrvarch_cfg).

Bitfield layouts are transcribed from the AndeStar V5 SPA spec
(`/Work/v5_spa/src/andes_v5_machine_mode_csr.txt`):

* ``mmsc_cfg``   (0xFC2) -- machine misc config; feature-presence bits.
* ``mrvarch_cfg`` (0xFCA) -- RISC-V arch-extension presence bits.

Each field is mapped to a ``config.inc`` macro / derived march token where one
exists; fields without a config.inc source are *carried* from the Alioth
reference value so the derived word remains a refinement of the reference
rather than dropping unknown bits.  ``diff_fields`` produces a per-bit
breakdown (derived vs reference, with the source of each bit) for the
"emit both + diff" output mode.

The low 32 bits of ``mmsc_cfg`` are identical on RV32/RV64; on RV64 the high
32 bits (mmsc_cfg2-equivalent fields, whose layout is not transcribed here)
are carried verbatim from the reference value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# field tables: (name, lsb, width, source_key)   source_key=None => carried
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
MMSC_CFG_FIELDS = [
    ("ECC",     0, 1, "ecc"),
    ("TLB_ECC", 1, 2, "tlb_ecc"),
    ("ECD",     3, 1, "codense"),
    ("PFT",     4, 1, "powerbrake"),
    ("HSP",     5, 1, None),
    ("ACE",     6, 1, "ace"),
    ("ADDPMC",  7, 5, None),
    ("VPLIC",  12, 1, "vplic"),
    ("EV5PE",  13, 1, "perf"),
    ("LMSLVP", 14, 1, "slaveport"),
    ("PMNDS",  15, 1, None),
    ("CCTLCSR", 16, 1, None),
    ("EFHW",   17, 1, None),
    ("VCCTL",  18, 2, None),
    ("EXCSLVL", 20, 2, None),
    ("NOPMC",  22, 1, None),
    ("SPE_AFT", 23, 1, None),
    ("ESLEEP", 24, 1, None),
    ("PPI",    25, 1, None),
    ("FIO",    26, 1, None),
    ("CLIC",   27, 1, None),
    ("ECLIC",  28, 1, None),
    ("EDSP",   29, 1, "dsp"),
    ("PPMA",   30, 1, "ppma"),
    ("MSC_EXT", 31, 1, None),
]

# mrvarch_cfg: every bit maps to a march token (or a token-family).  Version
# subfields (SM_VERSION/SS_VERSION) have no config.inc source and are carried.
MRVARCH_CFG_FIELDS = [
    ("Zba",          0, 1, "zba"),
    ("Zbb",          1, 1, "zbb"),
    ("Zbc",          2, 1, "zbc"),
    ("Zbs",          3, 1, "zbs"),
    ("Smepmp",       4, 1, "smepmp"),
    ("Svinval",      5, 1, "svinval"),
    ("Smstateen",    6, 1, "smstateen"),
    ("Sscofpmf",     7, 1, "sscofpmf"),
    ("Sstc",         8, 1, "sstc"),
    ("Zicbom",       9, 1, "zicbom"),
    ("Zicbop",      10, 1, "zicbop"),
    ("Zicboz",      11, 1, "zicboz"),
    ("Zbk",         12, 1, "zbk"),
    ("Zkn",         13, 1, "zkn"),
    ("Zks",         14, 1, "zks"),
    ("Zkt",         15, 1, "zkt"),
    ("Zkr",         16, 1, "zkr"),
    ("SM_VERSION",  17, 3, None),
    ("SS_VERSION",  20, 3, None),
    ("Svpbmt",      23, 1, "svpbmt"),
    ("Svnapot",     24, 1, "svnapot"),
    ("Zihintpause", 25, 1, "zihintpause"),
    ("Zca",         26, 1, "zca"),
    ("Zcb",         27, 1, "zcb"),
    ("Zcd",         28, 1, "zcd"),
    ("Zcf",         29, 1, "zcf"),
    ("Zcmp",        30, 1, "zcmp"),
    ("Zcmt",        31, 1, "zcmt"),
]


@dataclass
class FieldDiff:
    name: str
    lsb: int
    width: int
    derived: int
    reference: int
    source: str  # config.inc macro / march token, or "carried"

    @property
    def changed(self) -> bool:
        return self.derived != self.reference


def _mask(width: int) -> int:
    return (1 << width) - 1


def _token_source(token: str) -> str:
    return f"march:{token}"


def build(fields, sources: dict, tokens: frozenset[str], reference: int) -> tuple[int, list[FieldDiff]]:
    """Compute a CSR word from its field table.

    ``sources`` maps a field's source_key to either an int value or a bool.
    For mrvarch-style token fields the source_key is looked up in ``tokens``.
    Fields whose value is None/absent are carried from ``reference``.
    """
    value = 0
    diffs: list[FieldDiff] = []
    # carry any bits above bit 31 (RV64 high half) from the reference verbatim.
    high = reference & ~0xFFFFFFFF
    value |= high
    for name, lsb, width, key in fields:
        m = _mask(width)
        ref_field = (reference >> lsb) & m
        if key is None:
            derived_field = ref_field
            src = "carried"
        elif key in sources:
            raw = sources[key]
            derived_field = (int(raw) & m) if raw is not None else ref_field
            src = sources.get(key + "@src", f"cfg:{key}")
        else:
            # token-presence field (mrvarch)
            present = key in tokens
            derived_field = 1 if present else 0
            src = _token_source(key) if present else f"march:!{key}"
        value |= (derived_field & m) << lsb
        diffs.append(FieldDiff(name, lsb, width, derived_field, ref_field, src))
    return value, diffs


def summary(diffs: list[FieldDiff]) -> str:
    """Compact one-line changed-fields summary (+SET / -CLEARED / NAME r->d)."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    for d in diffs:
        if not d.changed:
            continue
        if d.width == 1:
            parts.append(("+" if d.derived else "-") + d.name)
        else:
            parts.append(f"{d.name} {d.reference}->{d.derived}")
    return " ".join(parts) if parts else "(identical)"


def format_diff(title: str, derived: int, reference: int, diffs: list[FieldDiff],
                only_changed: bool = False) -> str:
    lines = [f"{title}: derived=0x{derived:x}  reference=0x{reference:x}"
             f"  ({'differs' if derived != reference else 'identical'})"]
    lines.append(f"  {'field':<12}{'bits':<8}{'der':<5}{'ref':<5}source")
    for d in diffs:
        if only_changed and not d.changed:
            continue
        bits = f"[{d.lsb+d.width-1}:{d.lsb}]" if d.width > 1 else f"[{d.lsb}]"
        flag = "*" if d.changed else " "
        lines.append(f" {flag}{d.name:<12}{bits:<8}{d.derived:<5}{d.reference:<5}{d.source}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is a **TCL-based CPU configuration tool suite** for Andes RISC-V softcore processors plus a working **`config.inc` → `-march` converter** and a family of downstream **target-format generators** (QEMU cfg, SID conf, VEP). The TCL tools (under `config_tool/`) take user-selected ISA and hardware features and generate Verilog preprocessor configuration files (`config.inc`); the converters (under `scripts/`) read any such file and emit (a) a versioned RISC-V `-march` string identical to the canonical `NDS_ISA_STRING`, or (b) a target-tool config that treats `config.inc` as the authoritative source for CPU options.

See [`README.md`](README.md) for the top-level entry point and full file inventory.

## Running the Tools

No build step required — these are standalone TCL scripts.

```bash
# Interactive GUI mode (requires Tk)
./config_tool/<variant>_nds-softcore-config.tcl

# Batch mode: load a saved config and generate output
./config_tool/<variant>_nds-softcore-config.tcl --load config.cfg --generate

# Batch mode: override options directly
./config_tool/<variant>_nds-softcore-config.tcl --soft-config NDS_ISA_BASE=rv64i NDS_RVC_SUPPORT=yes --generate

# Load an extra TCL file (useful for extensions)
./config_tool/<variant>_nds-softcore-config.tcl -x extra.tcl
```

Key flags: `--help`, `--generate` (batch/no GUI), `--soft-config key=val ...`, `--load <file.cfg>`, `--debug`, `-fs <size>` (font size).

## Validation & Regression Testing

There is no pytest/unit-test harness. Validation is done by the converters'
own `--check` mode and by the SID regression matrix.

```bash
# Primary regression: every converter change MUST keep both passing.
# Re-derives -march for each file and diffs against the embedded NDS_ISA_STRING.
python3 scripts/config_to_march.py --check config_inc/*.inc
bash    scripts/config_to_march.sh    --check config_inc/*.inc   # bash port, same output

# After rule changes, regenerate the per-file report and review the diff.
python3 scripts/gen_march_report.py        # rewrites docs/CPU_CONFIG_REPORT.md

# SID conf round-trip: generate then diff against the sidconf/ ground truth.
python3 scripts/gen_sid_conf_batch.py --template-auto-cpu --out-dir out/sid_conf
python3 scripts/compare_sid_conf.py --reference-dir sidconf --generated-dir out/sid_conf --out-dir out/sid_compare
```

Expected baseline: **31/36** files with an embedded `NDS_ISA_STRING` match
byte-for-byte; the 5 known mismatches are unversioned ax66-family strings.

### SID regression matrix

A larger generation+runtime matrix lives under the `scripts/run_sid_regression_*`
tools, driven by `configs/sid_regression_matrix.json`. Cases are classified
`GEN_PASS`/`PASS`/`XFAIL` (expected) vs `GEN_FAIL`/`FAIL` (unexpected); the
closure goal is `unexpected=0`. See `docs/SID_REGRESSION_MATRIX.md` for phase
history and matrix dimensions.

```bash
# Generation-only smoke (no SID runtime), limited case count
python3 scripts/run_sid_regression_matrix.py --run --no-sid --max-cases 6

# Full sharded run with merged report + triage summary
python3 scripts/run_sid_regression_shards.py --shard-count 8 --from-shard 0 --to-shard 7 --gdb-smoke
python3 scripts/summarize_sid_regression_report.py out/.../merged/report.csv

# SID runtime checks need RV32/RV64 smoke ELFs (gdbserver attach sanity):
python3 scripts/build_sid_smoke_bins.py        # sources in tests/sid_smoke/
```

Runner knobs: `--run`/`--no-sid`, `--max-cases`, `--case-regex`, `--resume`,
`--shard-index`/`--shard-count`, `--gdb-smoke` (SID+GDB precheck, attaches a
per-case rv32/rv64 ELF auto-selected by CPU name).

## Architecture

### File Layout

All 36 CPU variants share the same internal framework. Each `*_nds-softcore-config.tcl` file is self-contained (~5000–10000 lines) and follows the same structure:

1. **CLI parsing** (`getopt`) — handles `--soft-config`, `--load`, `--generate`, etc.
2. **Option declarations** (`design_option`) — define all configurable CPU parameters with allowed values, defaults, constraints, and `to_define` code-gen blocks.
3. **Constraint/dependency rules** (`constraint`, `end_dependency_checker`) — enforce valid combinations (e.g., vector requires FP, 64-bit requires specific MMU schemes).
4. **GUI creation** (`create_gui`) — builds the Tk interface; skipped in `--generate` mode.
5. **Code generation** (`gen_config`) — iterates all options, executes each `to_define` block, and writes Verilog `` `define `` macros to `config.inc`.

### CPU Variants

| Series | Cores |
|--------|-------|
| A | a25, a27, a27l2, a45, a45mp, a46mp, a46mpv |
| AX | ax25mp (1c/4c), ax27, ax27l2, ax45, ax45mpv, ax46, ax46mp, ax46mpv, ax46-se, ax66 |
| D | d23, d23_corgi, d23_se_dcls, d23_se_sc, d25, d45 |
| N | n25, n25f |
| NX | nx25_ae350, nx25f_ae350, nx27v |

### Option Definition Pattern

```tcl
design_option NDS_ISA_BASE {} {
    full_name  {ISA base}
    value      {rv32e rv32i rv64i}
    default    rv64i
    to_define  {
        echo {`define NDS_ISA_BASE    "$value"}
    }
}
```

The `to_define` block is executed during `gen_config`; `$value` holds the selected value. Output goes to `config.inc`.

### Key Configuration Domains

- **ISA base**: `NDS_ISA_BASE` (rv32e/rv32i/rv64i)
- **Extensions**: `NDS_RVC_SUPPORT`, `NDS_RVA_SUPPORT`, `NDS_RVF/D_SUPPORT`, `NDS_RVV_SUPPORT`, `NDS_DSP_SUPPORT`, `NDS_ACE_SUPPORT`, `NDS_BFLOAT16_SUPPORT`
- **Memory**: ILM/DLM sizes, cache configs, TLB entries, PMP/PMA
- **MMU/VM**: sv32/sv39/sv48, privilege modes (1=M, 2=M+U, 3=M+S+U)
- **Vector**: VLEN, ELEN, SIMD_WIDTH, VLS_DATA_WIDTH

### State / Output Files

- `*.cfg` — saved configuration (key=value, loadable with `--load`)
- `config.inc` — generated Verilog `` `define `` macros (primary output)

## NDS_ISA_STRING / -march conversion

The end goal of this repo — generating a RISC-V `-march` string from a
`config.inc` — is **implemented**. Only **6 of 36** TCL configs contain a
`constraint NDS_ISA_STRING` block: 5 are byte-identical to canonical
`ax46mpv` (a46mp, a46mpv, ax46-se, ax46mp, ax46mpv), and `ax66` uses its
own unversioned format. The other 30 variants need rules derived from the
canonical and filtered to their option set.

### Converters (table-driven)

The mapping between config variables and `-march` tokens is **not**
hard-coded in either converter. It lives in a single plain-text DSL
file, **`scripts/march_rules.txt`**, which is the source of truth for
both implementations. To add/change/re-version a rule, edit only that
file — both converters reload it at startup.

- **`scripts/march_rules.txt`** — DSL rule table. Format:
  `<condition> | <token1> [<token2> ...]`. Conditions support `NAME`,
  `!NAME`, `NAME == val`, `NAME != val`, joined by `&&`. Rules apply
  in file order.
- **`scripts/config_to_march.py`** — Python converter. `derive_march`
  is a one-liner over `apply_rules(cfg, RULES, helpers)`.
  - `python3 scripts/config_to_march.py <file.inc> [...]`
  - `python3 scripts/config_to_march.py --check config_inc/*.inc`
- **`scripts/march_rules.py`** — Python rule loader + DSL evaluator.
- **`scripts/config_to_march.sh`** — pure bash converter that loads the
  same `march_rules.txt`. Requires bash ≥ 4.
- **`scripts/gen_march_report.py`** — regenerates `docs/CPU_CONFIG_REPORT.md`,
  the per-file report with `-march`, CPU ID, memory subsystem settings,
  and per-token rationale.
- **`scripts/config_to_profile.py`** — additive companion to the march
  converter; emits a structured CPU profile (`march` + MMU/cache/HVM/ILM/DLM
  + CPU identity + Andes CPU features) as text or `--json`, for
  toolchain/simulator/ACE integration. Does **not** modify the march path.

Current accuracy: **31/36** files with an embedded `NDS_ISA_STRING` match
byte-for-byte. The 5 mismatches are unversioned ax66-family strings.

Both converters also emit a **CPU ID** alongside the `-march`, extracted
from `` `define NDS_CPUID `` (last two hex digits of the Verilog literal
— e.g. `16'h8a46` → `46`, `20'h00023` → `23`). An `x` suffix is appended
when `NDS_ISA_BASE == rv64i`, so the same `45` core appears as `45` in
32-bit configs and `45x` in 64-bit configs. Output format:
`<path>: march=<march> cpuid=<cpuid>`.

Full DSL grammar, worked examples, and validation workflow are in
[`docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md §4 "Updating the mapping"`](docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md#4-updating-the-mapping).

### Documentation (under `docs/`)

- **[`docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md`](docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_DESIGN.md)** —
  full design doc for the Python converter: parser/accessor/rule-engine
  layers, per-section variable→token mapping, validation, limitations.
- **[`docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_SH_DESIGN.md`](docs/CONFIG_TO_MARCH_SH_DESIGN.md)** —
  what's specific to the bash port.
- **[`docs/NDS_ISA_STRING_analysis.md`](docs/NDS_ISA_STRING_analysis.md)** —
  source-of-truth spec. Decoded canonical rules (sections 1–14), per-tier
  proposed constraints for the 30 variants without one, ax66's format,
  pseudocode for a converter.
- **[`docs/CONFIG_INC_ANALYSIS.md`](docs/CONFIG_INC_ANALYSIS.md)** —
  feasibility study of the 97 `config_inc/*.inc` files.
- **[`docs/config_variables_coverage.md`](docs/config_variables_coverage.md)** —
  coverage matrix of `NDS_*` variables across all 36 TCL configurators.
- **[`docs/CPU_CONFIG_REPORT.md`](docs/CPU_CONFIG_REPORT.md)** — generated
  per-file report: `-march`, CPU ID, memory subsystem, per-token explanation.
- **[`docs/SIDCONF_USAGE.md`](docs/SIDCONF_USAGE.md)** — SID converter usage,
  topology rules, runtime check, batch metadata, compare workflow.
- **[`docs/SIDCONF_ANALYSIS.md`](docs/SIDCONF_ANALYSIS.md)** — SID format
  analysis: `cpu-option` token inventory and topology shape.
- **[`docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_SIDCONF_PLAN.md`](docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_SIDCONF_PLAN.md)** —
  phase-by-phase plan and progress tracker for the `config.inc → sid.conf`
  work (all 9 phases currently marked Completed).
- **[`docs/SIDCONF_UNCONFIRMED_OPTIONS.md`](docs/SIDCONF_UNCONFIRMED_OPTIONS.md)** —
  remaining SID `cpu-option` keys not yet mapped to a `config.inc` macro.
- **[`docs/sidconf_comments.md`](docs/sidconf_comments.md)** — source-of-truth
  notes from the SID owner that drove the confirmed mappings.
- **[`docs/SID_REGRESSION_MATRIX.md`](docs/SID_REGRESSION_MATRIX.md)** —
  phase history, matrix dimensions, and pass/XFAIL classification for the
  `config.inc → sid.conf` regression matrix.
- **[`docs/SID_TEMPLATE_AUTO_SELECTION_PLAN.md`](docs/SID_TEMPLATE_AUTO_SELECTION_PLAN.md)** —
  plan for `--template-auto-cpu` runtime CPU-template matching in `sidconf/`.
- **[`docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_STL_H_PLAN.md`](docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_STL_H_PLAN.md)** —
  design/plan + phase tracker for the `config.inc → nds_stl_rte_cpu.h`
  (Software Test Library runtime CPU header) converter; tracked as gitea
  issue #1. Confirmed-subset converter is implemented; blocked macros await
  the spec PPT.
- **[`docs/STL_RTE_CPU_USAGE.md`](docs/STL_RTE_CPU_USAGE.md)** — user guide
  for `config_inc_to_stl_h.py` / `gen_stl_h_batch.py`: options, output
  format, macro mapping, missing-source/critical-warning behavior,
  validation, batch layout, exit codes.
- **[`docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_ALIOTH_PLAN.md`](docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_ALIOTH_PLAN.md)** —
  design + mapping reference for `config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py`: Alioth's
  two config layers (external customer cfg vs internal `iss` cfg), the
  per-section variable→key mapping, `misa`/`marchid` derivation, ACE
  handling, dialect tolerance, and `--check` validation against the
  Alioth `doc/external_config/` schema + `cfg/<ip>/iss/` reference.

### Downstream target generators (CPU-first; `config.inc` is authoritative)

These all share **`scripts/config_inc_shared.py`** for CPU-model
derivation, march-token normalization, Verilog hex parsing, and
`load_cpu_inc_model` (cfg + march + tokens + xlen). When adding a new
converter or refactoring an existing one, prefer extending the shared
helpers over re-deriving the same data.

- **`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`** — QEMU cfg generator. Emits
  `[machine]` (AIA-aware), CPU ISA globals from the derived march, and
  `[andes-config "cpu"]` properties for options not represented in
  march. `--with-platform` adds SOC globals (ILM/DLM/HVM); `--qemu-v9-strict`
  matches QEMU v9 unmapped-token semantics.
- **`scripts/gen_qemu_cfg_batch.py`** — batches the above over normal
  Andes 23/25/27/45/46/65/66 sets; reports non-strict unmapped march
  tokens.
- **`scripts/config_inc_to_sid_conf.py`** — SID conf generator.
  `--cpu-option-only` or `--full-conf` via board templates from
  `sidconf/`. Supported families: `22/23/225/25/27/45` (`23` = D23
  partial). Topology controls (`--topology smp/amp`, `--cores`,
  `--mhartids`); AE350 AMP slave-port windows are assigned per core when
  `NDS_SLAVE_PORT_SUPPORT` is enabled. Optional `--sid-check` runtime probe.
- **`scripts/gen_sid_conf_batch.py`** — SID batch generator with optional
  per-target topology metadata JSON.
- **`scripts/compare_sid_conf.py`** — normalizes generated vs reference
  SID confs; emits detail JSON, expected/unexpected split JSON, summary CSV.
- **`scripts/config_inc_to_vep.py`** — patches an AE350 VEP template using
  `config.inc` as authoritative source for CPU-centric options + selected
  platform fields (ILM/DLM/HVM, AIA guests). Keeps platform wiring from
  the template.
- **`scripts/gen_vep_batch.py`** — batches VEP patching across normal
  Andes families. Includes a 46-series → AX45MPV-1C template fallback
  when no direct AE350 VEP template exists.
- **`scripts/split_vep_diff_report.py`** — splits a VEP diff JSON into
  *expected* (cpu-option keys derived from `config.inc`/march, divergence
  intentional under config.inc-authoritative policy) vs *unexpected*,
  plus a CSV summary.
- **`scripts/config_inc_to_stl_h.py`** — STL runtime CPU header generator.
  Emits `nds_stl_rte_cpu.h` (`#define CONFIG_*` macros) from `config.inc`
  for gitea issue #1. Mapping is a typed Python table (`MAPPING` + per-kind
  value funcs), **not** the march DSL. Covers the confirmed ~25-macro
  subset; the 7 macros with no source in any config.inc (`HAS_MSCEXT`,
  `HAS_MRVARCH`, `HAS_CCTL_AUTOINC`, `HAS_NDS_ISA_STR/LEA/BFO/BBZ`) are
  emitted as `// #define ...` comments, never guessed. `--check` self-validates
  (all macros present, types well-formed); output is deterministic.
  When a mapped attribute's source macro is absent from `config.inc`, the
  line is annotated with `// no macro info: <NDS_MACRO> ...` and a `CRITICAL`
  warning is printed to stderr in **bold red** on a TTY (plain when piped,
  so CSVs/logs stay clean). Missing sources do not fail generation.
- **`scripts/gen_stl_h_batch.py`** — batches the STL header over the normal
  Andes family filter (same as `gen_qemu_cfg_batch.py`); per-CPU output dir
  + summary CSV. See `docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_STL_H_PLAN.md`.
- **`scripts/config_inc_to_alioth_yaml.py`** — Alioth (`sc_sim`) config YAML
  generator. Emits **both** Alioth layers as single self-contained files:
  the **external** customer cfg (`top.cluster.<core>.*` / `general.*`
  snake_case knobs, validatable against `<Alioth>/doc/external_config/<ip>.yaml`)
  and the **internal** `iss` cfg (`isa_*` flags + `misa`/`marchid`/`xlen`/
  `vlen`/`elen`/MMU). `misa`/`marchid` are computed and verified bit-for-bit
  against `<Alioth>/cfg/<ip>/iss/+iss.cfg.yml`. `mmsc_cfg`/`mrvarch_cfg` are
  **SPA-spec bit-derived** via `scripts/alioth_csr.py` (field maps from
  `/Work/v5_spa/src/andes_v5_machine_mode_csr.txt`): emitted as the primary
  value plus the Alioth reference + changed-field summary ("emit both + diff");
  full per-bit breakdown via `--csr-diff`. The checked-in Alioth reference is a
  loose template, so spec-derived values are intentionally more accurate.
  `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` remain base reference values.
  **ACE** is handled on both layers (external `support_ace` + `ace.*`; internal
  `ace_enable` + `ace_helper.*` + ACE-overlay `mmsc_cfg`), emitted only for
  ACE-capable IPs. `--layer external|internal|both`, `--cores`, `--core-name`,
  `--out-dir`; `--check` validates external keys vs the shipped schema and iss
  scalars vs the reference. See `docs/CONFIG_INC_TO_ALIOTH_PLAN.md`.
- **`scripts/gen_alioth_yaml_batch.py`** — batches the Alioth YAML over the
  Alioth-supported IP set (ax45mp, ax46mp/mpv, a46mp/mpv, nx45v, d23→d23v, …);
  per-CPU output dir + summary CSV.

### Reference SID conf corpus (`sidconf/`)

27 default `*.vep.conf` files from AST542 covering AE250 and AE350 boards.
Used both as templates by `config_inc_to_sid_conf.py` (AE250 →
`ADP-AE250-N25.vep.conf`, AE350 single-core → `ADP-AE350-AX45MPV-1C.vep.conf`,
AE350 AMP → `ADP-AE350-N25F-AMP.vep.conf`) and as ground truth for
`compare_sid_conf.py`.

### Helper scripts

- **`scripts/scan_tcl_configs.py`** — extracts constraint blocks,
  `design_option` declarations, and `to_define` macro mappings from every
  `*-nds-softcore-config.tcl`. Modes:
  - `python3 scripts/scan_tcl_configs.py` — presence summary
  - `--canonical-compare` — per-variant coverage of canonical options
  - `--json out.json` — full machine-readable dump
  - `--dump-constraints dir/` — write each constraint body to a file
- **`scripts/analyze_config_inc.py`** — earlier feasibility analyzer over
  the `config_inc/` corpus.

### Variant tiers (by canonical-option coverage)

| Tier | Coverage | Variants |
|---|---|---|
| A | 34/34 | a46mp, a46mpv, ax46-se, ax46mp, ax46mpv (have constraint) |
| B | 28/34 | a45, a45mp, ax45, ax45-cheri, ax45mp, ax45mpv, d45, d45-se, n45, nx45, nx45v |
| B' | 18/34 | ax45v |
| C | 17/34 | a27, a27l2, ax27, ax27l2, nx27v |
| D | 15/34 | a25, ax25, ax25mp_1c, ax25mp_4c, d25, n25, n25f, nx25_ae350, nx25f_ae350 |
| E | 4/34  | d23, d23_corgi, d23_se_dcls, d23_se_sc |
| F | own format | ax66 |

### Macro mapping quirks (for any converter implementation)

- Most options emit a macro of the **same name** plus an `_INT` numeric form.
  Prefer `_INT` for boolean comparisons.
- `NDS_SSTC_SUPPORT` emits **only** `` `NDS_SSTC_SUPPORT_INT`` (no plain form).
- `NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT` emits `` `NDS_VECTOR_DOT_SUPPORT_INT`` (DOT, not VDOT).
- `NDS_ZILSD_SUPPORT` / `NDS_ZCMLSD_SUPPORT` are declared as `{0 1}` but the
  canonical constraint compares against `"yes"` — these rules are dead in the
  canonical TCL. A correct converter should treat `_INT == 1` as the trigger.

content.text:
Verified. Here is the grounding for our discussion, then the design choice.

## What the tool gives us
The converter reads any `config.inc` and emits four things: a `-march` string, a QEMU `-cpu` cfg, a profile JSON, and (most relevant) an **Alioth ISS manifest**. On our real premium `config.inc` it produced `xandescodense` (= uitb) but **no** `xandesdsp` (= no ucode) - it already encodes the gaps the probe found the hard way.

## The key realization: `mmsc_cfg`
`scripts/alioth_csr.py` maps the Andes hardware register `mmsc_cfg` (CSR `0xFC2`) bit-by-bit to config.inc gates:

| mmsc_cfg bit | gate | our CSR(s) |
|---|---|---|
| EDSP (29) | `dsp` | ucode (F4) |
| PPMA (30) | `ppma` | pmacfg/pmaaddr (F3) |
| PFT (4) | `powerbrake` | mpft_ctl (F6) |
| ECC (0) | `ecc` | mecc_code (F5) |
| HSP (5) | (hardware) | mhsp_ctl/msp_* (F7) |
| ECD (3) | `codense` | uitb (F1) |
| PMNDS (15) | (hardware) | mcountermask_m (F8) |

I confirmed **QEMU implements `mmsc_cfg` and already self-gates on it** (`cpu_helper.c`, `pmu.c` read these bits; `cpu.c:951` sets them at reset). It is a read-only register, so it is NOT in our transport list today - but it is readable on both engines.

So there are **two sources of the same truth**: the offline `config.inc` (via the converter) and the runtime `mmsc_cfg` the core reports itself.

## The design fork (drain/restore gating)
The dangerous side is **restore**, not drain. Draining an extra CSR from QEMU is a harmless read; *restoring* a CSR the vsim core does not implement is what HANGS. So the gate belongs in `ResumeDriver`, keyed on the **destination** core's capability.

| | A. Offline manifest | B. Runtime `mmsc_cfg` |
|---|---|---|
| Source | converter(config.inc) -> per-engine file | read 0xFC2 from live vsim core |
| Plumbing | driver loads file -> allow-list -> plugin+resume | ResumeDriver reads 0xFC2, gates its restore loop |
| Coverage | all 13 CSRs (incl. milmb/jvt) | most; a few lack a presence bit |
| Self-correcting | no (file must track RTL) | yes (HW reports itself) |
| Kills the EDSP/ECC hang | yes | yes |

## Honest gaps
- `mmsc_cfg` gates the dangerous CSRs (dsp/ecc/ppma/powerbrake/hsp) but NOT all 13 - milmb/mdlmb/mclk_ctl/jvt are gated by other config bits, so B alone leaves a few on "tolerant no-op".
- Gating **avoids triggering** the hang; it does not **fix** the latent hang (you chose to stop on that - gating is still the correct behavior regardless).

## My recommendation
Make **B (runtime `mmsc_cfg`)** the spine: add `mmsc_cfg`+`mrvarch_cfg` to the drained state, and in `ResumeDriver` skip any Andes CSR whose destination presence bit is clear. It needs no per-engine files, self-corrects per engine, and directly kills both hang cases. Use the **converter (A) as the offline oracle** - to document the full gate map and cross-check `mmsc_cfg` in a test (does the RTL's reported register match what config.inc says?).

## Question
Which do you want as the **primary** gate - the runtime `mmsc_cfg` register (self-describing, no files), or the offline converter manifest (most complete, but one file per engine)? My vote is `mmsc_cfg` primary + converter as the offline checker.

Sorry, too complex. Let me explain simple.

## The problem (simple)
Every Andes CPU is a little different. Some CPUs have feature X, some do not.

Hybrid copies CPU state from QEMU to vsim. The state includes special registers (CSRs).

Bad thing: if we copy a CSR that the vsim CPU does **not** have -> vsim **freezes** (the hang you saw).

So we must know first: **which CSRs does this CPU have?** Then copy only those.

## Simple picture
Think about packing a bag for a friend.
- If you put in something the bag cannot hold -> the bag breaks.
- So you need a list: "what can this bag hold?"

For our CPU, the "list of what it has" can come from **two places**:

- **Place 1 - the config file** (`config.inc`). Each CPU has one. It says "I have DSP: no, I have PMA: yes..." The tool you gave me reads this file.

- **Place 2 - a register inside the CPU** called `mmsc_cfg`. The CPU itself tells you "I have these features." We just read it while running.

Both places say the **same thing**. One is a file (read before run), one is a register (read during run).

## My one question
Which place should hybrid use to get the list?

- File (config.inc) -> need one file per CPU.
- Register (mmsc_cfg) -> no file, the CPU tells us itself.

I think the register is easier. But you decide.

Do you want me to show a tiny real example first (what the file says vs what the register says for the premium CPU), so it is clearer?

## The plan in 3 steps
1. **Offline, once per CPU:** read its `config.inc`, make a small list - "this CPU has these Andes CSRs." Save the list.
2. **Run time:** the driver reads the list for the CPU you picked.
3. **Drain + restore:** copy only the CSRs on the list. Skip the rest. No freeze.

## The one new thing I build
A small rule table. One line per CSR. Each line says which config feature turns that CSR on:

```
ucode     needs DSP        (premium: no  -> skip)
pmaaddr   needs PMA        (premium: no  -> skip)
mpft_ctl  needs PowerBrake (premium: no  -> skip)
uitb      needs CoDense    (premium: yes -> copy)
```

This table is small (about 13 lines) and works for **every** CPU, old or new. A new CPU just needs its `config.inc` - no code change. That is why we do not hardcode a list per CPU (your rule: no hardcode, keep it portable).

## Why this is good over time
- One rule table -> all CPUs covered.
- Add a new CPU later -> just drop in its `config.inc`.
- The freeze cannot come back, on any CPU.

Before I touch any real hybrid code, let me build a tiny demo:
- input: premium `config.inc`

content.text:
Yes - it is OK. Better than OK: **your framework is already built this way.** I checked, and both halves already exist.

## Two things already in place

**1. The vsim core already knows its own config.**
When a core is built, its `config.inc` is compiled into a C++ header. The premium header literally contains:
```
#define _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT 0     <- no DSP  -> skip ucode
#define _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT 1 <- CoDense -> copy uitb
#define _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT 0 <- no ECC  -> skip mecc_code
```
The core wrapper already uses this pattern (`has_shared_cache = NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`). So a core computing "which CSRs do I have" is the same trick, already in use.

**2. The engine already self-reports.**
Each `sim_<core>` binary answers `--describe` with a JSON card (today it reports `vlen`, `triggers`, `kind`, `state`). The andesim driver reads that card - "the framework keeps zero per-engine code; every capability comes from here" (its own words). Adding a CSR list to the card is the natural next field.

## The shape
```
config.inc --(build time)--> core compiled with _NDS_* feature macros
        |
 sim_<core> --describe -->  { vlen:512, ..., "andes_csrs": ["uitb","milmb",...] }
        |
 andesim driver reads the card  (already does this for vlen/triggers)
        |
 drain + restore ONLY those CSRs   -> no freeze, on any core
```

## This still matches your "offline file" choice
The truth still comes from `config.inc`, **offline, at build time**. The only change: the core *carries* that truth and hands it over at startup, instead of us shipping a separate file beside it. A separate file can fall out of sync with the RTL; this cannot.

## Where the converter fits
The converter (`cpu_config_to_march_converter`) becomes the **offline checker**: it reads the same `config.inc` and must produce the same CSR list the core reports. A test compares them.
```
config.inc --(converter)--> caps  ==[test must match]==  core's --describe caps
```
This is the flywheel: if someone changes an RTL config and the self-report drifts, the test catches it.

## One decision for you
Who computes the CSR list?
- **A. The core computes it** (C++, from its compiled-in macros). Converter = checker only. Simpler; no Python in the build.
- **B. The converter computes it** at build time, baked into the card. One rule table, but couples the build to Python.

My vote: **A** (core self-reports) + converter as the offline checker. Want me to go deeper on A and show the exact small piece the core would add?

content.text:
Going deep on A. Here is the exact mechanism, who computes it, and who uses it.

## The whole picture (who does what)
```
config.inc --(build)--> core has _NDS_* macros built in
                              |
        +---------------------+------------------------+
        |                                              |
  RESTORE (in vsim, same process)              --describe card
  reads macros directly,                       core lists its CSRs
  skips CSRs it lacks  -> no freeze                   |
                                              andesim driver reads card
                                              skips them in --verify -> no false diff
```
Two users, one truth. The dangerous one (restore) is **in the vsim process**, so it reads the built-in macros directly - it does not even need the card. The card is only so the **driver** knows what to skip when it compares.

## Piece 1 - the table gains a "needs which feature" column
Today the 13 CSRs live in one table in `state_abi.h`. Add one column - the feature gate:
```c
//  field            addr    name          gate
X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb",        HYB_GATE_CODENSE)     \
X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode",       HYB_GATE_DSP)         \
X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl",    HYB_GATE_POWERBRAKE)  \
X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code",   HYB_GATE_ECC)         \
X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl",    HYB_GATE_STACKSAFE)   \
...
```
This stays the **single source of truth** - add a CSR = one line, every consumer follows.

## Piece 2 - the core turns a gate into yes/no (this is the new small piece)
One small function in vsim. It is the ONLY place that touches the built-in macros:
```cpp
// vsim: andes_caps.hpp   (uses the V<core>_config.h macros already included)
constexpr bool gate_on(HybridGate g) {
  switch (g) {
    case HYB_GATE_DSP:        return _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT;
    case HYB_GATE_CODENSE:    return _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT;
    case HYB_GATE_POWERBRAKE: return _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT;
    case HYB_GATE_STACKSAFE:  return _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT;
    case HYB_GATE_ECC:        return _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT || _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT;
    case HYB_GATE_PMA:        return _NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0;
    case HYB_GATE_ILM:        return _NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0;
    // ...
    case HYB_GATE_ALWAYS:     return true;   // mxstatus etc.
  }
}
```
The CSR names are NOT repeated here - they stay in the table. This switch only maps each gate to the matching config macro.

## Piece 3 - restore uses it (one-line change, kills the freeze)
```cpp
// before:  always write -> freezes when the CSR is absent
#define X(field, addr, name, gate)  write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
// after:   write only if the core has it
#define X(field, addr, name, gate)  if (gate_on(gate)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
```

## Piece 4 - the card + driver verify
`--describe` runs the same table+`gate_on` to emit `"andes_csrs":[...]`; the driver stores it in `EngineDescriptor` (already parses `vlen`/`triggers` this way) and `state_diff` skips any CSR not in that list.

## Honest gap
About 8 gates are crisp and confirmed by the probe (dsp, codense, powerbrake, stacksafe, ecc, ilm, dlm, perf-monitor). About 4 need confirming before I trust them: `jvt`, `pma`, `mxstatus`, `mclk_ctl`. I will confirm each against the spec/config, not guess.

## Plan (smallest first, TDD)
1. **vsim, test first:** unit test - "premium `gate_on` says DSP=off, CoDense=on." Then add the table column + `gate_on`. (RED -> GREEN, no engine run needed.)
2. vsim: gate the restore loop (Piece 3) + the drain re-read + `--describe` emit.
3. andesim: `EngineDescriptor.andes_csrs` + `state_diff` skip.
4. converter: offline checker test (its caps == card caps).

1	// B7: doctest for the QEMU-plugin V-drain decision function.
2	//
3	// The plugin's V-state drain used to gate on `v->vlenb` (the register
4	// handle truthiness) AND `s.vlenb > 0`. The combination silently omits
5	// the V block whenever the stub advertises some V state but not vlenb,
6	// confusing "stub broke" with "V disabled at runtime". This test pins
7	// the four-case truth table: SKIP when no V at all, ABORT when partial,
8	// SKIP when V advertised but disabled (vlenb=0), OK otherwise.
9	
10	#define DOCTEST_CONFIG_IMPLEMENT_WITH_MAIN
11	#include "doctest.h"
12	
13	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  // HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX (the L11 ceiling)
14	#include "hybrid/v_drain_policy.h"
15	
16	TEST_CASE("no V advertised at all -> SKIP")
17	{
18	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/0, /*has_other_v=*/0,
19	                              /*vlenb_value=*/0)
20	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP);
21	}
22	
23	TEST_CASE("vlenb missing but vtype/vl/etc advertised -> ABORT")
24	{
25	  // The "broken stub" case the original gate hid. Don't silently emit a
26	  // zero-filled V block: the resume side then restores garbage V state.
27	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/0, /*has_other_v=*/1,
28	                              /*vlenb_value=*/0)
29	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT);
30	}
31	
32	TEST_CASE("vlenb advertised but value=0 -> SKIP (V disabled at runtime)")
33	{
34	  // QEMU may expose the V feature in XML even when V is not enabled in
35	  // the CPU at runtime; vlenb then reads 0. Treat as "no V live".
36	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
37	                              /*vlenb_value=*/0)
38	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP);
39	}
40	
41	TEST_CASE("vlenb advertised, value>0 -> OK")
42	{
43	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
44	                              /*vlenb_value=*/16)
45	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK);
46	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
47	                              /*vlenb_value=*/64)
48	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK);
49	}
50	
51	TEST_CASE("L11: vlenb at the wire-format ceiling -> OK (VLEN 1024)")
52	{
53	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
54	                              /*vlenb_value=*/HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
55	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK);
56	}
57	
58	TEST_CASE("L11: vlenb above the wire-format ceiling -> ABORT, not a "
59	          "silent clamp")
60	{
61	  // The old drain clamped the copy to HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX and dropped
62	  // the upper bytes of every V register without a word. Refuse instead:
63	  // the state file cannot represent this engine's V regfile.
64	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
65	                              /*vlenb_value=*/HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX + 1)
66	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT);
67	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/1,
68	                              /*vlenb_value=*/2 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
69	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT);
70	}
71	
72	TEST_CASE("vlenb advertised alone (no other V) is still ABORT-equivalent: "
73	          "policy treats vlenb-only as no V context")
74	{
75	  // Edge case: stub advertises vlenb but no other V regs. This is
76	  // unusual; treat as SKIP since we have no V data to actually drain.
77	  // (Documented behaviour, not a runtime failure mode QEMU emits.)
78	  CHECK(hybrid_v_drain_policy(/*has_vlenb=*/1, /*has_other_v=*/0,
79	                              /*vlenb_value=*/16)
80	        == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP);
81	}

  vsim_add_test(${name} ${source})
  target_include_directories(${name} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  add_dependencies(check ${name})
endfunction()

# Hybrid simulator (QEMU + Verilator) build integration.

option(VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID "Enable hybrid QEMU+Verilator co-simulation" OFF)

set(VSIM_QEMU_ROOT "/local/nick/qemu_v5"
  CACHE PATH "Path to QEMU source tree used to build the hybrid TCG plugin")

# Register a header-only hybrid doctest: build it (vsim_add_test marks it
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL), expose the shared ABI headers from the andesim_abi
# submodule (external/andesim_abi/hybrid), and wire it into the `check`
# target. The include path is inert for the handful of tests that do not
# pull in state_abi.h.
function(hybrid_add_test name source)
  vsim_add_test(${name} ${source})
  target_include_directories(${name} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  add_dependencies(check ${name})
endfunction()

# The ABI test is always built so struct layout drift is caught even in
# non-hybrid builds. It has no SystemC/Verilator dependency.
hybrid_add_test(test_state_abi tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp)

# B7: pure-C V-drain decision policy. Header-only, no SystemC dependency.
hybrid_add_test(test_v_drain_policy tests/hybrid/v_drain_policy.test.cpp)

# Shared-mem smoke: glues MmapBacking + SimpleMemory and verifies bytes are
# visible through an independent mmap of the same file. Links SystemC, so it
# keeps the explicit registration instead of hybrid_add_test.
vsim_add_test(test_shared_mem_smoke tests/hybrid/shared_mem_smoke.test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(test_shared_mem_smoke PRIVATE
  lib_fmt
  lib_spdlog
  lib_systemc
  ${VSIM_LINK_LIBS}
)
add_dependencies(test_shared_mem_smoke ext_fmt ext_spdlog ext_systemc)
add_dependencies(check test_shared_mem_smoke)

# Section 9: validates the narrowed QEMU-virt RAM region + mmap composition.
vsim_add_test(test_shared_mem_offset tests/hybrid/shared_mem_offset.test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(test_shared_mem_offset PRIVATE
  lib_fmt
  lib_spdlog
  lib_systemc
  ${VSIM_LINK_LIBS}
)
add_dependencies(test_shared_mem_offset ext_fmt ext_spdlog ext_systemc)
add_dependencies(check test_shared_mem_offset)

1	// Oracle differential compare (verify_oracle F2): field-wise diff of two
2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).
4	//
5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31],
8	//            mepc/mcause (round-trip), mscratch (L23) + mtval/mie (L24) --
9	//            round-trip M-mode CSRs restored at resume + re-read at drain;
10	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
11	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.
12	//   skipped: mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, mip, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[].
13	//            mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp/PMP are passthrough on the vsim side
14	//            (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read). mip IS
15	//            re-read but excluded here -- its pending bits are hardware-driven
16	//            and diverge between the engines' clocks. mstatus is excluded for
17	//            its dirty/impl-defined bits.
18	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret -- the engines count cycles/insns differently
19	//            by design.
20	#ifndef ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
21	#define ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
22	
23	#include <string>
24	#include <vector>
25	
26	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
27	
28	namespace andes_sim {
29	
30	// One strictly-compared field that differs: "pc", "x5", "f31", "vl",
31	// "v3[7]" (register + byte offset), "flags", ...
32	struct FieldDiff {
33	  std::string field;
34	  unsigned long long ref = 0;
35	  unsigned long long got = 0;
36	};
37	
38	struct DiffReport {
39	  int compared = 0;  // count of strictly compared fields
40	  std::vector<FieldDiff> diffs;
41	  bool ok() const { return diffs.empty(); }
42	};
43	
44	DiffReport diff_states(const hybrid_state_v1& ref, const hybrid_state_v1& got);
45	
46	// Print `r` as "[state-diff] ..." lines: one per mismatch, then the
47	// PASS/FAIL verdict. Shared by the state-diff subcommand and run --verify.
48	void print_diff_report(const DiffReport& r);
49	
50	}  // namespace andes_sim
51	
52	#endif  // ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.

This is the OFFLINE checker for the andesim hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in
Python, the C++ gate logic the vsim engine compiles in
(src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp + andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine
reports the same list via `sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the
andesim driver uses it to skip --verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this
on the same config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the
offline config and the built engine (the flywheel).

Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

Usage:
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from config_to_march import _int, is_yes, parse_inc  # noqa: E402


def _ecc_any(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC (type != none)."""
    for blk in ("NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE",
                "NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE"):
        n = _int(cfg, blk)
        if n is not None and n > 0:
            return True
    return False


def gates(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    """Feature gates, mirroring andes_caps_from_config() in the vsim binary."""
    return {
        "DSP":          is_yes(cfg, "NDS_DSP_SUPPORT"),
        "CODENSE":      is_yes(cfg, "NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT"),
        "POWERBRAKE":   is_yes(cfg, "NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT"),
        "STACKSAFE":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT"),
        "PERF_MONITOR": is_yes(cfg, "NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR"),
        "PMA":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PMA_ENTRIES") or 0) > 0,
        "ILM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "DLM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "ECC":          _ecc_any(cfg),
        "ALWAYS":       True,
    }


# (csr name, gate) in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST order, then the PMA group markers --
# mirrors andes_caps.hpp andes_gate_for() + supported_andes_csr_names().
_CSR_GATES = [
    ("mxstatus",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("mpft_ctl",       "POWERBRAKE"),
    ("mclk_ctl",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("milmb",          "ILM"),
    ("mdlmb",          "DLM"),
    ("mecc_code",      "ECC"),
    ("mhsp_ctl",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_bound",      "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_base",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("mcountermask_m", "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("uitb",           "CODENSE"),
    ("jvt",            "CODENSE"),
    ("ucode",          "DSP"),
    ("pmacfg",         "PMA"),
    ("pmaaddr",        "PMA"),
]


def supported_andes_csrs(cfg: dict) -> list:
    g = gates(cfg)
    return [name for name, gate in _CSR_GATES if g[gate]]


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    if argv and argv[0] == "--check":
        if len(argv) < 2:
            print(__doc__)
            return 2
        got = supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(Path(argv[1])))
        want = argv[2:]
        if got != want:
            print(f"MISMATCH\n  got:  {got}\n  want: {want}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("OK: " + " ".join(got))
        return 0
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    print(" ".join(supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(Path(argv[0])))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
#
#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
#      option, not an engine column).
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
#
# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen  [$4=dlen  $5=elen]
  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"dlen":${4:-0},"elen":${5:-0},"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256 192 32

# 2 + 3 + 4: qemu built-in present; fakeA discovered with its fields
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null) \
  || fail "list engines exited non-zero"
echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu64" || fail "built-in qemu64 not listed:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA not discovered:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "256" || fail "fakeA vlen (256) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "cycle-accurate" || fail "fakeA kind not shown:"$'\n'"$out"

# 4b. RVV hw params: XLEN/DLEN/ELEN columns; an engine that reports none
# (the qemu built-in) shows "-" for each.
for col in XLEN VLEN DLEN ELEN; do
  echo "$out" | head -1 | grep -qw "$col" \
    || fail "list engines: $col column header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
done
echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "192" \
  || fail "fakeA dlen (192) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "32" \
  || fail "fakeA elen (32) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -w "qemu64" | grep -q -- "-" \
  || fail "qemu64 row should show '-' for unreported params:"$'\n'"$out"

# 5. hot-plug: drop a SECOND engine, re-run (no rebuild), both appear
make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeB" "vsim:fakeB" 128
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA missing after hot-plug"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeB" \
  || fail "HOT-PLUG: fakeB not discovered without rebuild:"$'\n'"$out"

# 6. sidecar fallback: a binary with no --describe + a <bin>.json descriptor
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 3
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
{"id":"vsim:sidecar","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
SIDE
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:sidecar" \
  || fail "SIDECAR fallback failed (vsim:sidecar not listed):"$'\n'"$out"

# 7. (opportunistic) real default scan: if vsim is built, its sim_* binaries
# must self-describe and appear. Skipped when vsim has not been built.
if ls "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/"sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  out=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^vsim:" \
    || fail "default scan discovered no real vsim engine:"$'\n'"$out"
fi

ok "F2 engine registry + self-describe"
