# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,
`mcctlcommand` issues a cache op) is an instruction in CSR clothing, not state.
Those are excluded **with a documented reason**, asserted by the guard - that is
how "nothing missed" is satisfied without 142 meaningless round-trips.

## Architecture

Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:

1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)
   iterates the list, so **adding a CSR is one line** and no consumer drifts.

2. **Capability-gated, not assumed.** Each new CSR maps to a feature gate in
   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.

3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks
   inventory <-> matrix <-> `state_abi.h` and **fails CI** on any drift: a CSR the
   spec adds, a CSR transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a promised CSR
   missing from the ABI. Refresh path: `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`
   (PDF -> inventory) then `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (inventory -> matrix).

## Per-feature definition of done

Each expansion feature (F3+) is ONE CSR block and must deliver all of:

- [ ] `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` X() line(s) in the ABI submodule (+ pin bump in andesim and vsim)
- [ ] QEMU plugin drains it (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`)
- [ ] `ResumeDriver` restores it (tolerant, capability-gated)
- [ ] `StateDrain` re-reads it
- [ ] `state_diff` verifies it (with the right exclusions, e.g. HW-driven latches)
- [ ] `andes_caps.hpp` gate entry + `classify_csr_coverage.py` stays in parity
- [ ] one per-section round-trip fixture under `tests/fixtures/`, run on premium
- [ ] guard test still green; ROADMAP state updated

Cross-repo note: the ABI lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned by BOTH
andesim and the external vsim. A block touches 3 repos (ABI + vsim consumers +
qemu_plugin), like the v3 Andes block did.

## Features

| ID | Feature | CSRs | Depends | State |
|----|---------|------|---------|-------|
| F1 | Completeness guard test | (none - foundation) | - | TODO |
| F2 | ABI scaffold: `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` + `hybrid_m_ext_csr` + `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT` + v4 + consumers iterate | (structural) | F1 | TODO |
| F3 | Machine Configuration | menvcfg, mseccfg | F2 | TODO |
| F4 | NMI handling | mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus, mnvec, mrnxvec | F2 | TODO |
| F5 | Counters / perf-monitor | mhpmcounter3-6, mhpmevent3-6, mcounteren, mcountinhibit, mcounterwen, mcounterinten, mcountermask_s, mcountermask_u | F2 | TODO |
| F6 | Andes trap-save | mdcause, mslideleg, msavestatus, msaveepc1/2, msavecause1/2, msavedcause1/2 | F2 | TODO |
| F7 | CLIC | mtvt, mintthresh, mirq_entry | F2 | TODO |
| F8 | State-enable | mstateen0-3 | F2 | TODO |
| F9 | Memory / peripheral | mppib, mfiob, mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata | F2 | TODO |
| F10 | PMA extend (16 -> 48) | pmacfg4/6/8/10, pmaaddr16-47 | F2 | TODO |
| F11 | Triggers (guarded - shares Debug Module) | tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext | F2 | TODO |
| F12 | U-delta (M+U; deferred, premium is M-only) | uzobctl, umisc_ctl, sleepvalue, ucctlbeginaddr | F2 | TODO |
| F13 | Exclusion assertions + guard tighten + docs (USER_GUIDE) | (the 142 excluded) | F3-F12 | TODO |

## Risks / judgment calls already baked in

- **Side-effecting CSRs stay excluded even under "expand all"**: `pushmcause`,
  `pushmepc`, `pushmxstatus`, `mnxti`, `mscratchcsw`, `mscratchcswl`,
  `mcctlcommand`, `mintsel_jal` - reading/writing performs an action, so the value
  is not state. Documented per-CSR in the matrix.
- **Triggers (F11) touch the Debug Module** the handoff itself drives. Transported
  last, behind its own gate, with a fixture that checks the DM handshake still
  works.
- **Premium is M-only**: F12 (U-delta) ships in the ABI but cannot be round-trip
  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.

# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,
`mcctlcommand` issues a cache op) is an instruction in CSR clothing, not state.
Those are excluded **with a documented reason**, asserted by the guard - that is
how "nothing missed" is satisfied without 142 meaningless round-trips.

## Architecture

Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:

1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)
   iterates the list, so **adding a CSR is one line** and no consumer drifts.

2. **Capability-gated, not assumed.** Each new CSR maps to a feature gate in
   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.

3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks
   inventory <-> matrix <-> `state_abi.h` and **fails CI** on any drift: a CSR the
   spec adds, a CSR transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a promised CSR
   missing from the ABI. Refresh path: `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`
   (PDF -> inventory) then `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (inventory -> matrix).

## Per-feature definition of done

Each expansion feature (F3+) is ONE CSR block and must deliver all of:

- [ ] `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` X() line(s) in the ABI submodule (+ pin bump in andesim and vsim)
- [ ] QEMU plugin drains it (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`)
- [ ] `ResumeDriver` restores it (tolerant, capability-gated)
- [ ] `StateDrain` re-reads it
- [ ] `state_diff` verifies it (with the right exclusions, e.g. HW-driven latches)
- [ ] `andes_caps.hpp` gate entry + `classify_csr_coverage.py` stays in parity
- [ ] one per-section round-trip fixture under `tests/fixtures/`, run on premium
- [ ] guard test still green; ROADMAP state updated

Cross-repo note: the ABI lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned by BOTH
andesim and the external vsim. A block touches 3 repos (ABI + vsim consumers +
qemu_plugin), like the v3 Andes block did.

## Features

| ID | Feature | CSRs | Depends | State |
|----|---------|------|---------|-------|
| F1 | Completeness guard test | (none - foundation) | - | TODO |
| F2 | ABI scaffold: `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` + `hybrid_m_ext_csr` + `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT` + v4 + consumers iterate | (structural) | F1 | TODO |
| F3 | Machine Configuration | menvcfg, mseccfg | F2 | TODO |
| F4 | NMI handling | mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus, mnvec, mrnxvec | F2 | TODO |
| F5 | Counters / perf-monitor | mhpmcounter3-6, mhpmevent3-6, mcounteren, mcountinhibit, mcounterwen, mcounterinten, mcountermask_s, mcountermask_u | F2 | TODO |
| F6 | Andes trap-save | mdcause, mslideleg, msavestatus, msaveepc1/2, msavecause1/2, msavedcause1/2 | F2 | TODO |
| F7 | CLIC | mtvt, mintthresh, mirq_entry | F2 | TODO |
| F8 | State-enable | mstateen0-3 | F2 | TODO |
| F9 | Memory / peripheral | mppib, mfiob, mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata | F2 | TODO |
| F10 | PMA extend (16 -> 48) | pmacfg4/6/8/10, pmaaddr16-47 | F2 | TODO |
| F11 | Triggers (guarded - shares Debug Module) | tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext | F2 | TODO |
| F12 | U-delta (M+U; deferred, premium is M-only) | uzobctl, umisc_ctl, sleepvalue, ucctlbeginaddr | F2 | TODO |
| F13 | Exclusion assertions + guard tighten + docs (USER_GUIDE) | (the 142 excluded) | F3-F12 | TODO |

## Risks / judgment calls already baked in

- **Side-effecting CSRs stay excluded even under "expand all"**: `pushmcause`,
  `pushmepc`, `pushmxstatus`, `mnxti`, `mscratchcsw`, `mscratchcswl`,
  `mcctlcommand`, `mintsel_jal` - reading/writing performs an action, so the value
  is not state. Documented per-CSR in the matrix.
- **Triggers (F11) touch the Debug Module** the handoff itself drives. Transported
  last, behind its own gate, with a fixture that checks the DM handshake still
  works.
- **Premium is M-only**: F12 (U-delta) ships in the ABI but cannot be round-trip
  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Completeness guard for the Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage (the flywheel).

Cross-checks three artifacts and fails on any drift, so "nothing missed" is a
machine-checked invariant, not a hope:

  1. csr_inventory.csv  -- the spec snapshot (every CSR in the SPA Chapter 5)
  2. csr_coverage.csv   -- each CSR's transport disposition (the matrix)
  3. include/hybrid/state_abi.h -- what the wire format ACTUALLY transports

Checks (any failure exits non-zero):
  A. completeness  : matrix covers exactly the inventory's CSR set
  B. policy parity : re-running scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py reproduces the
                     committed matrix (offline policy == matrix)
  C. abi vs matrix : every CSR the ABI transports has a transport-disposition in
                     the matrix (never an excluded one), and every "carried
                     today" CSR is actually present in the ABI

NEW/NEW_TRIG/NEW_UDELTA CSRs not yet in the ABI are reported as PENDING (the
ROADMAP backlog), not failures -- the guard tightens automatically as each
expansion feature lands and the CSR appears in the ABI.

Usage: check_coverage.py [--abi PATH] [--quiet]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import classify_csr_coverage as policy  # noqa: E402

TRANSPORT = {"TRANSPORT_NOW", "NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"}

# Standard CSRs named as direct scalar fields in struct hybrid_state_v1.
STD_FIELDS = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mip", "mie", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr",
    "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl",
}
# Array groups: matrix rows whose name starts with one of these are transported
# as a block (pmpcfg[]/pmpaddr[]/pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] in the ABI).
ARRAY_PREFIX = ("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr", "pmacfg", "pmaaddr")
# V CSRs are transported but defined by the RVV spec, not this SPA -> not in the
# inventory; exclude them from the ABI<->matrix cross-check.
V_NAMES = {"vstart", "vtype", "vl", "vlenb", "vxsat", "vxrm", "vcsr", "vreg"}


def norm(name: str) -> str:
    """Canonical CSR name across representations (case, fi/fl ligatures, x/y)."""
    n = name.split("/")[0].strip().lower()
    return n.replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")


def abi_macro_csrs(abi_text: str) -> set:
    """Normalized names from every X(field, addr, "name") in a *_CSR_LIST macro."""
    out = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'X\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+\s*,\s*"[^"]*"\s*\)',
                         abi_text):
        out.add(norm(m.group(1)))
    return out


def load(path: Path) -> list:
    return list(csv.DictReader(path.open()))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--abi", default=str(ROOT / "include/hybrid/state_abi.h"))
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    inv = load(HERE / "csr_inventory.csv")
    cov = load(HERE / "csr_coverage.csv")
    abi = Path(args.abi).read_text()
    errs: list = []

    # A. completeness: matrix covers exactly the spec inventory.
    inv_addrs = [r["addr"] for r in inv]
    if sorted(r["addr"] for r in cov) != sorted(inv_addrs):
        errs.append("A: coverage CSR set != inventory CSR set")
    inv_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in inv}
    cov_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in cov}
    if inv_key != cov_key:
        miss = inv_key - cov_key
        extra = cov_key - inv_key
        errs.append(f"A: inventory/coverage row mismatch missing={miss} extra={extra}")

    # B. policy parity: classify(inventory) reproduces the committed matrix.
    for ir, cr in zip(inv, cov):
        got = policy.classify(ir["addr"], ir["priv"], ir["name"], ir["mode"],
                              ir["section"])
        if got != cr["decision"]:
            errs.append(f"B: {ir['name']} classify={got} matrix={cr['decision']}")

    # C. abi vs matrix.
    abi_names = abi_macro_csrs(abi) | {norm(n) for n in STD_FIELDS}
    cov_by_name = {norm(r["name"]): r["decision"] for r in cov}
    # forward: nothing the ABI transports may be an excluded CSR
    for an in sorted(abi_names):
        if an in V_NAMES:
            continue
        dec = cov_by_name.get(an)
        if dec is None:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but it is not in the matrix")
        elif dec not in TRANSPORT:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but matrix says {dec} (excluded)")
    # reverse: every carried-today CSR must be present in the ABI
    pending = []
    for r in cov:
        nn = norm(r["name"])
        pref = next((p for p in ARRAY_PREFIX if nn.startswith(p)), None)
        in_abi = (nn in abi_names) or (pref is not None and f"{pref}[" in abi)
        if r["decision"] == "TRANSPORT_NOW":
            if nn in V_NAMES:
                continue
            if not in_abi:
                errs.append(f"C: carried-today CSR '{r['name']}' missing from ABI")
        elif r["decision"] in TRANSPORT and not in_abi:
            pending.append(r["name"])

    if errs:
        print("CSR COVERAGE GUARD: FAIL", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errs:
            print("  - " + e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not args.quiet:
        print(f"CSR coverage guard OK: {len(inv)} CSRs classified, "
              f"matrix==policy, ABI transports only matrix-approved CSRs")
        if pending:
            print(f"  PENDING (ROADMAP backlog, not yet in ABI): "
                  f"{len(pending)} -> {', '.join(pending)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CSR coverage completeness guard (the "nothing missed" flywheel).
#
# Fails if the spec inventory snapshot, the coverage matrix, and the wire format
# (include/hybrid/state_abi.h) ever drift apart -- a CSR the spec adds, a CSR
# transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a carried-today CSR dropped from
# the ABI. See tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py for the exact checks and
# docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md for the disposition of every CSR.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "python3 required"

out=$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/check_coverage.py" 2>&1) || fail "coverage guard FAILED"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out"
ok "csr coverage guard: spec inventory == matrix == ABI (no drift)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

import socket, subprocess, time, re, sys, os

proc=subprocess.Popen([QEMU,"-M","virt","-cpu","andes-ax45mpv","-nographic",
    "-S","-gdb",f"tcp::{PORT}","-monitor","none","-serial","none"],
    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
def rsp_pkt(payload):
    csum=sum(payload.encode())&0xff
    return f"${payload}#{csum:02x}".encode()
def recv_pkt(s):
    buf=b""
    while b"#" not in buf or len(buf.split(b"#")[-1])<2:
        d=s.recv(4096)
        if not d: break
        buf+=d
    # strip ack '+'
    m=buf.find(b"$")
    e=buf.find(b"#",m)
    return buf[m+1:e].decode(errors="replace")
try:
    time.sleep(1.0)
    if proc.poll() is not None:
        print("QEMU exited early:", proc.stderr.read().decode()[:500]); sys.exit(1)
    s=socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1",PORT),timeout=5)
    s.sendall(b"+")
    # read the csr xml in chunks
    xml=""; off=0
    while True:
        s.sendall(rsp_pkt(f"qXfer:features:read:riscv-csr.xml:{off:x},1000"))
        time.sleep(0.05); pkt=recv_pkt(s); s.sendall(b"+")
        if not pkt: break
        kind,data=pkt[0],pkt[1:]
        # unescape RSP '}' escaping
        out=bytearray(); i=0; b=data.encode('latin1')
        while i<len(b):
            if b[i]==0x7d: out.append(b[i+1]^0x20); i+=2
            else: out.append(b[i]); i+=1
        xml+=out.decode('latin1')
        if kind=='l': break
        off+=0x1000
    names=re.findall(r'<reg name="([^"]+)"',xml)
    print("NUM_CSR_REGS",len(names))
    print(" ".join(names))
finally:
    proc.terminate()

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// The hardware feature that gates each Andes CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base Andes V5 machine CSR every core has; never gated off).
26	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
27	  ALWAYS = 0,
28	  DSP,
29	  CODENSE,
30	  POWERBRAKE,
31	  STACKSAFE,
32	  ECC,
33	  PMA,
34	  ILM,
35	  DLM,
36	  PERF_MONITOR,
37	};
38	
39	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
40	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
41	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
42	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
43	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
44	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
45	{
46	  switch (csr_addr) {
47	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
48	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
49	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // jvt   (Zcmt/CoDense)
50	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
51	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
52	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
53	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
54	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
55	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
56	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
57	    case 0x7D1: return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;   // mcountermask_m
58	    default:
59	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
60	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
61	        return AndesGate::PMA;
62	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
63	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
64	        return AndesGate::PMA;
65	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
66	  }
67	}
68	
69	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
70	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
71	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
72	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
73	struct AndesCaps {
74	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
75	
76	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
77	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
78	
79	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
80	  {
81	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
82	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
83	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
84	  }
85	
86	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
87	  {
88	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
89	  }
90	
91	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
92	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
93	  {
94	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
95	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
96	  }
97	};
98	
99	// The Andes scalar CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card.
100	// Iterates HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST (the single source of truth for the set).
101	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
102	{
103	  std::vector<std::string> out;
104	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
105	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
106	#undef X
107	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
108	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
109	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
110	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
111	  return out;
112	}
113	
114	}  // namespace hybrid
115	
116	#endif  // ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP

content.text:
Now the picture is unambiguous, and it changes your "premium only" choice in a way you could not have known up front.

## The constraint

vsim **premium is M-only** (priv=1). QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` models S+U+M, so it *exposes* CSRs (menvcfg, mcounteren, the U-delta block...) that **vsim premium does not implement**. Restoring a CSR vsim lacks can hang the DM. So on premium I can only round-trip-verify CSRs an **M-only core actually has**.

Mapping the 49 ADD targets against real engine capability:

| where it can be VERIFIED | count | examples |
|--------------------------|-------|----------|
| **premium (M-only)** can test | ~14 | mhpmcounter3-6, mhpmevent3-6, mcountinhibit, mcounterwen/inten, mdcause, mcctlbeginaddr/data |
| needs **d23 (M+U+S, priv=3)** | ~20 | menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_s/u, mslideleg, mstateen0-3, triggers (d23 has TRIGGER_NUM=2), uzobctl/umisc_ctl/sleepvalue/ucctlbeginaddr |
| **no built engine models it** | ~15 | mseccfg (ePMP), mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mrnxvec (Smrnmi), mtvt/mintthresh (CLIC - QEMU doesn't even expose), mppib/mfiob (PPI/FIO=0), pmacfg4-10/pmaaddr16-47 (premium has 4 PMA entries) |

**Premium-only verifies ~14 of 49.** The point of this work is *verification* ("驗證...正確支援交換state") - transporting 35 CSRs that no test can exercise is not verification, it is dead ABI.

`d23` (already built, M+U+S, priv=3, 2 triggers) lifts verified coverage to ~34/49. The last ~15 need a config that no built engine has - I transport them forward-looking and document them.

This is a real fork your earlier "premium only" answer could not anticipate, so I am surfacing it rather than building 35 untestable fields:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Completeness guard for the Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage (the flywheel).

Cross-checks three artifacts and fails on any drift, so "nothing missed" is a
machine-checked invariant, not a hope:

  1. csr_inventory.csv  -- the spec snapshot (every CSR in the SPA Chapter 5)
  2. csr_coverage.csv   -- each CSR's transport disposition (the matrix)
  3. include/hybrid/state_abi.h -- what the wire format ACTUALLY transports

Checks (any failure exits non-zero):
  A. completeness  : matrix covers exactly the inventory's CSR set
  B. policy parity : re-running scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py reproduces the
                     committed matrix (offline policy == matrix)
  C. abi vs matrix : every CSR the ABI transports has a transport-disposition in
                     the matrix (never an excluded one), and every "carried
                     today" CSR is actually present in the ABI

NEW/NEW_TRIG/NEW_UDELTA CSRs not yet in the ABI are reported as PENDING (the
ROADMAP backlog), not failures -- the guard tightens automatically as each
expansion feature lands and the CSR appears in the ABI.

Usage: check_coverage.py [--abi PATH] [--quiet]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import classify_csr_coverage as policy  # noqa: E402

TRANSPORT = {"TRANSPORT_NOW", "NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"}

# Standard CSRs named as direct scalar fields in struct hybrid_state_v1.
STD_FIELDS = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mip", "mie", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr",
    "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl",
}
# Array groups: matrix rows whose name starts with one of these are transported
# as a block (pmpcfg[]/pmpaddr[]/pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] in the ABI).
ARRAY_PREFIX = ("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr", "pmacfg", "pmaaddr")
# V CSRs are transported but defined by the RVV spec, not this SPA -> not in the
# inventory; exclude them from the ABI<->matrix cross-check.
V_NAMES = {"vstart", "vtype", "vl", "vlenb", "vxsat", "vxrm", "vcsr", "vreg"}
# CSRs carried inside a composite ABI field, not as their own field. fcsr packs
# frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], so both round-trip via the single fcsr field.
COMPOSITE = {"fflags": "fcsr", "frm": "fcsr"}


def norm(name: str) -> str:
    """Canonical CSR name across representations (case, fi/fl ligatures, x/y)."""
    n = name.split("/")[0].strip().lower()
    return n.replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")


def abi_macro_csrs(abi_text: str) -> set:
    """Normalized names from every X(field, addr, "name") in a *_CSR_LIST macro."""
    out = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'X\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+\s*,\s*"[^"]*"\s*\)',
                         abi_text):
        out.add(norm(m.group(1)))
    return out


def load(path: Path) -> list:
    return list(csv.DictReader(path.open()))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--abi", default=str(ROOT / "include/hybrid/state_abi.h"))
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    inv = load(HERE / "csr_inventory.csv")
    cov = load(HERE / "csr_coverage.csv")
    abi = Path(args.abi).read_text()
    errs: list = []

    # A. completeness: matrix covers exactly the spec inventory.
    inv_addrs = [r["addr"] for r in inv]
    if sorted(r["addr"] for r in cov) != sorted(inv_addrs):
        errs.append("A: coverage CSR set != inventory CSR set")
    inv_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in inv}
    cov_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in cov}
    if inv_key != cov_key:
        miss = inv_key - cov_key
        extra = cov_key - inv_key
        errs.append(f"A: inventory/coverage row mismatch missing={miss} extra={extra}")

    # B. policy parity: classify(inventory) reproduces the committed matrix.
    for ir, cr in zip(inv, cov):
        got = policy.classify(ir["addr"], ir["priv"], ir["name"], ir["mode"],
                              ir["section"])
        if got != cr["decision"]:
            errs.append(f"B: {ir['name']} classify={got} matrix={cr['decision']}")

    # C. abi vs matrix.
    abi_names = abi_macro_csrs(abi) | {norm(n) for n in STD_FIELDS}
    cov_by_name = {norm(r["name"]): r["decision"] for r in cov}
    # forward: nothing the ABI transports may be an excluded CSR
    for an in sorted(abi_names):
        if an in V_NAMES:
            continue
        dec = cov_by_name.get(an)
        if dec is None:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but it is not in the matrix")
        elif dec not in TRANSPORT:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but matrix says {dec} (excluded)")
    # reverse: every carried-today CSR must be present in the ABI
    pending = []
    for r in cov:
        nn = norm(r["name"])
        pref = next((p for p in ARRAY_PREFIX if nn.startswith(p)), None)
        in_abi = (nn in abi_names) or (pref is not None and f"{pref}[" in abi) \
            or (COMPOSITE.get(nn) in abi_names)
        if r["decision"] == "TRANSPORT_NOW":
            if nn in V_NAMES:
                continue
            if not in_abi:
                errs.append(f"C: carried-today CSR '{r['name']}' missing from ABI")
        elif r["decision"] in TRANSPORT and not in_abi:
            pending.append(r["name"])

    if errs:
        print("CSR COVERAGE GUARD: FAIL", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errs:
            print("  - " + e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not args.quiet:
        print(f"CSR coverage guard OK: {len(inv)} CSRs classified, "
              f"matrix==policy, ABI transports only matrix-approved CSRs")
        if pending:
            print(f"  PENDING (ROADMAP backlog, not yet in ABI): "
                  f"{len(pending)} -> {', '.join(pending)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Completeness guard for the Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage (the flywheel).

Cross-checks three artifacts and fails on any drift, so "nothing missed" is a
machine-checked invariant, not a hope:

  1. csr_inventory.csv  -- the spec snapshot (every CSR in the SPA Chapter 5)
  2. csr_coverage.csv   -- each CSR's transport disposition (the matrix)
  3. include/hybrid/state_abi.h -- what the wire format ACTUALLY transports

Checks (any failure exits non-zero):
  A. completeness  : matrix covers exactly the inventory's CSR set
  B. policy parity : re-running scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py reproduces the
                     committed matrix (offline policy == matrix)
  C. abi vs matrix : every CSR the ABI transports has a transport-disposition in
                     the matrix (never an excluded one), and every "carried
                     today" CSR is actually present in the ABI

NEW/NEW_TRIG/NEW_UDELTA CSRs not yet in the ABI are reported as PENDING (the
ROADMAP backlog), not failures -- the guard tightens automatically as each
expansion feature lands and the CSR appears in the ABI.

Usage: check_coverage.py [--abi PATH] [--quiet]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import classify_csr_coverage as policy  # noqa: E402

TRANSPORT = {"TRANSPORT_NOW", "NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"}

# Standard CSRs named as direct scalar fields in struct hybrid_state_v1.
STD_FIELDS = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mip", "mie", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr",
    "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl",
}
# Array groups: matrix rows whose name starts with one of these are transported
# as a block (pmpcfg[]/pmpaddr[]/pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] in the ABI).
ARRAY_PREFIX = ("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr", "pmacfg", "pmaaddr")
# V CSRs are transported but defined by the RVV spec, not this SPA -> not in the
# inventory; exclude them from the ABI<->matrix cross-check.
V_NAMES = {"vstart", "vtype", "vl", "vlenb", "vxsat", "vxrm", "vcsr", "vreg"}
# CSRs carried inside a composite ABI field, not as their own field. fcsr packs
# frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], so both round-trip via the single fcsr field.
COMPOSITE = {"fflags": "fcsr", "frm": "fcsr"}


def norm(name: str) -> str:
    """Canonical CSR name across representations (case, fi/fl ligatures)."""
    n = name.strip().lower()
    return n.replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")


# gdb/ABI name -> spec name, where the wire format uses a different mnemonic.
ABI_ALIAS = {"mcirq_entry": "mirq_entry"}


def matrix_keys(name: str) -> set:
    """All names a matrix row can be referenced by: each '/'-alternate, and each
    member of a 'prefixN~M' range (so the ABI's individual mhpmcounter3 matches
    the spec's mhpmcounter3~6 row)."""
    keys = set()
    for part in name.split("/"):
        part = part.strip()
        m = re.match(r"^(.*?)(\d+)~(\d+)$", part)
        if m:
            pre, a, b = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
            for i in range(a, b + 1):
                keys.add(norm(pre + str(i)))
        keys.add(norm(part))
    return keys


def abi_macro_csrs(abi_text: str) -> set:
    """Normalized names from every X(field, addr, "name") in a *_CSR_LIST macro."""
    out = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'X\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+\s*,\s*"[^"]*"\s*\)',
                         abi_text):
        out.add(norm(m.group(1)))
    return out


def load(path: Path) -> list:
    return list(csv.DictReader(path.open()))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--abi", default=str(ROOT / "include/hybrid/state_abi.h"))
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    inv = load(HERE / "csr_inventory.csv")
    cov = load(HERE / "csr_coverage.csv")
    abi = Path(args.abi).read_text()
    errs: list = []

    # A. completeness: matrix covers exactly the spec inventory.
    inv_addrs = [r["addr"] for r in inv]
    if sorted(r["addr"] for r in cov) != sorted(inv_addrs):
        errs.append("A: coverage CSR set != inventory CSR set")
    inv_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in inv}
    cov_key = {(r["addr"], r["name"]) for r in cov}
    if inv_key != cov_key:
        miss = inv_key - cov_key
        extra = cov_key - inv_key
        errs.append(f"A: inventory/coverage row mismatch missing={miss} extra={extra}")

    # B. policy parity: classify(inventory) reproduces the committed matrix.
    for ir, cr in zip(inv, cov):
        got = policy.classify(ir["addr"], ir["priv"], ir["name"], ir["mode"],
                              ir["section"])
        if got != cr["decision"]:
            errs.append(f"B: {ir['name']} classify={got} matrix={cr['decision']}")

    # C. abi vs matrix.
    abi_names = abi_macro_csrs(abi) | {norm(n) for n in STD_FIELDS}
    cov_by_name = {}
    for r in cov:
        for k in matrix_keys(r["name"]):
            cov_by_name[k] = r["decision"]
    # forward: nothing the ABI transports may be an excluded CSR
    for an in sorted(abi_names):
        if an in V_NAMES:
            continue
        dec = cov_by_name.get(ABI_ALIAS.get(an, an))
        if dec is None:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but it is not in the matrix")
        elif dec not in TRANSPORT:
            errs.append(f"C: ABI transports '{an}' but matrix says {dec} (excluded)")
    # reverse: every carried-today CSR must be present in the ABI
    pending = []
    for r in cov:
        nn = norm(r["name"])
        pref = next((p for p in ARRAY_PREFIX if nn.startswith(p)), None)
        in_abi = (nn in abi_names) or (pref is not None and f"{pref}[" in abi) \
            or (COMPOSITE.get(nn) in abi_names)
        if r["decision"] == "TRANSPORT_NOW":
            if nn in V_NAMES:
                continue
            if not in_abi:
                errs.append(f"C: carried-today CSR '{r['name']}' missing from ABI")
        elif r["decision"] in TRANSPORT and not in_abi:
            pending.append(r["name"])

    if errs:
        print("CSR COVERAGE GUARD: FAIL", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errs:
            print("  - " + e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not args.quiet:
        print(f"CSR coverage guard OK: {len(inv)} CSRs classified, "
              f"matrix==policy, ABI transports only matrix-approved CSRs")
        if pending:
            print(f"  PENDING (ROADMAP backlog, not yet in ABI): "
                  f"{len(pending)} -> {', '.join(pending)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.

The OFFLINE checker for the hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in Python, the C++ gate
logic the vsim engine compiles in (src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp +
andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine reports the same list via
`sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the andesim driver uses it to skip
--verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this on the engine's own build
config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the offline
config and the built engine (the flywheel; see tests/andes_sim/
test_andes_caps_parity.sh).

Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

Self-contained: the config.inc parser below is ported from Andes'
cpu_config_to_march_converter (parse_inc / is_yes / _int), so this depends only
on the Python stdlib.

Usage:
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# --- config.inc parsing (ported from cpu_config_to_march_converter) ----------
_DEFINE_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*`define\s+(\w+)(?:\s+(.+?))?\s*(?://\s*(.*))?$')


def parse_inc(path) -> dict:
    """{macro: string-value} from a Verilog config.inc (`define KEY VALUE)."""
    out: dict = {}
    for line in Path(path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = _DEFINE_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1)
        raw = (m.group(2) or "").strip().rstrip(",")
        comment = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        if not raw:                                   # bare `define NAME flag
            out.setdefault(name, "1")
            continue
        if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):  # quoted string
            out[name] = raw[1:-1]
            continue
        c = comment.strip().strip('"')                # numeric + // symbolic
        if c and " " not in c:
            out[name] = c
            try:
                int(raw, 0)
                out.setdefault(name + "_INT", raw)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            continue
        out[name] = raw                               # bare integer / token
    return out


def _str(cfg: dict, key: str) -> str:
    if key in cfg:
        return cfg[key].strip().strip('"')
    if key + "_INT" in cfg:
        return cfg[key + "_INT"].strip()
    return ""


def _int(cfg: dict, key: str):
    """Numeric view: prefer the _INT companion macro, else parse the value."""
    for k in (key + "_INT", key):
        if k in cfg:
            try:
                return int(cfg[k], 0)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return None


def is_yes(cfg: dict, key: str) -> bool:
    s = _str(cfg, key).lower()
    if s in ("yes", "true", "on"):
        return True
    if s in ("no", "false", "off", ""):
        return False
    n = _int(cfg, key)
    return n is not None and n == 1


# --- Andes-CSR capability derivation -----------------------------------------
def _ecc_any(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC (type != none)."""
    for blk in ("NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE",
                "NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE"):
        n = _int(cfg, blk)
        if n is not None and n > 0:
            return True
    return False


def gates(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    """Feature gates, mirroring andes_caps_from_config() in the vsim binary."""
    return {
        "DSP":          is_yes(cfg, "NDS_DSP_SUPPORT"),
        "CODENSE":      is_yes(cfg, "NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT"),
        "POWERBRAKE":   is_yes(cfg, "NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT"),
        "STACKSAFE":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT"),
        "PERF_MONITOR": is_yes(cfg, "NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR"),
        "PMA":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PMA_ENTRIES") or 0) > 0,
        "ILM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "DLM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "ECC":          _ecc_any(cfg),
        "ALWAYS":       True,
    }


# (csr name, gate) in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST order, then the PMA group markers --
# mirrors andes_caps.hpp andes_gate_for() + supported_andes_csr_names().
_CSR_GATES = [
    ("mxstatus",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("mpft_ctl",       "POWERBRAKE"),
    ("mclk_ctl",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("milmb",          "ILM"),
    ("mdlmb",          "DLM"),
    ("mecc_code",      "ECC"),
    ("mhsp_ctl",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_bound",      "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_base",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("mcountermask_m", "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("uitb",           "CODENSE"),
    ("jvt",            "CODENSE"),
    ("ucode",          "DSP"),
    ("pmacfg",         "PMA"),
    ("pmaaddr",        "PMA"),
]


def supported_andes_csrs(cfg: dict) -> list:
    g = gates(cfg)
    return [name for name, gate in _CSR_GATES if g[gate]]


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    if argv and argv[0] == "--check":
        if len(argv) < 2:
            print(__doc__)
            return 2
        got = supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[1]))
        want = argv[2:]
        if got != want:
            print(f"MISMATCH\n  got:  {got}\n  want: {want}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("OK: " + " ".join(got))
        return 0
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    print(" ".join(supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[0]))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"

"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \

  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \

  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"

  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"

---
name: premium-mext-csr-capability
description: "which writable M-mode CSRs the premium engine can actually verify in the hybrid handoff"
metadata:
  type: project
---

The v4 M-ext CSR transport (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`, 51 CSRs) is capability-gated.
On `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only, priv=1) only **17** are implemented and thus
round-trip-verifiable: the perf-counter set (mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6,
mhpmevent3-6, mcounterwen, mcounterinten), mdcause, and the 5 trigger CSRs
(tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext). Premium enables exactly these via
PERF_MONITOR + TRIGGER + ALWAYS gates; the other 34 are gated OFF (UMODE/SMODE/
EXCSLVL/SMRNMI/CLIC/SMSTATEEN/CCTL/PPI/FIO/EPMP all absent in its config.inc).

Key gotcha: QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` models full S+U+M and EXPOSES CSRs (menvcfg,
mcounteren, the U-delta block, mcctl*) that vsim premium does NOT implement.
QEMU-gdbstub-exposes != vsim-implements; restoring a CSR vsim lacks can stall the
DM. So capability is decided from vsim's config.inc (andes_caps_from_config), not
from what QEMU drains. `mhpmcounter3-6` are HW counters that increment during the
ROI, so they are transported+restored but verify-EXCLUDED (like mcycle/mip).

To dump an engine's real exposed CSR set, speak RSP qXfer:features:read:
riscv-csr.xml to its gdbstub. Related: [[andes-engine-config-source]].

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.

The OFFLINE checker for the hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in Python, the C++ gate
logic the vsim engine compiles in (src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp +
andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine reports the same list via
`sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the andesim driver uses it to skip
--verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this on the engine's own build
config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the offline
config and the built engine (the flywheel; see tests/andes_sim/
test_andes_caps_parity.sh).

Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

Self-contained: the config.inc parser below is ported from Andes'
cpu_config_to_march_converter (parse_inc / is_yes / _int), so this depends only
on the Python stdlib.

Usage:
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# --- config.inc parsing (ported from cpu_config_to_march_converter) ----------
_DEFINE_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*`define\s+(\w+)(?:\s+(.+?))?\s*(?://\s*(.*))?$')


def parse_inc(path) -> dict:
    """{macro: string-value} from a Verilog config.inc (`define KEY VALUE)."""
    out: dict = {}
    for line in Path(path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = _DEFINE_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1)
        raw = (m.group(2) or "").strip().rstrip(",")
        comment = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        if not raw:                                   # bare `define NAME flag
            out.setdefault(name, "1")
            continue
        if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):  # quoted string
            out[name] = raw[1:-1]
            continue
        c = comment.strip().strip('"')                # numeric + // symbolic
        if c and " " not in c:
            out[name] = c
            try:
                int(raw, 0)
                out.setdefault(name + "_INT", raw)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            continue
        out[name] = raw                               # bare integer / token
    return out


def _str(cfg: dict, key: str) -> str:
    if key in cfg:
        return cfg[key].strip().strip('"')
    if key + "_INT" in cfg:
        return cfg[key + "_INT"].strip()
    return ""


def _int(cfg: dict, key: str):
    """Numeric view: prefer the _INT companion macro, else parse the value."""
    for k in (key + "_INT", key):
        if k in cfg:
            try:
                return int(cfg[k], 0)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return None


def is_yes(cfg: dict, key: str) -> bool:
    s = _str(cfg, key).lower()
    if s in ("yes", "true", "on"):
        return True
    if s in ("no", "false", "off", ""):
        return False
    n = _int(cfg, key)
    return n is not None and n == 1


# --- Andes-CSR capability derivation -----------------------------------------
def _ecc_any(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC (type != none)."""
    for blk in ("NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE",
                "NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE"):
        n = _int(cfg, blk)
        if n is not None and n > 0:
            return True
    return False


def _any_yes(cfg: dict, *keys: str) -> bool:
    return any(is_yes(cfg, k) for k in keys)


def gates(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    """Feature gates, mirroring andes_caps_from_config() in the vsim binary."""
    priv = _int(cfg, "NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS") or 1   # 1=M, 2=M+U, 3=M+S+U
    return {
        "DSP":          is_yes(cfg, "NDS_DSP_SUPPORT"),
        "CODENSE":      is_yes(cfg, "NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT"),
        "POWERBRAKE":   is_yes(cfg, "NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT"),
        "STACKSAFE":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT"),
        "PERF_MONITOR": is_yes(cfg, "NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR"),
        "PMA":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PMA_ENTRIES") or 0) > 0,
        "ILM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "DLM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "ECC":          _ecc_any(cfg),
        "ALWAYS":       True,
        # v4 M-ext gates.
        "UMODE":        priv >= 2,
        "SMODE":        priv >= 3,
        "TRIGGER":      (_int(cfg, "NDS_NUM_TRIGGER") or 0) > 0,
        "EPMP":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMEPMP", "NDS_EPMP"),
        "SMRNMI":       _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMRNMI", "NDS_RNMI"),
        "EXCSLVL":      (_int(cfg, "NDS_EXCSLVL") or 0) > 0,
        "CLIC":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_ECLIC", "NDS_CLIC"),
        "SMSTATEEN":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMSTATEEN"),
        "CCTL":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_CCTLCSR", "NDS_CCTL"),
        "PPI":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "FIO":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0
                        or is_yes(cfg, "NDS_FIO"),
    }


# (csr name, gate) in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST order, then the PMA group markers --
# mirrors andes_caps.hpp andes_gate_for() + supported_andes_csr_names().
_CSR_GATES = [
    ("mxstatus",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("mpft_ctl",       "POWERBRAKE"),
    ("mclk_ctl",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("milmb",          "ILM"),
    ("mdlmb",          "DLM"),
    ("mecc_code",      "ECC"),
    ("mhsp_ctl",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_bound",      "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_base",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("mcountermask_m", "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("uitb",           "CODENSE"),
    ("jvt",            "CODENSE"),
    ("ucode",          "DSP"),
    ("pmacfg",         "PMA"),
    ("pmaaddr",        "PMA"),
    # v4 M-ext CSRs, in HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST order (gdb mnemonics, matching
    # supported_andes_csr_names which iterates that list after the Andes block).
    ("menvcfg",        "UMODE"),
    ("mseccfg",        "EPMP"),
    ("mcounteren",     "UMODE"),
    ("mcountinhibit",  "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter3",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter4",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter5",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter6",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent3",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent4",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent5",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent6",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mcounterwen",    "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mcounterinten",  "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mcountermask_s", "SMODE"),
    ("mcountermask_u", "UMODE"),
    ("mnscratch",      "SMRNMI"),
    ("mnepc",          "SMRNMI"),
    ("mncause",        "SMRNMI"),
    ("mnstatus",       "SMRNMI"),
    ("mnvec",          "SMRNMI"),
    ("mrnxvec",        "SMRNMI"),
    ("mdcause",        "ALWAYS"),
    ("mslideleg",      "SMODE"),
    ("msavestatus",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msaveepc1",      "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavecause1",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msaveepc2",      "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavecause2",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavedcause1",   "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavedcause2",   "EXCSLVL"),
    ("mtvt",           "CLIC"),
    ("mintthresh",     "CLIC"),
    ("mcirq_entry",    "CLIC"),
    ("mstateen0",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen1",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen2",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen3",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mcctlbeginaddr", "CCTL"),
    ("mcctldata",      "CCTL"),
    ("mppib",          "PPI"),
    ("mfiob",          "FIO"),
    ("tselect",        "TRIGGER"),
    ("tdata1",         "TRIGGER"),
    ("tdata2",         "TRIGGER"),
    ("tcontrol",       "TRIGGER"),
    ("mcontext",       "TRIGGER"),
    ("uzobctl",        "UMODE"),
    ("ucctlbeginaddr", "UMODE"),
    ("sleepvalue",     "UMODE"),
    ("umisc_ctl",      "UMODE"),
]


def supported_andes_csrs(cfg: dict) -> list:
    g = gates(cfg)
    return [name for name, gate in _CSR_GATES if g[gate]]


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    if argv and argv[0] == "--check":
        if len(argv) < 2:
            print(__doc__)
            return 2
        got = supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[1]))
        want = argv[2:]
        if got != want:
            print(f"MISMATCH\n  got:  {got}\n  want: {want}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("OK: " + " ".join(got))
        return 0
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    print(" ".join(supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[0]))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

**Predecessor.** `docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` (RESOLVED) added the v3
Andes block - 13 scalar CSRs + PMA - and the capability-gating flywheel. This
ROADMAP reuses that exact pattern (one X-macro list, capability-gated, parity
flywheel) to cover the remaining writable M-mode CSRs across the whole spec.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,
`mcctlcommand` issues a cache op) is an instruction in CSR clothing, not state.
Those are excluded **with a documented reason**, asserted by the guard - that is
how "nothing missed" is satisfied without 142 meaningless round-trips.

## Architecture

Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:

1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)
   iterates the list, so **adding a CSR is one line** and no consumer drifts.

2. **Capability-gated, not assumed.** Each new CSR maps to a feature gate in
   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.

3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks
   inventory <-> matrix <-> `state_abi.h` and **fails CI** on any drift: a CSR the
   spec adds, a CSR transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a promised CSR
   missing from the ABI. Refresh path: `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`
   (PDF -> inventory) then `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (inventory -> matrix).

## Per-feature definition of done

Each expansion feature (F3+) is ONE CSR block and must deliver all of:

- [ ] `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` X() line(s) in the ABI submodule (+ pin bump in andesim and vsim)
- [ ] QEMU plugin drains it (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`)
- [ ] `ResumeDriver` restores it (tolerant, capability-gated)
- [ ] `StateDrain` re-reads it
- [ ] `state_diff` verifies it (with the right exclusions, e.g. HW-driven latches)
- [ ] `andes_caps.hpp` gate entry + `classify_csr_coverage.py` stays in parity
- [ ] one per-section round-trip fixture under `tests/fixtures/`, run on premium
- [ ] guard test still green; ROADMAP state updated

Cross-repo note: the ABI lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned by BOTH
andesim and the external vsim. A block touches 3 repos (ABI + vsim consumers +
qemu_plugin), like the v3 Andes block did.

  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.
