#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md from the coverage CSV, in spec order.

Walks tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv in its committed row order -- which is the
AndeStar V5 SPA Chapter 5 table order (extract_csr_inventory.py reads the summary
tables top to bottom) -- and emits one row per CSR under its table + section
heading, so a human can review it side by side with the PDF without jumping
around. Regenerate after re-running classify_csr_coverage.py.

Usage: render_csr_matrix.py            # writes docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md
       render_csr_matrix.py --stdout   # print instead
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
COV = ROOT / "tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md"

# mode tag (set by the extractor per summary table) -> PDF table heading.
TABLE = {
    "M-std":   "Table 5 - RISC-V Standard Machine Mode CSRs",
    "M-andes": "Table 6 - AndeStar V5 Machine Mode CSRs",
    "D-std":   "Table 7 - AndeStar V5 Debug Mode CSRs",
    "S-std":   "Table 8 - RISC-V Standard Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "S-andes": "Table 9 - AndeStar V5 Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "U-std":   "Table 10 - RISC-V Standard User Mode CSRs",
    "U-andes": "Table 11 - AndeStar V5 User Mode CSRs",
    "H-std":   "Table 12 - RISC-V Standard Hypervisor Mode CSRs",
}

LABEL = {
    "TRANSPORT_NOW": "carried (pre-v4)",
    "NEW":           "ADD -> v4 m_ext",
    "NEW_TRIG":      "ADD -> v4 m_ext (trigger)",
    "NEW_UDELTA":    "ADD -> v4 m_ext (M+U)",
    "CONST_RO":      "excl: read-only config",
    "EXCL_RV32":     "excl: RV32-only",
    "EXCL_SIDEFX":   "excl: side-effecting",
    "EXCL_W1C_HW":   "excl: W1C / HW-driven",
    "EXCL_INDIRECT": "excl: indirect-access",
    "EXCL_NEXT":     "excl: N-ext trap",
    "EXCL_DEBUG":    "excl: debug-internal",
    "EXCL_MODE":     "excl: mode unsupported (S/H)",
    "EXCL_RO":       "excl: read-only",
    "EXCL_TRAP":     "excl: trap-cause latch",
}

HEADER = """# Andes CSR coverage matrix (spec-table order)

Every CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7` against the hybrid handoff, for the
supported envelope: **bare-metal, single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free
ROI**. Rows are in the PDF's Chapter 5 summary-table order (Table 5 -> 12,
sections top to bottom) so this reads side by side with the spec.

Generated by `scripts/render_csr_matrix.py` from
`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`; do not hand-edit. The guard
`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` fails CI if the spec inventory, this matrix's
data, and `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` ever drift apart.

## Dispositions

- **carried (pre-v4)** - already in `hybrid_state_v1` before this work.
- **ADD -> v4 m_ext** - landed as the v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` block,
  capability-gated (trigger/M+U variants noted). See
  `docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` for per-section verification status.
- **excl: ...** - correctly not transported; the reason is the qualifier
  (read-only config, RV32 shadow, side-effecting, S/H mode-unsupported,
  debug-internal, indirect-access, N-ext trap, trap-cause latch).

Counts: 41 carried + 49 ADD (landed v4) + 142 excluded = 232.

## Full matrix
"""


def main(argv):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(COV.open()))
    out = [HEADER]
    cur_mode = cur_sec = None
    for r in rows:
        if r["mode"] != cur_mode:
            cur_mode = r["mode"]
            cur_sec = None
            out.append(f"\n### {TABLE.get(cur_mode, cur_mode)}\n")
        if r["section"] != cur_sec:
            cur_sec = r["section"]
            out.append(f"\n**{cur_sec}**\n")
            out.append("| addr | name | priv | disposition |")
            out.append("|------|------|------|-------------|")
        out.append(f"| `{r['addr']}` | {r['name']} | {r['priv']} | "
                   f"{LABEL.get(r['decision'], r['decision'])} |")
    text = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
    if "--stdout" in argv:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    else:
        OUT.write_text(text)
        print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(rows)} CSRs, spec order)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

- **ADD -> v4 m_ext** - landed as the v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` block,
  capability-gated (trigger/M+U variants noted). See
  `docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` for per-section verification status.
- **excl: ...** - correctly not transported; the reason is the qualifier
  (read-only config, RV32 shadow, side-effecting, S/H mode-unsupported,
  debug-internal, indirect-access, N-ext trap, trap-cause latch).

Counts: 41 carried + 49 ADD (landed v4) + 142 excluded = 232.

## Full matrix
"""


def main(argv):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(COV.open()))
    out = [HEADER]
    cur_mode = cur_sec = None
    for r in rows:
        if r["mode"] != cur_mode:
            cur_mode = r["mode"]
            cur_sec = None
            out.append(f"\n### {TABLE.get(cur_mode, cur_mode)}\n")
        if r["section"] != cur_sec:
            cur_sec = r["section"]
            out.append(f"\n**{cur_sec}**\n")
            out.append("| addr | name | priv | disposition |")
            out.append("|------|------|------|-------------|")
        out.append(f"| `{r['addr']}` | {r['name']} | {r['priv']} | "
                   f"{LABEL.get(r['decision'], r['decision'])} |")
    text = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
    if "--stdout" in argv:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    else:
        OUT.write_text(text)
        print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(rows)} CSRs, spec order)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render docs/csr_coverage.ipynb from the coverage CSV, in spec-table order.

Walks tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv in committed row order -- the AndeStar V5
SPA Chapter 5 table order (extract_csr_inventory.py reads the summary tables top
to bottom) -- and emits a Jupyter notebook (markdown cells, one per PDF table) so
a human can review it side by side with the spec. Each CSR row carries its
transport disposition, a verification STATUS, and, for the verified ones, WHICH
test file proves it.

Regenerate after re-running classify_csr_coverage.py or changing the status map.

Usage: render_csr_matrix.py            # writes docs/csr_coverage.ipynb
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
COV = ROOT / "tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "docs/csr_coverage.ipynb"

TABLE = {
    "M-std":   "Table 5 - RISC-V Standard Machine Mode CSRs",
    "M-andes": "Table 6 - AndeStar V5 Machine Mode CSRs",
    "D-std":   "Table 7 - AndeStar V5 Debug Mode CSRs",
    "S-std":   "Table 8 - RISC-V Standard Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "S-andes": "Table 9 - AndeStar V5 Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "U-std":   "Table 10 - RISC-V Standard User Mode CSRs",
    "U-andes": "Table 11 - AndeStar V5 User Mode CSRs",
    "H-std":   "Table 12 - RISC-V Standard Hypervisor Mode CSRs",
}

DISPO = {
    "TRANSPORT_NOW": "carried (pre-v4)",
    "NEW": "ADD -> v4 m_ext", "NEW_TRIG": "ADD -> v4 m_ext (trigger)",
    "NEW_UDELTA": "ADD -> v4 m_ext (M+U)",
    "CONST_RO": "read-only config", "EXCL_RV32": "RV32-only",
    "EXCL_SIDEFX": "side-effecting", "EXCL_W1C_HW": "W1C / HW-driven",
    "EXCL_INDIRECT": "indirect-access", "EXCL_NEXT": "N-ext trap",
    "EXCL_DEBUG": "debug-internal", "EXCL_MODE": "mode unsupported (S/H)",
    "EXCL_RO": "read-only", "EXCL_TRAP": "trap-cause latch",
}

# Round-trip TESTED (in-ROI self-check): matrix row name -> test fixture.
TESTED = {
    "mscratch": "rt_csr_survival.S", "mepc": "rt_csr_survival.S",
    "mcause": "rt_csr_survival.S", "mtval": "rt_csr_survival.S",
    "mie": "rt_csr_survival.S", "fcsr": "rt_c_fcsr.c",
    "mcountinhibit": "rt_m_ext_counters.S", "mhpmevent3~6": "rt_m_ext_counters.S",
    "mcounterinten": "rt_m_ext_counters.S",
    "tselect": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S", "tdata2": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S",
    "mcontext": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S",
}
# Transported + restored but NOT strict-compared (engine-divergent / boot-static
# / measurement): matrix row name -> how it is exercised + why not compared.
TRANSPORTED = {
    "mhpmcounter3~6": "restored via rt_m_ext_counters.S; HW counter, --verify-excluded",
    "mdcause": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; vsim HW-set, --verify-excluded",
    "mcontrol/tdata1": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; trigger default differs, --verify-excluded",
    "tcontrol": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; trigger default differs, --verify-excluded",
    "mstatus": "passthrough (restored, not compared)",
    "mtvec": "passthrough (restored, not compared)",
    "mip": "restored, not compared (HW-driven pending bits)",
    "mcycle": "cycle measurement (not compared)",
    "minstret": "cycle measurement (not compared)",
    "medeleg": "drained, not restored (M-only engine)",
    "mideleg": "drained, not restored (M-only engine)",
    "satp": "drained, not restored (M-only engine; S-mode)",
    "mcache_ctl": "boot-static (restored, not re-drained)",
    "mmisc_ctl": "boot-static (restored, not re-drained)",
    "msp_bound": "Andes block; --verify-excluded (engine-reset-divergent)",
    "msp_base": "Andes block; --verify-excluded (engine-reset-divergent)",
}
ANDES9 = {"mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "mecc_code",
          "mhsp_ctl", "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "jvt", "ucode"}


def status(name: str, dec: str):
    """(status, note) for a CSR row."""
    n = name.lower().replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")
    if n in ("fflags", "frm"):
        return "tested", "rt_c_fcsr.c (packed in fcsr)"
    if name in TESTED:
        return "tested", TESTED[name]
    if name in TRANSPORTED:
        return "transported", TRANSPORTED[name]
    if dec == "TRANSPORT_NOW":
        if name.startswith(("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr")):
            return "carried", "M-mode PMP pass-through"
        if name.startswith(("pmacfg", "pmaaddr")):
            return "carried", "Andes PMA block, capability-gated"
        if name in ANDES9:
            return "carried", "Andes block, capability-gated (test_andes_caps_parity.sh)"
        return "carried", "transported via the handoff"
    if dec in ("NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"):
        return "forward-looking", "gated off on premium; pending a capable engine (e.g. d23 for M+U)"
    return "excluded", DISPO[dec]  # the reason


MARK = {"tested": "[x] tested", "transported": "[~] transported",
        "carried": "[x] carried", "forward-looking": "[ ] forward-looking",
        "excluded": "[-] excluded"}

INTRO = """# Andes V5 CSR hybrid-handoff coverage

Review sheet for **every CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`**, in the PDF's
Chapter 5 summary-table order (Table 5 -> 12, sections top to bottom) so it reads
side by side with the spec. Envelope: bare-metal, single-hart, M-mode or

"""Render docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md from the coverage CSV, in spec order.

around. Regenerate after re-running classify_csr_coverage.py.

Usage: render_csr_matrix.py            # writes docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md
       render_csr_matrix.py --stdout   # print instead
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
COV = ROOT / "tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "docs/csr_coverage_matrix.md"

# mode tag (set by the extractor per summary table) -> PDF table heading.
TABLE = {
    "M-std":   "Table 5 - RISC-V Standard Machine Mode CSRs",
    "M-andes": "Table 6 - AndeStar V5 Machine Mode CSRs",
    "D-std":   "Table 7 - AndeStar V5 Debug Mode CSRs",
    "S-std":   "Table 8 - RISC-V Standard Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "S-andes": "Table 9 - AndeStar V5 Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "U-std":   "Table 10 - RISC-V Standard User Mode CSRs",
    "U-andes": "Table 11 - AndeStar V5 User Mode CSRs",
    "H-std":   "Table 12 - RISC-V Standard Hypervisor Mode CSRs",
}

LABEL = {
    "TRANSPORT_NOW": "carried (pre-v4)",
    "NEW":           "ADD -> v4 m_ext",
    "NEW_TRIG":      "ADD -> v4 m_ext (trigger)",
    "NEW_UDELTA":    "ADD -> v4 m_ext (M+U)",
    "CONST_RO":      "excl: read-only config",
    "EXCL_RV32":     "excl: RV32-only",
    "EXCL_SIDEFX":   "excl: side-effecting",
    "EXCL_W1C_HW":   "excl: W1C / HW-driven",
    "EXCL_INDIRECT": "excl: indirect-access",
    "EXCL_NEXT":     "excl: N-ext trap",
    "EXCL_DEBUG":    "excl: debug-internal",
    "EXCL_MODE":     "excl: mode unsupported (S/H)",
    "EXCL_RO":       "excl: read-only",
    "EXCL_TRAP":     "excl: trap-cause latch",
}

HEADER = """# Andes CSR coverage matrix (spec-table order)

Every CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7` against the hybrid handoff, for the
supported envelope: **bare-metal, single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free
ROI**. Rows are in the PDF's Chapter 5 summary-table order (Table 5 -> 12,
sections top to bottom) so this reads side by side with the spec.

Generated by `scripts/render_csr_matrix.py` from
`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`; do not hand-edit. The guard
`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` fails CI if the spec inventory, this matrix's
data, and `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` ever drift apart.

## Dispositions

- **carried (pre-v4)** - already in `hybrid_state_v1` before this work.
- **ADD -> v4 m_ext** - landed as the v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` block,
  capability-gated (trigger/M+U variants noted). See
  `docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` for per-section verification status.
- **excl: ...** - correctly not transported; the reason is the qualifier
  (read-only config, RV32 shadow, side-effecting, S/H mode-unsupported,
  debug-internal, indirect-access, N-ext trap, trap-cause latch).

Counts: 41 carried + 49 ADD (landed v4) + 142 excluded = 232.

## Full matrix
"""


def main(argv):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(COV.open()))
    out = [HEADER]
    cur_mode = cur_sec = None
    for r in rows:
        if r["mode"] != cur_mode:
            cur_mode = r["mode"]
            cur_sec = None
            out.append(f"\n### {TABLE.get(cur_mode, cur_mode)}\n")
        if r["section"] != cur_sec:
            cur_sec = r["section"]
            out.append(f"\n**{cur_sec}**\n")
            out.append("| addr | name | priv | disposition |")
            out.append("|------|------|------|-------------|")
        out.append(f"| `{r['addr']}` | {r['name']} | {r['priv']} | "
                   f"{LABEL.get(r['decision'], r['decision'])} |")
    text = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
    if "--stdout" in argv:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    else:
        OUT.write_text(text)
        print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(rows)} CSRs, spec order)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

13	## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

15	The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
16	`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

25	read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
26	engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,

31	## Architecture
32	
33	Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:
34	
35	1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
36	   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
37	   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
38	   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)

40

42	   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
43	   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
44	   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
45	   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.
46	
47	3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
48	   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (marker or PC) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/archive/hybrid_plan.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT or PC)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andesim`
35	
36	`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
37	self-builds on first use). It drives `run` itself, orchestrating QEMU and
38	vsim directly; building is done by `scripts/build_all.sh` (which delegates to
39	`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`). Sections 1-7 document those underlying
40	scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
41	the driver.
42	
43	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
44	
45	```sh
46	bash scripts/build_all.sh                             # qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
47	./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
48	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
49	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
50	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # the hybrid e2e suite (or scripts/test_all.sh for unit+contract+e2e)
51	```
52	
53	Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:
54	
55	```
56	summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
57	```
58	
59	Subcommand cheat sheet:
60	
61	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
62	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
63	| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
64	| `bash scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]`               | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `plugin`, `fixtures`, `runtime` (qemu and vsim are external prebuilt binaries, not built here). |
65	| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
66	| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff and REQUIRES `--trigger marker|pc` to delimit the ROI; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
67	| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the hybrid e2e suite directly (qemu+vsim round-trips). |
68	| `bash scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit\|contract\|e2e]`     | Run the full test surface: C++ unit tests + driver contracts + the e2e suite. |
69	
70	Run `./andesim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
71	`ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal developer-only flags and the `list fixtures`
72	target). The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
73	underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andesim`
74	(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 1. Build and environment setup
79	
80	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
81	
82	Install these on the host once:
83	
84	| Package          | Notes                                                |
85	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
86	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
87	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
88	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
89	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
90	| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests                           |
91	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
92	| `pkg-config`     | plugin build (glib-2.0)                              |
93	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
94	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
95	| QEMU             | prebuilt external binary; set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (not built here) |
96	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
97	
98	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
99	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
100	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
101	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
102	
103	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
104	
105	```sh
106	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
107	cd hybrid_sim
108	```
109	
110	If you forgot `--recursive`:
111	
112	```sh
113	git submodule update --init --recursive
114	```
115	
116	Submodules under this repo:
117	
118	| Path             | What it is                                          |
119	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
120	| `include/`     | the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): `hybrid_state_v1` wire contract under `include/hybrid/` |
121	
122	vsim is no longer a submodule -- it is a prebuilt **external** binary, like QEMU.
123	Build it in your own vsim (`hybrid_vsim`) checkout and point `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
124	(`config.env`) at its `build/` dir; see 1.3.
125	
126	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
127	
128	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
129	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
130	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
131	
132	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
133	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
134	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
135	`config.env`:
136	
137	```sh
138	# config.env
139	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
140	```
141	
142	The variables today:
143	
144	| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
145	|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
146	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
147	| `QEMU_BIN_DIR`    | External prebuilt QEMU build dir holding `qemu-system-riscv64` (this repo no longer builds QEMU). |
148	| `VSIM_BIN_DIR`    | External prebuilt vsim build dir holding the `sim_*` binaries (this repo no longer builds vsim; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning it). |
149	
150	How it propagates:
151	
152	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
153	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
154	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
155	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
156	  the variable is missing.

Done. `docs/csr_coverage.ipynb` replaces the md.

## What you get

Open it in Jupyter or VS Code. It is **10 markdown cells in PDF order**:
- Intro + status legend
- Counts summary
- One cell per spec table: **Table 5 → 6 → 7 ... → 12**, sections top-to-bottom, matching the PDF so you can read side by side

Each CSR row has six columns: `addr | name | priv | disposition | status | test / note`. The status marks tell you done/not-done at a glance:

| mark | meaning | count |
|------|---------|-------|
| `[x] tested` | round-trip self-check; **test file named** (e.g. `rt_m_ext_counters.S`) | 14 |
| `[x] carried` | pre-v4 PMP/PMA/Andes block | 21 |
| `[~] transported` | restored but not strict-compared; note says why | 16 |
| `[ ] forward-looking` | in v4 ABI, gated off on premium; pending a capable engine | 39 |
| `[-] excluded` | correctly not transported; note = reason | 142 |

Example row (Counter section): `mcountinhibit` → `[x] tested` → `rt_m_ext_counters.S`; `mtvt` → `[ ] forward-looking` → `gated off on premium`.

## Regenerate

It is generated, not hand-edited:
```sh
python3 scripts/render_csr_matrix.py   # reads tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv
```
The status/test mapping lives at the top of that script - edit it there when a new test lands. Committed as `7c5a3e5`; the old `.md` is deleted and all references (USER_GUIDE, ROADMAP, guard) repoint to the notebook.

message.content: what does ' transported' mean?

content.text:
`transported` = the CSR **does cross the handoff** (QEMU drains it -> vsim restores it -> vsim drains it again), but its value is **deliberately not compared** by `--verify`, because the two engines legitimately hold different values.

Contrast with the neighbours:
- `tested` - restored **and** read back == what was written. Value proven correct (in-ROI self-check).
- `transported` - restored, but value **not checked** - comparing would false-fail because QEMU and vsim disagree by design.
- `forward-looking` - premium does **not** implement it, so it is gated off and never moved on this engine.

Why a value can't be compared (the note on each row says which applies):
- **counts during the ROI**: `mhpmcounter3-6` increment as code runs, so vsim (cycle) and QEMU (functional) diverge - same reason `mcycle`/`minstret` aren't compared.
- **hardware-set on one engine**: `mdcause` - vsim treats it as HW-written, so a software write drains back 0.
- **different reset defaults / WARL width**: `tdata1`, `tcontrol`, `mcontext` (trigger machinery differs between the two models).
- **passthrough / HW-driven**: `mstatus`, `mtvec` (both sides identical by construction), `mip` (timer bit), `msp_bound`/`msp_base`.

So `transported` is weaker than `tested` (we know it *moves*, we don't assert the *value*) but stronger than `forward-looking` (which doesn't move at all on premium). It's the same bucket as the long-standing `msp_bound`/`mip` handling.

| CSR | what really happens |

| `mstatus`, `mtvec` | **restored** into vsim, but value not compared because it is **passthrough** - vsim restores QEMU's entry snapshot and a trap-free ROI never changes it, so both sides are equal *by construction*. | `medeleg`, `mideleg` | **not restored at all**. They are S-mode delegation CSRs; the M-only premium engine has no S-mode, so QEMU *drains* them into the state file but vsim does **not** write them back. Only half the round-trip happens. |

So only `mie` is round-trip `tested` here; `misa` is excluded (read-only). My earlier "transported = can't compare" was an oversimplification - it doesn't fit either of these.

"""Render docs/csr_coverage.ipynb from the coverage CSV, in spec-table order.

inventory, the matrix data, and `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.

|--------|---------|---------------------------|

implementation WARL-fixes or hardwires them (e.g. `misa` is pinned to the ISA),
so there is no state to exchange.
"""


def md_cell(src: str) -> dict:
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {}, "source": src.splitlines(keepends=True)}


def main() -> int:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(COV.open()))
    cells = [md_cell(INTRO)]

    c = Counter(status(r["name"], r["decision"])[0] for r in rows)
    summ = ["## Counts\n\n", "| status | CSRs |\n", "|--------|------|\n"]
    for k in ("done", "blocked", "na"):
        summ.append(f"| {MARK[k]} | {c.get(k, 0)} |\n")
    summ.append(f"| **total** | **{len(rows)}** |\n")
    cells.append(md_cell("".join(summ)))

    buf: list = []

    def flush():
        if buf:
            cells.append(md_cell("".join(buf)))

    for r in rows:
        if r["mode"] != cur_mode:
            flush(); buf.clear()
            cur_mode, cur_sec = r["mode"], None
            buf.append(f"## {TABLE.get(cur_mode, cur_mode)}\n")
        if r["section"] != cur_sec:
            cur_sec = r["section"]
            buf.append(f"\n### {cur_sec}\n\n")
            buf.append("| addr | name | priv | status | detail (test / missing / why) |\n")
            buf.append("|------|------|------|--------|-------------------------------|\n")
        st, detail = status(r["name"], r["decision"])
        buf.append(f"| `{r['addr']}` | {r['name']} | {r['priv']} | {MARK[st]} | {detail} |\n")
    flush()

    nb = {
        "cells": cells,
        "metadata": {
            "kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3", "language": "python",
                           "name": "python3"},
            "language_info": {"name": "python"},
        },
        "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 5,
    }
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(nb, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(rows)} CSRs; "
          + ", ".join(f"{k}={c.get(k, 0)}" for k in ('done', 'blocked', 'na')) + ")")
    return 0

    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render docs/csr_coverage.ipynb from the coverage CSV, in spec-table order.

Walks tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv in committed row order -- the AndeStar V5
SPA Chapter 5 table order (extract_csr_inventory.py reads the summary tables top
to bottom) -- and emits a Jupyter notebook (markdown cells, one per PDF table) so
a human can review it side by side with the spec. Each CSR row carries its
transport disposition, a verification STATUS, and, for the verified ones, WHICH
test file proves it.

Regenerate after re-running classify_csr_coverage.py or changing the status map.

Usage: render_csr_matrix.py            # writes docs/csr_coverage.ipynb
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
COV = ROOT / "tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "docs/csr_coverage.ipynb"

TABLE = {
    "M-std":   "Table 5 - RISC-V Standard Machine Mode CSRs",
    "M-andes": "Table 6 - AndeStar V5 Machine Mode CSRs",
    "D-std":   "Table 7 - AndeStar V5 Debug Mode CSRs",
    "S-std":   "Table 8 - RISC-V Standard Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "S-andes": "Table 9 - AndeStar V5 Supervisor Mode CSRs",
    "U-std":   "Table 10 - RISC-V Standard User Mode CSRs",
    "U-andes": "Table 11 - AndeStar V5 User Mode CSRs",
    "H-std":   "Table 12 - RISC-V Standard Hypervisor Mode CSRs",
}

DISPO = {
    "TRANSPORT_NOW": "carried (pre-v4)",
    "NEW": "ADD -> v4 m_ext", "NEW_TRIG": "ADD -> v4 m_ext (trigger)",
    "NEW_UDELTA": "ADD -> v4 m_ext (M+U)",
    "CONST_RO": "constant (RO/WARL)", "EXCL_RV32": "RV32-only",
    "EXCL_SIDEFX": "side-effecting", "EXCL_W1C_HW": "W1C / HW-driven",
    "EXCL_INDIRECT": "indirect-access", "EXCL_NEXT": "N-ext trap",
    "EXCL_DEBUG": "debug-internal", "EXCL_MODE": "mode unsupported (S/H)",
    "EXCL_RO": "read-only", "EXCL_TRAP": "trap-cause latch",
}

# Round-trip TESTED (in-ROI self-check): matrix row name -> test fixture.
TESTED = {
    "mscratch": "rt_csr_survival.S", "mepc": "rt_csr_survival.S",
    "mcause": "rt_csr_survival.S", "mtval": "rt_csr_survival.S",
    "mie": "rt_csr_survival.S", "fcsr": "rt_c_fcsr.c",
    "mcountinhibit": "rt_m_ext_counters.S", "mhpmevent3~6": "rt_m_ext_counters.S",
    "mcounterinten": "rt_m_ext_counters.S",
    "tselect": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S", "tdata2": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S",
    "mcontext": "rt_m_ext_trigcause.S",
}
# Transported + restored but NOT strict-compared (engine-divergent / boot-static
# / measurement): matrix row name -> how it is exercised + why not compared.
TRANSPORTED = {
    "mhpmcounter3~6": "restored via rt_m_ext_counters.S; HW counter, --verify-excluded",
    "mdcause": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; vsim HW-set, --verify-excluded",
    "mcontrol/tdata1": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; trigger default differs, --verify-excluded",
    "tcontrol": "restored via rt_m_ext_trigcause.S; trigger default differs, --verify-excluded",
    "mstatus": "passthrough: both sides equal by construction (compare adds nothing)",
    "mtvec": "passthrough: both sides equal by construction (compare adds nothing)",
    "mip": "engine-divergent: HW-driven pending bits (timer)",
    "mcycle": "engine-divergent: cycle measurement (counts differently by design)",
    "minstret": "engine-divergent: instret measurement (counts differently by design)",
    "mcache_ctl": "boot-static: restored, not re-drained",
    "mmisc_ctl": "boot-static: restored, not re-drained",
    "msp_bound": "engine-divergent: reset value differs (Andes block)",
    "msp_base": "engine-divergent: reset value differs (Andes block)",
}
ANDES9 = {"mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "mecc_code",
          "mhsp_ctl", "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "jvt", "ucode"}

# Drained by QEMU but NOT restored into vsim: S-mode CSRs the M-only premium
# engine does not implement, so only half the round-trip happens.
DRAINED_ONLY = {"medeleg", "mideleg", "satp"}

# Per-CSR note where the bucket disposition is imprecise -- an MRW CSR that is
# WARL-fixed / hardwired, so it behaves constant despite being writable.
NOTE_OVERRIDE = {
    "misa": "MRW but WARL-fixed to the engine's ISA; each engine derives it, nothing to exchange",
    "tdata3": "MRW but hardwired to 0 (spec: always return 0)",
    "tinfo": "MRW but a read-only trigger-info register",
}


def status(name: str, dec: str):
    """(status, note) for a CSR row."""
    n = name.lower().replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")
    if n in ("fflags", "frm"):
        return "tested", "rt_c_fcsr.c (packed in fcsr)"
    if name in TESTED:
        return "tested", TESTED[name]
    if name in DRAINED_ONLY:
        return "drained-only", ("QEMU drains it into the state file; vsim (M-only) "
                                "does not restore this S-mode CSR")
    if name in TRANSPORTED:
        return "novalue", TRANSPORTED[name]
    if dec == "TRANSPORT_NOW":
        if name.startswith(("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr")):
            return "carried", "M-mode PMP pass-through"
        if name.startswith(("pmacfg", "pmaaddr")):
            return "carried", "Andes PMA block, capability-gated"
        if name in ANDES9:
            return "carried", "Andes block, capability-gated (test_andes_caps_parity.sh)"
        return "carried", "transported via the handoff"
    if dec in ("NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"):
        return "forward-looking", "gated off on premium; pending a capable engine (e.g. d23 for M+U)"
    return "excluded", NOTE_OVERRIDE.get(name, DISPO[dec])  # the reason


MARK = {"tested": "[x] tested", "carried": "[x] carried",
        "novalue": "[~] restored, not compared",
        "drained-only": "[!] drained only (not restored)",
        "forward-looking": "[ ] forward-looking",
        "excluded": "[-] excluded"}

INTRO = """# Andes V5 CSR hybrid-handoff coverage

Review sheet for **every CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`**, in the PDF's
Chapter 5 summary-table order (Table 5 -> 12, sections top to bottom) so it reads
side by side with the spec. Envelope: bare-metal, single-hart, M-mode or
M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

Auto-generated by `scripts/render_csr_matrix.py` from
`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`; do not hand-edit. The guard
`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` fails CI if the spec inventory, the matrix
data, and `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` ever drift apart.

## Status legend

| mark | meaning |
|------|---------|
| `[x] tested` | restored into vsim **and** the value is verified (in-ROI self-check); test file named |
| `[x] carried` | transported before v4 (PMP/PMA/Andes block); proven by the handoff suite |
| `[~] restored, not compared` | restored into vsim, but the value is **not** `--verify`-compared. Either **passthrough** (both sides equal by construction, so a compare adds nothing) or **engine-divergent** (a counter, HW-set value, or differing reset default) -- the note says which |
| `[!] drained only (not restored)` | QEMU records it in the state file, but vsim does **not** restore it (S-mode CSRs on the M-only engine). Only half the round-trip happens |
| `[ ] forward-looking` | in the v4 ABI but gated **off** on the premium (M-only) engine; round-trip pending a capable engine |
| `[-] excluded` | correctly **not** transported; the note is the reason |

Note: a CSR's `priv` (e.g. MRW) is the spec's architectural read/write class.
Some MRW CSRs are still `constant (RO/WARL)` here because the implementation
WARL-fixes or hardwires them (e.g. `misa` is pinned to the engine's ISA), so
there is no state to exchange.

Done so far: the v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` block (51 CSRs) is transported and
capability-gated. On `ax45mpv_premium` the perf-monitor + trigger + mdcause CSRs
are gated on (tested / restored); the rest ride forward-looking.
"""


def md_cell(src: str) -> dict:
    lines = src.splitlines(keepends=True)
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {}, "source": lines}


def main() -> int:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(COV.open()))
    cells = [md_cell(INTRO)]

    # summary counts
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter(status(r["name"], r["decision"])[0] for r in rows)
    summ = ["## Counts\n\n", "| status | CSRs |\n", "|--------|------|\n"]
    for k in ("tested", "carried", "transported", "forward-looking", "excluded"):
        summ.append(f"| {MARK[k]} | {c.get(k, 0)} |\n")
    summ.append(f"| **total** | **{len(rows)}** |\n")
    cells.append(md_cell("".join(summ)))

    # one cell per table, sections in order
    cur_mode = None
    buf: list = []

    def flush():
        if buf:
            cells.append(md_cell("".join(buf)))

    cur_sec = None
    for r in rows:
        if r["mode"] != cur_mode:
            flush(); buf.clear()
            cur_mode = r["mode"]; cur_sec = None
            buf.append(f"## {TABLE.get(cur_mode, cur_mode)}\n")
        if r["section"] != cur_sec:
            cur_sec = r["section"]
            buf.append(f"\n### {cur_sec}\n\n")
            buf.append("| addr | name | priv | disposition | status | test / note |\n")
            buf.append("|------|------|------|-------------|--------|-------------|\n")
        st, note = status(r["name"], r["decision"])
        buf.append(f"| `{r['addr']}` | {r['name']} | {r['priv']} | "
                   f"{DISPO[r['decision']]} | {MARK[st]} | {note} |\n")
    flush()

    nb = {
        "cells": cells,
        "metadata": {
            "kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3", "language": "python",
                           "name": "python3"},
            "language_info": {"name": "python"},
        },
        "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 5,
    }
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(nb, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(rows)} CSRs, {len(cells)} cells, spec order)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

CONTEXT. The Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator hands off architectural state from QEMU (functional) to vsim (cycle-accurate) across a region of interest (ROI). Every CSR in the AndeStar V5 SPA is classified into THREE buckets, for the supported envelope: bare-metal, single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

THE THREE BUCKETS:
- done   : the handoff transports it AND the current engine (ax45mpv_premium) implements it, so it is restored into vsim now.
- blocked: it is IN SCOPE (M-mode state, or U-mode state since we support M+U) and we WANT to transport it, but premium's config lacks the needed mode/extension, so it can't be exercised yet (would work on a different engine). Name what is missing.
- na     : we do NOT transport it, by design. Either (a) OUTSIDE the envelope: needs S-mode or Hypervisor - INCLUDING M-mode registers whose function requires S-mode (medeleg, mideleg, mcountermask_s, mslideleg) and S paging (satp); or (b) NOT transportable state: read-only (MRO/URO) config/info, OR MRW-but-WARL-fixed/hardwired (misa pinned to ISA, tdata3 always-0, tinfo read-only info), RV32-only high-half shadow on this RV64 core, side-effecting/instruction-like (pushmcause/pushmepc/pushmxstatus, mnxti, mscratchcsw/mscratchcswl, mcctlcommand, mintsel_jal, wfe, txevt, ucctlcommand), indirect-access mechanism (miselect/mireg*), debug-mode-internal (dcsr/dpc/dscratch0/dscratch1/dexc2dbg/ddcause), write-1-clear/HW-driven status (mcounterovf), N-extension user trap state (ustatus/uie/utvec/uscratch/uepc/ucause/utval/uip), or a trap-cause latch (udcause).

GROUND TRUTH - engine ax45mpv_premium (M-only, priv=1, RV64GCV):
IMPLEMENTS (handoff transports + gate ON) these custom/Andes/ext CSRs:
  mxstatus, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, pmacfg0, pmacfg2, pmaaddr0..3,
  mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3, mhpmcounter4, mhpmcounter5, mhpmcounter6,
  mhpmevent3, mhpmevent4, mhpmevent5, mhpmevent6, mcounterinten, mdcause,
  tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
ALSO always transports this standard M-mode state: mstatus, mie, mtvec, mepc, mcause, mtval, mscratch, mip, mcycle, minstret, fcsr (frm/fflags), pmpcfg0..15, pmpaddr0..63 (M-mode pass-through), mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl.
LACKS (feature OFF, so those CSRs are gated off / absent on premium):
  - privilege: U-mode, S-mode, Hypervisor (priv=1)

1. Needs S-mode/Hypervisor (incl. medeleg, mideleg, mcountermask_s, mslideleg, satp) -> na.
2. Read-only/WARL-fixed/hardwired (MRO/URO config & info; misa, tdata3, tinfo) -> na.

4. Side-effecting/instruction-like -> na (list above).
5. Indirect-access (miselect/mireg*) -> na.
6. Debug-mode-internal -> na.
7. W1C/HW-driven status (mcounterovf) -> na. N-ext user trap CSRs -> na. udcause -> na.
8. Otherwise transportable M/U state:
   - premium IMPLEMENTS it (ground truth) -> done.
   - premium LACKS the mode/extension -> blocked (name what is missing: "U-mode", "POWERBRAKE", "ECC", "STACKSAFE", "DSP", "CLIC", "Smrnmi", "Smstateen", "ePMP", "CCTL", "PPI", "FIO", "exception save-levels").

## Disagreements (all the same class of error)

All six are Andes CSRs the audited file marked `done`, but the stated ground truth explicitly lists them under LACKS (the feature is OFF on `ax45mpv_premium`), so by the decision order they are in-scope M/U state whose feature is missing -> `blocked`:

- `0x7C8 msp_base`: done -> blocked (premium lacks STACKSAFE)
- `0x801 ucode`: done -> blocked (premium lacks DSP)

## Root cause / pattern

The audited file appears to have classified the entire Andes v3 transport block as `done`, but the prompt's ground truth IMPLEMENTS list omits these six and instead names them in LACKS (`POWERBRAKE -> mpft_ctl`, `ECC -> mecc_code`, `STACKSAFE -> mhsp_ctl/msp_bound/msp_base`, `DSP -> ucode`). Premium is RV64GCV with those Andes features off, so they cannot be exercised yet -> `blocked`. Fair challenge - let me answer it directly, because the wording made it look wrong.

`medeleg` **is** physically an M-mode CSR (you access it from M-mode). But:

1. **It exists only if the core implements S-mode.** Per the AndeStar existence table: `medeleg` exists iff `misa[18]` (S) or `misa[13]` (N-ext user traps). message.content: 所以  blocked statu 目前是有沒有drain and restore? 還是只是沒有驗證而已 缺少engine

content.text:
Good, precise question. **Blocked is more than "unverified" - on premium the CSR is NOT restored into vsim and NOT re-read from it.** The capability gate skips it entirely.

Mechanically, per the code (`ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` both wrap each CSR in `if (caps_.supports_csr(addr))`):

| bucket | QEMU drains it? | vsim **restores** it? | vsim **re-drains** it? | `--verify` compares? |
|--------|----------------|----------------------|------------------------|----------------------|
| **done** | yes | **yes** | **yes** | yes |
| **done (value not compared)** | yes | **yes** | **yes** | no (engine-divergent / counter) |
| **blocked** | maybe* | **NO** | **NO** | no |

\* QEMU may still drain it into the state file if its CPU model exposes it (e.g. `menvcfg`), but that value is **never applied** to the cycle engine.

So for a **blocked** CSR on premium:
- The transport **code** is already there - it's in the v4 ABI and the same generic X-macro loop as every other CSR.
- But `caps_.supports_csr(addr)` returns **false** (premium's config has the feature off), so the DMI write (restore) and the DMI read (re-drain) are **skipped**. Not "done and unchecked" - **not done on the vsim side at all**.
- Why skipped and not just unchecked: restoring a CSR the RTL doesn't implement **hangs the Debug Module** handshake (the original bug the capability gate was built to prevent).

The "missing engine" part: it is **only** the per-engine gate that's off. Point the same code at an engine whose `config.inc` has that feature on (U-mode, CLIC, Smrnmi, ...) and it restores + re-reads + verifies the CSR with **zero code change**. That's the whole meaning of `blocked` = "wired, but this engine can't, another engine can".

Contrast: **`done (value not compared)`** (e.g. `mhpmcounter3-6`, `mdcause`) really IS drained + restored + re-drained - only the final value *comparison* is skipped because the two engines legitimately differ.

message.content: 可是我們之前不是就在討論 根據core config 決定哪些要drain and restore? 為什麼沒有 blocked state, QEMU 還會drain?

content.text:
Sharp catch. The resolution is that there are **three** state operations, not two, and "drain" means different things:

| # | operation | direction | config-gated? |
|---|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | **QEMU plugin drain** (producer) | QEMU -> state file | **NO** - gated by what *QEMU* exposes |
| 2 | **ResumeDriver restore** | state file -> vsim | **YES** - vsim caps |
| 3 | **StateDrain** (cycle-engine drain) | vsim -> state file | **YES** - vsim caps |

When we discussed "根據 config 決定要 drain and restore," that was **#2 and #3 - the vsim side**. Both DO skip blocked CSRs. The capability gate lives in vsim (`ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain`), keyed by **vsim's** `config.inc`, because that's where it must be: restoring a CSR vsim's RTL lacks hangs the Debug Module. So for a blocked CSR, #2 and #3 are skipped - exactly the config-based decision.

**#1 (the QEMU drain) is a different thing.** It's the producer, running *inside QEMU*, and it drains whatever QEMU's gdbstub exposes - a **superset**. It is NOT gated by vsim's config, on purpose:

- The plugin runs in QEMU and doesn't know the target vsim engine (the engine is chosen at runtime by the orchestrator, a separate process).
- QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` models S+U+M, so it *does* expose `menvcfg`, `mcounteren`, etc. - vsim premium does not implement them. That model mismatch is why QEMU drains things vsim won't take.
- Draining extra is **harmless**: read-only from QEMU's side (no DM, no hang), and vsim simply never restores them. Verify also skips them (not in vsim's `--describe` list). The values just sit unused in the file.
- Bonus: it keeps the state file **engine-agnostic** - the same drained file could resume on any vsim engine, each taking its own subset.

So nothing is inconsistent: the config decision is fully applied where it matters (vsim restore + vsim drain). The QEMU producer drain is intentionally a wider net.

**Your instinct is still valid though** - we *could* also gate #1 by passing vsim's supported-CSR list (we already compute it for `--verify`) into the plugin, so QEMU only drains what this engine will use. That would shrink the file and make #1 match #2/#3 conceptually. It's a cleanup, not a correctness fix, and the cost is tying each drained file to one engine. Want me to wire that?

content.text:
Let me use a simple picture.

Think of the handoff like **mailing a box** from QEMU to vsim.

- **QEMU = packs the box.** It throws in **every** CSR it has. It does not look at vsim's config - it just packs everything. (This is the "QEMU drain" you asked about.)
- **vsim = opens the box.** It only takes out the CSRs **its own config says it has**. Anything it doesn't have, it **leaves in the box, untouched**.

A **blocked** CSR = vsim opens the box, sees that CSR, but its config says *"I don't have this"* -> it **does not take it out** (does not restore, does not read it back).

So:
- "**decide by config**" = the rule lives on **vsim's side** - vsim deciding what to **take out**.
- QEMU still **packed** it because QEMU packs everything; that's harmless - vsim just ignores it.

Why the rule must be on vsim's side, not QEMU's: if **vsim** tries to take out a CSR it doesn't really have, **the machine freezes** (the hang we kept hitting). So vsim must check its config before touching each one. QEMU only *writes a file* - that can never freeze anything, so QEMU doesn't need to check.

**Blocked = vsim left it in the box.** The value may sit in the file (QEMU put it there), but vsim never used it.

content.text:
Continuing the box picture: right now QEMU packs everything. We want to **hand QEMU the receiver's shopping list first**, so it only packs those.

We already have that list. Before every run we ask vsim `--describe`, and it returns `andes_csrs` = exactly the CSRs it implements (we already use this for `--verify`). So no new source of truth - just give that same list to QEMU's plugin.

## The plan (3 small changes)

1. **Plugin** gains one optional arg, e.g. `csrs=mxstatus:mclk_ctl:mcountinhibit:...`. When present, it drains only the custom/Andes/m_ext CSRs in that set; the standard M-mode ones (mstatus, mie, mtvec, ...) are always packed because every engine has them.
2. **Orchestrator** (the `andesim` driver + `tests/e2e.sh`): read `andes_csrs` from `--describe`, format it as that `csrs=` arg, pass it on the `-plugin` line.
3. **No arg given -> pack everything** (today's behavior). Back-compatible; the filter is opt-in.

## Why it's safe

The list comes from `--describe`, which vsim derives from the **same `config.inc`** as its restore gate. The flywheel test already proves `--describe == offline deriver == vsim caps`, byte-for-byte. So:

> QEMU's "pack list" == vsim's "unpack list", by construction. They cannot disagree.

## What you gain / give up

- **Gain:** smaller state file (only useful CSRs); the `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT/ANDES` flag is set only when a *supported* CSR is packed (cleaner); producer and consumer now follow one config decision - which is the consistency you were asking about.
- **Give up:** the state file becomes tied to that one engine (you couldn't replay it on a different vsim). For a hybrid run (QEMU -> one chosen vsim) that costs nothing.

## One decision for you

The filter only touches the **custom/Andes/m_ext** CSRs (the gated ones). Two ways to match the plugin list against vsim's:

- **A. by name** (what `--describe` already emits, e.g. `mcirq_entry`) - simplest, zero new plumbing.
- **B. by address** - matches vsim's gate (which keys on address) more directly, but the plugin would need an addr list and the driver would have to map names->addrs.

I'd pick **A** (names) - it reuses the exact string `--describe` returns. 

Want me to build it (plugin filter + orchestrator passing the list + a contract test that the packed set == `--describe`)? It's TDD-able: a test that drains with a filter and asserts the un-listed CSR fields are 0.

# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

**Predecessor.** `docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` (RESOLVED) added the v3
Andes block - 13 scalar CSRs + PMA - and the capability-gating flywheel. This
ROADMAP reuses that exact pattern (one X-macro list, capability-gated, parity
flywheel) to cover the remaining writable M-mode CSRs across the whole spec.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,
`mcctlcommand` issues a cache op) is an instruction in CSR clothing, not state.
Those are excluded **with a documented reason**, asserted by the guard - that is
how "nothing missed" is satisfied without 142 meaningless round-trips.

## Architecture

Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:

1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)
   iterates the list, so **adding a CSR is one line** and no consumer drifts.

2. **Capability-gated, not assumed.** Each new CSR maps to a feature gate in
   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.

3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks
   inventory <-> matrix <-> `state_abi.h` and **fails CI** on any drift: a CSR the
   spec adds, a CSR transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a promised CSR
   missing from the ABI. Refresh path: `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`
   (PDF -> inventory) then `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (inventory -> matrix).

## Per-feature definition of done

Each expansion feature (F3+) is ONE CSR block and must deliver all of:

- [ ] `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` X() line(s) in the ABI submodule (+ pin bump in andesim and vsim)
- [ ] QEMU plugin drains it (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`)
- [ ] `ResumeDriver` restores it (tolerant, capability-gated)
- [ ] `StateDrain` re-reads it
- [ ] `state_diff` verifies it (with the right exclusions, e.g. HW-driven latches)
- [ ] `andes_caps.hpp` gate entry + `classify_csr_coverage.py` stays in parity
- [ ] one per-section round-trip fixture under `tests/fixtures/`, run on premium
- [ ] guard test still green; ROADMAP state updated

Cross-repo note: the ABI lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned by BOTH
andesim and the external vsim. A block touches 3 repos (ABI + vsim consumers +
qemu_plugin), like the v3 Andes block did.

## Features

| ID | Feature | CSRs | State |
|----|---------|------|-------|
| F1 | Completeness guard test | (foundation) | **DONE** (`e0a6891`) |
| F2 | ABI v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` (51 CSRs) + all consumers + capability gates | (structural) | **DONE** (ABI `1e07582`, vsim `9d972ba`, andesim `8b952d6`) |
| F5 | Counters / perf-monitor | mcountinhibit, mhpmevent3-6, mcounterinten (+ HW counters restored, verify-excluded) | **DONE** (`fcf5ecb`/`e321da1`) - found + fixed the mcounterwen UMODE gate bug |
| F6 | Andes trap-save (mdcause subset) | mdcause | **DONE** (`b110977`) - transported; verify-excluded (vsim HW-set) |
| F11 | Triggers | tselect, tdata2, mcontext (round-trip); tdata1/tcontrol verify-excluded | **DONE** (`b110977`) |
| F3 | Machine Configuration | menvcfg, mseccfg | FORWARD-LOOKING (premium gates UMODE/EPMP off; no engine to verify) |
| F4 | NMI handling | mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus, mnvec, mrnxvec | FORWARD-LOOKING (SMRNMI off) |
| F7 | CLIC | mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry | FORWARD-LOOKING (CLIC off) |
| F8 | State-enable | mstateen0-3 | FORWARD-LOOKING (SMSTATEEN off) |
| F9 | Memory / peripheral | mppib, mfiob, mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata | FORWARD-LOOKING (PPI/FIO/CCTL off) |
| F10 | PMA extend (16 -> 48) | pmacfg4/6/8/10, pmaaddr16-47 | DEFERRED (premium has 4 PMA entries; user chose premium-only) |
| F12 | U-delta | uzobctl, umisc_ctl, sleepvalue, ucctlbeginaddr | FORWARD-LOOKING (UMODE off; needs M+U engine) |
| F13 | Docs + verification-status (this section) | (the 142 excluded) | **DONE** |

## Outcome (2026-06-28)

All 51 writable M-mode CSRs are transported in ABI v4, capability-gated. On the
verification engine (ax45mpv_premium, M-only) **25** are implemented and gated on;
the other **26** are gated off and ride forward-looking for an engine that
implements the feature (CLIC, Smrnmi, Smstateen, ePMP, U-mode, ...).

Of the 25 premium-gated CSRs, verification status:
- **round-trip tested** (in-ROI self-check, marker + pc): mcountinhibit,
  mhpmevent3/4 (and 5/6 by the same gate), mcounterinten, tselect, tdata2,
  mcontext (`tests/fixtures/rt_m_ext_counters.S`, `rt_m_ext_trigcause.S`).
- **transported + restored, verify-excluded** (engine-divergent, like
  msp_bound/mip): mhpmcounter3-6 (HW counters), mdcause (vsim HW-set),
  tdata1/tcontrol (trigger defaults), mcontext at arbitrary width.

"Nothing missed" is enforced not by a fixture per CSR but by the machine-checked
guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`): every one of the 232 spec CSRs is
classified, the matrix matches the offline policy, and the ABI transports exactly
the matrix-approved set. The forward-looking sections (F3/F4/F7/F8/F9/F12) are
verified-correct *as transported-and-gated-off* by the guard + the parity
flywheel; their round-trip verification waits on a capable engine.

## Risks / judgment calls already baked in

- **Side-effecting CSRs stay excluded even under "expand all"**: `pushmcause`,
  `pushmepc`, `pushmxstatus`, `mnxti`, `mscratchcsw`, `mscratchcswl`,
  `mcctlcommand`, `mintsel_jal` - reading/writing performs an action, so the value
  is not state. Documented per-CSR in the matrix.
- **Triggers (F11) touch the Debug Module** the handoff itself drives. Transported
  last, behind its own gate, with a fixture that checks the DM handshake still
  works.
- **Premium is M-only**: F12 (U-delta) ships in the ABI but cannot be round-trip
  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CSR coverage completeness guard (the "nothing missed" flywheel).
#
# Fails if the spec inventory snapshot, the coverage matrix, and the wire format
# (include/hybrid/state_abi.h) ever drift apart -- a CSR the spec adds, a CSR
# transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a carried-today CSR dropped from
# the ABI. See tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py for the exact checks and
# docs/csr_coverage.ipynb for the disposition of every CSR.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "python3 required"

out=$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/check_coverage.py" 2>&1) || fail "coverage guard FAILED"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out"
ok "csr coverage guard: spec inventory == matrix == ABI (no drift)"

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Config-Driven CSR Capability Gating in vsim Hybrid Handoff

---

### 1. Config.inc / Config Source

**Where config is exposed:**
- **Built config.inc**: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc` (embedded in binary via linker symbols `_binary_config_inc_start` / `_binary_config_inc_end`)
- **Source config**: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl/config.inc`

**How engine exposes config at runtime:**
- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:33-40` — `print_cpu_configuration()` dumps embedded config.inc via linker symbols
- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:47-108` — `describe_engine()` function scans the embedded blob for `NDS_VLEN`, `NDS_DLEN`, `NDS_ELEN`, `NDS_XLEN` and emits JSON descriptor

**Example lines from built config** (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`):
```verilog
`define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1         // M-only
`define NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT `NDS_CFG_NO       // no DSP -> ucode CSR gated off
`define NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT `NDS_CFG_NO // no stack-safe -> msp_bound/base gated
`define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT `NDS_CFG_YES  // CoDense enabled -> jvt/uitb active
`define NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB    64                 // ILM present -> milmb active
`define NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB    32                 // DLM present -> mdlmb active
`define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER   2                   // debug triggers present
`define NDS_PMA_ENTRIES    4                  // PMA block active
```

---

### 2. AndesCaps Structure and andes_caps_from_config()

**AndesCaps struct definition:**
- **File**: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:119-143`

**Key components:**
```cpp
enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
  ALWAYS = 0,        // unconditionally present (every core)
  DSP,               // ucode (0x801) CSR gate
  CODENSE,           // uitb/jvt gating
  POWERBRAKE,        // mpft_ctl gating
  STACKSAFE,         // msp_bound/base/mhsp_ctl gating
  ECC,               // mecc_code gating
  // ... more gates for ILM, DLM, PERF_MONITOR, U/S-mode CSRs, CLIC, Smstateen, etc.
};

struct AndesCaps {
  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;  // bit per AndesGate

  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const {
    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);  // Line 138-142
  }
};
```

**andes_gate_for() function** (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:59-113`):
Maps each CSR address to its enabling gate:
```cpp
constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr) {
  switch (csr_addr) {
    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode
    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;           // mecc_code
    case 0x7C6: case 0x7C7: case 0x7C8:
      return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;               // mhsp_ctl/msp_bound/msp_base
    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;           // milmb
    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;           // mdlmb
    // ... 49 more cases for v4 M-ext CSRs ...
    default:
      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || ...)
        return AndesGate::PMA;
      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                  // mxstatus, mclk_ctl
  }
}
```

**andes_caps_from_config() binding** (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp:16-90`):
Converts config.inc macros to AndesCaps at runtime:
```cpp
inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config() {
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();

#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);  // Line 20-21
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);  // Line 29-30
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);  // Line 38-39
#endif
// ... 50+ more feature gates ...
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);  // Line 54-55: gates menvcfg/mcounteren/U-delta CSRs
#endif
  return c;  // Line 89
}
```

---

### 3. --describe Emits andes_csrs List

**Function**: `supported_andes_csr_names()` (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:149-164`)
```cpp
inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps) {
  std::vector<std::string> out;
  #define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)   // Line 153: iterates X-macro, filters by caps
  #undef X
  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");  // Line 157
  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr"); // Line 158
  #define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)   // Line 161: v4 M-ext CSRs, same gating
  #undef X
  return out;
}
```

**Integration in --describe** (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:47-108`):
- Line 90-91: Calls `supported_andes_csr_names(hybrid::andes_caps_from_config())`
- Line 92-95: Emits JSON array `"andes_csrs": [...]` for the driver to use in verify gating

**Example output** (ax45mpv_premium, M-only, no DSP/ECC/STACKSAFE):
```json
"andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", 
               "mhsp_ctl", "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "jvt", "pmacfg", "pmaaddr", ...]
```
(notably absent: ucode [DSP gated], mecc_code [ECC gated], msp_bound/msp_base [STACKSAFE gated])

---

### 4. Restore Gating in ResumeDriver

**File**: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`

**Constructor** (lines 98-101):
```cpp
explicit ResumeDriver(DmiBus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
                      AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
    : bus_{bus}, scratch_gpa_{scratch_gpa}, caps_{caps}  // Line 100: stores caps_
{}
```

**Andes CSR restore gating** (lines 259-273):
```cpp
if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES) {
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
      HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)  // Line 262: X-macro loop, per-CSR gate check
#undef X
  // PMA ordering: all pmaaddr before pmacfg
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM; ++i)
    if (caps_.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + i))  // Line 268: gate each pmaaddr
      write_csr_tolerant(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + i, state.andes.pmaaddr[i]);
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM; ++i)
    if (caps_.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * i))  // Line 271: gate each pmacfg
      write_csr_tolerant(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * i, state.andes.pmacfg[i]);
}
```

**M-ext CSR restore gating** (lines 280-285):
```cpp
if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT) {
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.m_ext.field);
      HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)  // Line 283: X-macro loop with per-CSR gating
#undef X
}
```

**Effect**: CSRs gated off (unsupported on target core) are never written, avoiding DMI hangs observed with unimplemented CSRs like ucode (no DSP) or mecc_code (no ECC).

---

### 5. Drain Gating in StateDrain

**File**: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`

**Constructor** (lines 36-39):
```cpp
explicit StateDrain(DmiBus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
                    AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
    : bus_{bus}, scratch_gpa_{scratch_gpa}, caps_{caps}  // Line 38: stores caps_
{}
```

**Andes CSR drain gating** (lines 123-137):
```cpp

#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
    state.andes.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));  // Line 125-126
      HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)  // Line 127: X-macro loop, per-CSR gate
#undef X

    if (caps_.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * i))  // Line 130: gate pmacfg
      state.andes.pmacfg[i] =
        read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * i));
  for (int i = 0; i < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM; ++i)
    if (caps_.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + i))  // Line 134: gate pmaaddr
      state.andes.pmaaddr[i] =
        read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + i));

```

**M-ext CSR drain gating** (lines 142-148):
```cpp
if (input.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT) {
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
    state.m_ext.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));  // Line 144-145
```

// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
// tests never need the generated header.
//
// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
#pragma once

#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"

namespace hybrid {

inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
{
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();

#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::CODENSE);       // uitb, jvt
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT) && _NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountermask_m
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
#endif
  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
#endif

  // v4 M-ext gates. Privilege-level gates from NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS
  // (1 = M, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U). An absent knob reads as off -- safe.
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);         // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u, U-delta
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMODE);         // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER) && (_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::TRIGGER);       // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMEPMP) && _NDS_SMEPMP) || (defined(_NDS_EPMP) && _NDS_EPMP)
  c.set(AndesGate::EPMP);          // mseccfg
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMRNMI) && _NDS_SMRNMI) || (defined(_NDS_RNMI) && _NDS_RNMI)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMRNMI);        // mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_EXCSLVL) && (_NDS_EXCSLVL > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::EXCSLVL);       // msave*
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_ECLIC) && _NDS_ECLIC) || (defined(_NDS_CLIC) && _NDS_CLIC)
  c.set(AndesGate::CLIC);          // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_SMSTATEEN) && _NDS_SMSTATEEN
  c.set(AndesGate::SMSTATEEN);     // mstateen0..3
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_CCTLCSR) && _NDS_CCTLCSR) || (defined(_NDS_CCTL) && _NDS_CCTL)
  c.set(AndesGate::CCTL);          // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PPI);           // mppib
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
    (defined(_NDS_FIO) && _NDS_FIO)
  c.set(AndesGate::FIO);           // mfiob
#endif

  return c;
}

}  // namespace hybrid
