toolUseResult.originalFile:
# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1, FV2 | NOT STARTED |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build: submodule `tools/cpu_config_to_march_converter` (or vendor the ~5 imported scripts). Build image gains `python3`. | - | NOT STARTED |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*`. | FV0 | NOT STARTED |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | NOT STARTED |
| FE2E | both | A fixture using an extension the old `-cpu` omitted now executes in the QEMU leg; hybrid cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | NOT STARTED |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- Submodule vs vendor (FV0) is a vsim-repo call; either keeps the generator out
  of the shipped product. Staleness is guarded in CI (regenerate + diff), not at
  runtime.

# VerilatorHelpers.cmake
# Provides vsim_add_verilated_cpu() to create custom commands for Verilator flow.

function(vsim_add_verilated_cpu CPU_NAME)
  string(TOUPPER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_UPPER)

  set(CPU_SERIES "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_SERIES}")
  set(RTL "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_RTL_PACKAGE}")
  set(CONFIG "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG}")
  set(CONFIG_DIR "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_DIR}")
  set(CONFIG_INC_FILTER "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_INC_FILTER}")
  set(EXTRA_FLAGS "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_EXTRA_VERILATOR_FLAGS}")
  set(LIBACEASIM_PATH "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_LIBACEASIM_PATH}")

  set(CPU_BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/V${CPU_NAME}")
  set(OBJ_SC_DIR "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/obj_sc")

  # Build verilator flags
  set(VL_FLAGS "")
  if(VSIM_SAVABLE)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --savable)
  endif()
  if(VSIM_DEBUG_FST)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace-fst --trace-threads 2)
  elseif(VSIM_DEBUG)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace)
  endif()
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS
    -O3 --x-assign fast --x-initial fast
    --noassert --Wno-fatal --no-timing
    --pins-sc-uint --pins-sc-biguint
  )
  separate_arguments(_extra_flags UNIX_COMMAND "${EXTRA_FLAGS}")
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS ${_extra_flags})

  # CCS optimization flags

# tools/qemu_cfg - config.inc -> QEMU `-readconfig` generator (vendored)

Build-time tool that distills a CPU's `config.inc` into a QEMU `-readconfig`
cfg (per-extension `[global]` properties + vlen/elen + ILM/DLM/HVM). The vsim
build (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`) runs it once per engine and bakes the
output into the binary as a second blob next to `config.inc`; the engine then
emits it on `sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config`. The andesim driver feeds that to
QEMU's fast-forward leg (`-readconfig`) so the functional engine executes the
**same ISA** the cycle-accurate engine models. One source of truth: `config.inc`.

## Provenance

Vendored (minimal subset) from
`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/`. Only the files on the `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py` import chain are
copied here - NOT the 13 MB upstream repo (TCL `config_tool` + sample corpus):

- `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py` (entry point)
- `config_to_march.py`, `config_inc_shared.py`, `march_rules.py`, `march_rules.txt`

## Re-sync (keep in parity with upstream)

```sh
u=$(mktemp -d); git clone --depth 1 \
  https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter "$u"
cp "$u"/scripts/{config_inc_to_qemu_cfg,config_to_march,config_inc_shared,march_rules}.py \
   "$u"/scripts/march_rules.txt tools/qemu_cfg/
```

A CI staleness check (re-run the copy, `git diff --exit-code tools/qemu_cfg`)
keeps this honest without making the generator a runtime dependency.

## Usage (what the build runs)

```sh
python3 tools/qemu_cfg/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py <config.inc> \
    --cpu-model <family> --with-platform -o qemu.cfg
```

`--cpu-model` is required here because the file is literally named `config.inc`
(the tool otherwise derives the QEMU driver name from the filename).

# VerilatorHelpers.cmake
# Provides vsim_add_verilated_cpu() to create custom commands for Verilator flow.

function(vsim_add_verilated_cpu CPU_NAME)
  string(TOUPPER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_UPPER)

  set(CPU_SERIES "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_SERIES}")
  set(RTL "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_RTL_PACKAGE}")
  set(CONFIG "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG}")
  set(CONFIG_DIR "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_DIR}")
  set(CONFIG_INC_FILTER "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_INC_FILTER}")
  set(EXTRA_FLAGS "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_EXTRA_VERILATOR_FLAGS}")
  set(LIBACEASIM_PATH "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_LIBACEASIM_PATH}")

  set(CPU_BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/V${CPU_NAME}")
  set(OBJ_SC_DIR "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/obj_sc")

  # Build verilator flags
  set(VL_FLAGS "")
  if(VSIM_SAVABLE)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --savable)
  endif()
  if(VSIM_DEBUG_FST)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace-fst --trace-threads 2)
  elseif(VSIM_DEBUG)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace)
  endif()
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS
    -O3 --x-assign fast --x-initial fast
    --noassert --Wno-fatal --no-timing
    --pins-sc-uint --pins-sc-biguint
  )
  separate_arguments(_extra_flags UNIX_COMMAND "${EXTRA_FLAGS}")
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS ${_extra_flags})

  # CCS optimization flags
  set(CCS_OPT "-isystem ${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include -std=c++20 -Os -march=x86-64-v3 -fPIC -DSC_DISABLE_API_VERSION_CHECK=1")
  if(VSIM_CCS_OPT)
    string(APPEND CCS_OPT " ${VSIM_CCS_OPT}")
  endif()

  set(_cpu_src_dir "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/${RTL}")
  set(_config_src "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/${CONFIG}")
  set(_cpu_config_inc "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/${CONFIG_DIR}/config.inc")
  set(_copy_stamp "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/.copy.stamp")
  set(_config_stamp "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/.config.stamp")
  set(_verilate_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.verilate.stamp")
  set(_make_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.make.stamp")
  set(_defines_raw "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_defines.raw")
  set(_defines_filtered "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_defines.filtered")
  set(_config_object "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.o")
  set(_config_header "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_config.h")

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_copy_stamp}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -rf "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    COMMAND cp -a "${_cpu_src_dir}" "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_copy_stamp}"
    DEPENDS "${_cpu_src_dir}/flists/flist.in"
    COMMENT "Preparing CPU build tree for ${CPU_NAME} (${RTL})"

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_stamp}" "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/last_config.cfg"
    BYPRODUCTS "${_cpu_config_inc}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      tclsh "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/config_tools/nds-softcore-config"
      --load "${_config_src}"
      --generate

    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_config_stamp}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_copy_stamp}" "${_config_src}"
    COMMENT "Generating nds config for ${CPU_NAME}"

    OUTPUT "${_verilate_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}.mk"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"

  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_make_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      make
      -C obj_sc
      -f "V${RTL}.mk"
      "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"
      "OPT=${CCS_OPT}"
      -Bj32
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_make_stamp}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_verilate_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}.mk"
    COMMENT "Compiling verilated objects for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_cpu_config_inc}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    DEPENDS "${_config_stamp}" "${_make_stamp}" "${_cpu_config_inc}"
    COMMENT "Copying config.inc for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_object}"
    COMMAND ld -r -b binary -o config.o config.inc
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    COMMENT "Building config object for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    COMMAND ar rcs "V${RTL}__ALL.a" config.o
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_make_stamp}" "${_config_object}"
    COMMENT "Embedding config object into V${RTL}__ALL.a"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_defines_raw}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/dump_verilator_defines.py"
      --verilator "${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
      --config-inc "${_cpu_config_inc}"
      --output "${_defines_raw}"
    DEPENDS "${_config_stamp}" "${_cpu_config_inc}" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/dump_verilator_defines.py"
    COMMENT "Dumping Verilog defines for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_defines_filtered}"
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/filter_verilog_defines.py"
      --input "${_defines_raw}"
      --filter "${CONFIG_INC_FILTER}"
      --output "${_defines_filtered}"
    DEPENDS "${_defines_raw}" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/filter_verilog_defines.py"
    COMMENT "Filtering Verilog defines for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_header}"
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/verilog_defines_to_c.py"
      --input "${_defines_filtered}"
      --output "${_config_header}.tmp"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_config_header}.tmp" "${_config_header}"

    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    "${_config_header}"
  )

  # LIBACEASIM_PATH can be:
  #   "stubs/<N>"            → build from stubs/<N>/ directory
  #   "/absolute/path/..."   → pre-built; no build step, just link
  #   ""                     → no libaceasim

    set(_asim_lib_in_series "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}/libaceasim.a")

    add_custom_command(

      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_directory "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/ver.c"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/makefile"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_asim_prepare_stamp}"
      DEPENDS "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}/ace.v" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c"

        "${CPU_SERIES}"
        "verilator=${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
        "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"
      WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_prepare_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
      COMMENT "Building stub libaceasim for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_asim_lib_in_series}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_lib_in_series}"
      COMMENT "Staging libaceasim.a for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )
    list(APPEND _verilated_outputs "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a")
  endif()

  # Custom target for this CPU's verilated artifacts
  add_custom_target(verilated_${CPU_NAME} DEPENDS ${_verilated_outputs})
endfunction()

# VerilatorHelpers.cmake
# Provides vsim_add_verilated_cpu() to create custom commands for Verilator flow.

# config.inc -> QEMU `-readconfig` generator (see tools/qemu_cfg/README.md). Run
# once per engine to bake a `qemu.cfg` blob next to `config.inc`, dumped by
# `sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config`. Defaults to the vendored copy; point at an
# external/upstream checkout to override. Set empty to embed an empty cfg (the
# andesim driver then falls back to its default -cpu).
set(CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/qemu_cfg/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py"
    CACHE FILEPATH "config.inc -> QEMU -readconfig cfg generator (empty to disable)")

function(vsim_add_verilated_cpu CPU_NAME)
  string(TOUPPER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_UPPER)

  set(CPU_SERIES "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_SERIES}")
  set(RTL "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_RTL_PACKAGE}")
  set(CONFIG "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG}")
  set(CONFIG_DIR "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_DIR}")
  set(CONFIG_INC_FILTER "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_CONFIG_INC_FILTER}")
  set(EXTRA_FLAGS "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_EXTRA_VERILATOR_FLAGS}")
  set(LIBACEASIM_PATH "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_LIBACEASIM_PATH}")

  set(CPU_BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/V${CPU_NAME}")
  set(OBJ_SC_DIR "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/obj_sc")

  # Build verilator flags
  set(VL_FLAGS "")
  if(VSIM_SAVABLE)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --savable)
  endif()
  if(VSIM_DEBUG_FST)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace-fst --trace-threads 2)
  elseif(VSIM_DEBUG)
    list(APPEND VL_FLAGS --trace)
  endif()
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS
    -O3 --x-assign fast --x-initial fast
    --noassert --Wno-fatal --no-timing
    --pins-sc-uint --pins-sc-biguint
  )
  separate_arguments(_extra_flags UNIX_COMMAND "${EXTRA_FLAGS}")
  list(APPEND VL_FLAGS ${_extra_flags})

  # CCS optimization flags
  set(CCS_OPT "-isystem ${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include -std=c++20 -Os -march=x86-64-v3 -fPIC -DSC_DISABLE_API_VERSION_CHECK=1")
  if(VSIM_CCS_OPT)
    string(APPEND CCS_OPT " ${VSIM_CCS_OPT}")
  endif()

  set(_cpu_src_dir "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/${RTL}")
  set(_config_src "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/${CONFIG}")
  set(_cpu_config_inc "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/${CONFIG_DIR}/config.inc")
  set(_copy_stamp "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/.copy.stamp")
  set(_config_stamp "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/.config.stamp")
  set(_verilate_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.verilate.stamp")
  set(_make_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.make.stamp")
  set(_defines_raw "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_defines.raw")
  set(_defines_filtered "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_defines.filtered")
  set(_config_object "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.o")
  set(_config_header "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}_config.h")

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_copy_stamp}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -rf "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    COMMAND cp -a "${_cpu_src_dir}" "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_copy_stamp}"
    DEPENDS "${_cpu_src_dir}/flists/flist.in"
    COMMENT "Preparing CPU build tree for ${CPU_NAME} (${RTL})"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_stamp}" "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/last_config.cfg"
    BYPRODUCTS "${_cpu_config_inc}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      tclsh "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/config_tools/nds-softcore-config"
      --load "${_config_src}"
      --generate
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E compare_files "${_config_src}" "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/last_config.cfg"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_config_stamp}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_copy_stamp}" "${_config_src}"
    COMMENT "Generating nds config for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_verilate_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}.mk"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      "${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
      -f flists/flist.in
      --prefix "V${RTL}"
      --sc
      --Mdir obj_sc
      ${VL_FLAGS}
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_verilate_stamp}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    DEPENDS ext_systemc "${_config_stamp}" "${_cpu_src_dir}/flists/flist.in"
    COMMENT "Running Verilator for ${CPU_NAME}"
    COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_make_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      make
      -C obj_sc
      -f "V${RTL}.mk"
      "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"
      "OPT=${CCS_OPT}"
      -Bj32
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_make_stamp}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_verilate_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}.mk"
    COMMENT "Compiling verilated objects for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_cpu_config_inc}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    DEPENDS "${_config_stamp}" "${_make_stamp}" "${_cpu_config_inc}"
    COMMENT "Copying config.inc for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_object}"
    COMMAND ld -r -b binary -o config.o config.inc
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    COMMENT "Building config object for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    COMMAND ar rcs "V${RTL}__ALL.a" config.o
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${_make_stamp}" "${_config_object}"
    COMMENT "Embedding config object into V${RTL}__ALL.a"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_defines_raw}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
      "NDS_HOME=${CPU_BUILD_DIR}"
      "SYSTEMC_INCLUDE=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/include"
      "SYSTEMC_LIBDIR=${DEPS_DIR}/systemc/lib"
      "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/dump_verilator_defines.py"
      --verilator "${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
      --config-inc "${_cpu_config_inc}"
      --output "${_defines_raw}"
    DEPENDS "${_config_stamp}" "${_cpu_config_inc}" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/dump_verilator_defines.py"
    COMMENT "Dumping Verilog defines for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_defines_filtered}"
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/filter_verilog_defines.py"
      --input "${_defines_raw}"
      --filter "${CONFIG_INC_FILTER}"
      --output "${_defines_filtered}"
    DEPENDS "${_defines_raw}" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/filter_verilog_defines.py"
    COMMENT "Filtering Verilog defines for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_header}"
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/verilog_defines_to_c.py"
      --input "${_defines_filtered}"
      --output "${_config_header}.tmp"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_config_header}.tmp" "${_config_header}"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -f "${_config_header}.tmp"
    DEPENDS "${_defines_filtered}" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/verilog_defines_to_c.py"
    COMMENT "Generating V${RTL}_config.h for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  # Collect outputs for the custom target
  set(_verilated_outputs
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    "${_config_header}"
  )

  # Step 3: Optionally build libaceasim.a from stubs
  # LIBACEASIM_PATH can be:
  #   "stubs/<N>"            → build from stubs/<N>/ directory
  #   "/absolute/path/..."   → pre-built; no build step, just link
  #   ""                     → no libaceasim
  if(LIBACEASIM_PATH)
    set(_asim_prepare_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.asim_prepare.stamp")
    set(_asim_lib_in_series "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}/libaceasim.a")

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${_asim_prepare_stamp}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -rf "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_directory "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/ver.c"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/makefile"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_asim_prepare_stamp}"
      DEPENDS "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}/ace.v" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c"
      COMMENT "Preparing aceasim sources for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${_asim_lib_in_series}"
      COMMAND make
        "INCDIR=${CONFIG_DIR}"
        "${CPU_SERIES}"
        "verilator=${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
        "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"
      WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_prepare_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
      COMMENT "Building stub libaceasim for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_asim_lib_in_series}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_lib_in_series}"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).

#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its

#

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# QEMU-match feature (docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md): vsim `--print-qemu-config`
# emits the engine's QEMU `-readconfig` cfg -- its config.inc distilled to
# per-extension `[global]` properties -- and the andesim plan executor injects
# it into the QEMU fast leg so the functional engine runs the same ISA the
# cycle-accurate engine models.
#
# Two layers:
#   1. unit (fast, always runs): plan-test covers stage_qemu_cfg (probe ->
#      workdir/qemu.cfg, with the tolerant fallback) and the fast-leg-only
#      `-readconfig` injection. Pure; no engine.
#   2. engine contract (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise):
#      sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config exits 0 and emits a [global] block whose
#      driver is andes-<family>-riscv-cpu (the family the QEMU leg selects).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. unit: stage_qemu_cfg + the -readconfig injection contract
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
PLANTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-plan-test"
[ -x "$PLANTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $PLANTEST"
"$PLANTEST" >/dev/null || fail "plan unit tests (stage_qemu_cfg / -readconfig) failed"
ok "unit: stage_qemu_cfg + fast-leg -readconfig injection"

# 2. engine contract. Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does:
#    VSIM_BIN_DIR (env, then config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP engine contract: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

out=$("$SIM" --print-qemu-config 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-qemu-config exit $rc: $out"
# family: sim_<family>_<variant> -> andes-<family>-riscv-cpu
base=$(basename "$SIM"); base=${base#sim_}; family=${base%%_*}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '\[global\]' || fail "no [global] block: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "andes-${family}-riscv-cpu" \
  || fail "driver not andes-${family}-riscv-cpu: $out"
ok "engine contract: $(basename "$SIM") --print-qemu-config -> andes-${family}-riscv-cpu cfg"

# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1 | **DONE** (`stage_qemu_cfg` + probe in `run_plan.cpp`, `plan_test.cpp`) |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build: submodule `tools/cpu_config_to_march_converter` (or vendor the ~5 imported scripts). Build image gains `python3`. | - | NOT STARTED |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*`. | FV0 | NOT STARTED |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | NOT STARTED |
| FE2E | both | A fixture using an extension the old `-cpu` omitted now executes in the QEMU leg; hybrid cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | NOT STARTED |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- Submodule vs vendor (FV0) is a vsim-repo call; either keeps the generator out
  of the shipped product. Staleness is guarded in CI (regenerate + diff), not at
  runtime.

# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1 | **DONE** (`stage_qemu_cfg` + probe in `run_plan.cpp`, `plan_test.cpp`) |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build. **Vendored** the 4 imported scripts to `tools/qemu_cfg/` (not the 13M repo; `python3` already a build dep). Overridable via the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cache var. | - | **DONE** (`tools/qemu_cfg/`) |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py --cpu-model <family>` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*` -> `ar` into `V<RTL>__ALL.a`. | FV0 | **DONE** (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`) |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | **DONE** (`src/main.cpp`) |
| FE2E | both | A fixture using an extension the old `-cpu` omitted now executes in the QEMU leg; hybrid cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | NOT STARTED |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- Submodule vs vendor (FV0) is a vsim-repo call; either keeps the generator out
  of the shipped product. Staleness is guarded in CI (regenerate + diff), not at
  runtime.

119	## 2. ABI conformance
120	
121	Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
122	state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
123	`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
124	little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
125	the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
126	engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.
127	
128	## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)
129	
130	`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
131	shares it:
132	
133	1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
134	   present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
135	   `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
136	2. The scan directory is:
137	   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
138	     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
139	   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
140	     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
141	     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
142	3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
143	   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
144	   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
145	   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
146	4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.
147	
148	Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
149	Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
150	no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.
151	
152	## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)
153	
154	1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
155	   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
156	   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
157	2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
158	   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
159	3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
160	   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
161	4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "jvt"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{trigger}`   | the plugin comma-suffix for the trigger (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
   present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
   `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.

# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1 | **DONE** (`stage_qemu_cfg` + probe in `run_plan.cpp`, `plan_test.cpp`) |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build. **Vendored** the 4 imported scripts to `tools/qemu_cfg/` (not the 13M repo; `python3` already a build dep). Overridable via the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cache var. | - | **DONE** (`tools/qemu_cfg/`) |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py --cpu-model <family>` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*` -> `ar` into `V<RTL>__ALL.a`. | FV0 | **DONE** (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`) |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | **DONE** (`src/main.cpp`) |
| FE2E | both | A real hybrid run probes the engine, injects `-readconfig`, QEMU accepts it, cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | **DONE** (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh` green with live injection; QEMU accepts the baked premium cfg) |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Outcome (2026-06-29)

All features DONE and verified end to end:

- vsim rebuilt; every engine carries a baked `qemu.cfg` blob.
  `sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-qemu-config` emits a 2425-byte cfg
  (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 xandesv5isa zba zbb zbc zbs zfh zfbfmin ... ilm/dlm/hvm`),
  **byte-identical** to the build-time bake.
- QEMU **accepts** that cfg via `-readconfig` (no property errors) -- the
  converter's globals match the `andes-ax45mpv-riscv-cpu` type.
- The real 2-step hybrid (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh`) passes with `-readconfig`
  injected live; cycle figure unaffected.
- Driver unit suites all green; the consumer side falls back cleanly for any
  engine lacking the flag.

**Robustness caveat (documented, not blocking):** the tolerant fallback covers
an engine *without* `--print-qemu-config`. It does NOT cover an engine that
emits a cfg whose property the running QEMU lacks -- that makes `-readconfig`
fail and the fast leg error. Mitigation if it ever bites: a `--qemu-v9-strict`
bake (drops unknown tokens) or a driver-side probe of QEMU's property set. The
verification QEMU accepts the current cfgs, so this is latent.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- Submodule vs vendor (FV0) is a vsim-repo call; either keeps the generator out
  of the shipped product. Staleness is guarded in CI (regenerate + diff), not at
  runtime.

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	# One-off generator for docs/config_gating_tutorial.ipynb.
3	import json, sys
4	
5	cells = []  # (kind, text)
6	
7	def md(t):  cells.append(("markdown", t))
8	def code(t): cells.append(("code", t))
9	
10	md(r"""# Tutorial: how the softcore config file drives the hybrid handoff
11	
12	This page explains, in simple steps, **how one file -- the softcore's
13	`config.inc` -- decides what the QEMU -> vsim handoff does**.
14	
15	Two questions:
16	
17	1. **What gets exchanged?** How `config.inc` decides which CSRs QEMU *drains*
18	   and which CSRs vsim *restores*.
19	2. **How do the two engines match?** How the driver fills QEMU's command-line
20	   options so QEMU imitates the same engine you picked for vsim.
21	
22	## The one big idea (an analogy)
23	
24	- `config.inc` is the **chip's spec sheet** -- the list of parts this CPU has
25	  (privilege levels, DSP, stack-safety, ILM/DLM, triggers, PMA, ...).
26	- **vsim** is a chip **built from that spec sheet**. It physically only has the
27	  parts the sheet lists. Ask it for a part it does not have and the debug module
28	  stalls.
29	- **QEMU** is a **generic imitator**. It can pretend to be many chips. We must
30	  *tell* it which chip to imitate.
31	
32	The handoff moves a **save game** (the architectural state: GPRs, FPRs, CSRs,
33	vector regs) from QEMU to vsim, so vsim can measure the cycle-accurate region.""")
34	
35	md(r"""## The cast: 3 actors, 1 source of truth
36	
37	```
38	        config.inc   (the chip's spec sheet: NDS_* defines)
39	             |
40	             |  compiled INTO the vsim binary at build time
41	             v
42	   +-----------------------+
43	   |   vsim  sim_<core>    |  has ONLY the parts the sheet lists
44	   +-----------------------+
45	             |
46	             |  sim_<core> --describe  ->  { "vlen":..., "andes_csrs":[...] }
47	             v
48	   +-----------------------+
49	   |   andesim driver      |  reads --describe, then TELLS QEMU what to imitate
50	   +-----------------------+
51	             |
52	             |  -cpu ...   vlen=...   -plugin ...,outfile=...
53	             v
54	   +-----------------------+
55	   |   QEMU (generic)      |  flexible imitator; matched via options
56	   +-----------------------+
57	```
58	
59	`config.inc` is written once, at chip-build time. Everything else **reads** it:
60	vsim is compiled from it; `--describe` re-publishes it; the driver uses
61	`--describe` to gate verification and to fill QEMU's options.""")
62	
63	md(r"""---
64	# Part 1 -- what gets exchanged (drain vs restore)
65	
66	The save game is touched **three** times. Only some are filtered by the spec
67	sheet.
68	
69	```
70	   QEMU (functional)                       vsim (cycle-accurate)
71	   -----------------                       ---------------------
72	   run program ...
73	   hit ROI trigger
74	        |
75	   (1) DRAIN  ---- state file (save game) ---->  (2) RESTORE
76	       pack ALL CSRs                                 unpack ONLY the CSRs
77	       QEMU exposes                                  the spec sheet lists
78	       (NOT filtered)                                (caps-gated)
79	                                                          |
80	                                                     run the ROI
81	                                                          |
82	                                                     (3) RE-DRAIN
83	                                                     read back ONLY the
84	                                                     caps-listed CSRs
85	                                                          |
86	                                                  cycle figure = mcycle delta
87	```
88	
89	| step | who | filtered by config? |
90	|------|-----|---------------------|
91	| (1) drain   | QEMU plugin       | **No** -- packs everything QEMU exposes (a superset) |
92	| (2) restore | vsim ResumeDriver | **Yes** -- writes only CSRs the engine has |
93	| (3) re-drain| vsim StateDrain   | **Yes** -- reads only CSRs the engine has |
94	| verify (`--verify`) | andesim driver | **Yes** -- compares only the engine's CSRs |
95	
96	**Why is drain (1) not filtered?** Loading a CSR the chip does not have would
97	**hang** the debug module. So the *consumer* (vsim) must filter. The *producer*
98	(QEMU) is allowed to be lazy and pack extra -- the consumer throws the extra
99	away. One side filters; that is enough.""")
100	
101	md(r"""## Step A: config.inc -> a set of "gates"
102	
103	Real lines from `ax45mpv_premium`'s spec sheet
104	(`.../Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`; `NDS_CFG_NO`=0, `NDS_CFG_YES`=1):
105	
106	```verilog
107	`define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1            // M-only (no U, no S)
108	`define NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT        `NDS_CFG_NO   // 0 -> ucode absent
109	`define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT    `NDS_CFG_YES  // 1 -> uitb, jvt present
110	`define NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB             64           // ILM present -> milmb
111	`define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER             2            // triggers present
112	`define NDS_PMA_ENTRIES             4            // PMA present
113	```
114	
115	(A full real trace of this engine is the **worked example** at the end.)
116	
117	At runtime, `andes_caps_from_config()` turns each `NDS_*` macro into a **gate**
118	(on/off). This is the ONE place that binds a feature to its macro
119	(`src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`):
120	
121	```cpp
122	inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config() {
123	  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
124	#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
125	  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);            // ucode
126	#endif
127	#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
128	  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);      // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
129	#endif
130	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
131	  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);          // menvcfg, mcounteren, U-delta CSRs
132	#endif
133	  // ... one block per feature ...
134	  return c;
135	}
136	```
137	
138	A macro that is **absent** reads as "feature off" -- so a core whose config
139	omits a knob stays safe (never a crash).""")
140	
141	md(r"""## Step B: a gate -> a yes/no per CSR
142	
143	`supports_csr(addr)` maps a CSR address to its gate and answers "does this
144	engine have it?" (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`):
145	
146	```cpp
147	constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const {
148	  const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);   // addr -> which gate
149	  return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);     // ALWAYS, or gate set
150	}
151	```
152	
153	So the chain is:
154	
155	```
156	config.inc  --andes_caps_from_config-->  gates  --supports_csr(addr)-->  yes/no
157	```""")
158	
159	code(r"""%%bash
160	# LIVE: peek at a real spec sheet. Set VSIM_BIN_DIR to your vsim build/ dir;
161	# set ENGINE to inspect a different core (default = the tutorial's example).
162	: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
163	: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
164	cfg="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V${ENGINE}/obj_sc/config.inc"
165	[ -f "$cfg" ] || cfg=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/*/obj_sc/config.inc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
166	echo "spec sheet: ${cfg:-<not found>}"
167	echo "---"
168	grep -E 'NDS_(NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS|DSP_SUPPORT_INT|STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT|ILM_SIZE_KB|DLM_SIZE_KB|PMA_ENTRIES|NUM_TRIGGER)' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
169	  || echo "(build the engine, or set VSIM_BIN_DIR, to see live values)" """)
170	
171	md(r"""## Step C: the gate filters restore and re-drain
172	
173	**(2) restore** -- vsim writes a CSR only if its engine has it
174	(`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`):
175	
176	```cpp
177	#define X(field, addr, name) \
178	  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
179	    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)        // one line per CSR; gate per line
180	#undef X
181	```
182	
183	**(3) re-drain** -- vsim reads a CSR back only if its engine has it
184	(`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`):
185	
186	```cpp
187	#define X(field, addr, name) \
188	  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
189	    state.andes.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));
190	    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
191	#undef X
192	```
193	
194	The same `caps_` is built from config at startup and handed to both
195	(`src/simulator.hpp`):
196	
197	```cpp
198	hybrid::ResumeDriver driver(bus, v_scratch_gpa(),
199	                            hybrid::andes_caps_from_config());
200	```
201	
202	**(1) drain** -- QEMU packs every CSR its gdbstub exposes, with **no** caps gate
203	(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`):
204	
205	```c
206	// The vsim caps gate decides which of these the cycle engine actually
207	// restores, so draining an absent-on-vsim CSR here is harmless.
208	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD(field, addr, name)  \
209	    s.m_ext.field = read_reg64(v->m_ext_##field); \
210	    if (v->m_ext_##field) has_m_ext = 1;
211	    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD)
212	#undef HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD
213	```
214	
215	Picture the filter (config = M-only, DSP off, ECC off):
216	
217	```
218	   state file:   mxstatus   ucode    milmb    mecc_code
219	   supports_csr?    yes       NO       yes        NO
220	                    |                   |
221	                    v                   v
222	   vsim writes:   mxstatus            milmb        (ucode, mecc_code skipped)
223	```""")
224	
225	code(r"""%%bash
226	# LIVE: the engine re-publishes its spec sheet as the CSR filter set.
227	: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
228	: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
229	sim="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_${ENGINE}"
230	[ -x "$sim" ] || sim=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
231	echo "engine: ${sim:-<not found>}"
232	echo "--- CSRs this engine implements (the filter set) ---"
233	"$sim" --describe 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
234	import sys, json
235	try: d = json.load(sys.stdin)
236	except Exception: print("(no --describe output; build the engine first)"); sys.exit()
237	print("vlen       =", d.get("vlen"))
238	print("andes_csrs =", ", ".join(d.get("andes_csrs", [])) or "(none)")'""")
239	
240	md(r"""---
241	# Part 2 -- how QEMU is matched to the vsim engine
242	
243	You **pick** a vsim engine (e.g. `sim_ax45mpv_premium`). Its spec sheet is fixed
244	(compiled in). QEMU is generic, so the driver must hand it options that make it
245	imitate the same chip. Three things to match:
246	
247	| what | QEMU option | how it is set |
248	|------|-------------|---------------|
249	| cpu family | `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` | from an invoke **template** |
250	| vector width | `vlen=512` | **synced** from the engine's `--describe` |
251	| handoff hooks | `-plugin ...,outfile=...,enter_pc=...` | from the run plan (trigger) |""")
252	
253	md(r"""## The invoke template (with holes to fill)
254	
255	Each engine carries an argv **template** with `{placeholders}`. QEMU's fast-leg
256	template (`driver/engine_registry.cpp`):
257	
258	```cpp
259	d.invoke.push_back(
260	  {"fast-leg",
261	   {"{bin}", "-object",
262	    "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}",
263	    "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem", "-cpu",
264	    "andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}", "-nographic", "-semihosting-config",
265	    "enable=on,target=native", "-bios", "{elf}", "-plugin",
266	    "{plugin},outfile={state_out}{trigger}"}});
267	```
268	
269	The plan executor fills the holes from a map (`driver/run_plan.cpp`):
270	
271	```cpp
272	const std::map<std::string, std::string> m = {
273	    {"bin", eng->bin_path},   {"elf", plan.elf},
274	    {"plugin", ctx.plugin_path},
275	    {"mmap", ctx.mmap_path},  {"mmap_size", std::to_string(ctx.mem_size)},
276	    {"state_out", state_out},
277	    {"trigger", lt.plugin_suffix},   // marker: empty;  pc: ",enter_pc=0x..."
278	    {"vlen", vlen_str},
279	};
280	std::vector<std::string> argv = build_argv(*tmpl, m, err);
281	```
282	
283	The key match -- `{vlen}` is taken from the **accurate-leg engine's**
284	descriptor, so QEMU's vector width equals vsim's:
285	
286	```cpp
287	// hw-config sync: {vlen} comes from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor.
288	long vlen = 0;
289	for (const Step& s : plan.steps)
290	  if (s.role == "accurate-leg")
291	    if (const EngineDescriptor* e = find_engine(engines, s.engine_id))
292	      if (e->vlen > 0) vlen = e->vlen;
293	```""")
294	
295	md(r"""## Closing the gap: the engine -> qemu-cpu map
296	
297	**Current state.** The rv64 fast-leg template **hardcodes** `andes-ax45mpv`
298	(only `{vlen}` is synced). The shell e2e harness works around this per fixture
299	with an explicit `QEMU_CPU` (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`):
300	
301	```
302	rt_priv_smode|... VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128
303	```
304	
305	**The fix is a tiny lookup.** Every vsim engine id is `<family>_<config-variant>`,
306	and QEMU already ships one `-cpu` per family:
307	
308	```
309	qemu_cpu  =  "andes-" + engine_id.split("_")[0]
310	```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# One-off generator for docs/config_gating_tutorial.ipynb.
import json, sys

cells = []  # (kind, text)

def md(t):  cells.append(("markdown", t))
def code(t): cells.append(("code", t))

md(r"""# Tutorial: how the softcore config file drives the hybrid handoff

This page explains, in simple steps, **how one file -- the softcore's
`config.inc` -- decides what the QEMU -> vsim handoff does**.

Two questions:

1. **What gets exchanged?** How `config.inc` decides which CSRs QEMU *drains*
   and which CSRs vsim *restores*.
2. **How do the two engines match?** How the driver fills QEMU's command-line
   options so QEMU imitates the same engine you picked for vsim.

## The one big idea (an analogy)

- `config.inc` is the **chip's spec sheet** -- the list of parts this CPU has
  (privilege levels, DSP, stack-safety, ILM/DLM, triggers, PMA, ...).
- **vsim** is a chip **built from that spec sheet**. It physically only has the
  parts the sheet lists. Ask it for a part it does not have and the debug module
  stalls.
- **QEMU** is a **generic imitator**. It can pretend to be many chips. We must
  *tell* it which chip to imitate.

The handoff moves a **save game** (the architectural state: GPRs, FPRs, CSRs,
vector regs) from QEMU to vsim, so vsim can measure the cycle-accurate region.""")

md(r"""## The cast: 3 actors, 1 source of truth

```
        config.inc   (the chip's spec sheet: NDS_* defines)
             |
             |  compiled INTO the vsim binary at build time
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   vsim  sim_<core>    |  has ONLY the parts the sheet lists
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  sim_<core> --describe  ->  { "vlen":..., "andes_csrs":[...] }
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   andesim driver      |  reads --describe, then TELLS QEMU what to imitate
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  -cpu ...   vlen=...   -plugin ...,outfile=...
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   QEMU (generic)      |  flexible imitator; matched via options
   +-----------------------+
```

`config.inc` is written once, at chip-build time. Everything else **reads** it:
vsim is compiled from it; `--describe` re-publishes it; the driver uses
`--describe` to gate verification and to fill QEMU's options.""")

md(r"""---
# Part 1 -- what gets exchanged (drain vs restore)

The save game is touched **three** times. Only some are filtered by the spec
sheet.

```
   QEMU (functional)                       vsim (cycle-accurate)
   -----------------                       ---------------------
   run program ...
   hit ROI trigger
        |
   (1) DRAIN  ---- state file (save game) ---->  (2) RESTORE
       pack ALL CSRs                                 unpack ONLY the CSRs
       QEMU exposes                                  the spec sheet lists
       (NOT filtered)                                (caps-gated)
                                                          |
                                                     run the ROI
                                                          |
                                                     (3) RE-DRAIN
                                                     read back ONLY the
                                                     caps-listed CSRs
                                                          |
                                                  cycle figure = mcycle delta
```

| step | who | filtered by config? |
|------|-----|---------------------|
| (1) drain   | QEMU plugin       | **No** -- packs everything QEMU exposes (a superset) |
| (2) restore | vsim ResumeDriver | **Yes** -- writes only CSRs the engine has |
| (3) re-drain| vsim StateDrain   | **Yes** -- reads only CSRs the engine has |
| verify (`--verify`) | andesim driver | **Yes** -- compares only the engine's CSRs |

**Why is drain (1) not filtered?** Loading a CSR the chip does not have would
**hang** the debug module. So the *consumer* (vsim) must filter. The *producer*
(QEMU) is allowed to be lazy and pack extra -- the consumer throws the extra
away. One side filters; that is enough.""")

md(r"""## Step A: config.inc -> a set of "gates"

Real lines from `ax45mpv_premium`'s spec sheet
(`.../Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`; `NDS_CFG_NO`=0, `NDS_CFG_YES`=1):

```verilog
`define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1            // M-only (no U, no S)
`define NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT        `NDS_CFG_NO   // 0 -> ucode absent
`define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT    `NDS_CFG_YES  // 1 -> uitb, jvt present
`define NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB             64           // ILM present -> milmb
`define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER             2            // triggers present
`define NDS_PMA_ENTRIES             4            // PMA present
```

(A full real trace of this engine is the **worked example** at the end.)

At runtime, `andes_caps_from_config()` turns each `NDS_*` macro into a **gate**
(on/off). This is the ONE place that binds a feature to its macro
(`src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`):

```cpp
inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config() {
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);            // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);      // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);          // menvcfg, mcounteren, U-delta CSRs
#endif
  // ... one block per feature ...
  return c;
}
```

A macro that is **absent** reads as "feature off" -- so a core whose config
omits a knob stays safe (never a crash).""")

md(r"""## Step B: a gate -> a yes/no per CSR

`supports_csr(addr)` maps a CSR address to its gate and answers "does this
engine have it?" (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`):

```cpp
constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const {
  const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);   // addr -> which gate
  return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);     // ALWAYS, or gate set
}
```

So the chain is:

```
config.inc  --andes_caps_from_config-->  gates  --supports_csr(addr)-->  yes/no
```""")

code(r"""%%bash
# LIVE: peek at a real spec sheet. Set VSIM_BIN_DIR to your vsim build/ dir;
# set ENGINE to inspect a different core (default = the tutorial's example).
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
cfg="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V${ENGINE}/obj_sc/config.inc"
[ -f "$cfg" ] || cfg=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/*/obj_sc/config.inc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "spec sheet: ${cfg:-<not found>}"
echo "---"
grep -E 'NDS_(NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS|DSP_SUPPORT_INT|STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT|ILM_SIZE_KB|DLM_SIZE_KB|PMA_ENTRIES|NUM_TRIGGER)' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(build the engine, or set VSIM_BIN_DIR, to see live values)" """)

md(r"""## Step C: the gate filters restore and re-drain

**(2) restore** -- vsim writes a CSR only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)        // one line per CSR; gate per line
#undef X
```

**(3) re-drain** -- vsim reads a CSR back only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
    state.andes.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
#undef X
```

The same `caps_` is built from config at startup and handed to both
(`src/simulator.hpp`):

```cpp
hybrid::ResumeDriver driver(bus, v_scratch_gpa(),
                            hybrid::andes_caps_from_config());
```

**(1) drain** -- QEMU packs every CSR its gdbstub exposes, with **no** caps gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`):

```c
// The vsim caps gate decides which of these the cycle engine actually
// restores, so draining an absent-on-vsim CSR here is harmless.
#define HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD(field, addr, name)  \
    s.m_ext.field = read_reg64(v->m_ext_##field); \
    if (v->m_ext_##field) has_m_ext = 1;
    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD)
#undef HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD
```

Picture the filter (config = M-only, DSP off, ECC off):

```
   state file:   mxstatus   ucode    milmb    mecc_code
   supports_csr?    yes       NO       yes        NO
                    |                   |
                    v                   v
   vsim writes:   mxstatus            milmb        (ucode, mecc_code skipped)
```""")

code(r"""%%bash
# LIVE: the engine re-publishes its spec sheet as the CSR filter set.
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
sim="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_${ENGINE}"
[ -x "$sim" ] || sim=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
echo "engine: ${sim:-<not found>}"
echo "--- CSRs this engine implements (the filter set) ---"
"$sim" --describe 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
import sys, json
try: d = json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception: print("(no --describe output; build the engine first)"); sys.exit()
print("vlen       =", d.get("vlen"))
print("andes_csrs =", ", ".join(d.get("andes_csrs", [])) or "(none)")'""")

md(r"""---
# Part 2 -- how QEMU is matched to the vsim engine

You **pick** a vsim engine (e.g. `sim_ax45mpv_premium`). Its spec sheet is fixed
(compiled in). QEMU is generic, so the driver must hand it options that make it
imitate the same chip. Three things to match:

| what | QEMU option | how it is set |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| cpu family | `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` | from an invoke **template** |
| vector width | `vlen=512` | **synced** from the engine's `--describe` |
| handoff hooks | `-plugin ...,outfile=...,enter_pc=...` | from the run plan (trigger) |""")

md(r"""## The invoke template (with holes to fill)

Each engine carries an argv **template** with `{placeholders}`. QEMU's fast-leg
template (`driver/engine_registry.cpp`):

```cpp
d.invoke.push_back(
  {"fast-leg",
   {"{bin}", "-object",
    "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}",
    "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem", "-cpu",
    "andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}", "-nographic", "-semihosting-config",
    "enable=on,target=native", "-bios", "{elf}", "-plugin",
    "{plugin},outfile={state_out}{trigger}"}});
```

The plan executor fills the holes from a map (`driver/run_plan.cpp`):

```cpp
const std::map<std::string, std::string> m = {
    {"bin", eng->bin_path},   {"elf", plan.elf},
    {"plugin", ctx.plugin_path},
    {"mmap", ctx.mmap_path},  {"mmap_size", std::to_string(ctx.mem_size)},
    {"state_out", state_out},
    {"trigger", lt.plugin_suffix},   // marker: empty;  pc: ",enter_pc=0x..."
    {"vlen", vlen_str},
};
std::vector<std::string> argv = build_argv(*tmpl, m, err);
```

The key match -- `{vlen}` is taken from the **accurate-leg engine's**
descriptor, so QEMU's vector width equals vsim's:

```cpp
// hw-config sync: {vlen} comes from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor.
long vlen = 0;
for (const Step& s : plan.steps)
  if (s.role == "accurate-leg")
    if (const EngineDescriptor* e = find_engine(engines, s.engine_id))
      if (e->vlen > 0) vlen = e->vlen;
```""")

md(r"""## Closing the gap: the engine -> qemu-cpu map

**Current state.** The rv64 fast-leg template **hardcodes** `andes-ax45mpv`
(only `{vlen}` is synced). The shell e2e harness works around this per fixture
with an explicit `QEMU_CPU` (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`):

```
rt_priv_smode|... VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128
```

**The fix is a tiny lookup.** Every vsim engine id is `<family>_<config-variant>`,
and QEMU already ships one `-cpu` per family:

```
qemu_cpu  =  "andes-" + engine_id.split("_")[0]
```

The config-variant suffix (`premium`, `mp2`, `advanced`, `makatau`) is a vsim
