#!/usr/bin/env bash
# QEMU-match feature (docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md): vsim `--print-qemu-config`
# emits the engine's QEMU `-readconfig` cfg -- its config.inc distilled to
# per-extension `[global]` properties -- and the andesim plan executor injects
# it into the QEMU fast leg so the functional engine runs the same ISA the
# cycle-accurate engine models.
#
# Two layers:
#   1. unit (fast, always runs): plan-test covers stage_qemu_cfg (probe ->
#      workdir/qemu.cfg, with the tolerant fallback) and the fast-leg-only
#      `-readconfig` injection. Pure; no engine.
#   2. engine contract (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise):
#      sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config exits 0 and emits a [global] block whose
#      driver is andes-<family>-riscv-cpu (the family the QEMU leg selects).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. unit: stage_qemu_cfg + the -readconfig injection contract
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
PLANTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-plan-test"
[ -x "$PLANTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $PLANTEST"
"$PLANTEST" >/dev/null || fail "plan unit tests (stage_qemu_cfg / -readconfig) failed"
ok "unit: stage_qemu_cfg + fast-leg -readconfig injection"

# 2. engine contract. Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does:
#    VSIM_BIN_DIR (env, then config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP engine contract: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

out=$("$SIM" --print-qemu-config 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-qemu-config exit $rc: $out"
# family: sim_<family>_<variant> -> andes-<family>-riscv-cpu
base=$(basename "$SIM"); base=${base#sim_}; family=${base%%_*}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '\[global\]' || fail "no [global] block: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "andes-${family}-riscv-cpu" \
  || fail "driver not andes-${family}-riscv-cpu: $out"
ok "engine contract: $(basename "$SIM") --print-qemu-config -> andes-${family}-riscv-cpu cfg"

input.new_string:
md(r"""## The implemented match: `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig`

Matching only the cpu **family** (above) is not enough: two configs in the same
family can differ in **extensions** -- one enables CoDense or Zfh, another does
not. So the engine publishes its **whole ISA** as a ready-made QEMU cfg.

At vsim **build time**, `config.inc` is distilled into a QEMU `-readconfig` file
-- one `[global]` per extension -- and baked into the binary right next to
`config.inc` (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`, via the
`cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule). `sim_<core> --print-qemu-config`

# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1 | **DONE** (`stage_qemu_cfg` + probe in `run_plan.cpp`, `plan_test.cpp`) |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build as the `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` **submodule** (`python3` already a build dep). Path overridable via the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cache var. | - | **DONE** (`.gitmodules`) |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py --cpu-model <family>` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*` -> `ar` into `V<RTL>__ALL.a`. | FV0 | **DONE** (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`) |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | **DONE** (`src/main.cpp`) |
| FE2E | both | A real hybrid run probes the engine, injects `-readconfig`, QEMU accepts it, cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | **DONE** (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh` green with live injection; QEMU accepts the baked premium cfg) |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Outcome (2026-06-29)

All features DONE and verified end to end:

- vsim rebuilt; every engine carries a baked `qemu.cfg` blob.
  `sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-qemu-config` emits a 2425-byte cfg
  (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 xandesv5isa zba zbb zbc zbs zfh zfbfmin ... ilm/dlm/hvm`),
  **byte-identical** to the build-time bake.
- QEMU **accepts** that cfg via `-readconfig` (no property errors) -- the
  converter's globals match the `andes-ax45mpv-riscv-cpu` type.
- The real 2-step hybrid (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh`) passes with `-readconfig`
  injected live; cycle figure unaffected.
- Driver unit suites all green; the consumer side falls back cleanly for any
  engine lacking the flag.

**Robustness caveat (documented, not blocking):** the tolerant fallback covers
an engine *without* `--print-qemu-config`. It does NOT cover an engine that
emits a cfg whose property the running QEMU lacks -- that makes `-readconfig`
fail and the fast leg error. Mitigation if it ever bites: a `--qemu-v9-strict`
bake (drops unknown tokens) or a driver-side probe of QEMU's property set. The
verification QEMU accepts the current cfgs, so this is latent.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- FV0 is the `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule (single upstream
  source, no fork). It is a vsim **build** dependency only -- it never ships with
  andesim or runs at andesim runtime; the engine carries just the baked cfg.

# ROADMAP: match the QEMU producer's ISA to the vsim engine

**Goal.** The QEMU fast-forward leg must execute the **same ISA** the selected
vsim engine implements - extensions and all (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`,
vlen, ...). Today `driver/engine_registry.cpp` hardcodes `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}`, so any extension the engine's `config.inc` enabled
but that string omits either traps in QEMU1 (config ON, qemu OFF) or runs on a
chip the engine does not model (config OFF, qemu ON). Both legs must be driven
by **one source of truth: the engine's frozen `config.inc`.**

## Mechanism (single source of truth)

```
        config.inc  (embedded blob in sim_<engine>, frozen at build)
        /                                  \
 andes_caps_from_config              cpu_config_to_march_converter (BUILD-time, once)
   -> AndesGate                         -> qemu.cfg  ([global] per-extension props)
   -> CSR save/restore                  -> baked as a 2nd blob in sim_<engine>
   (already shipped)                       -> `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` dumps it
                                              -> andesim feeds it to QEMU `-readconfig`
```

The converter (`https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`,
`scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`) is a **code generator run at vsim build
time only**. Its ~30-line output ships baked inside the engine binary, exactly
like `config.inc` already is (`ld -r -b binary`). The generator never ships with
`andesim` and is never run at andesim runtime - andesim only calls
`--print-qemu-config` and reads the result. Proven: feeding
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-config` through the converter yields a complete
`-readconfig` cfg (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 ... zba zbb zfh xandesv5isa ilm/dlm/hvm`).

## Locked decisions

- **vsim is the integration point, not andesim.** A new vsim CLI flag
  `--print-qemu-config` (sibling of `--print-config` / `--describe`) emits the
  cfg. andesim stays converter-free.
- **Bake at build, do not reimplement in C++.** The march/Zb*/Zfh mapping lives
  in the converter (97 ground-truth samples + `--check`); duplicating it in vsim
  C++ would drift. vsim runs the converter once in CMake and dumps the blob.
- **Tolerant fallback.** An engine without `--print-qemu-config` (older build or
  a drop-in not built through vsim's CMake) makes andesim fall back to today's
  hardcoded `-cpu`. No regression.
- **Only the QEMU (fast) leg gets `-readconfig`.** vsim never sees it.

## Features

| ID | Repo | Feature | Depends | State |
|----|------|---------|---------|-------|
| FA1 | andesim | `plan_argvs` injects `-readconfig {qemu_cfg}` into the fast leg when `RuntimeCtx.qemu_cfg` is set; nothing when empty (fallback). Pure, unit-tested. | - | **DONE** (`plan_test.cpp`, `run_plan.cpp`) |
| FA2 | andesim | `run_plan` obtains the cfg by running the accurate engine's `--print-qemu-config`, writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`; tolerant fallback if the flag is absent/empty. | FA1 | **DONE** (`stage_qemu_cfg` + probe in `run_plan.cpp`, `plan_test.cpp`) |
| FV0 | vsim | Converter available at build as the `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` **submodule** (`python3` already a build dep). Path overridable via the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cache var. | - | **DONE** (`.gitmodules`) |
| FV1 | vsim | CMake bake: run `config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py --cpu-model <family>` on the engine's `config.inc` -> `obj_sc/qemu.cfg` -> `ld -r -b binary` -> `_binary_qemu_cfg_*` -> `ar` into `V<RTL>__ALL.a`. | FV0 | **DONE** (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`) |
| FV2 | vsim | `--print-qemu-config` dumps the embedded blob (mirror `print_cpu_configuration`). | FV1 | **DONE** (`src/main.cpp`) |
| FE2E | both | A real hybrid run probes the engine, injects `-readconfig`, QEMU accepts it, cycle figure stays correct. | FV2, FA2 | **DONE** (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh` green with live injection; QEMU accepts the baked premium cfg) |
| FA3 | andesim | `run --mode hybrid --dry-run` prints the exact per-leg commands (QEMU with the staged `-readconfig`, then vsim) without spawning. `render_argv` (shell-quoted) + `PlanResult.argvs` + `PlanOptions.dry_run`. | FA2 | **DONE** (`render_argv` in `argv.hpp`; `plan_test.cpp` + smoke-test dry-run check) |

## Per-feature definition of done

- **FA1:** `andesim-plan-test` asserts the fast leg carries `-readconfig <cfg>`
  when `ctx.qemu_cfg` set, the accurate leg never does, and an empty cfg injects
  nothing. All existing plan tests stay green.
- **FA2:** with a stub engine that prints a cfg, `run_plan` writes the file and
  `ctx.qemu_cfg` points at it; a stub that errors on the flag leaves it empty.
- **FV1/FV2:** `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` byte-matches the converter run
  on that engine's `config.inc`; `--print-config` unaffected.
- **FE2E:** the matched run passes and the cycle figure is unchanged vs a
  hand-matched `-cpu`.

## Outcome (2026-06-29)

All features DONE and verified end to end:

- vsim rebuilt; every engine carries a baked `qemu.cfg` blob.
  `sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-qemu-config` emits a 2425-byte cfg
  (`m a f d c b v vlen=512 xandesv5isa zba zbb zbc zbs zfh zfbfmin ... ilm/dlm/hvm`),
  **byte-identical** to the build-time bake.
- QEMU **accepts** that cfg via `-readconfig` (no property errors) -- the
  converter's globals match the `andes-ax45mpv-riscv-cpu` type.
- The real 2-step hybrid (`test_andes_sim_f6.sh`) passes with `-readconfig`
  injected live; cycle figure unaffected.
- Driver unit suites all green; the consumer side falls back cleanly for any
  engine lacking the flag.

**Robustness caveat (documented, not blocking):** the tolerant fallback covers
an engine *without* `--print-qemu-config`. It does NOT cover an engine that
emits a cfg whose property the running QEMU lacks -- that makes `-readconfig`
fail and the fast leg error. Mitigation if it ever bites: a `--qemu-v9-strict`
bake (drops unknown tokens) or a driver-side probe of QEMU's property set. The
verification QEMU accepts the current cfgs, so this is latent.

## Notes / judgment calls

- vlen is specified both inline (`-cpu ...,vlen=512`) and via the cfg `[global]`;
  both come from the same `config.inc`, so they agree (explicit `-cpu` wins). The
  cfg's job is the **extensions** the inline string omits. If a conflict ever
  surfaces, drop the inline `,vlen=` and let the cfg own it.
- FV0 is the `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule (single upstream
  source, no fork). It is a vsim **build** dependency only -- it never ships with
  andesim or runs at andesim runtime; the engine carries just the baked cfg.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# QEMU-match feature (docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md): vsim `--print-qemu-config`
# emits the engine's QEMU `-readconfig` cfg -- its config.inc distilled to
# per-extension `[global]` properties -- and the andesim plan executor injects
# it into the QEMU fast leg so the functional engine runs the same ISA the
# cycle-accurate engine models.
#
# Two layers:
#   1. unit (fast, always runs): plan-test covers stage_qemu_cfg (probe ->
#      workdir/qemu.cfg, with the tolerant fallback) and the fast-leg-only
#      `-readconfig` injection. Pure; no engine.
#   2. engine contract (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise):
#      sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config exits 0 and emits a [global] block whose
#      driver is andes-<family>-riscv-cpu (the family the QEMU leg selects).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. unit: stage_qemu_cfg + the -readconfig injection contract
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
PLANTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-plan-test"
[ -x "$PLANTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $PLANTEST"
"$PLANTEST" >/dev/null || fail "plan unit tests (stage_qemu_cfg / -readconfig) failed"
ok "unit: stage_qemu_cfg + fast-leg -readconfig injection"

# 2. engine contract. Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does:
#    VSIM_BIN_DIR (env, then config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP engine contract: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

out=$("$SIM" --print-qemu-config 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-qemu-config exit $rc: $out"
# family: sim_<family>_<variant> -> andes-<family>-riscv-cpu
base=$(basename "$SIM"); base=${base#sim_}; family=${base%%_*}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '\[global\]' || fail "no [global] block: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "andes-${family}-riscv-cpu" \
  || fail "driver not andes-${family}-riscv-cpu: $out"
ok "engine contract: $(basename "$SIM") --print-qemu-config -> andes-${family}-riscv-cpu cfg"

# 3. end-to-end (no spawn): `run --mode hybrid --dry-run` prints both legs, and
#    the QEMU leg carries -readconfig <cfg> -- i.e. the probe -> stage -> inject
#    chain is wired. Needs the andesim binary + a fixture ELF; SKIPs otherwise.
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ]; then
  id="vsim:${base}"
  out=$(VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --dry-run --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>/dev/null)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 2 command' \
    || fail "dry-run did not print 2 commands: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-readconfig' \
    || fail "dry-run QEMU leg missing -readconfig: $out"
  ok "dry-run: hybrid command preview shows both legs + -readconfig"
else
  ok "SKIP dry-run check (need build/andesim + a tests/fixtures/*.elf)"
fi

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
No — and the direction is backwards. `--describe` is the load-bearing one; `--print-qemu-config` is the narrow accessory.

**What each is for (they do not overlap):**

| | `--describe` | `--print-qemu-config` |
|---|---|---|
| Output | JSON object (`EngineDescriptor`) | QEMU `-readconfig` ini text |
| Who reads it | **andesim** (engine discovery) | **QEMU** (the fast leg) — opaque to andesim |
| Carries | `id`, `type`, `kind`, **`invoke` argv templates per role**, `vlen/dlen/elen/xlen`, `triggers`, `roles`, `state` caps, `andes_csrs` verify-list, `result` rule | only the ISA extensions + vlen, as QEMU CPU properties |

Analogy: `--describe` is the engine's **ID card + instruction manual** — without it andesim does not even know the engine exists, what it is called, or *the command line to launch it* (`invoke`). `--print-qemu-config` is **one config file for a different program (QEMU)**. You cannot throw away the manual because you happen to have one accessory file.

Concretely, `descriptor_from_json` (`engine_descriptor.hpp:54`) builds the whole registry from `--describe`. The qemu cfg has none of `id` / `invoke` / `roles` / `triggers` / `andes_csrs`. Their only shared field is `vlen`. So dropping `--describe` deletes engine discovery entirely.

**The real consolidation (likely your intent):** fold the cfg *into* `--describe`, and drop `--print-qemu-config` as a separate flag. Today a hybrid run spawns the **same vsim binary twice** for metadata: once in discovery (`--describe`) and again in `run_plan.cpp:253` (`--print-qemu-config`). If vsim's `--describe` JSON gained an optional `qemu_cfg` string field (it already has the baked blob in hand), andesim would get the cfg from the discovery probe it *already* runs — one subprocess instead of two, and one fewer flag to maintain.

That keeps `--describe` (mandatory contract) and removes the redundant *probe*, not the manual.

Want me to do that merge — add `qemu_cfg` to the `--describe` contract and retire the separate `--print-qemu-config` probe? It touches both repos (vsim emits the field; andesim reads `e->qemu_cfg` instead of spawning). I would keep `--print-qemu-config` as a thin debug-only dump, or delete it fully — your call.

content.text:
這就是 `--describe` 的真面目。它是引擎自己填的一張**自我介紹表**（JSON）。

**先看這張表每一行的意思（用上面真的輸出）：**

```
"id": "verilator:ax45mpv_mp2"        <- 我的名字 (andesim 用它來指認我)
"kind": "cycle-accurate"             <- 我是哪種引擎 (精準/功能)
"vlen": 512 ...                      <- 我的向量寬度等硬體參數
"triggers": ["csr", "pc"]            <- 我支援哪些切換點
"roles": ["standalone","accurate-leg"] <- 我能當哪條腿 (我能當 vsim 那條)
"andes_csrs": [...]                  <- 我有實作這些 CSR (--verify 只比這些)
"invoke": {                          <- *** 最重要 ***
   "accurate-leg": ["{bin}","{elf}","--resume-from-qemu","{state_in}", ...]
}                                    <- 要啟動我, 就照這行填空再執行
"result": "stderr:cycles"           <- 跑完去 stderr 撈 cycles 數字
```

**為什麼需要它？因為 andesim 裡面「沒有任何一行針對特定引擎的程式碼」。**

andesim 是**一個** driver，但要驅動**很多種**引擎：qemu、vsim ax45mpv、vsim ax66、未來的 alioth/sid。每一個引擎的指令列、參數、名字都不一樣。

問題是：andesim 怎麼知道一個它**從沒見過**的引擎要怎麼啟動？

答案：它不靠記憶，它直接**問引擎本人**。它跑 `引擎 --describe`，引擎回一張上面這種表。andesim 讀 `invoke` 那行，把 `{bin}` `{elf}` `{state_in}` 這些空格填好，就能跑了。

**用簡單比喻：**
新員工報到，工廠經理（andesim）從沒見過他。經理不去背全世界每個員工，他只發一張表給新員工：「填一下 - 你叫什麼？你會做什麼？要怎麼啟動你？」員工填完交回（這就是 `--describe`），經理照著表就會用他了。

**好處（這就是「為什麼需要」的核心）：**
- 丟一個新引擎 binary 進資料夾 -> andesim 問它 `--describe` -> 馬上能用，**andesim 完全不用改、不用重編**。
- 沒有 `--describe`，你就得把每個引擎的指令列**寫死**在 andesim 原始碼裡，每加一個引擎就要改 andesim 再重編一次。

**和 `--print-qemu-config` 的差別（接上一輪）：**
- `--describe` 回答：「要怎麼啟動**我**（vsim 這顆）？」
- `--print-qemu-config` 回答：「要怎麼設定**另一顆**引擎（QEMU），讓它的指令集跟我一樣？」

兩個問題不同，所以是兩個東西。`--describe` 是身分證（不能丟），`--print-qemu-config` 只是一個給 QEMU 用的設定檔（可以併進身分證裡）。

要我把 `--print-qemu-config` 併進 `--describe` 嗎？還是你只是想先搞懂、暫時不動？

`diff` 證明了一切。5 顆引擎裡，我挑差最多的兩顆（`ax45mpv_premium` 64-bit 有向量 vs `d23` 32-bit 無向量），結果**整張表只差 3 行**：

```
id            <- 不一樣
vlen/dlen/... <- 不一樣
andes_csrs    <- 不一樣
其餘全部 (type, kind, triggers, roles, state, invoke, result) <- 一模一樣
```

最重要的 `invoke`（啟動指令）在兩顆完全不同的核上**逐字相同**。

**這就是答案的核心：把欄位分成兩堆。**

| 欄位 | 每顆 vsim 都一樣？ | 真正的來源 |
|------|------|------|
| type, kind, triggers, roles, state, **invoke**, result | **一樣** | vsim 的 CLI 設計（同一份原始碼編出來的，當然一樣） |
| id | 不同 | **檔名**（sim_d23 -> d23） |
| vlen/dlen/elen/xlen | 不同 | config.inc（而且 `--print-qemu-config` 已經帶 vlen 了） |
| andes_csrs | 不同 | config.inc |

看出來了嗎？`--describe` 回傳的東西，**一大半是每顆都一樣的**。一樣的東西卻被複製進每一顆 binary，這就是浪費。

---

**所以「不需要 --describe」的設計是這樣：**

1. **andesim 內建一張「vsim 家族設定檔」** —— 把那 7 個固定欄位寫死一次（就像 andesim **現在已經**內建一張 qemu 的描述表）。
2. **掃資料夾找 `sim_*`** —— 檔名就是 id。不用問，不用 JSON。
3. **剩下唯二會變的（vlen 群 + andes_csrs）來自 config.inc** —— 重用你**已經在做**的那次探測：`--print-qemu-config` 已經帶 vlen 跟擴充了，再讓它（或一個 `--print-config`）多吐一份 csr 清單即可。

結果：`--describe` 刪掉。每次 hybrid 的探測從 **2 次（describe + qemu-config）變 1 次**。固定的樣板不再重複塞進每顆 binary。

---

**誠實講代價（我不會藏）：**

你會失去「丟一個**全新種類**引擎（alioth、sid）零改 andesim 碼」這個能力 —— 新種類要在 andesim 加一張家族設定檔（約 10 行 + 重編）。

但是：
- 新的 vsim **設定**（ax90、ax99...）還是**零改碼** —— 丟個 `sim_*` 進去，檔名當 id，參數從 config dump 拿。
- **qemu 本來就是寫死的**（它根本沒實作 `--describe`）。所以你只是讓 vsim 跟 qemu **一致**，不是發明新做法 —— 你是把「唯一一個用不同方式做的地方」收掉。

一句話：`--describe` 是為了「未來有很多種未知引擎」設計的，但你實際上只有 qemu + vsim 兩種，qemu 已經寫死，所以這個通用協定 90% 在做白工。

---

要我動手嗎？這是跨兩個 repo 的重構（andesim 加家族設定檔 + 改 discovery；vsim 拿掉 `--describe`，把 csr 清單併進 config dump）。照規矩我會先寫**失敗測試**再改。先確認你要走這條，我再開 ROADMAP 拆成一次一個 feature。

`diff_states` 的程式碼我讀了，答案很明確：**有兩張 csr 清單，拿掉 `--describe` 只砸到其中一張。**

**第 1 張 — ABI 線格式清單 `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`（不受影響）**
住在共享標頭 `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`，是編譯期固定的 13 個 Andes scalar CSR。andesim **本來就有**，`state_diff.cpp:121` 直接 `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` 在跑。跟 `--describe` 無關。拿掉 `--describe`，它**動都不會動**。

**第 2 張 — 每顆引擎的「實作了哪些 CSR」清單 `andes_csrs`（這張才會被砸）**
就是你之前看到 diff 裡 premium 報 **25 個**、d23 報 **13 個不同的**那張。它現在搭 `--describe` 過來，在 `cmd_run.cpp:424` 餵進 `diff_states` 當 `--verify` 的閘門。

**如果直接拿掉 `--describe`、又不補，會發生什麼（具體傷害）：**

`acc->andes_csrs` 變空。然後看 `state_diff.cpp:112` 這行：

```cpp
if (andes_supported.empty()) return true;   // 空 = 每個 CSR 都算「有支援」
```

空清單被當成「**全部都比**」。於是 `--verify` 會去比對**引擎根本沒實作**的 CSR —— 而 vsim 從沒 restore/re-read 過它們（值是垃圾）—— 結果就是 **`--verify` 假性失敗（false FAIL）**。這就是拿掉後不補的後果。

**所以結論：這張清單不能丟，只能「搬家」。** 它的根源是 config.inc 的 `NDS_*` 旗標（決定哪個 CSR 存在 = 決定要不要比）。兩條搬法：

| | A. 換管道（務實） | B. andesim 自己算（純粹） |
|---|---|---|
| 做法 | vsim 還是吐這張小清單，只是改用 config-dump 那個旗標（順便餵 QEMU match 的同一次探測） | vsim 只吐**原始 config.inc**，andesim 用共享邏輯自己算出清單 |
| 代價 | 探測從胖 JSON 縮成一張小清單，**清單照樣 ship**。簡單 | 要把 gate 邏輯搬進共享標頭。**但**我剛查過：`supports_csr` 那套邏輯現在**不在** `include/`，只在 vsim 裡；而且真實清單（premium 25 個含 debug/perfmon）比 13 個 ABI scalar 廣很多 -> 要搬的邏輯不少，較重 |

一句話：拿掉 `--describe` **不會**讓 csr list 消失，但你**必須**把這張「每顆不同的 verify 閘門清單」搬到別的管道，否則 `--verify` 會開始假性失敗。最省力是 A（清單照舊預算好、換個旗標吐出來）。

content.text:
核心原因:**「排 (drain/讀)」和「寫 (restore)」不對稱,而 QEMU 不知道對方是哪顆引擎。**

我已在 `hybrid_handoff.c:344-359` 確認:plugin 對 satp/medeleg/mideleg/M-ext CSR 全部**無條件讀**進 struct,handle 不存在就讀 0。第 347 行註解直說: `draining an absent-on-vsim CSR here is harmless`。

**四個理由:**

1. **「沒用」是相對的,不是絕對的。** satp/medeleg 是 S-mode CSR。預設引擎 ax45mpv 是 M-only,不實作 -> 不 restore。但換成 ax66 (S/U-capable) 就**有用**。同一個 drain 檔可能餵給不同引擎。

2. **生產者 (QEMU plugin) 不知道消費者是誰。** plugin 跑在 QEMU 裡,手上沒有目標引擎的 config.inc,不知道接收方是 M-only 還是 S/U。所以它**排全集**,讓消費者自己挑。這就是 producer/consumer 分工。

3. **讀很安全,寫才危險 (這是關鍵)。** 在 QEMU 讀一個 CSR 是無害的 (handle 是 NULL 就讀 0)。但把一個引擎**沒有**的 CSR **寫進** vsim hart (透過 Debug Module) 會**卡住 Debug Module**。所以過濾器**只能放在「寫」那邊 (vsim consumer)**,不能放「讀」那邊。在 QEMU 端先過濾沒有好處,只是多花力氣。

4. **排出來的記錄本身有價值。** 那些沒被 restore 的 CSR 留在 `hybrid_state_v1` 當**完整快照** —— 給未來做 S/U 的引擎用,也給 debug/archive 看。

一句話:QEMU 多排幾個 CSR 幾乎免費又安全;真正的成本只在「寫回 vsim」那一步,而那一步**本來就有 caps gate 過濾**。所以「讀全集、寫過濾」是最省事又最安全的設計。

===== CELL [0] (markdown) =====
# Tutorial: how the softcore config file drives the hybrid handoff

This page explains, in simple steps, **how one file -- the softcore's
`config.inc` -- decides what the QEMU -> vsim handoff does**.

Two questions:

1. **What gets exchanged?** How `config.inc` decides which CSRs QEMU *drains*
   and which CSRs vsim *restores*.
2. **How do the two engines match?** How the driver fills QEMU's command-line
   options so QEMU imitates the same engine you picked for vsim.

## The one big idea (an analogy)

- `config.inc` is the **chip's spec sheet** -- the list of parts this CPU has
  (privilege levels, DSP, stack-safety, ILM/DLM, triggers, PMA, ...).
- **vsim** is a chip **built from that spec sheet**. It physically only has the
  parts the sheet lists. Ask it for a part it does not have and the debug module
  stalls.
- **QEMU** is a **generic imitator**. It can pretend to be many chips. We must
  *tell* it which chip to imitate.

The handoff moves a **save game** (the architectural state: GPRs, FPRs, CSRs,
vector regs) from QEMU to vsim, so vsim can measure the cycle-accurate region.

===== CELL [1] (markdown) =====
## The cast: 3 actors, 1 source of truth

```
        config.inc   (the chip's spec sheet: NDS_* defines)
             |
             |  compiled INTO the vsim binary at build time
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   vsim  sim_<core>    |  has ONLY the parts the sheet lists
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  sim_<core> --describe  ->  { "vlen":..., "andes_csrs":[...] }
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   andesim driver      |  reads --describe, then TELLS QEMU what to imitate
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  -cpu ...   vlen=...   -plugin ...,outfile=...
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   QEMU (generic)      |  flexible imitator; matched via options
   +-----------------------+
```

`config.inc` is written once, at chip-build time. Everything else **reads** it:
vsim is compiled from it; `--describe` re-publishes it; the driver uses
`--describe` to gate verification and to fill QEMU's options.

===== CELL [2] (markdown) =====
---
# Part 1 -- what gets exchanged (drain vs restore)

The save game is touched **three** times. Only some are filtered by the spec
sheet.

```
   QEMU (functional)                       vsim (cycle-accurate)
   -----------------                       ---------------------
   run program ...
   hit ROI trigger
        |
   (1) DRAIN  ---- state file (save game) ---->  (2) RESTORE
       pack ALL CSRs                                 unpack ONLY the CSRs
       QEMU exposes                                  the spec sheet lists
       (NOT filtered)                                (caps-gated)
                                                          |
                                                     run the ROI
                                                          |
                                                     (3) RE-DRAIN
                                                     read back ONLY the
                                                     caps-listed CSRs
                                                          |
                                                  cycle figure = mcycle delta
```

| step | who | filtered by config? |
|------|-----|---------------------|
| (1) drain   | QEMU plugin       | **No** -- packs everything QEMU exposes (a superset) |
| (2) restore | vsim ResumeDriver | **Yes** -- writes only CSRs the engine has |
| (3) re-drain| vsim StateDrain   | **Yes** -- reads only CSRs the engine has |
| verify (`--verify`) | andesim driver | **Yes** -- compares only the engine's CSRs |

**Why is drain (1) not filtered?** Loading a CSR the chip does not have would
**hang** the debug module. So the *consumer* (vsim) must filter. The *producer*
(QEMU) is allowed to be lazy and pack extra -- the consumer throws the extra
away. One side filters; that is enough.

===== CELL [3] (markdown) =====
## Step A: config.inc -> a set of "gates"

Real lines from `ax45mpv_premium`'s spec sheet
(`.../Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`; `NDS_CFG_NO`=0, `NDS_CFG_YES`=1):

```verilog
`define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1            // M-only (no U, no S)
`define NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT        `NDS_CFG_NO   // 0 -> ucode absent
`define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT    `NDS_CFG_YES  // 1 -> uitb, jvt present
`define NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB             64           // ILM present -> milmb
`define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER             2            // triggers present
`define NDS_PMA_ENTRIES             4            // PMA present
```

(A full real trace of this engine is the **worked example** at the end.)

At runtime, `andes_caps_from_config()` turns each `NDS_*` macro into a **gate**
(on/off). This is the ONE place that binds a feature to its macro
(`src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`):

```cpp
inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config() {
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);            // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);      // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);          // menvcfg, mcounteren, U-delta CSRs
#endif
  // ... one block per feature ...
  return c;
}
```

A macro that is **absent** reads as "feature off" -- so a core whose config
omits a knob stays safe (never a crash).

===== CELL [4] (markdown) =====
## Step B: a gate -> a yes/no per CSR

`supports_csr(addr)` maps a CSR address to its gate and answers "does this
engine have it?" (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`):

```cpp
constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const {
  const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);   // addr -> which gate
  return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);     // ALWAYS, or gate set
}
```

So the chain is:

```
config.inc  --andes_caps_from_config-->  gates  --supports_csr(addr)-->  yes/no
```

===== CELL [5] (code) =====
%%bash
# LIVE: peek at a real spec sheet. Set VSIM_BIN_DIR to your vsim build/ dir;
# set ENGINE to inspect a different core (default = the tutorial's example).
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
cfg="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V${ENGINE}/obj_sc/config.inc"
[ -f "$cfg" ] || cfg=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/*/obj_sc/config.inc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "spec sheet: ${cfg:-<not found>}"
echo "---"
grep -E 'NDS_(NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS|DSP_SUPPORT_INT|STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT|ILM_SIZE_KB|DLM_SIZE_KB|PMA_ENTRIES|NUM_TRIGGER)' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(build the engine, or set VSIM_BIN_DIR, to see live values)" 

===== CELL [6] (markdown) =====
## Step C: the gate filters restore and re-drain

**(2) restore** -- vsim writes a CSR only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)        // one line per CSR; gate per line
#undef X
```

**(3) re-drain** -- vsim reads a CSR back only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
    state.andes.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
#undef X
```

The same `caps_` is built from config at startup and handed to both
(`src/simulator.hpp`):

```cpp
hybrid::ResumeDriver driver(bus, v_scratch_gpa(),
                            hybrid::andes_caps_from_config());
```

**(1) drain** -- QEMU packs every CSR its gdbstub exposes, with **no** caps gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`):

```c
// The vsim caps gate decides which of these the cycle engine actually
// restores, so draining an absent-on-vsim CSR here is harmless.
#define HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD(field, addr, name)  \
    s.m_ext.field = read_reg64(v->m_ext_##field); \
    if (v->m_ext_##field) has_m_ext = 1;
    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD)
#undef HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD
```

Picture the filter (config = M-only, DSP off, ECC off):

```
   state file:   mxstatus   ucode    milmb    mecc_code
   supports_csr?    yes       NO       yes        NO
                    |                   |
                    v                   v
   vsim writes:   mxstatus            milmb        (ucode, mecc_code skipped)
```

===== CELL [7] (code) =====
%%bash
# LIVE: the engine re-publishes its spec sheet as the CSR filter set.
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
sim="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_${ENGINE}"
[ -x "$sim" ] || sim=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
echo "engine: ${sim:-<not found>}"
echo "--- CSRs this engine implements (the filter set) ---"
"$sim" --describe 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
import sys, json
try: d = json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception: print("(no --describe output; build the engine first)"); sys.exit()
print("vlen       =", d.get("vlen"))
print("andes_csrs =", ", ".join(d.get("andes_csrs", [])) or "(none)")'

===== CELL [8] (markdown) =====
---
# Part 2 -- how QEMU is matched to the vsim engine

You **pick** a vsim engine (e.g. `sim_ax45mpv_premium`). Its spec sheet is fixed
(compiled in). QEMU is generic, so the driver must hand it options that make it
imitate the same chip. Four things to match:

| what | QEMU option | how it is set |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| cpu family | `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` | from an invoke **template** |
| vector width | `vlen=512` | **synced** from the engine's `--describe` |
| **ISA extensions** | `-readconfig engine.cfg` | from the engine's **`--print-qemu-config`** (the demo below) |
| handoff hooks | `-plugin ...,outfile=...,enter_pc=...` | from the run plan (trigger) |

===== CELL [9] (markdown) =====
## The invoke template (with holes to fill)

Each engine carries an argv **template** with `{placeholders}`. QEMU's fast-leg
template (`driver/engine_registry.cpp`):

```cpp
d.invoke.push_back(
  {"fast-leg",
   {"{bin}", "-object",
    "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}",
    "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem", "-cpu",
    "andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}", "-nographic", "-semihosting-config",
    "enable=on,target=native", "-bios", "{elf}", "-plugin",
    "{plugin},outfile={state_out}{trigger}"}});
```

The plan executor fills the holes from a map (`driver/run_plan.cpp`):

```cpp
const std::map<std::string, std::string> m = {
    {"bin", eng->bin_path},   {"elf", plan.elf},
    {"plugin", ctx.plugin_path},
    {"mmap", ctx.mmap_path},  {"mmap_size", std::to_string(ctx.mem_size)},
    {"state_out", state_out},
    {"trigger", lt.plugin_suffix},   // marker: empty;  pc: ",enter_pc=0x..."
    {"vlen", vlen_str},
};
std::vector<std::string> argv = build_argv(*tmpl, m, err);
```

The key match -- `{vlen}` is taken from the **accurate-leg engine's**
descriptor, so QEMU's vector width equals vsim's:

```cpp
// hw-config sync: {vlen} comes from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor.
long vlen = 0;
for (const Step& s : plan.steps)
  if (s.role == "accurate-leg")
    if (const EngineDescriptor* e = find_engine(engines, s.engine_id))
      if (e->vlen > 0) vlen = e->vlen;
```

===== CELL [10] (markdown) =====
## Closing the gap: the engine -> qemu-cpu map

**Current state.** The rv64 fast-leg template **hardcodes** `andes-ax45mpv`
(only `{vlen}` is synced). The shell e2e harness works around this per fixture
with an explicit `QEMU_CPU` (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`):

```
rt_priv_smode|... VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128
```

**The fix is a tiny lookup.** Every vsim engine id is `<family>_<config-variant>`,
and QEMU already ships one `-cpu` per family:

```
qemu_cpu  =  "andes-" + engine_id.split("_")[0]
```

The config-variant suffix (`premium`, `mp2`, `advanced`, `makatau`) is a vsim
micro-architecture tweak; it does **not** change the ISA family, so every variant
of a family shares one QEMU `-cpu` (QEMU models the ISA, not the cycle
micro-arch). `vlen` is matched separately (Part 2).

Grounded against the engines built here and `qemu-system-riscv* -cpu help`:

| vsim engine (id)   | family   | QEMU `-cpu`     | QEMU binary          |
|--------------------|----------|-----------------|----------------------|
| `ax45mpv_premium`  | ax45mpv  | `andes-ax45mpv` | qemu-system-riscv64  |
| `ax45mpv_mp2`      | ax45mpv  | `andes-ax45mpv` | qemu-system-riscv64  |
| `ax46mpv_advanced` | ax46mpv  | `andes-ax46mpv` | qemu-system-riscv64  |
| `ax66_makatau`     | ax66     | `andes-ax66`    | qemu-system-riscv64  |
| `d23`              | d23      | `andes-d23`     | qemu-system-riscv32  |

(rv32 `d23` pairs with `qemu-system-riscv32`; the rv64 engines with
`qemu-system-riscv64`.)

===== CELL [11] (code) =====
%%bash
# LIVE: derive each engine's QEMU -cpu by the rule, and check QEMU provides it.
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ANDESIM_ROOT:=/home/nick/work/andesim}"
qd=$(grep -E '^QEMU_BIN_DIR=' "$ANDESIM_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
avail=$({ "${VSIM_QEMU:-$qd/qemu-system-riscv64}" -cpu help 2>/dev/null
          "${VSIM_QEMU32:-$qd/qemu-system-riscv32}" -cpu help 2>/dev/null; } | awk '{print $1}')
printf "%-20s %-9s %-16s %s\n" "engine id" "family" "QEMU -cpu" "QEMU provides?"
for s in "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_*; do
  case "$s" in *.json|*.txt) continue;; esac
  [ -x "$s" ] || continue
  id=$("$s" --describe 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import sys,json
try: print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("id","").split(":")[-1])
except: pass')
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  fam=${id%%_*}; cpu="andes-$fam"
  echo "$avail" | grep -qx "$cpu" && ok="yes" || ok="no"
  printf "%-20s %-9s %-16s %s\n" "$id" "$fam" "$cpu" "$ok"
done

===== CELL [12] (markdown) =====
## The implemented match: `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig`

Matching only the cpu **family** (above) is not enough: two configs in the same
family can differ in **extensions** -- one enables CoDense or Zfh, another does
not. So the engine publishes its **whole ISA** as a ready-made QEMU cfg.

At vsim **build time**, `config.inc` is distilled into a QEMU `-readconfig` file
-- one `[global]` per extension -- and baked into the binary right next to
`config.inc` (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`, via the
`cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule). `sim_<core> --print-qemu-config`
dumps it; it is the **same spec sheet** the gates in Part 1 come from.

The driver runs that for the chosen engine and hands the file to QEMU's fast leg
(`driver/run_plan.cpp` + `plan_argvs`):

```cpp
// run_plan: stage the accurate engine's cfg under the plan workdir
ctx.qemu_cfg = stage_qemu_cfg(
    wd, run_process({e->bin_path, "--print-qemu-config"}, kQemuCfgProbeMs));
// plan_argvs: append it to the fast (QEMU) leg only
if (step.role == "fast-leg" && !ctx.qemu_cfg.empty()) {
  argv.push_back("-readconfig");
  argv.push_back(ctx.qemu_cfg);
}
```

**Tolerant:** an engine whose binary predates the flag exits non-zero on it, so
`stage_qemu_cfg` returns `""` and the fast leg keeps its plain `-cpu` -- no
regression. **One source:** the Part 1 gates and this cfg are two readings of one
`config.inc`, so QEMU and vsim cannot disagree on the ISA.

> The `-readconfig` globals target `andes-<family>-riscv-cpu`, so they only land
> when `-cpu` picks that same family. The fast-leg template still hardcodes
> `andes-ax45mpv` (the family map above is the remaining piece for *other*
> families), so today this is exact for the `ax45mpv` family -- the demo engine.

The demo below shows both halves: the cfg the engine emits, then
`andesim run --mode hybrid --dry-run` -- which prints the **exact** two-leg
command (QEMU with `-readconfig`, then vsim) **without running anything**.

===== CELL [13] (code) =====
%%bash
# LIVE DEMO: the engine's ISA -> the real QEMU command, end to end.
: "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build}"
: "${ANDESIM_ROOT:=/home/nick/work/andesim}"
: "${ENGINE:=ax45mpv_premium}"
sim="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_${ENGINE}"
if [ ! -x "$sim" ]; then
  sim=$(ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
  ENGINE=$(basename "${sim:-sim_?}" | sed 's/^sim_//')
fi

echo "### 1. sim_${ENGINE} --print-qemu-config  (the engine's full ISA, compact) ###"
"$sim" --print-qemu-config 2>/dev/null \
  | awk '/property/{p=$3} /value/{print p" = "$3}' | tr -d '"' \
  || echo "(rebuild the engine with the converter to populate this)"

# Summary

- **One source of truth:** `config.inc` (the spec sheet). vsim is built from it.
- **`--describe`** re-publishes it: `vlen` + the `andes_csrs` filter list.
- **Drain (QEMU)** packs a superset -- *not* config-gated.
- **Restore + re-drain + verify** filter by `supports_csr(addr)`, which comes
  from `andes_caps_from_config()`. One side filtering is enough, and it must be
  the consumer (writing an absent CSR hangs the debug module).
- **Matching QEMU to the engine:** `{vlen}` synced from `--describe`, **plus** the
  engine's full ISA handed to QEMU via `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig`
  (implemented; preview it with `andesim run --mode hybrid --dry-run`). The cpu
  **family** map (`andes-<family>`) is the remaining piece for non-`ax45mpv`
  families.

### Footnote -- a possible next step

Because drain is a superset, the state file currently contains CSRs the chosen
vsim will ignore. We *could* also gate the drain by passing the engine's
`andes_csrs` list (already known from `--describe`) into the plugin as a new arg.
That would make the producer and consumer follow the same spec sheet, at the cost
of making the state file engine-specific. Not implemented yet -- see the earlier
design discussion.

===== CELL [0] (markdown) =====
# Tutorial: how the softcore config file drives the hybrid handoff

This page explains, in simple steps, **how one file -- the softcore's
`config.inc` -- decides what the QEMU -> vsim handoff does**.

Two questions:

1. **What gets exchanged?** How `config.inc` decides which CSRs QEMU *drains*
   and which CSRs vsim *restores*.
2. **How do the two engines match?** How the driver fills QEMU's command-line
   options so QEMU imitates the same engine you picked for vsim.

## The one big idea (an analogy)

- `config.inc` is the **chip's spec sheet** -- the list of parts this CPU has
  (privilege levels, DSP, stack-safety, ILM/DLM, triggers, PMA, ...).
- **vsim** is a chip **built from that spec sheet**. It physically only has the
  parts the sheet lists. Ask it for a part it does not have and the debug module
  stalls.
- **QEMU** is a **generic imitator**. It can pretend to be many chips. We must
  *tell* it which chip to imitate.

The handoff moves a **save game** (the architectural state: GPRs, FPRs, CSRs,
vector regs) from QEMU to vsim, so vsim can measure the cycle-accurate region.

===== CELL [1] (markdown) =====
## The cast: 3 actors, 1 source of truth

```
        config.inc   (the chip's spec sheet: NDS_* defines)
             |
             |  compiled INTO the vsim binary at build time
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   vsim  sim_<core>    |  has ONLY the parts the sheet lists
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  sim_<core> --describe  ->  { "vlen":..., "andes_csrs":[...] }
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   andesim driver      |  reads --describe, then TELLS QEMU what to imitate
   +-----------------------+
             |
             |  -cpu ...   vlen=...   -plugin ...,outfile=...
             v
   +-----------------------+
   |   QEMU (generic)      |  flexible imitator; matched via options
   +-----------------------+
```

`config.inc` is written once, at chip-build time. Everything else **reads** it:
vsim is compiled from it; `--describe` re-publishes it; the driver uses
`--describe` to gate verification and to fill QEMU's options.

===== CELL [2] (markdown) =====
---
# Part 1 -- what gets exchanged (drain vs restore)

The save game is touched **three** times. Only some are filtered by the spec
sheet.

```
   QEMU (functional)                       vsim (cycle-accurate)
   -----------------                       ---------------------
   run program ...
   hit ROI trigger
        |
   (1) DRAIN  ---- state file (save game) ---->  (2) RESTORE
       pack ALL CSRs                                 unpack ONLY the CSRs
       QEMU exposes                                  the spec sheet lists
       (NOT filtered)                                (caps-gated)
                                                          |
                                                     run the ROI
                                                          |
                                                     (3) RE-DRAIN
                                                     read back ONLY the
                                                     caps-listed CSRs
                                                          |
                                                  cycle figure = mcycle delta
```

| step | who | filtered by config? |
|------|-----|---------------------|
| (1) drain   | QEMU plugin       | **No** -- packs everything QEMU exposes (a superset) |
| (2) restore | vsim ResumeDriver | **Yes** -- writes only CSRs the engine has |
| (3) re-drain| vsim StateDrain   | **Yes** -- reads only CSRs the engine has |
| verify (`--verify`) | andesim driver | **Yes** -- compares only the engine's CSRs |

**Why is drain (1) not filtered?** Loading a CSR the chip does not have would
**hang** the debug module. So the *consumer* (vsim) must filter. The *producer*
(QEMU) is allowed to be lazy and pack extra -- the consumer throws the extra
away. One side filters; that is enough.

===== CELL [3] (markdown) =====
## Step A: config.inc -> a set of "gates"

Real lines from `ax45mpv_premium`'s spec sheet
(`.../Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`; `NDS_CFG_NO`=0, `NDS_CFG_YES`=1):

```verilog
`define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1            // M-only (no U, no S)
`define NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT        `NDS_CFG_NO   // 0 -> ucode absent
`define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT    `NDS_CFG_YES  // 1 -> uitb, jvt present
`define NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB             64           // ILM present -> milmb
`define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER             2            // triggers present
`define NDS_PMA_ENTRIES             4            // PMA present
```

(A full real trace of this engine is the **worked example** at the end.)

At runtime, `andes_caps_from_config()` turns each `NDS_*` macro into a **gate**
(on/off). This is the ONE place that binds a feature to its macro
(`src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`):

```cpp
inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config() {
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);            // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);      // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);          // menvcfg, mcounteren, U-delta CSRs
#endif
  // ... one block per feature ...
  return c;
}
```

A macro that is **absent** reads as "feature off" -- so a core whose config
omits a knob stays safe (never a crash).

===== CELL [4] (markdown) =====
## Step B: a gate -> a yes/no per CSR

`supports_csr(addr)` maps a CSR address to its gate and answers "does this
engine have it?" (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`):

```cpp
constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const {
  const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);   // addr -> which gate
  return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);     // ALWAYS, or gate set
}
```

So the chain is:

```
config.inc  --andes_caps_from_config-->  gates  --supports_csr(addr)-->  yes/no
```

## Step C: the gate filters restore and re-drain

**(2) restore** -- vsim writes a CSR only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) write_csr_tolerant(addr, state.andes.field);
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)        // one line per CSR; gate per line
#undef X
```

**(3) re-drain** -- vsim reads a CSR back only if its engine has it
(`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`):

```cpp
#define X(field, addr, name) \
  if (caps_.supports_csr(addr)) \
    state.andes.field = read_register_64(bus_, regno_csr(addr));
    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
#undef X
```

The same `caps_` is built from config at startup and handed to both
(`src/simulator.hpp`):

```cpp

                            hybrid::andes_caps_from_config());
```

**(1) drain** -- QEMU packs every CSR its gdbstub exposes, with **no** caps gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`):

```c
// The vsim caps gate decides which of these the cycle engine actually
// restores, so draining an absent-on-vsim CSR here is harmless.
#define HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD(field, addr, name)  \
    s.m_ext.field = read_reg64(v->m_ext_##field); \
    if (v->m_ext_##field) has_m_ext = 1;
    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD)
#undef HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD
```

Picture the filter (config = M-only, DSP off, ECC off):

   supports_csr?    yes       NO       yes        NO

                    v                   v

```

# Part 2 -- how QEMU is matched to the vsim engine

You **pick** a vsim engine (e.g. `sim_ax45mpv_premium`). Its spec sheet is fixed
(compiled in). QEMU is generic, so the driver must hand it options that make it
imitate the same chip. Four things to match:

| what | QEMU option | how it is set |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| cpu family | `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` | from an invoke **template** |
| vector width | `vlen=512` | **synced** from the engine's `--describe` |
| **ISA extensions** | `-readconfig engine.cfg` | from the engine's **`--print-qemu-config`** (the demo below) |
| handoff hooks | `-plugin ...,outfile=...,enter_pc=...` | from the run plan (trigger) |

===== CELL [9] (markdown) =====
## The invoke template (with holes to fill)

Each engine carries an argv **template** with `{placeholders}`. QEMU's fast-leg
template (`driver/engine_registry.cpp`):

```cpp
d.invoke.push_back(
  {"fast-leg",
   {"{bin}", "-object",
    "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}",
    "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem", "-cpu",
    "andes-ax45mpv,vlen={vlen}", "-nographic", "-semihosting-config",
    "enable=on,target=native", "-bios", "{elf}", "-plugin",
    "{plugin},outfile={state_out}{trigger}"}});
```

The plan executor fills the holes from a map (`driver/run_plan.cpp`):

```cpp
const std::map<std::string, std::string> m = {
    {"bin", eng->bin_path},   {"elf", plan.elf},
    {"plugin", ctx.plugin_path},
    {"mmap", ctx.mmap_path},  {"mmap_size", std::to_string(ctx.mem_size)},
    {"state_out", state_out},
    {"trigger", lt.plugin_suffix},   // marker: empty;  pc: ",enter_pc=0x..."
    {"vlen", vlen_str},
};
std::vector<std::string> argv = build_argv(*tmpl, m, err);
```

The key match -- `{vlen}` is taken from the **accurate-leg engine's**
descriptor, so QEMU's vector width equals vsim's:

```cpp
// hw-config sync: {vlen} comes from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor.
long vlen = 0;
for (const Step& s : plan.steps)
  if (s.role == "accurate-leg")
    if (const EngineDescriptor* e = find_engine(engines, s.engine_id))
      if (e->vlen > 0) vlen = e->vlen;
```

## Closing the gap: the engine -> qemu-cpu map

**Current state.** The rv64 fast-leg template **hardcodes** `andes-ax45mpv`
(only `{vlen}` is synced). The shell e2e harness works around this per fixture
with an explicit `QEMU_CPU` (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`):

```

```

**The fix is a tiny lookup.** Every vsim engine id is `<family>_<config-variant>`,
and QEMU already ships one `-cpu` per family:

```
qemu_cpu  =  "andes-" + engine_id.split("_")[0]
```

The config-variant suffix (`premium`, `mp2`, `advanced`, `makatau`) is a vsim
micro-architecture tweak; it does **not** change the ISA family, so every variant
of a family shares one QEMU `-cpu` (QEMU models the ISA, not the cycle
micro-arch). `vlen` is matched separately (Part 2).

Grounded against the engines built here and `qemu-system-riscv* -cpu help`:

| `d23`              | d23      | `andes-d23`     | qemu-system-riscv32  |

(rv32 `d23` pairs with `qemu-system-riscv32`; the rv64 engines with
`qemu-system-riscv64`.)

## The implemented match: `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig`

Matching only the cpu **family** (above) is not enough: two configs in the same
family can differ in **extensions** -- one enables CoDense or Zfh, another does
not. So the engine publishes its **whole ISA** as a ready-made QEMU cfg.

At vsim **build time**, `config.inc` is distilled into a QEMU `-readconfig` file
-- one `[global]` per extension -- and baked into the binary right next to
`config.inc` (`cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake`, via the
`cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule). `sim_<core> --print-qemu-config`
dumps it; it is the **same spec sheet** the gates in Part 1 come from.

The driver runs that for the chosen engine and hands the file to QEMU's fast leg
(`driver/run_plan.cpp` + `plan_argvs`):

```cpp
// run_plan: stage the accurate engine's cfg under the plan workdir
ctx.qemu_cfg = stage_qemu_cfg(
    wd, run_process({e->bin_path, "--print-qemu-config"}, kQemuCfgProbeMs));
// plan_argvs: append it to the fast (QEMU) leg only
if (step.role == "fast-leg" && !ctx.qemu_cfg.empty()) {
  argv.push_back("-readconfig");
  argv.push_back(ctx.qemu_cfg);
}
```

**Tolerant:** an engine whose binary predates the flag exits non-zero on it, so
`stage_qemu_cfg` returns `""` and the fast leg keeps its plain `-cpu` -- no
regression. **One source:** the Part 1 gates and this cfg are two readings of one
`config.inc`, so QEMU and vsim cannot disagree on the ISA.

> The `-readconfig` globals target `andes-<family>-riscv-cpu`, so they only land
> when `-cpu` picks that same family. The fast-leg template still hardcodes
> `andes-ax45mpv` (the family map above is the remaining piece for *other*
> families), so today this is exact for the `ax45mpv` family -- the demo engine.

The demo below shows both halves: the cfg the engine emits, then
`andesim run --mode hybrid --dry-run` -- which prints the **exact** two-leg
command (QEMU with `-readconfig`, then vsim) **without running anything**.

# Summary

- **One source of truth:** `config.inc` (the spec sheet). vsim is built from it.
- **`--describe`** re-publishes it: `vlen` + the `andes_csrs` filter list.
- **Drain (QEMU)** packs a superset -- *not* config-gated.
- **Restore + re-drain + verify** filter by `supports_csr(addr)`, which comes
  from `andes_caps_from_config()`. One side filtering is enough, and it must be
  the consumer (writing an absent CSR hangs the debug module).
- **Matching QEMU to the engine:** `{vlen}` synced from `--describe`, **plus** the
  engine's full ISA handed to QEMU via `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig`
  (implemented; preview it with `andesim run --mode hybrid --dry-run`). The cpu
  **family** map (`andes-<family>`) is the remaining piece for non-`ax45mpv`
  families.

### Footnote -- a possible next step

Because drain is a superset, the state file currently contains CSRs the chosen
vsim will ignore. We *could* also gate the drain by passing the engine's
`andes_csrs` list (already known from `--describe`) into the plugin as a new arg.
That would make the producer and consumer follow the same spec sheet, at the cost
of making the state file engine-specific. Not implemented yet -- see the earlier
design discussion.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regenerate docs/config_gating_tutorial.ipynb.

Redesign goals (per PM): concept first, then depth; every demo clean, meaningful,
and shown FROM THE andesim COMMAND LINE (not by poking sim_/qemu directly).

Structure (~11 cells):
  Part 0  the one idea + a picture (concept, no code)
  Part 1  3 live demos, each one `andesim` command:
            list engines -> run --dry-run (MATCH) -> run (the cycle payoff)
  Part 2  short "under the hood" appendix (FILTER + MATCH mechanics, file pointers)
  Summary
"""
import json, sys

cells = []

def md(text):
    cells.append(("markdown", text))

def code(text):
    cells.append(("code", text))

# Shared, portable preamble for the live demos: resolve the repo root and the
# andesim binary without hardcoding a user path; pick the first vsim engine if
# ENGINE is not overridden; skip gracefully if nothing is built.
PREAMBLE = (
    'ROOT="${ANDESIM_ROOT:-$(cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null '
    '|| echo .)" && pwd)}"\n'
    'ANDESIM="$ROOT/build/andesim"\n'
    '[ -x "$ANDESIM" ] || { echo "(build andesim first: bash $ROOT/scripts/build_all.sh)"; exit 0; }'
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Part 0
md(r"""# How `andesim` keeps QEMU and vsim in sync

You ask `andesim` one thing: **run my program and tell me how many cycles the
hot region takes.**

It answers with two engines and a hand-off between them:

- **QEMU** -- a *fast, generic* engine. It runs your program up to the hot
  region. It can pretend to be many different chips.
- **vsim** -- a *cycle-accurate* engine. It takes over the live state, runs the
  hot region, and counts the cycles. It is **one specific chip**, built from
  that chip's spec sheet, `config.inc`.

The whole trick is **one rule**: both engines must agree on the **same chip**.
Otherwise the state QEMU hands over does not fit the chip vsim models.

The single source of that agreement is **`config.inc`**, baked into the vsim
engine at build time. From it, `andesim` keeps **two promises**:

| promise | meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **MATCH**  | make QEMU imitate the *same chip* vsim is -- same ISA, same vector width. |
| **FILTER** | move only the architectural state this chip actually has (skip parts it does not). |

Everything below is shown **from where you sit: the `andesim` command line.**
Three commands, then a short look under the hood.""")

md(r"""## The picture

```
                    config.inc  (the chip's spec sheet)
                         |  baked into the vsim engine at build
                         v
   you pick a chip:   andesim run --engine vsim:<chip> ...
                         |
       andesim reads the chip, then drives both engines:
                         |
   +-------- MATCH ------+------ FILTER --------+
   |                                            |
   v                                            v
 QEMU imitates <chip>                  only <chip>'s state is
 (same ISA + vlen),                    restored into vsim
 runs program -> hot region                   |
   |                                          |
   +------ hands the live state over ----------+
                         |
                         v
          vsim (<chip>) runs the hot region -> cycle count
```

`config.inc` is written once. vsim is built from it; `andesim` reads it (through
the engine) to keep both promises. You never touch it -- you just **pick a
chip**.""")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Part 1
md(r"""---
# Part 1 -- see it from `andesim`

Three commands. Each is something you would actually type.

1. **`andesim list engines`** -- the chips you can pick.
2. **`andesim run --dry-run`** -- watch the **MATCH** promise: the exact QEMU
   command andesim builds.
3. **`andesim run`** -- the payoff: your cycle number.""")

md(r"""## 1. `andesim list engines` -- the chips you can pick

`andesim` finds every vsim engine and reads each one's spec **for you**. Notice
the chips *differ*: `ax66_makatau` has `vlen=128`, `d23` is 32-bit with no
vector. That per-chip difference is exactly why andesim must MATCH and FILTER
for the chip you choose.""")

code('%%bash\n' + PREAMBLE + '\n"$ANDESIM" list engines')

md(r"""## 2. `andesim run --dry-run` -- the MATCH promise, in the open

`--dry-run` builds the **exact** commands andesim would run, and prints them
**without executing**. Read the QEMU (fast) leg and the MATCH is right there:

- `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` -- the vector width **synced** from the chip.
- `-readconfig .../qemu.cfg` -- the chip's **full ISA**, distilled from
  `config.inc` at build time (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`, ...).

The second leg is vsim, told to resume from the state file QEMU writes. (Long
directories are trimmed below so the matched options stand out.)""")

code('%%bash\n' + PREAMBLE + '\n'
     'ENGINE="${ENGINE:-$("$ANDESIM" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk \'/^vsim:/{print $1; exit}\')}"\n'
     'ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"\n'
     '[ -n "$ENGINE" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ] || { echo "(need a vsim engine + a fixture ELF)"; exit 0; }\n'
     'echo "# engine: $ENGINE"\n'
     '"$ANDESIM" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1 \\\n'
     "  | sed -E 's#/[^ ,]*/##g'")

md(r"""## 3. `andesim run` -- the payoff

Drop `--dry-run` and it runs for real: the matched QEMU executes up to the hot
region, hands the live state to vsim, and vsim runs the region and reports the
cycle count. The **`[marker window_cycles]`** line is your answer.""")

code('%%bash\n' + PREAMBLE + '\n'
     'ENGINE="${ENGINE:-$("$ANDESIM" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk \'/^vsim:/{print $1; exit}\')}"\n'
     'ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"\n'
     '[ -n "$ENGINE" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ] || { echo "(need a vsim engine + a fixture ELF)"; exit 0; }\n'
     'echo "# engine: $ENGINE"\n'
     '"$ANDESIM" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1 \\\n'
     "  | grep -vE 'Copyright|^Version'")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Part 2
md(r"""---
# Part 2 -- under the hood (how the two promises are kept)

Both promises are two readings of the **same `config.inc`**, so QEMU and vsim
can never disagree on the chip.

### FILTER -- move only the state this chip has

`config.inc` becomes a yes/no answer per CSR:

```
config.inc --(andes_caps_from_config)--> gates --(supports_csr addr)--> yes / no
```

The vsim engine restores and re-reads a CSR **only when `supports_csr()` says
yes** (writing a CSR the chip lacks would hang its debug module). That same set
is published as the engine's `andes_csrs`, and `andesim` uses it to compare
**only this chip's CSRs** on `--verify` (`driver/state_diff.cpp`).

QEMU, by contrast, **drains a superset** with no gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) -- one side filtering is enough, and it must be
the *consumer* (vsim), because reading extra in QEMU is harmless but writing
extra into vsim is not.

### MATCH -- make QEMU the same chip

At vsim **build time**, `config.inc` is distilled into a QEMU `-readconfig` file
(one `[global]` per extension) and baked into the engine. `sim_<chip>
--print-qemu-config` dumps it. `andesim` runs that for the chosen engine and
injects `-readconfig` into the QEMU leg only (`driver/run_plan.cpp`:
`stage_qemu_cfg` + `plan_argvs`) -- the `-readconfig` line you saw in Demo 2. An
engine that predates the flag makes andesim fall back to a plain `-cpu`, so
there is no regression.

> The exact `NDS_*`-macro-to-CSR mapping lives in the vsim engine
> (`andes_caps_from_config` / `supports_csr`), built from `config.inc`. This page
> stays at the andesim level on purpose.""")

md(r"""---
# Summary

- You **pick a chip**; `andesim` makes the two engines agree on it.
- **MATCH** (`--dry-run` shows it): QEMU gets the chip's `vlen` and its full ISA
  via `-readconfig`, both from `config.inc`.
- **FILTER**: only the chip's CSRs are restored / re-read / verified;
  `supports_csr()` (from `config.inc`) is the gate. QEMU drains a superset; the
  consumer filters.
- **One source of truth:** `config.inc`. Everything else just reads it.

Three commands to remember:

```
andesim list engines        # the chips
andesim run --dry-run ...    # the matched command (MATCH)
andesim run ...              # the cycle figure
```""")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- emit
def src(text):
    lines = text.split("\n")
    return [l + "\n" for l in lines[:-1]] + [lines[-1]]

nb = {
    "cells": [],
    "metadata": {
        "kernelspec": {"display_name": "Bash", "language": "bash", "name": "bash"},
        "language_info": {"name": "bash"},
    },
    "nbformat": 4,
    "nbformat_minor": 5,
}
for i, (kind, text) in enumerate(cells):
    cell = {"cell_type": kind, "id": f"c{i}", "metadata": {}, "source": src(text)}
    if kind == "code":
        cell["outputs"] = []
        cell["execution_count"] = None
    nb["cells"].append(cell)

out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "docs/config_gating_tutorial.ipynb"
with open(out, "w") as f:
    json.dump(nb, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=True)
    f.write("\n")
print(f"wrote {out}: {len(nb['cells'])} cells")

========== CELL [0] markdown ==========
# How `andesim` keeps QEMU and vsim in sync

You ask `andesim` one thing: **run my program and tell me how many cycles the
hot region takes.**

It answers with two engines and a hand-off between them:

- **QEMU** -- a *fast, generic* engine. It runs your program up to the hot
  region. It can pretend to be many different chips.
- **vsim** -- a *cycle-accurate* engine. It takes over the live state, runs the
  hot region, and counts the cycles. It is **one specific chip**, built from
  that chip's spec sheet, `config.inc`.

The whole trick is **one rule**: both engines must agree on the **same chip**.
Otherwise the state QEMU hands over does not fit the chip vsim models.

The single source of that agreement is **`config.inc`**, baked into the vsim
engine at build time. From it, `andesim` keeps **two promises**:

| promise | meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **MATCH**  | make QEMU imitate the *same chip* vsim is -- same ISA, same vector width. |
| **FILTER** | move only the architectural state this chip actually has (skip parts it does not). |

Everything below is shown **from where you sit: the `andesim` command line.**
Three commands, then a short look under the hood.

========== CELL [1] markdown ==========
## The picture

```
                    config.inc  (the chip's spec sheet)
                         |  baked into the vsim engine at build
                         v
   you pick a chip:   andesim run --engine vsim:<chip> ...
                         |
       andesim reads the chip, then drives both engines:
                         |
   +-------- MATCH ------+------ FILTER --------+
   |                                            |
   v                                            v
 QEMU imitates <chip>                  only <chip>'s state is
 (same ISA + vlen),                    restored into vsim
 runs program -> hot region                   |
   |                                          |
   +------ hands the live state over ----------+
                         |
                         v
          vsim (<chip>) runs the hot region -> cycle count
```

`config.inc` is written once. vsim is built from it; `andesim` reads it (through
the engine) to keep both promises. You never touch it -- you just **pick a
chip**.

========== CELL [2] markdown ==========
---
# Part 1 -- see it from `andesim`

Three commands. Each is something you would actually type.

1. **`andesim list engines`** -- the chips you can pick.
2. **`andesim run --dry-run`** -- watch the **MATCH** promise: the exact QEMU
   command andesim builds.
3. **`andesim run`** -- the payoff: your cycle number.

========== CELL [3] markdown ==========
## 1. `andesim list engines` -- the chips you can pick

`andesim` finds every vsim engine and reads each one's spec **for you**. Notice
the chips *differ*: `ax66_makatau` has `vlen=128`, `d23` is 32-bit with no
vector. That per-chip difference is exactly why andesim must MATCH and FILTER
for the chip you choose.

========== CELL [5] markdown ==========
## 2. `andesim run --dry-run` -- the MATCH promise, in the open

`--dry-run` builds the **exact** commands andesim would run, and prints them
**without executing**. Read the QEMU (fast) leg and the MATCH is right there:

- `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` -- the vector width **synced** from the chip.
- `-readconfig .../qemu.cfg` -- the chip's **full ISA**, distilled from
  `config.inc` at build time (CoDense, Zfh, Zb*, `xandesv5isa`, ...).

The second leg is vsim, told to resume from the state file QEMU writes. (Long
directories are trimmed below so the matched options stand out.)

========== CELL [7] markdown ==========
## 3. `andesim run` -- the payoff

Drop `--dry-run` and it runs for real: the matched QEMU executes up to the hot
region, hands the live state to vsim, and vsim runs the region and reports the
cycle count. The **`[marker window_cycles]`** line is your answer.

========== CELL [9] markdown ==========
---
# Part 2 -- under the hood (how the two promises are kept)

Both promises are two readings of the **same `config.inc`**, so QEMU and vsim
can never disagree on the chip.

### FILTER -- move only the state this chip has

`config.inc` becomes a yes/no answer per CSR:

```
config.inc --(andes_caps_from_config)--> gates --(supports_csr addr)--> yes / no
```

The vsim engine restores and re-reads a CSR **only when `supports_csr()` says
yes** (writing a CSR the chip lacks would hang its debug module). That same set
is published as the engine's `andes_csrs`, and `andesim` uses it to compare
**only this chip's CSRs** on `--verify` (`driver/state_diff.cpp`).

QEMU, by contrast, **drains a superset** with no gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) -- one side filtering is enough, and it must be
the *consumer* (vsim), because reading extra in QEMU is harmless but writing
extra into vsim is not.

### MATCH -- make QEMU the same chip

At vsim **build time**, `config.inc` is distilled into a QEMU `-readconfig` file
(one `[global]` per extension) and baked into the engine. `sim_<chip>
--print-qemu-config` dumps it. `andesim` runs that for the chosen engine and
injects `-readconfig` into the QEMU leg only (`driver/run_plan.cpp`:
`stage_qemu_cfg` + `plan_argvs`) -- the `-readconfig` line you saw in Demo 2. An
engine that predates the flag makes andesim fall back to a plain `-cpu`, so
there is no regression.

> The exact `NDS_*`-macro-to-CSR mapping lives in the vsim engine
> (`andes_caps_from_config` / `supports_csr`), built from `config.inc`. This page
> stays at the andesim level on purpose.

========== CELL [10] markdown ==========
---
# Summary

- You **pick a chip**; `andesim` makes the two engines agree on it.
- **MATCH** (`--dry-run` shows it): QEMU gets the chip's `vlen` and its full ISA
  via `-readconfig`, both from `config.inc`.
- **FILTER**: only the chip's CSRs are restored / re-read / verified;
  `supports_csr()` (from `config.inc`) is the gate. QEMU drains a superset; the
  consumer filters.
- **One source of truth:** `config.inc`. Everything else just reads it.

Three commands to remember:

```
andesim list engines        # the chips
andesim run --dry-run ...    # the matched command (MATCH)
andesim run ...              # the cycle figure
```

# Part 2 -- under the hood (how the two promises are kept)

Both promises are two readings of the **same `config.inc`**, so QEMU and vsim
can never disagree on the chip.

### FILTER -- move only the state this chip has

`config.inc` becomes a yes/no answer per CSR:

```
config.inc --(andes_caps_from_config)--> gates --(supports_csr addr)--> yes / no
```

The vsim engine restores and re-reads a CSR **only when `supports_csr()` says
yes** (writing a CSR the chip lacks would hang its debug module). That same set
is published as the engine's `andes_csrs`, and `andesim` uses it to compare
**only this chip's CSRs** on `--verify` (`driver/state_diff.cpp`).

QEMU, by contrast, **drains a superset** with no gate
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) -- one side filtering is enough, and it must be
the *consumer* (vsim), because reading extra in QEMU is harmless but writing
extra into vsim is not.

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}
