#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --dry-run applies to ALL run modes (fast, cycle, hybrid): it prints the exact
# command(s) andesim WOULD spawn, shell-quoted, and executes nothing. Regression
# guard for the bug where fast/cycle silently ignored --dry-run and ran the
# program (e.g. `run --mode fast hello.elf --dry-run` printed "hello").
#
# Layers:
#   1. fast   (always; needs only build/andesim + a fixture ELF): prints the
#      full qemu command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   2. cycle  (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise): the vsim standalone
#      command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   3. hybrid (regression): still prints 2 commands.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command and runs nothing. Use the
#    reported arg order (flag AFTER the ELF) to lock the repro.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-machine andes_ae350' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing the qemu command: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-bios' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing -bios <elf>: $out"
ok "fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command, executes nothing"

# Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does (VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP cycle + hybrid --dry-run: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi
id="vsim:$(basename "$SIM" | sed 's/^sim_//')"

# 2. cycle: standalone vsim engine, --dry-run previews its command, runs nothing.
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --dry-run \
      --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "$(basename "$SIM")" \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run missing the vsim command: $out"
ok "cycle: --dry-run prints the vsim standalone command, executes nothing"

# 3. hybrid regression: still 2 commands (probe -> stage -> inject path intact).
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
      --dry-run --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 2 command' \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run regression: not 2 commands: $out"
ok "hybrid: --dry-run still prints 2 commands"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F7 contract: `run --mode fast` -- QEMU-only, transparent passthrough.
# Three layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): passthrough_argv fills the qemu `standalone`
#      invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) and appends the post-`--` engine args
#      verbatim -- including a `-gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. CLI error paths (no engine needed): missing --mode, unknown model,
#      missing ELF, an extra positional, and engine!=qemu each exit 2 with a
#      clear message.
#   3. real passthrough (needs built qemu + a fixture): launch
#      `run --mode fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::PORT -S`; the gdbstub port opens and
#      qemu halts at reset -- the done-when "port opens, halts, debugger
#      connects". exec_passthrough's exit-code propagation is already covered
#      by the F5 infra test (and observed here only indirectly).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: the argv-assembly contract carries the passthrough behavior
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (passthrough_argv) failed"

# assert `$BIN run ...` exits with $1 and its combined output matches regex $2
expect_rc_match() {
  local want_rc="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want_rc for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "output missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2. CLI error paths (deterministic; no qemu)
expect_rc_match 2 'mode .* is required.*--help' "$BIN" run
expect_rc_match 2 "unknown model 'bogus'"    "$BIN" run --mode bogus p.elf
expect_rc_match 2 'missing ELF.*workload'     "$BIN" run --mode fast
expect_rc_match 2 'engine args go after --'  "$BIN" run --mode fast a.elf b.elf
expect_rc_match 2 "engine must be 'qemu'"    "$BIN" run --mode fast --engine vsim:x p.elf

# 3. real passthrough: a frozen-at-reset gdbstub port opens (guarded on artifacts)
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  PORT=$(( 40000 + (RANDOM % 20000) ))
  BG=""
  cleanup() { [ -n "${BG:-}" ] && kill "$BG" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "tcp::$PORT" 2>/dev/null; true; }
  trap cleanup EXIT
  # -S halts the cpu at reset, so the stub listens regardless of the ELF body.
  "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ELF" -- -gdb "tcp::$PORT" -S </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  BG=$!
  opened=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    if timeout 1 bash -c ">/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT" 2>/dev/null; then opened=1; break; fi
    sleep 0.25
  done
  cleanup; trap - EXIT; wait "$BG" 2>/dev/null
  [ "$opened" -eq 1 ] || fail "fast passthrough: gdbstub port $PORT never opened"
  echo "[ok] real fast passthrough: qemu gdbstub halted + listening on :$PORT"
else
  echo "[skip] real fast run: qemu and/or fixture not built ($QEMU / $ELF)"
fi

Here's the plan before I touch anything.

## Goal
`andesim run --mode fast prog.elf` should auto-pick `qemu-system-riscv32` for an rv32 ELF and `qemu-system-riscv64` for an rv64 ELF. **Today it always defaults to rv64** unless you pass `--engine qemu32`.

## The source of truth = the ELF itself
Every ELF carries a class byte, `e_ident[EI_CLASS]` (1 = rv32, 2 = rv64). The repo's ELF reader already reads exactly this byte (`elf_syms.cpp:56`). So we read it straight from the binary you are about to run - no guessing.

Good news: the rv32 side is **already wired** in `builtin_qemu_arch(32)` (it picks `qemu-system-riscv32` + `-cpu andes-d23`). `run_fast` just never *chooses* 32. So the change is small.

1. **Add `elf_xlen(path)` -> 32 / 64 / 0** to `elf_syms.cpp` (reuses the existing `<elf.h>` slurp+read pattern). This is the "identify rv32 or rv64" piece.
2. **Use it in `run_fast`:** if `--engine` is not given, call `elf_xlen(elf)` and pass 32/64 to `builtin_qemu_arch()`. Explicit `--engine qemu32/qemu64` still wins. If the ELF can't be read, keep today's rv64 default (no regression).

- If you pass `--engine qemu64` on an rv32 ELF (explicit contradicts the ELF), the explicit choice **wins**, plus a one-line warning. Override beats auto-detect.

SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the driver respects the ELF's class (rv32/rv64).
#   - fast  auto-picks qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (dry-run shows it).
#   - cycle/hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen, both ways,
#     with one shared clear error and WITHOUT launching the engine.
# The rv64 direction is fully testable now (rv64 fixtures + the rv32 d23 engine);
# the rv32-ELF direction is added in F3 once rv32 fixtures exist.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF"

# fast: an rv64 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv64 (no --engine). --dry-run so
# nothing runs; the picked binary is visible in the previewed command.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"

# Resolve the rv32 engine (d23). SKIP the cycle check if it is not built.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
if [ ! -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
  ok "SKIP cycle arch-match: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

# cycle: an rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine -> clear arch-mismatch error, exit 2,
# WITHOUT launching the sim.
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
      --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
  || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"

# ROADMAP: rv32 support (rv32 alongside rv64, end to end)

**Goal.** andesim runs rv32 ELFs as a first-class peer of rv64: `fast` picks the
matching `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the ELF, `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an
engine whose width differs, and the runtime + fixtures build for both arches from
two toolchains.

## Shared facts (one source of truth)

- The ELF class byte `e_ident[EI_CLASS]` (1=rv32, 2=rv64) is the truth for an
  ELF's width. The repo's ELF reader already reads it (`elf_syms.cpp`).
- **Two separate toolchains** (not one multilib):
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` = rv64 (`nds64le`, `riscv64-unknown-elf-`),
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32 (`nds32le`, `riscv32-unknown-elf-`).
- rv32 baseline = `-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d` (the d23 engine has m,a,f,d,c),

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the andesim runtime builds for BOTH arches from two
# toolchains. ARCH=rv64 (default) -> build/runtime/, ARCH=rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32/.
# The produced objects must be the right ELF class (rv64=ELFCLASS64, rv32=ELFCLASS32).
#
#   rv64 always runs (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32; SKIPs if unset.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }
elf_class() { od -An -j4 -N1 -tu1 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }   # 1=ELF32 2=ELF64

TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC64" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

# rv64 (default ARCH): library + crt0 land in build/runtime and are ELFCLASS64.
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv64 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv64 runtime build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: missing build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/crt0.o")" = "2" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS64"
ok "rv64 runtime -> build/runtime (ELFCLASS64)"

# rv32: needs the second toolchain. SKIP cleanly if absent.
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 runtime: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv32 runtime build failed (ARCH=rv32, HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$TC32)"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: missing build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/crt0.o")" = "1" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS32"
ok "rv32 runtime -> build/runtime/rv32 (ELFCLASS32)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the user-facing andes-sim runtime (runtime/). Produces
# build/runtime/ with libandes_sim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andes-sim.ld,
# andes-sim.specs and include/andes_sim/ROI.h -- the artifacts users link
# with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
#
# Self-contained: loads HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN from the repo-root config.env the
# same way setup.sh does, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

if [[ ! -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]]; then
  echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Resolve the toolchain. An exported HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN in the environment
# wins; otherwise fall back to config.env (created from the template on
# first use, matching setup.sh).
if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]]; then
      echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi

if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

make -C "$SRC" TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
#
# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }

# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi
[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"

# rv64 (required).
if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"

# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
else
  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
fi

# ROADMAP: rv32 support (rv32 alongside rv64, end to end)

**Goal.** andesim runs rv32 ELFs as a first-class peer of rv64: `fast` picks the
matching `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the ELF, `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an
engine whose width differs, and the runtime + fixtures build for both arches from
two toolchains.

## Shared facts (one source of truth)

- The ELF class byte `e_ident[EI_CLASS]` (1=rv32, 2=rv64) is the truth for an
  ELF's width. The repo's ELF reader already reads it (`elf_syms.cpp`).
- **Two separate toolchains** (not one multilib):
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` = rv64 (`nds64le`, `riscv64-unknown-elf-`),
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32 (`nds32le`, `riscv32-unknown-elf-`).
- rv32 baseline = `-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d` (the d23 engine has m,a,f,d,c),
  mirroring rv64's `rv64gc/lp64d`.
- **Runtime layout (decided):** rv64 stays at `build/runtime/` (back-compat with
  the documented `-B build/runtime` link command); rv32 lands at
  `build/runtime/rv32/`. Linked with `-B build/runtime/rv32`.

## Features

| ID | Feature | Key files | Depends | State |
|----|---------|-----------|---------|-------|
| F1 | arch-aware run dispatch | `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}`, `elf_syms_test.cpp`, `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` | - | **DONE** |
| F2 | dual-arch runtime | `runtime/Makefile`, `config.env.example`, `scripts/build_runtime.sh` | config `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` | TODO |
| F3 | rv32 fixtures | `tests/fixtures/Makefile`, new rv32 fixtures | F2 | TODO |
| F4 | wire + docs | `scripts/build_all.sh`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | F1-F3 | TODO |

### F1 - arch-aware run dispatch
- `elf_xlen(path)` -> 32 / 64 / 0 (reads only `e_ident`).
- **fast**: no `--engine` -> auto-pick `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the
  ELF. Explicit `--engine qemu32/qemu64` wins (+ warn if it contradicts the ELF).
- **cycle + hybrid**: one shared `elf_engine_arch_error(elf, eng)` (DRY) rejects
  an ELF whose class != the engine's `xlen`; identical wording. hybrid keeps its
  extra "fast leg is rv64-only" guard (`hybrid_hw_check`).
- Tested now: `elf_xlen` unit (32 fabricated + 64 real fixture + 0 garbage);
  `cycle --engine vsim:d23 <rv64.elf>` errors. The rv32-ELF directions are
  smoke-tested in F3 (no rv32 fixture yet).

### F2 - dual-arch runtime
- Parameterize `runtime/Makefile` by `ARCH` (rv64 default): CC prefix, `-march`/
  `-mabi`, and `OUT` (`build/runtime` for rv64, `build/runtime/rv32` for rv32).
- `config.env.example`: add `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`.
- `scripts/build_runtime.sh`: build both arches; also fix its stale artifact
  names (it echoes `libandes_sim_runtime.a`/`andes-sim.specs`; the Makefile now
  produces `libandesim_runtime.a`/`andesim.specs`).

### F3 - rv32 fixtures
- Parameterize `tests/fixtures/Makefile` by `ARCH`; add >=1 asm + >=1 C rv32
  fixture (the C one links the rv32 runtime from F2).
- Enables the real rv32 end-to-end + the rv32-direction smoke tests for F1.

### F4 - wire + docs
- `scripts/build_all.sh runtime` builds both arches.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: rv32 section (two toolchains, the rv32 link command, the
  arch-match rules for fast/cycle/hybrid).

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md F3) ---------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                 $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                 $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1+F3 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the driver respects the ELF's class (rv32/rv64).
#   - fast  auto-picks qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (and runs it).
#   - cycle/hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen, both ways,
#     with one shared clear error and WITHOUT launching the engine.
# Independent, gated sections: rv64 always; the rv32 directions need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (build the rv32 fixture) and skip cleanly without it.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF"

vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)

# --- A. fast: an rv64 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv64 (no --engine) ------
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"

# --- B. cycle: rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run -------
if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
    || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
fi

# --- C. rv32 directions: need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 to build an rv32 fixture -----
TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 directions: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
rv32elf="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rv32_c_hello.elf"
[ -f "$rv32elf" ] || fail "rv32 fixture missing after build: $rv32elf"

# fast: the rv32 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv32.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv32' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv32 for an rv32 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv32 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv32"

# fast: and it actually runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime end to end).
QD=$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)
if [ -x "$QD/qemu-system-riscv32" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hello from QEMU1' \
    || fail "rv32 fixture did not run/print on qemu-system-riscv32: $out"
  ok "fast: rv32 fixture runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime works)"
else
  ok "SKIP rv32 run: no qemu-system-riscv32 under $QD"
fi

# cycle: the rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error.
rv64eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim" && $4=="64"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
    || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
fi

# ROADMAP: rv32 support (rv32 alongside rv64, end to end)

**Goal.** andesim runs rv32 ELFs as a first-class peer of rv64: `fast` picks the
matching `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the ELF, `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an
engine whose width differs, and the runtime + fixtures build for both arches from
two toolchains.

## Shared facts (one source of truth)

- The ELF class byte `e_ident[EI_CLASS]` (1=rv32, 2=rv64) is the truth for an
  ELF's width. The repo's ELF reader already reads it (`elf_syms.cpp`).
- **Two separate toolchains** (not one multilib):
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` = rv64 (`nds64le`, `riscv64-unknown-elf-`),
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32 (`nds32le`, `riscv32-unknown-elf-`).
- rv32 baseline = `-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d` (the d23 engine has m,a,f,d,c),
  mirroring rv64's `rv64gc/lp64d`.
- **Runtime layout (decided):** rv64 stays at `build/runtime/` (back-compat with
  the documented `-B build/runtime` link command); rv32 lands at
  `build/runtime/rv32/`. Linked with `-B build/runtime/rv32`.

## Features

| ID | Feature | Key files | Depends | State |
|----|---------|-----------|---------|-------|
| F1 | arch-aware run dispatch | `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}`, `elf_syms_test.cpp`, `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` | - | **DONE** |
| F2 | dual-arch runtime | `runtime/Makefile`, `config.env{,.example}`, `scripts/build_runtime.sh`, `runtime/{handler.c,vplat_syscalls.c}` (rv64-ism fixes) | config `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` | **DONE** |
| F3 | rv32 fixtures | `tests/fixtures/Makefile`, new rv32 fixtures | F2 | TODO |
| F4 | wire + docs | `scripts/build_all.sh`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | F1-F3 | TODO |

### F1 - arch-aware run dispatch
- `elf_xlen(path)` -> 32 / 64 / 0 (reads only `e_ident`).
- **fast**: no `--engine` -> auto-pick `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the
  ELF. Explicit `--engine qemu32/qemu64` wins (+ warn if it contradicts the ELF).
- **cycle + hybrid**: one shared `elf_engine_arch_error(elf, eng)` (DRY) rejects
  an ELF whose class != the engine's `xlen`; identical wording. hybrid keeps its
  extra "fast leg is rv64-only" guard (`hybrid_hw_check`).
- Tested now: `elf_xlen` unit (32 fabricated + 64 real fixture + 0 garbage);
  `cycle --engine vsim:d23 <rv64.elf>` errors. The rv32-ELF directions are
  smoke-tested in F3 (no rv32 fixture yet).

### F2 - dual-arch runtime
- Parameterize `runtime/Makefile` by `ARCH` (rv64 default): CC prefix, `-march`/
  `-mabi`, and `OUT` (`build/runtime` for rv64, `build/runtime/rv32` for rv32).
- `config.env.example`: add `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`.
- `scripts/build_runtime.sh`: build both arches; also fix its stale artifact
  names (it echoes `libandes_sim_runtime.a`/`andes-sim.specs`; the Makefile now
  produces `libandesim_runtime.a`/`andesim.specs`).

### F3 - rv32 fixtures
- Parameterize `tests/fixtures/Makefile` by `ARCH`; add >=1 asm + >=1 C rv32
  fixture (the C one links the rv32 runtime from F2).
- Enables the real rv32 end-to-end + the rv32-direction smoke tests for F1.

### F4 - wire + docs
- `scripts/build_all.sh runtime` builds both arches.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: rv32 section (two toolchains, the rv32 link command, the
  arch-match rules for fast/cycle/hybrid).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ;;
esac

871	---
872	
873	## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)
874	
875	A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
876	only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
877	semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
878	"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
879	per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
880	(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
881	engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
882	and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
883	adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
884	runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.
885	
886	| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
887	|---------|--------|------------------|------|
888	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
889	| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
890	| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |
891	
892	The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandesim_runtime.a`. Build it once
893	(`scripts/build_all.sh runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
894	then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
895	no `-lgloss_vh`):
896	
897	```sh
898	"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
899	  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
900	```
901	
902	`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
903	`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
904	`-specs=andesim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
905	adds `-T andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
906	list to `--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
907	libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.
908	
909	Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:
910	
911	```sh
912	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
913	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
914	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
915	```
916	
917	Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
918	diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
919	the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
920	would never extract it from a `.a`.

---

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandesim_runtime.a`. Build it once
(`scripts/build_all.sh runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
`-specs=andesim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
adds `-T andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.

Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
would never extract it from a `.a`.

See `docs/andesim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb` for a step-by-step walkthrough

diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
would never extract it from a `.a`.

### 5.1 rv32 and rv64

The runtime builds for **both** widths from two toolchains (`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`
= rv64, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32; section 1.3). `scripts/build_all.sh
runtime` builds both when `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` is set:

- rv64 -> `build/runtime/` (link `-B build/runtime`, as above).
- rv32 -> `build/runtime/rv32/` (link `-B build/runtime/rv32`).

The rv32 link is the same shape with the rv32 compiler and `-march=rv32gc
-mabi=ilp32d`:

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

**The driver follows the ELF's width.** `run` reads the ELF's class
(rv32/rv64) and:

- **fast** auto-selects `qemu-system-riscv32` or `qemu-system-riscv64` to match
  the ELF -- no flag needed (an explicit `--engine qemu32`/`qemu64` overrides,
  with a warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- **cycle** / **hybrid** reject an ELF whose width does not match the chosen
  engine, up front, instead of a cryptic failure deep inside the engine:

  ```
  $ ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium prog_rv32.elf
  andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
    -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
  ```

# ROADMAP: rv32 support (rv32 alongside rv64, end to end)

**Goal.** andesim runs rv32 ELFs as a first-class peer of rv64: `fast` picks the
matching `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the ELF, `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an
engine whose width differs, and the runtime + fixtures build for both arches from
two toolchains.

## Shared facts (one source of truth)

- The ELF class byte `e_ident[EI_CLASS]` (1=rv32, 2=rv64) is the truth for an
  ELF's width. The repo's ELF reader already reads it (`elf_syms.cpp`).
- **Two separate toolchains** (not one multilib):
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` = rv64 (`nds64le`, `riscv64-unknown-elf-`),
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32 (`nds32le`, `riscv32-unknown-elf-`).
- rv32 baseline = `-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d` (the d23 engine has m,a,f,d,c),
  mirroring rv64's `rv64gc/lp64d`.
- **Runtime layout (decided):** rv64 stays at `build/runtime/` (back-compat with
  the documented `-B build/runtime` link command); rv32 lands at
  `build/runtime/rv32/`. Linked with `-B build/runtime/rv32`.

## Features

| ID | Feature | Key files | Depends | State |
|----|---------|-----------|---------|-------|
| F1 | arch-aware run dispatch | `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}`, `elf_syms_test.cpp`, `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` | - | **DONE** |
| F2 | dual-arch runtime | `runtime/Makefile`, `config.env{,.example}`, `scripts/build_runtime.sh`, `runtime/{handler.c,vplat_syscalls.c}` (rv64-ism fixes) | config `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` | **DONE** |
| F3 | rv32 fixtures | `tests/fixtures/Makefile` (rv32 set: `rv32_spin`, `rv32_c_hello`), `test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` (rv32 dirs) | F2 | **DONE** |
| F4 | wire + docs | `scripts/build_all.sh`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | F1-F3 | TODO |

### F1 - arch-aware run dispatch
- `elf_xlen(path)` -> 32 / 64 / 0 (reads only `e_ident`).
- **fast**: no `--engine` -> auto-pick `qemu-system-riscv32`/`riscv64` from the
  ELF. Explicit `--engine qemu32/qemu64` wins (+ warn if it contradicts the ELF).
- **cycle + hybrid**: one shared `elf_engine_arch_error(elf, eng)` (DRY) rejects
  an ELF whose class != the engine's `xlen`; identical wording. hybrid keeps its
  extra "fast leg is rv64-only" guard (`hybrid_hw_check`).
- Tested now: `elf_xlen` unit (32 fabricated + 64 real fixture + 0 garbage);
  `cycle --engine vsim:d23 <rv64.elf>` errors. The rv32-ELF directions are
  smoke-tested in F3 (no rv32 fixture yet).

### F2 - dual-arch runtime
- Parameterize `runtime/Makefile` by `ARCH` (rv64 default): CC prefix, `-march`/
  `-mabi`, and `OUT` (`build/runtime` for rv64, `build/runtime/rv32` for rv32).
- `config.env.example`: add `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`.
- `scripts/build_runtime.sh`: build both arches; also fix its stale artifact
  names (it echoes `libandes_sim_runtime.a`/`andes-sim.specs`; the Makefile now
  produces `libandesim_runtime.a`/`andesim.specs`).

### F3 - rv32 fixtures
- Parameterize `tests/fixtures/Makefile` by `ARCH`; add >=1 asm + >=1 C rv32
  fixture (the C one links the rv32 runtime from F2).
- Enables the real rv32 end-to-end + the rv32-direction smoke tests for F1.

### F4 - wire + docs
- `scripts/build_all.sh runtime` builds both arches.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: rv32 section (two toolchains, the rv32 link command, the
  arch-match rules for fast/cycle/hybrid).

## What landed (F1-F4, all TDD: RED -> GREEN)

**F3 - rv32 fixtures** (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`)

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

**1. `tests/fixtures/Makefile:9-11` - the rv64 toolchain gate fires at parse time for `make rv32`, which needs only the rv32 toolchain.** The `$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set)` is unconditional (top-level, parse phase), so even a pure-rv32 build aborts without `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`. The tell: `test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh:618` is forced to pass `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$TC64` to a target that never touches it, and `config.env.example` advertises the arches as independent ("leave unset if you only target rv64"), implying rv32-only should symmetrically work. **Deeper fix:** mirror what `runtime/Makefile:27-43` already does right - gate each arch's toolchain per-ARCH (rv32 recipes use only `CC32`/`LD32`/`TOOLCHAIN32`; the grouped runtime target at :170 already delegates rv32-only correctly). The same altitude fix was applied to one Makefile but not its sibling. **Why it matters:** an rv32-only developer (the portability case the config story invites) cannot build fixtures; the file internally knows rv32 is independent yet its own gate contradicts that.

**2. `cmd_run.cpp:408,410` - the two hybrid guards exist only because hybrid hardcodes its fast leg to `qemu64` instead of following the ELF like `run_fast` does.** They are not redundant *today* (`hybrid_hw_check` asserts "fast leg is rv64-only"; `elf_engine_arch_error` asserts "ELF matches the vsim leg"), so I would not just merge their text. But there is a single unifying notion that subsumes both: *validate the ELF against every leg's engine descriptor* using the already-shared `elf_engine_arch_error` - call it on the fast-leg descriptor (`builtin_qemu_arch(64)`) and on `acc`. That deletes the bespoke `hybrid_hw_check` entirely. The reason it isn't done is the seam at `engine_registry.cpp:42` ("hybrid rv32 ... not wired yet") + the hardcoded `kQemuId64` fast leg at `cmd_run.cpp:416`. **Deeper fix (directional):** when the qemu32 hybrid leg is wired, have hybrid pick its fast-leg arch from the ELF (as `run_fast` already does); then `hybrid_hw_check` vanishes and one notion - "resolve/validate each leg against the ELF arch" - covers all three modes. **Why it matters:** the reviewer's instinct is right - the split is a symptom of hybrid not yet adopting fast's "follow the ELF" model, not two truly distinct layers.

## Medium

**3. `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:73-97` - the `#if __riscv_xlen == 64` gate is correctly placed, but its comment justifies it at the wrong altitude.** The block is genuinely uncompilable on rv32 (it uses rv64-only `ld`/`sd` against the 64-bit L2C MMIO), so a compile-time gate is unavoidable - and the *feature* condition ("does this core have an L2C") is already handled at runtime by the `mmsc_cfg` bit-46 check inside the asm. The defect is the comment ("The rv32 cores here (d23) have no L2") which frames the gate as an L2-presence fact. **Deeper fix:** reframe the comment to the real cause - "this sequence uses rv64-only `ld`/`sd` to reach the 64-bit L2C MMIO; an rv32 core *with* L2 would need a 32-bit-halves access path." **Why it matters:** a future rv32+L2 core maintainer reads "rv32 has no L2", trusts it, and silently ships with no L2 writeback (host reads stale `magicmem`). The runtime feature-check is the right mechanism; the comment hides the one case it doesn't cover.

## Soft / consistency (optional)

**4. `cmd_run.cpp:178-188` - fast's xlen selection is the only engine resolution of the three modes that lives outside the registry.** cycle and hybrid both go through `resolve_accurate_engine`; fast inlines the ELF-or-explicit-or-default + warn-on-conflict policy. A registry-level `resolve_qemu_engine(elf_xlen, want_id, warn&)` next to `builtin_qemu_arch`/`resolve_accurate_engine` would put all three modes' resolution in one layer and make the policy unit-testable (today only the shell test exercises it; `elf_syms_test.cpp` covers `elf_xlen` but not the selection). Small and single-use, so borderline - flagging for the layer symmetry, not as a defect.

**5. `cmd_run.cpp:183-187` - fast's explicit-engine-contradicts-ELF path warns then runs straight into qemu's cryptic "not of ELFCLASSxx".** That is the exact error `elf_engine_arch_error` was added to replace for cycle/hybrid. Since `qemu-system-riscv32` can never run an rv64 ELF (and vice versa), the warning enables no valid run - it just defers a guaranteed failure to a worse message. Routing the contradicting case through the same shared check (still as a warning, or an error to match cycle/hybrid) would close the gap. Minor and partly a documented-intent call.

## Well-placed (no change)

- `runtime/handler.c:25-48` - making the trap CSRs XLEN-wide (`unsigned long`) and computing `intbit = 1UL << (__riscv_xlen-1)` is a root-cause width fix, not a special-case; it also repairs the latent rv64 `mepc`/`mtval` truncation and the `& 0x80000000` interrupt-bit test. Correct altitude.
- `elf_engine_arch_error` shared by cycle and hybrid - one function, one wording. The DRY the commit message claims is real.
- **fast auto-pick vs cycle/hybrid validate is the right asymmetry**, justified by ownership: andesim owns the `qemu32`/`qemu64` pair and can construct either, so auto-pick is honest UX; it does not own the vsim engine (the user built one specific config), so it can only validate-and-reject - it cannot conjure an rv32 vsim that was never built. Do not force these into one "resolve" abstraction.
- runtime layout `build/runtime` (rv64) vs `build/runtime/rv32` - a deliberate, documented back-compat trade-off anchored to the existing `-B build/runtime` link command and docs. Defensible; symmetry here would break published user commands.</result>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1+F3 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the driver respects the ELF's class (rv32/rv64).
#   - fast  auto-picks qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (and runs it).
#   - cycle/hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen, both ways,
#     with one shared clear error and WITHOUT launching the engine.
# Independent, gated sections: rv64 always; the rv32 directions need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (build the rv32 fixture) and skip cleanly without it.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF"

vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)

# --- A. fast: an rv64 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv64 (no --engine) ------
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"

# --- B. cycle: rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run -------
if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
    || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
fi

# --- C. rv32 directions: need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 to build an rv32 fixture -----
TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 directions: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
rv32elf="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rv32_c_hello.elf"
[ -f "$rv32elf" ] || fail "rv32 fixture missing after build: $rv32elf"

# fast: the rv32 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv32.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv32' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv32 for an rv32 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv32 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv32"

# fast: and it actually runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime end to end).
QD=$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)
if [ -x "$QD/qemu-system-riscv32" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hello from QEMU1' \
    || fail "rv32 fixture did not run/print on qemu-system-riscv32: $out"
  ok "fast: rv32 fixture runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime works)"
else
  ok "SKIP rv32 run: no qemu-system-riscv32 under $QD"
fi

# cycle: the rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error.
rv64eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim" && $4=="64"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
    || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the andesim runtime builds for BOTH arches from two
# toolchains. ARCH=rv64 (default) -> build/runtime/, ARCH=rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32/.
# The produced objects must be the right ELF class (rv64=ELFCLASS64, rv32=ELFCLASS32).
#
#   rv64 always runs (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32; SKIPs if unset.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }
elf_class() { od -An -j4 -N1 -tu1 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }   # 1=ELF32 2=ELF64

TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC64" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

# rv64 (default ARCH): library + crt0 land in build/runtime and are ELFCLASS64.
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv64 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv64 runtime build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: missing build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/crt0.o")" = "2" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS64"
ok "rv64 runtime -> build/runtime (ELFCLASS64)"

# rv32: needs the second toolchain. SKIP cleanly if absent.
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 runtime: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv32 runtime build failed (ARCH=rv32, HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$TC32)"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: missing build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/crt0.o")" = "1" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS32"
ok "rv32 runtime -> build/runtime/rv32 (ELFCLASS32)"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by

# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)

                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).

                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file
